53// ============================================================================
54// phase-456 W8 — one subscription registration, stated as one value
55// ============================================================================
56
57/// What a subscription registration STATES — phase-456 W8.
58///
59/// The thirteen `register_subscription_*` / `add_arena_subscription_*` entry
60/// points differ in their DELIVERY SHAPE (typed, raw, borrowed, with-info,
61/// validated) and used to differ in their LANGUAGE, and each re-derived the
62/// same prologue from positional parameters: node identity, topic info, the
63/// declared-depth check, the backend call. Twelve copies of it, and exactly
64/// ONE of them asked the backend whether it dispatches in place.
65///
66/// This is that prologue's argument, as one value. A struct rather than nine
67/// parameters because the fields are independently optional and a caller must
68/// be able to say "I state nothing here" without reordering a call — the same
69/// reason `DescriptorInputs` is a struct one layer up.
70///
71/// Two of its fields are the axes phase-456 W8 found under issue 1319's five
72/// rows: [`backend_hint`](Self::backend_hint) is "does this site know the
73/// type's bound", and [`in_place_capable`](Self::in_place_capable) is what
74/// lets `Executor::open_subscription` ask the third axis once, for every
75/// caller, in every language.
76pub(crate) struct SubscriptionRequest<'a> {
77    /// `None` is the legacy single-node path: identity comes from the
78    /// executor's own name and namespace and the session is slot 0.
79    pub(crate) node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
80    pub(crate) topic_name: &'a str,
81    pub(crate) type_name: &'a str,
82    pub(crate) type_hash: &'a str,
83    pub(crate) qos: QoSProfile,
84    /// Bytes the CALL SITE says it expects to receive, for the BACKEND's
85    /// payload size class (phase-231 / RFC-0038, phase-402 W2).
86    ///
87    /// `None` — and, for a C caller whose ABI spells it `0`, a zero — means
88    /// "this site stated nothing", which is a different claim from "zero
89    /// bytes": `with_rx_buffer_hint(0)` would be the second.
90    pub(crate) backend_hint: Option<usize>,
91    /// Bytes ONE receive slot claims from the arena, already derived by the
92    /// caller that has the type.
93    ///
94    /// Not the same number as [`Self::backend_hint`] — the typed Rust path
95    /// hints the type's bound and sizes the slot from
96    /// `default_subscription_rx_bytes`, which may differ — so both travel.
97    /// Ignored entirely when [`SubscriptionOpen::in_place`] comes back true.
98    pub(crate) slot_bytes: usize,
99    /// Can THIS delivery shape dispatch out of the backend's own receive slot?
100    ///
101    /// A property of the shape, not of the backend: `process_raw_in_place`
102    /// hands the callback borrowed BYTES and nothing else, so a shape that
103    /// must also deliver a wire attachment (`_info`), an integrity status
104    /// (`_validated` / `_safety`) or a `MessageInfo` cannot use it however
105    /// capable the backend is. Stated per call site so an omission is a line
106    /// someone wrote rather than a question nobody asked — which is exactly
107    /// what the C path was before W8.
108    pub(crate) in_place_capable: bool,
109}
110
111/// The result of `Executor::open_subscription`: a claimed slot, a live backend
112/// subscriber, and the ONE answer to the in-place question.
113pub(crate) struct SubscriptionOpen {
114    /// The claimed entry slot. Claimed BEFORE the fallible work, per
115    /// `Executor::emplace_entry`'s rule.
116    pub(crate) slot: usize,
117    pub(crate) handle: session::RmwSubscriber,
118    /// **The only place in this crate that
119    /// `Subscription::supports_process_in_place` is read.**
120    ///
121    /// Before phase-456 W8 the read lived inside
122    /// `register_subscription_buffered_on`, which is the Rust typed path and
123    /// only that: every C and C++ subscription on zenoh or XRCE therefore
124    /// allocated a receive region the backend does not need, at the same order
125    /// as issue 1340's ~9.7 KiB per subscription. The irony phase-456 W8
126    /// measured is that the C callback is the BETTER candidate —
127    /// `RawSubscriptionCallback` is already `(const uint8_t*, size_t, void*)`,
128    /// a borrowed-bytes signature, where the Rust typed path has to produce an
129    /// owned `&M` from somewhere.
130    pub(crate) in_place: bool,
131    /// [`SubscriptionRequest::slot_bytes`], carried through so a caller's arena
132    /// arithmetic reads ONE local rather than re-deriving it.
133    pub(crate) slot_bytes: usize,
134    /// The QoS the backend was actually given — phase-454 W13 through
135    /// phase-456 W8.
136    ///
137    /// NOT the caller's `req.qos`. `declared_qos::honour` REWRITES the depth
138    /// when the system declared one, and the twelve prologues this function
139    /// replaced each passed that rewritten value on to the entry they built.
140    /// Returning it is what keeps that true with one honouring site: a caller
141    /// that stored `req.qos` instead would size its entry from a depth the
142    /// backend never saw, and nothing would fail — the subscription would
143    /// simply hold a different number of samples than the build reserved for
144    /// it.
145    pub(crate) qos: QoSProfile,
146}

169// Executor::open() factory method

171
172/// phase-271 / phase-392 W6 — the `'static` `u64` backing the `alloc`
173/// convenience constructors borrow, sized to `sizing`.
174///
175/// **The named static first, the heap second.** phase-271 made this a
176/// `Box::leak`, and a leak has no symbol: `mem-report` reads an ELF's symbol
177/// table, so the largest single RAM consumer of every Rust image was the one
178/// thing the memory instrument could not see (RFC-0002 § 4.4b). It is served
179/// from `executor::backing::EXECUTOR_BACKING` now — same bytes, same
180/// executor-lifetime reservation, in `.bss` where the linker can print them and
181/// out of the allocator arena that used to pay for them.
182///
183/// The heap arm is still reached, and both cases are legitimate rather than
184/// degraded: a SECOND executor opened through an `alloc` convenience
185/// constructor, and an entry sized past the build-time default. A tiered boot's
186/// spawned tiers are NOT that second executor any more: they open over the
187/// entry's `TierExecutorBacking` slots (`open_with_session_slot`, issue 1571). Neither is an error, so neither
188/// warns — `report_arena_headroom` is where an over-provisioned executor gets
189/// told about itself, and a duplicate line here would just be noise.
190///
191/// `alloc`-only — no_std-no-alloc entries supply their own `static`/stack
192/// backing via `open_in` / `from_session_in`.
193#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
194fn default_backing(sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing) -> &'static mut [MaybeUninit<u64>] {
195    let words = sizing.u64_len();
196    match super::backing::take(words) {
197        Some(backing) => backing,
198        None => alloc::boxed::Box::leak(alloc::boxed::Box::new_uninit_slice(words)),
199    }
200}

202#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
203impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
204    /// phase-271 — open a new executor session over caller-supplied `backing`,
205    /// sized by `sizing` (per-entry sizing). The core, non-generic sized entry
206    /// point: the `alloc` [`open`](Self::open) convenience leaks a default
207    /// backing and delegates here, and the `nros::main!` macro emits a backing
208    /// sized to the entry's own entity count.
209    ///
210    /// Phase 115.M.4 — auto-registers the cffi vtable for whichever
211    /// backend the build was configured for, mirroring the C++ side's
212    /// `#ifdef NROS_RMW_<NAME>` fan-out in `<rclcpp/node.hpp>`. The
213    /// runtime's atomic vtable slot is idempotent: a re-call of any
214    /// backend's `register()` is a no-op, so the fan-out below is safe
215    /// to invoke on every `Executor::open` (cheaper than a `Once` and
216    /// doesn't pull in `std::sync` for no_std targets).
217    ///
218    /// Connects to the middleware at the locator specified in `config`.
219    ///
220    /// # Safety
221    /// `backing` must be ≥ `sizing.u64_len()` words, live for `'s`, and be
222    /// otherwise untouched while the executor lives (see
223    /// [`from_session_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_in)).
224    pub unsafe fn open_in(
225        config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>,
226        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
227        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
228    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
229        use nros_rmw::Rmw;
230
231        // Phase 128.A.3 / 249 P4b.1 — manifest-driven backend selection.
232        //
233        // Every linked backend self-registered via its `.init_array`
234        // ctor before `main` (RFC-0042 §D3.3), so the registry is
235        // already populated — no runtime section walk.
236        //
237        // 1. Honour `config.rmw` — the caller's explicit backend selection,
238        //    mirroring ROS 2's `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`. On a hosted build
239        //    `nros::ExecutorConfigEnvExt::from_env` / `nros::env::resolve_hosted`
240        //    fill it from `$NROS_RMW`; issue 0687 moved that read to the edge,
241        //    because reading a process environment is what kept `std` in this
242        //    crate and an RTOS image has no environment to read.
243        // 2. With no selector, pick the unique registered backend.
244        //    Zero registered → `NoBackend`; more than one →
245        //    `Ambiguous` (user must select one, or use
246        //    `Executor::open_multi`).
247        let selector = config.rmw;
248        match nros_rmw_cffi::resolve_backend(selector.map(str::as_bytes)) {
249            nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Single(_) => {}
250            // Issue 0436 — these are SELECTION outcomes, not transport failures,
251            // and calling them `ConnectionFailed` actively misleads: a PX4 bridge
252            // that registered two backends reported "connection failed", which
253            // reads as a router/network problem and was chased as one. Nothing is
254            // connected at this point — the resolver has not chosen a backend yet.
255            //
256            // The variant still collapses into `NodeError::Transport` (the enum has
257            // no selection arm, and adding one is an ABI change across the C/C++
258            // seams), but `InvalidConfig` at least says "your configuration is
259            // unresolvable", and the std-gated line below names WHICH outcome.
260            other => {
261                {
262                    let why: &str = match other {
263                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::NoBackend => {
264                            "no RMW backend is registered"
265                        }
266                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Ambiguous => {
267                            "more than one RMW backend is registered and no \
268                             $NROS_RMW selector was set — name one (e.g. \
269                             NROS_RMW=uorb), or open per-backend sessions"
270                        }
271                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Unknown => {
272                            "$NROS_RMW names a backend that is not registered"
273                        }
274                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Single(_) => unreachable!(),
275                    };
276                    nros_log::log_error!(
277                        nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
278                        "cannot select an RMW backend — {why}"
279                    );
280                }
281                let _ = other;
282                return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::InvalidConfig));
283            }
284        }
285
286        // RFC-0109 D8 — the image's baked session properties (its bringup's
287        // own `rmw/<backend>` file, lowered at build time).
288        let session = super::session_props::with_session_properties(&[], |properties| {
289            let rmw_config = nros_rmw::RmwConfig {
290                locator: config.locator,
291                mode: config.mode,
292                domain_id: config.domain_id,
293                node_name: config.node_name,
294                namespace: config.namespace,
295                properties,
296            };
297            if let Some(name) = selector {
298                // Selector path: route to the specific named backend so
299                // the env-var-disambiguated outcome matches what the
300                // resolver above identified.
301                nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(name, &rmw_config)
302            } else {
303                nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw.open(&rmw_config)
304            }
305        })
306        .map_err(|e| {
307            // Issue 0465 — do not relabel. This used to discard the backend's
308            // error and report `ConnectionFailed` for every open failure, so an
309            // exhausted session pool (`InvalidConfig`) and a router that is not
310            // there produced the same sentence. Same lesson as the selection
311            // arm above: say which failure happened.
312            nros_log::log_error!(
313                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
314                "RMW session open failed — {e:?}"
315            );
316            NodeError::Transport(e)
317        })?;
318        // SAFETY: forwarded from this fn's contract — `backing`/`sizing` sized
319        // + alive for `'s`.
320        let mut executor = unsafe { Self::from_session_in(session, backing, sizing) };
321        {
322            // `config.clock_us` overrides the constructor's platform default
323            // (issue: assigning `None` here clobbered it and re-enabled the
324            // credit-the-requested-timeout fallback).
325            if let Some(clock) = config.clock_us {
326                executor.clock_us_fn = Some(clock);
327                executor.last_spin_end_us = Some(clock());
328            }
329            // issue 0671 — the SAME rule as `clock_us` directly above, which is
330            // why that one is guarded: a config that does not SPECIFY an epoch
331            // must not be read as "this target HAS no epoch". Assigning `None`
332            // here clobbered the constructor's platform default
333            // (`Some(default_epoch_us)`), and `ExecutorConfig::new` — the path
334            // `nros::init_*` + `ctx.config()` takes — leaves `epoch_us: None`,
335            // so EVERY hosted node built that way silently lost its wall clock.
336            // With no epoch, `Node::subscription` never attaches the age cell
337            // (it needs `(STAMP_OFFSET, epoch)` both `Some`), so a baked
338            // `max_age_ms` contract becomes a silently-dead monitor — the exact
339            // outcome RFC-0052 says must never happen. The rate monitor rides
340            // the GUARDED `clock_us_fn` and kept working, which is why only the
341            // age half went quiet.
342            if let Some(epoch) = config.epoch_us {
343                executor.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch);
344            }
345        }
346        executor.set_node_identity(config.node_name, config.namespace);
347        // Issue 0656 — beside the identity, for the same reason: an entity needs
348        // both to be addressable, and this half used to be dropped here.
349        executor.domain_id = config.domain_id;
350        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
351        executor.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
352        // Phase 277 W2.c — readiness marker for E2E harnesses. This is the
353        // single call-through `open()`/`open_sized()` share, so it fires on
354        // every platform that reaches here (native, freertos, zephyr,
355        // threadx, …) regardless of which RMW backend or board owns the
356        // boot path. It replaces the per-example synthetic
357        // `log::info!("Publishing messages")` markers W4 removes — those
358        // only proved a callback had fired at least once; this line proves
359        // the session itself is up, before any node/callback exists.
360        //
361        // STABILITY CONTRACT: the leading `"nros: session open"` text is
362        // load-bearing — test harnesses grep for it verbatim. Keep it
363        // stable even if the trailing `(rmw=...)` detail changes.
364        #[cfg(feature = "log")]
365        {
366            if let Some(name) = selector {
367                log::info!("nros: session open (rmw={name})");
368            } else {
369                log::info!("nros: session open");
370            }
371        }
372        Ok(executor)
373    }
374}

376#[cfg(all(feature = "rmw-cffi", feature = "alloc"))]
377impl Executor<'static> {
378    /// Open a new executor session using the active RMW backend, at the
379    /// build-time default sizing. Convenience over
380    /// [`open_in`](Self::open_in): leaks a default-sized backing (executor-
381    /// lifetime) so existing callers keep the zero-storage-arg signature.
382    /// Per-entry sizing goes through `open_in` / the `nros::main!` macro.
383    ///
384    /// # Example
385    ///
386    /// ```ignore
387    /// let config = ExecutorConfig::from_env().node_name("my_node");
388    /// let mut executor = Executor::open(&config)?;
389    /// ```
390    pub fn open(config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
391        Self::open_sized(config, super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT)
392    }
393
394    /// phase-271 — like [`open`](Self::open) but sized to a caller-supplied
395    /// `sizing` (its own declared topology) instead of the build-time default.
396    /// The `alloc` entry point the `nros::main!` macro's native board path uses
397    /// to size a fat entry (>default `MAX_CBS` callbacks) without a
398    /// workspace-global `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS`. Leaks a `sizing`-sized backing
399    /// (executor-lifetime); no-alloc entries use `open_in` with their own static.
400    pub fn open_sized(
401        config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>,
402        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
403    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
404        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words, `'static`,
405        // uniquely owned by the returned executor.
406        unsafe { Self::open_in(config, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
407    }
408
409    /// Phase 128.F.1 — explicit per-backend session declaration for
410    /// bridge mode. `specs[0]` becomes the primary session; `specs[1..]`
411    /// open as extras keyed by RMW name. After construction, every
412    /// `create_node_on(name, rmw)` call dispatches to whichever
413    /// session was opened under that RMW name (or, when the rmw name
414    /// matches the primary, the primary session itself).
415    ///
416    /// Single-backend callers should keep using
417    /// [`open`](Self::open) — this entry costs an extra
418    /// `open_with_rmw` per spec and adds no value when only one
419    /// backend is linked.
420    ///
421    /// `$NROS_RMW` env is ignored: bridge mode wants explicit names.
422    ///
423    /// Default-sized `alloc` convenience over
424    /// [`open_multi_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::open_multi_in) (leaks a default backing).
425    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
426    pub fn open_multi(specs: &[SessionSpec<'_>]) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
427        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
428        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words, `'static`.
429        unsafe { Self::open_multi_in(specs, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
430    }
431
432    /// Phase 104.C.1 — open the Executor against a specific RMW
433    /// backend by name. Selects from the named registry (Phase
434    /// 104.B.2). `rmw_name` must match one of the names a backend
435    /// registered under (`"zenoh"`, `"cyclonedds"`, `"xrce"`, …).
436    ///
437    /// Equivalent to [`Executor::open`] when the registry has exactly
438    /// one backend (the default-backend fast path). Use this entry
439    /// point in multi-backend builds where `Executor::open` would
440    /// pick the first-registered slot.
441    ///
442    /// Single-Executor multi-Node multi-RMW (the long-term Design X
443    /// from `docs/roadmap/phase-104-multi-backend-bridges.md`) is
444    /// follow-up work — Phase 104.C.2 + C.3.
445    ///
446    /// Default-sized `alloc` convenience over
447    /// [`open_with_rmw_in`](Self::open_with_rmw_in) (leaks a default backing).
448    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
449    pub fn open_with_rmw(rmw_name: &str, config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
450        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
451        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words, `'static`.
452        unsafe { Self::open_with_rmw_in(rmw_name, config, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
453    }
454}
455
456// phase-271 — no-alloc sized cores for the bridge/named open paths. In
457// `impl<'s>` (not the `'static` alloc block) so they stay available in
458// `rmw-cffi`-without-`alloc` builds (e.g. the `nros-bridge` no_std default),
459// which is where `open_multi`/`open_with_rmw` lived before.
460#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
461impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
462    /// Per-entry-sized [`open_multi`](Self::open_multi): carves `backing` for
463    /// the executor's tables instead of leaking a default one.
464    ///
465    /// # Safety
466    /// `backing`/`sizing` as in [`from_session_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_in).
467    pub(crate) unsafe fn open_multi_in(
468        specs: &[SessionSpec<'_>],
469        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
470        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
471    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
472        // Phase 249 P4b.1 — backends self-registered via their
473        // `.init_array` ctor before `main`; no runtime section walk.
474        let primary = specs
475            .first()
476            .ok_or(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed))?;
477        let primary_session =
478            nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(primary.rmw, &primary.to_rmw_config())
479                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?;
480        // SAFETY: forwarded from this fn's contract.
481        let mut executor = unsafe { Self::from_session_in(primary_session, backing, sizing) };
482        executor.set_node_identity("", "/");
483        // Phase 156 — see `Executor::open` for primary-identity
484        // recording rationale.
485        let _ = executor.primary_rmw_name.push_str(primary.rmw);
486        let _ = executor.primary_locator.push_str(primary.locator);
487        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
488        executor.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
489
490        for spec in specs.iter().skip(1) {
491            let session = nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(spec.rmw, &spec.to_rmw_config())
492                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?;
493            executor
494                .extra_sessions
495                .push(session)
496                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NodeTableFull)?;
497            // Issue 0436 — record WHICH backend/locator this extra is, so
498            // `NodeBuilder::rmw(name)` can find it instead of opening a second
499            // session against the same (singleton) backend.
500            {
501                let mut rmw_s = heapless::String::<32>::new();
502                let _ = rmw_s.push_str(spec.rmw);
503                let mut loc_s = heapless::String::<128>::new();
504                let _ = loc_s.push_str(spec.locator);
505                let _ = executor.extra_session_ids.push((rmw_s, loc_s));
506            }
507            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
508            {
509                let idx = executor.extra_sessions.len() - 1;
510                executor.install_wake_signal_on_extra(idx);
511            }
512        }
513
514        Ok(executor)
515    }
516
517    /// Per-entry-sized [`open_with_rmw`](Self::open_with_rmw): carves `backing`
518    /// for the executor's tables instead of leaking a default one.
519    ///
520    /// # Safety
521    /// `backing`/`sizing` as in [`from_session_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_in).
522    pub unsafe fn open_with_rmw_in(
523        rmw_name: &str,
524        config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>,
525        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
526        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
527    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
528        if !nros_rmw_cffi::backend_registered() {
529            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed));
530        }
531
532        let session = super::session_props::with_session_properties(&[], |properties| {
533            nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(
534                rmw_name,
535                &nros_rmw::RmwConfig {
536                    locator: config.locator,
537                    mode: config.mode,
538                    domain_id: config.domain_id,
539                    node_name: config.node_name,
540                    namespace: config.namespace,
541                    properties,
542                },
543            )
544        })
545        .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed))?;
546        // SAFETY: forwarded from this fn's contract.
547        let mut executor = unsafe { Self::from_session_in(session, backing, sizing) };
548        {
549            // `config.clock_us` overrides the constructor's platform default
550            // (issue: assigning `None` here clobbered it and re-enabled the
551            // credit-the-requested-timeout fallback).
552            if let Some(clock) = config.clock_us {
553                executor.clock_us_fn = Some(clock);
554                executor.last_spin_end_us = Some(clock());
555            }
556            // issue 0671 — the SAME rule as `clock_us` directly above, which is
557            // why that one is guarded: a config that does not SPECIFY an epoch
558            // must not be read as "this target HAS no epoch". Assigning `None`
559            // here clobbered the constructor's platform default
560            // (`Some(default_epoch_us)`), and `ExecutorConfig::new` — the path
561            // `nros::init_*` + `ctx.config()` takes — leaves `epoch_us: None`,
562            // so EVERY hosted node built that way silently lost its wall clock.
563            // With no epoch, `Node::subscription` never attaches the age cell
564            // (it needs `(STAMP_OFFSET, epoch)` both `Some`), so a baked
565            // `max_age_ms` contract becomes a silently-dead monitor — the exact
566            // outcome RFC-0052 says must never happen. The rate monitor rides
567            // the GUARDED `clock_us_fn` and kept working, which is why only the
568            // age half went quiet.
569            if let Some(epoch) = config.epoch_us {
570                executor.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch);
571            }
572        }
573        executor.set_node_identity(config.node_name, config.namespace);
574        // Phase 156 — record primary identity for the session-
575        // cache hit path. See `Executor::open` for the rationale.
576        let _ = executor.primary_rmw_name.push_str(rmw_name);
577        let _ = executor.primary_locator.push_str(config.locator);
578        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
579        executor.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
580        Ok(executor)
581    }
582}

584/// Phase 128.F.1 — per-backend session declaration for
585/// [`Executor::open_multi`]. Each spec names an RMW backend (must
586/// match one a backend registered under via
587/// `nros_rmw_cffi_register_named` / the `RMW_INIT_ENTRIES` linker
588/// section) and the locator + domain id to open against it.
589#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
590#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
591pub struct SessionSpec<'cfg> {
592    pub rmw: &'cfg str,
593    pub locator: &'cfg str,
594    pub domain_id: u32,
595    pub node_name: &'cfg str,
596    pub namespace: &'cfg str,
597    /// The session's backend-specific properties (`RmwConfig::properties`):
598    /// what its domain's RMW file lowers to (RFC-0109 D6, phase-514 W3b).
599    /// Empty: none — the image's baked table is the DEFAULT session's and is
600    /// never given to a spec.
601    pub properties: &'cfg [(&'cfg str, &'cfg str)],
602}
603
604#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
605impl<'cfg> SessionSpec<'cfg> {
606    /// Minimal spec — just RMW name + locator. Domain id defaults to
607    /// 0; node name and namespace are empty.
608    pub const fn new(rmw: &'cfg str, locator: &'cfg str) -> Self {
609        Self {
610            rmw,
611            locator,
612            domain_id: 0,
613            node_name: "",
614            namespace: "",
615            properties: &[],
616        }
617    }
618
619    /// The session's backend-specific properties.
620    pub const fn properties(mut self, properties: &'cfg [(&'cfg str, &'cfg str)]) -> Self {
621        self.properties = properties;
622        self
623    }
624
625    pub const fn domain_id(mut self, domain_id: u32) -> Self {
626        self.domain_id = domain_id;
627        self
628    }
629
630    pub const fn node_name(mut self, name: &'cfg str) -> Self {
631        self.node_name = name;
632        self
633    }
634
635    pub const fn namespace(mut self, ns: &'cfg str) -> Self {
636        self.namespace = ns;
637        self
638    }
639
640    fn to_rmw_config(self) -> nros_rmw::RmwConfig<'cfg> {
641        nros_rmw::RmwConfig {
642            locator: self.locator,
643            mode: nros_rmw::SessionMode::Client,
644            domain_id: self.domain_id,
645            node_name: self.node_name,
646            namespace: self.namespace,
647            properties: self.properties,
648        }
649    }
650}

652// Phase 128.A.3 — selector for the single-backend resolution path.
653//
654// On hosted (`std`) builds, read `$NROS_RMW`; mirrors ROS 2's
655// `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`. Returns the name as a byte vector so the
656// caller can pass it to `nros_rmw_cffi::resolve_backend` and (when
657// `Some`) to `CffiRmw::open_with_rmw`.
658//
659// On `no_std` / bare-metal builds, environment variables are not
660// available; resolution always falls through to the single-backend
661// or ambiguous path. Embedded users with multiple backends use the
662// bridge surface `Executor::open_multi` instead.
663// phase-359 W10 / issue 0687 — the private reader that stood here is gone, and
664// so is the shared one that briefly replaced it. `ExecutorConfig::rmw` carries
665// the selection instead: `nros::rmw_selector` reads the variable ONCE, at the
666// hosted edge, and every consumer takes the value.
667
668// ============================================================================
669// SessionStore — owned or borrowed session
670// ============================================================================
671
672/// Session storage: owned or borrowed via raw pointer.
673///
674/// The C API creates a session in `rclc_support_init()` before the
675/// executor. `Borrowed` lets the executor use that session without owning it.
676#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
677pub(crate) enum SessionStore {
678    Owned(session::ConcreteSession),
679    Borrowed(*mut session::ConcreteSession),
680}
681
682impl core::ops::Deref for SessionStore {
683    type Target = session::ConcreteSession;
684    fn deref(&self) -> &session::ConcreteSession {
685        match self {
686            SessionStore::Owned(s) => s,
687            SessionStore::Borrowed(ptr) => unsafe { &**ptr },
688        }
689    }
690}
691
692impl core::ops::DerefMut for SessionStore {
693    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut session::ConcreteSession {
694        match self {
695            SessionStore::Owned(s) => s,
696            SessionStore::Borrowed(ptr) => unsafe { &mut **ptr },
697        }
698    }
699}
700
701/// Phase 228.E — an opaque, `Send` handle to an [`Executor`]'s RMW session.
702///
703/// In the per-tier model the boot executor opens the one session and hands each
704/// spawned tier task a handle (not a borrow) so the task opens its own
705/// [`Executor`] over that *same* session across the RTOS task boundary. Wrapping
706/// the `pub(crate)` session pointer lets board crates (`nros-board-linux`,
707/// `nros-board-freertos`, …) name + move the handle without naming the session
708/// type. Obtain via [`Executor::session_handle`]; consume via
709/// [`Executor::open_with_session_handle`].
710#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
711pub struct SessionHandle(*mut session::ConcreteSession);
712
713// SAFETY: the per-tier model deliberately shares one session across RTOS tasks;
714// concurrent access is serialized by the RMW backend's internal locks (the RTOS
715// targets build zenoh-pico `Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=1` — RFC-0032 §5.0). The
716// boot executor owns the session and outlives every tier task.
717#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
718unsafe impl Send for SessionHandle {}
719
720#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
721impl SessionHandle {
722    /// Phase 274.W1 — convert to an opaque `*mut c_void` for C/C++ FFI.
723    ///
724    /// The returned pointer encodes the session address and is valid as long as
725    /// the owning executor lives. Reconstruct via [`Self::from_raw`].
726    pub fn into_raw(self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
727        self.0 as *mut core::ffi::c_void
728    }
729
730    /// Phase 274.W1 — reconstruct a `SessionHandle` from an opaque pointer
731    /// returned by [`Self::into_raw`].
732    ///
733    /// # Safety
734    /// `ptr` must be a pointer obtained from `into_raw()` on a `SessionHandle`
735    /// whose underlying session is still live and owned by its original executor.
736    pub unsafe fn from_raw(ptr: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> Self {
737        Self(ptr as *mut session::ConcreteSession)
738    }
739}
740
741/// Phase 228.C — pure callback-group filter decision. `None` = wildcard (accept
742/// every group); `Some` = accept only listed groups. Backs
743/// [`Executor::group_active`]; split out so the logic is unit-testable without a
744/// live session.
745pub(crate) fn group_filter_accepts(
746    active: Option<&[super::storage::ActiveGroup]>,
747    node: u64,
748    group: &str,
749) -> bool {
750    match active {
751        None => true,
752        Some(v) => v.iter().any(|(n, g)| *n == node && g.as_str() == group),
753    }
754}
755
756/// Bytes the parameter store asks the platform heap for, in ONE allocation.
757///
758/// Issue 1706 -- the size of THIS build's store, which folds every knob that
759/// shapes it (`MAX_PARAMETERS`, which a contract's `params:` derives, and the
760/// board's string/array capacities). No formula and no measured constant: the
761/// compiler's own answer, so the number reported below cannot drift from the
762/// allocation it describes.
763#[cfg(all(feature = "param-store", feature = "alloc"))]
764pub const PARAMETER_STORE_BYTES: usize = core::mem::size_of::<nros_params::ParameterStorage>();
765
766/// Issue 1706 -- a TEST seam standing in for a platform heap that returns NULL
767/// for the store's request, on the current thread only (tests run in
768/// parallel). Not a test `#[global_allocator]`: `check-feature-contract`
769/// clause (e) allows exactly one, `nros-platform`'s.
770#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", feature = "param-store"))]
771pub(crate) struct RefuseParameterStore;
772
773#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", feature = "param-store"))]
774std::thread_local! {
775    static REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE: core::cell::Cell<bool> = const { core::cell::Cell::new(false) };
776}
777
778#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", feature = "param-store"))]
779impl RefuseParameterStore {
780    // Only `executor::tests` arms it, and that module is mock-session only.
781    #[cfg(not(feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
782    pub(crate) fn arm() -> Self {
783        REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE.with(|c| c.set(true));
784        Self
785    }
786
787    fn armed() -> bool {
788        REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE.with(core::cell::Cell::get)
789    }
790}
791
792#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", feature = "param-store"))]
793impl Drop for RefuseParameterStore {
794    fn drop(&mut self) {
795        REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE.with(|c| c.set(false));
796    }
797}
