799/// Issue 2023 — create the executor's ONE `/parameter_events` publisher,
800/// `rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterEvent`, announced under `node`.
801///
802/// The ONE creation site `check-infra-queryable-counts` holds
803/// [`PARAM_EVENT_PUBLISHERS`](crate::parameter_services::PARAM_EVENT_PUBLISHERS)
804/// to. A node with a record goes through the node's own publisher path (its
805/// session, QoS overrides and the declared-QoS check); an executor with no
806/// registered node — a direct-API image whose parameter services the
807/// reconcile serves under the executor's own identity — publishes under that
808/// same identity on the primary session, so the events and the six services
809/// name one node.
810#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
811fn create_param_event_pub(
812    exec: &mut Executor<'_>,
813    node: super::node_record::NodeId,
814    qos: QoSProfile,
815) -> Result<session::RmwPublisher, NodeError> {
816    type Event = nros_rcl_interfaces::msg::ParameterEvent;
817    const TOPIC: &str = "/parameter_events";
818    if exec.nodes.get(node.index()).is_some() {
819        return exec.create_raw_publisher_handle_on(
820            node,
821            TOPIC,
822            <Event as RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
823            <Event as RosMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
824            qos,
825        );
826    }
827    let node_name = exec.node_name.clone();
828    let namespace = exec.namespace.clone();
829    let mut topic = TopicInfo::new(
830        TOPIC,
831        <Event as RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
832        <Event as RosMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
833    )
834    .with_domain(exec.domain_id)
835    .with_namespace(&namespace);
836    if !node_name.is_empty() {
837        topic = topic.with_node_name(&node_name);
838    }
839    let session = &mut *exec.session;
840    super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
841        &qos,
842        Session::supported_qos_policies(session),
843        "publisher",
844        TOPIC,
845    )?;
846    session
847        .create_publisher(&topic, qos)
848        .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::PublisherCreationFailed))
849}
850
851/// Issue 2023 — say that `/parameter_events` could not be created for a node
852/// whose parameter services did come up. Cold: it formats.
853#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
854#[cold]
855#[inline(never)]
856fn report_parameter_events_refused(e: NodeError) {
857    nros_log::log_error!(
858        nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
859        "/parameter_events could not be created ({:?}); the parameter services are up, \
860         but no parameter change is published. A publisher slot the image did not size \
861         for is the usual cause (issue 2023).",
862        e
863    );
864}
865
866/// Issue 1706 -- say, once, that the parameter store did not fit.
867///
868/// The RFC-0100 D11 shape, one layer up from Cyclone's boot check: the
869/// failure is named where it is decided, with the number a reader needs to
870/// size the heap, instead of surfacing as an anonymous halt in the allocator.
871/// What it can name is the REQUEST; the heap's own report (Zephyr's `HEAP
872/// EXHAUSTED` line, the board's `nros: heap peak` line) carries the capacity.
873#[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
874#[cold]
875fn report_parameter_store_refused() {
876    // Issue 1812 -- with no heap there was no allocation to refuse: the
877    // backing carved no store, and that is the whole story.
878    #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
879    {
880        let logger = nros_log::get_logger("nros");
881        nros_log::log_error!(
882            logger,
883            "parameter store refused: this executor's backing carves none and the build has no heap"
884        );
885        nros_log::log_error!(
886            logger,
887            "every parameter declaration on this executor is refused (issue 1812)"
888        );
889        nros_log::log_error!(
890            logger,
891            "open it with ExecutorSizing::params > 0 (NROS_PARAM_STORE=1, NROS_MAX_PARAMETERS)"
892        );
893    }
894    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
895    report_parameter_heap_store_refused();
896}
897
898/// The `alloc` half of [`report_parameter_store_refused`]: the heap refused
899/// the store's one allocation (issue 1706).
900#[cfg(all(feature = "param-store", feature = "alloc"))]
901#[cold]
902fn report_parameter_heap_store_refused() {
903    let slots = nros_params::MAX_PARAMETERS;
904    // THREE short lines, not one sentence: a log backend truncates a long
905    // line (Zephyr's cut the first draft at its slot count), and the number
906    // is the one part that must survive.
907    let logger = nros_log::get_logger("nros");
908    nros_log::log_error!(
909        logger,
910        "parameter store refused: needs {} bytes in one allocation ({} slots x {})",
911        PARAMETER_STORE_BYTES,
912        slots,
913        PARAMETER_STORE_BYTES / if slots == 0 { 1 } else { slots }
914    );
915    nros_log::log_error!(
916        logger,
917        "every parameter declaration on this executor is refused (issue 1706)"
918    );
919    // phase-382 W3' -- the remedy that takes the store OUT of the heap comes
920    // first: a build that knows the image builds a store carves it from the
921    // executor backing instead (`nros_params::IMPLIED_STORE_SLOTS`).
922    nros_log::log_error!(
923        logger,
924        "declare the parameters in the contract (params:) or state NROS_PARAM_STORE=1"
925    );
926    nros_log::log_error!(
927        logger,
928        "and the store is carved from the executor backing; or raise the image heap"
929    );
930}
931
932/// `text` typed as `declared`'s type — phase-482 W5. `None` when it does not
933/// parse as that type, or the type takes no override yet (arrays).
934///
935/// A `NotSet` declaration has no type to follow, so the text decides: `true` /
936/// `false`, then an integer, then a double, then a string — the order rcl's
937/// YAML reading gives an unquoted scalar.
938#[cfg(all(feature = "param-store", feature = "alloc"))]
939fn typed_param_override(
940    text: &str,
941    declared: &nros_params::ParameterValue,
942) -> Option<nros_params::ParameterValue> {
943    use nros_params::ParameterValue as V;
944    let boolean = |t: &str| match t {
945        "true" | "True" | "TRUE" => Some(true),
946        "false" | "False" | "FALSE" => Some(false),
947        _ => None,
948    };
949    let string = |t: &str| heapless::String::try_from(t).ok().map(V::String);
950    match declared {
951        V::Bool(_) => boolean(text).map(V::Bool),
952        V::Integer(_) => text.parse::<i64>().ok().map(V::Integer),
953        V::Double(_) => text.parse::<f64>().ok().map(V::Double),
954        V::String(_) => string(text),
955        V::NotSet => boolean(text)
956            .map(V::Bool)
957            .or_else(|| text.parse::<i64>().ok().map(V::Integer))
958            .or_else(|| text.parse::<f64>().ok().map(V::Double))
959            .or_else(|| string(text)),
960        _ => None,
961    }
962}
963
964#[cfg(test)]
965mod group_filter_tests {
966    use super::group_filter_accepts;
967    use crate::executor::storage::{ActiveGroup, node_identity_hash};
968
969    type Group = heapless::String<32>;
970
971    fn entry(node: &str, ns: &str, g: &str) -> ActiveGroup {
972        let mut s = Group::new();
973        s.push_str(g).unwrap();
974        (node_identity_hash(node, ns), s)
975    }
976
977    #[test]
978    fn wildcard_accepts_all() {
979        assert!(group_filter_accepts(
980            None,
981            node_identity_hash("n", "/"),
982            "anything"
983        ));
984    }
985
986    #[test]
987    fn set_accepts_only_listed_groups() {
988        let active = [entry("n", "/", "ctrl")];
989        let n = node_identity_hash("n", "/");
990        assert!(group_filter_accepts(Some(&active[..]), n, "ctrl"));
991        assert!(!group_filter_accepts(Some(&active[..]), n, "telem"));
992    }
993
994    /// issue 1172 — the SAME group id on a DIFFERENT node is not this tier's.
995    ///
996    /// This is the case the whole change exists for: two nodes may legitimately
997    /// declare `ctrl`, pinned to different tiers, and the old filter — keyed on
998    /// the group name alone — admitted both onto whichever tier asked first.
999    #[test]
1000    fn the_same_group_on_another_node_is_not_accepted() {
1001        let active = [entry("talker", "/", "ctrl")];
1002        assert!(group_filter_accepts(
1003            Some(&active[..]),
1004            node_identity_hash("talker", "/"),
1005            "ctrl"
1006        ));
1007        assert!(
1008            !group_filter_accepts(
1009                Some(&active[..]),
1010                node_identity_hash("listener", "/"),
1011                "ctrl"
1012            ),
1013            "another node's identically-named group must NOT be admitted"
1014        );
1015    }
1016
1017    /// The namespace is part of the identity, not decoration: two nodes may
1018    /// share a bare name under different namespaces, which is legal in ROS.
1019    #[test]
1020    fn the_same_name_under_another_namespace_is_a_different_node() {
1021        let active = [entry("talker", "/left", "ctrl")];
1022        assert!(!group_filter_accepts(
1023            Some(&active[..]),
1024            node_identity_hash("talker", "/right"),
1025            "ctrl"
1026        ));
1027    }
1028
1029    /// An empty namespace and `/` are the SAME node. Both ends normalise, and
1030    /// if only one did, a filter would never match what it named.
1031    #[test]
1032    fn an_empty_namespace_normalises_to_root() {
1033        assert_eq!(
1034            node_identity_hash("talker", ""),
1035            node_identity_hash("talker", "/")
1036        );
1037    }
1038
1039    /// The separator is load-bearing: without it `("ab","c")` and `("a","bc")`
1040    /// would hash alike, and a node name may contain any namespace character.
1041    #[test]
1042    fn the_name_namespace_split_cannot_be_forged() {
1043        assert_ne!(
1044            node_identity_hash("ab", "/c"),
1045            node_identity_hash("a", "b/c")
1046        );
1047    }
1048
1049    /// phase-409 — the wildcard and an EMPTY filter are different answers, and
1050    /// the carved table cannot tell them apart on its own (the old
1051    /// `Option<Vec>` could). `Executor::active_groups_filtering` is what keeps
1052    /// them apart; this pins the distinction at the decision itself.
1053    #[test]
1054    fn an_empty_filter_is_not_the_wildcard() {
1055        let empty: [ActiveGroup; 0] = [];
1056        let n = node_identity_hash("n", "/");
1057        assert!(!group_filter_accepts(Some(&empty[..]), n, "anything"));
1058        assert!(group_filter_accepts(None, n, "anything"));
1059    }
1060}
1061
1062// ============================================================================
1063// Executor
1064// ============================================================================
1065
1066/// Backend-agnostic executor that owns a session.
1067///
1068/// Provides `create_node()` for entity creation and `drive_io()` for polling.
1069///
1070/// # Callback Mode
1071///
1072/// The executor supports arena-based callback registration via the
1073/// `node_mut(id).subscription(t)` builder and
1074/// [`register_service()`](Self::register_service), with dispatch via
1075/// [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once). No heap allocation is needed.
1076///
1077/// The sizes are set via `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS` (default 4) and
1078/// `NROS_EXECUTOR_ARENA_SIZE` (default 4096) environment variables at build time.
1079///
1080/// Phase 124.B.2 — opaque context handed to the runtime wake
1081/// callback. Backends store the raw pointer + invoke the callback;
1082/// the callback decodes back to `&WakeCtx`.
1083///
1084/// `repr(align(64))` because an entity waker carries its slot in the low six
1085/// bits of a pointer to this struct (phase-397 W2, `entity_wake`).
1086#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1087#[repr(align(64))]
1088pub(crate) struct WakeCtx {
1089    pub(crate) flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>,
1090    /// The wake primitive. Phase 130.3 added it beside a `std::sync::Condvar`
1091    /// pair and noted that "a future migration to a single primitive flips one
1092    /// branch instead of two"; phase-359 W10 is that migration, and this is the
1093    /// one that survived.
1094    pub(crate) node_wake: Option<portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::node_wake::NodeWake>>,
1095    /// phase-397 W2 — one bit per entry slot an attributed arrival has marked
1096    /// since the executor last took the word. Set by an entity waker
1097    /// (`entity_wake`), never by the session-scoped callback, which cannot
1098    /// name an entry. W3 reads it instead of scanning.
1099    /// A `usize`, not a `u64`: 32-bit targets without 64-bit atomics have no
1100    /// `AtomicU64`, so the word names `usize::BITS` slots (`entity_wake::SLOTS`)
1101    /// and an entry above that keeps the session wake.
1102    pub(crate) ready: portable_atomic::AtomicUsize,
1103    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 (RFC-0108 D7) -- the band workers' wake objects
1104    /// (`Executor::attach_band_worker`), a list of `'static` waiters that is
1105    /// only ever pushed to. An attributed arrival wakes the worker whose band
1106    /// holds its slot; an unattributed one wakes every worker.
1107    pub(crate) band_waiters: portable_atomic::AtomicPtr<super::scheduler::BandWaiter>,
1108}
1109
1110#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1111impl WakeCtx {
1112    pub(crate) fn new(
1113        flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>,
1114        node_wake: Option<portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::node_wake::NodeWake>>,
1115    ) -> Self {
1116        Self {
1117            flag,
1118            node_wake,
1119            ready: portable_atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0),
1120            band_waiters: portable_atomic::AtomicPtr::new(core::ptr::null_mut()),
1121        }
1122    }
1123
1124    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 -- the wake for an arrival nothing attributes:
1125    /// the executor's own worker, and every band worker, since any of them
1126    /// may own the slot it is for.
1127    pub(crate) fn signal(&self) {
1128        self.signal_own();
1129        let mut w = self.band_waiters.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire);
1130        while !w.is_null() {
1131            // SAFETY: only `'static` waiters are linked, never unlinked.
1132            let waiter = unsafe { &*w };
1133            waiter.signal();
1134            w = waiter.next.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire);
1135        }
1136    }
1137
1138    /// The executor's own worker's wake: flag, then the primitive. Shared by
1139    /// the session callback and the entity waker so the two cannot drift.
1140    pub(crate) fn signal_own(&self) {
1141        // Phase 141.B.2 — capture T0 at cb entry. No-op when the
1142        // probe feature is off or no cycle reader is installed.
1143        #[cfg(feature = "wake-latency-probe")]
1144        super::wake_probe::on_wake();
1145        // Lock-free: the `flag` store is SeqCst and therefore happens-before any
1146        // subsequent acquire in the waiter, so a wake cannot be missed even though
1147        // nothing is held here.
1148        self.flag.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
1149        // phase-359 W10 — ONE primitive. This used to signal both a
1150        // `std::sync::Condvar` and (since phase 130.3) the `NodeWake`, "so the cb
1151        // keeps working whichever wait primitive spin_once is using". `spin_once`
1152        // now has only one, so this has only one to signal.
1153        if let Some(nw) = self.node_wake.as_ref() {
1154            nw.signal();
1155        }
1156    }
1157
1158    /// phase-397 W2 — an attributed arrival on entry `slot`: its bit, then the
1159    /// wake. The bit is set FIRST, so a waiter that sees the flag sees the bit.
1160    pub(crate) fn mark_ready(&self, slot: usize) {
1161        self.ready
1162            .fetch_or(1usize << slot, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
1163        // phase-509 P9b item 3 (RFC-0108 D7) -- only the worker whose band
1164        // holds the slot; the executor's own worker when no band does.
1165        let bit = 1usize << slot;
1166        let mut w = self.band_waiters.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire);
1167        while !w.is_null() {
1168            // SAFETY: only `'static` waiters are linked, never unlinked.
1169            let waiter = unsafe { &*w };
1170            if waiter.slots.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) & bit != 0 {
1171                waiter.signal();
1172                return;
1173            }
1174            w = waiter.next.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire);
1175        }
1176        self.signal_own();
1177    }
1178}
1179
1180/// Phase 124.B.2 — runtime wake callback.
1181///
1182/// RT-context contract:
1183///
1184/// * **Thread-safe**: callable from any thread. The cb is lock-free
1185///   on the cv path — no mutex held during `notify_all`. Lost-wakeup
1186///   is prevented by the waiter checking `wake_flag` under
1187///   `wake_mu` via the `wait_timeout_while` predicate.
1188/// * **NOT async-signal-safe on POSIX**: `pthread_cond_signal`
1189///   isn't on the POSIX async-signal-safe function list. For POSIX
1190///   signal handler wake, use a `signalfd` + select pattern in a
1191///   thread that owns the wake duty — that pattern is Linux-only
1192///   (`signalfd`/`eventfd` are Linux syscalls, not POSIX), which is
1193///   why the `WakeSignalFd` worker is gated `target_os = "linux"`.
1194/// * **RTOS ISR**: per-RTOS platform layer wraps the cv with an
1195///   ISR-safe primitive (`xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`,
1196///   `tx_event_flags_set` from ISR, `k_sem_give` from ISR on
1197///   Zephyr). Backend's ISR caller routes through the platform's
1198///   `signal_from_isr` API instead of this cb directly.
1199/// * **Bounded execution time**: O(1) — atomic store + cv notify.
1200///   No allocation, no contended lock.
1201///
1202/// The cb is the symbol backends invoke from their async wake path
1203/// (datagram arrival, worker-thread enqueue, etc.). It does
1204/// flag-write + condvar-signal in that order, lock-free.
1205#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1206pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
1207    if ctx.is_null() {
1208        return;
1209    }
1210    // SAFETY: ctx points at a `WakeCtx` owned by an Executor still
1211    // alive at the time of the call. `Executor::clear_wake_signal`
1212    // discharges that obligation — `set_wake_callback(None, _)` on the
1213    // primary and every extra session — from `Executor::close` (before
1214    // the session closes) and from the end of `Executor::drop` (before
1215    // `wake_ctx` is dropped). Issue 1385: until then this comment named
1216    // an "`install_wake_*` teardown path" that did not exist, and
1217    // `set_wake_callback(None` occurred nowhere in the tree but here.
1218    let wake = unsafe { &*(ctx as *const WakeCtx) };
1219    wake.signal();
1220}
1221
1222/// phase-436 — the callback a backend holds when several executors share its
1223/// session: signal every member of the [`WakeFanout`](super::wake_fanout)
1224/// whose address is `ctx`. The entry is a `static`, so `ctx` never dangles.
1225#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1226pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_fanout_wake_cb(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
1227    if ctx.is_null() {
1228        return;
1229    }
1230    // SAFETY: `ctx` is `WakeFanout::as_ctx` of a `static` pool entry.
1231    let fanout = unsafe { &*(ctx as *const super::wake_fanout::WakeFanout) };
1232    fanout.fire(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb);
1233}
1234
1235/// phase-467 Row 8 — the symbol a backend invokes when the ROS GRAPH changes.
1236///
1237/// `rmw_event_callback_t`'s shape, so it fits the ABI slot unchanged:
1238/// `user_data` plus a coalesced count, and no payload. The count is IGNORED on
1239/// purpose — a guard condition is a level, not a queue, so N changes observed
1240/// before the executor spins are one dispatch. That is the same collapse
1241/// `guard_try_process` already performs on a flag several `trigger()`s set.
1242///
1243/// RT-context contract: identical to [`nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`] and for the
1244/// same reason — a relaxed-store-plus-wake, O(1), no allocation, no lock. Both
1245/// are called from a transport or worker thread.
1246///
1247/// # Safety
1248///
1249/// `user_data` must be the pointer `Executor::install_graph_change_guard`
1250/// passed: a `GuardCondition` in a box that executor owns. The obligation is
1251/// discharged by `clear_graph_change_signal`, which retires the pointer from
1252/// the backend BEFORE the box is freed, from `close()` and from `drop`. Issue
1253/// 1385 is what the other ordering costs.
1254#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1255pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_runtime_graph_change_cb(
1256    user_data: *const core::ffi::c_void,
1257    _count: usize,
1258) {
1259    if user_data.is_null() {
1260        return;
1261    }
1262    // SAFETY: see this function's `# Safety`.
1263    let guard = unsafe { &*(user_data as *const GuardCondition) };
1264    guard.trigger();
1265}
1266
1267/// Phase 124.B.7.c — Linux signalfd worker.
1268///
1269/// Owns a Linux `eventfd` plus a worker task that `read()`s the
1270/// fd and forwards it as a wake. The eventfd
1271/// write side is async-signal-safe per the kernel contract
1272/// (`write(2)` to an eventfd is permitted from signal handlers),
1273/// closing the gap that `pthread_cond_signal` leaves open on POSIX.
1274///
1275/// Lifecycle:
1276///   * Constructed lazily in `Executor::signal_fd()` on first
1277///     caller request.
1278///   * `Drop` writes a shutdown sentinel + joins the worker.
1279///
1280/// Caller flow (signal handler):
1281///   1. Get fd via `Executor::signal_fd()` before installing the
1282///      handler.
1283///   2. Handler does `eventfd_write(fd, 1)` (equivalently,
1284///      `write(fd, &1u64, 8)`).
1285///   3. Worker thread reads the fd, signals wake_cv. spin_once
1286///      blocked in cv.wait_timeout_while sees flag=true and exits.
1287///
1288/// phase-359 W10 — the worker is a PLATFORM TASK, not a `std::thread`, and it
1289/// forwards through the same [`NodeWake`](super::node_wake::NodeWake) the
1290/// runtime wake callback uses rather than a `std::sync::Condvar`. The eventfd
1291/// itself is still Linux — that is what makes the write async-signal-safe — so
1292/// this stays `target_os = "linux"`; what it no longer is, is std-only.
1293#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1294pub struct WakeSignalFd {
1295    fd: core::ffi::c_int,
1296    ctx: portable_atomic_util::Arc<SignalFdCtx>,
1297    task: Option<nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask>,
1298}
1299
1300/// What the signalfd worker task needs, reachable through one pointer.
1301#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1302struct SignalFdCtx {
1303    fd: core::ffi::c_int,
1304    shutdown: portable_atomic::AtomicBool,
1305    /// The executor's wake state — the same `WakeCtx` the runtime callback
1306    /// decodes, reached as an address so the context is plainly `Send`.
1307    wake_ctx: usize,
1308}
1309
1310/// Worker entry: read the eventfd, forward as a wake, until shut down.
1311///
1312/// # Safety
1313/// `arg` must point at a live [`SignalFdCtx`] whose `wake_ctx` addresses a
1314/// `WakeCtx` that outlives this task.
1315#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1316unsafe extern "C" fn signal_fd_worker(arg: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
1317    // SAFETY: the spawn site passes `Arc::as_ptr` of a ctx it keeps alive until
1318    // after the join in `Drop`.
1319    let ctx = unsafe { &*(arg as *const SignalFdCtx) };
1320    loop {
1321        let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
1322        // SAFETY: reading 8 bytes from an eventfd into an 8-byte buffer.
1323        let n = unsafe { libc::read(ctx.fd, buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut core::ffi::c_void, 8) };
1324        if ctx.shutdown.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
1325            return core::ptr::null_mut();
1326        }
1327        if n <= 0 {
1328            // EINTR / EOF — shutdown was re-checked above, so loop.
1329            continue;
1330        }
1331        // Same effect as `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`, reached directly because
1332        // the shutdown check above plus `Drop`'s join is what guarantees the
1333        // `WakeCtx` is still alive.
1334        // SAFETY: `wake_ctx` addresses the executor's `WakeCtx`, which outlives
1335        // this task by that same guarantee.
1336        unsafe {
1337            let w = &*(ctx.wake_ctx as *const WakeCtx);
1338            w.flag.store(true, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
1339            if let Some(wake) = w.node_wake.as_ref() {
1340                wake.signal();
1341            }
1342        }
1343    }
1344}
1345
1346#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1347impl WakeSignalFd {
1348    /// Spawn the worker. `wake_ctx_ptr` is the `*const WakeCtx`
1349    /// produced by `Executor::wake_ctx_ptr` — same value the
1350    /// runtime wake cb decodes.
1351    ///
1352    /// phase-359 W10 — returns `NodeError` rather than `std::io::Error`. The
1353    /// only caller is `Executor::signal_fd`, and the errno detail it used to
1354    /// carry had no consumer: the one failure a caller can act on is "this
1355    /// platform would not give me the worker", which is what
1356    /// `NotInitialized` says — the eventfd and the task are both subsystems
1357    /// this capability requires and neither is guaranteed.
1358    fn new(wake_ctx_ptr: *const WakeCtx) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
1359        // SAFETY: `eventfd(2)` with a valid flag; returns -1 on failure.
1360        let fd = unsafe { libc::eventfd(0, libc::EFD_CLOEXEC) };
1361        if fd < 0 {
1362            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
1363        }
1364        let ctx = portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(SignalFdCtx {
1365            fd,
1366            shutdown: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
1367            wake_ctx: wake_ctx_ptr as usize,
1368        });
1369        let arg = portable_atomic_util::Arc::as_ptr(&ctx) as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
1370        // SAFETY: `arg` points at a ctx this struct owns and keeps alive until
1371        // after the join in `Drop`.
1372        let Some(task) = (unsafe {
1373            nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask::spawn(
1374                signal_fd_worker,
1375                arg,
1376                // A read(2) loop and one atomic store — the smallest stack any
1377                // port will honour is plenty.
1378                8192,
1379                c"nros-wakefd".as_ptr(),
1380            )
1381        }) else {
1382            // SAFETY: nothing else holds the fd — the task never started.
1383            unsafe { libc::close(fd) };
1384            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
1385        };
1386        Ok(Self {
1387            fd,
1388            ctx,
1389            task: Some(task),
1390        })
1391    }
1392
1393    /// Returns the writable eventfd. The caller (typically a POSIX
1394    /// signal handler) writes any non-zero 8-byte value to trigger
1395    /// a wake. `write(2)` on an eventfd is async-signal-safe per
1396    /// `eventfd(2)` man page.
1397    pub fn fd(&self) -> core::ffi::c_int {
1398        self.fd
1399    }
1400}
1401
1402#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1403impl Drop for WakeSignalFd {
1404    fn drop(&mut self) {
1405        self.ctx
1406            .shutdown
1407            .store(true, portable_atomic::Ordering::Release);
1408        // Wake the worker so it re-checks shutdown: it is blocked in `read`,
1409        // which only this write can release.
1410        let one: u64 = 1;
1411        // SAFETY: an 8-byte write to our own eventfd.
1412        unsafe {
1413            libc::write(self.fd, &one as *const u64 as *const core::ffi::c_void, 8);
1414        }
1415        if let Some(task) = self.task.take() {
1416            task.join();
1417        }
1418        // SAFETY: the worker has exited, so nothing else touches the fd.
1419        unsafe { libc::close(self.fd) };
1420    }
1421}
1422
1423/// Phase 124.B.7.b — ISR / interrupt-context wake callback.
1424///
1425/// Same semantics as [`nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`] but constrained to
1426/// async-signal-safe / ISR-safe primitives.
1427///
1428/// Per-platform routing:
1429///
1430/// * **POSIX (std)**: `pthread_cond_signal` is NOT on the POSIX
1431///   async-signal-safe function list. Calling from a SIGUSR1
1432///   handler is technically UB. Real fix (Phase 124.B.7.c) routes
1433///   via `signalfd`/`eventfd` + a runtime worker thread — Linux
1434///   only, since neither syscall is POSIX; until that lands,
1435///   signal-handler callers MUST use
1436///   `rclc_guard_condition_trigger` from a **separate thread** (not
1437///   from the handler itself), OR set the wake_flag and rely on
1438///   the next poll deadline. This cb currently aliases the regular
1439///   `wake_cb` and is safe only from non-signal-handler ISR-like
1440///   contexts (e.g. timer thread, kernel callback).
1441///
1442/// * **RTOS no_std (Zephyr/FreeRTOS/ThreadX)**: routes through the
1443///   platform-cffi `condvar_signal_from_isr` slot. Each backend
1444///   uses its ISR-safe variant — `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`,
1445///   `tx_semaphore_put`, `k_condvar_signal`.
1446///
1447/// `ctx` semantics identical to [`nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`].
1448#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1449#[allow(dead_code)] // Public exposure pending B.7.c signalfd worker.
1450pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb_from_isr(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
1451    // Today: alias regular wake_cb. POSIX signal-handler safety
1452    // pending B.7.c (signalfd worker-thread forward). Documented in
1453    // the contract above so callers know the boundary.
1454    unsafe { nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb(ctx) };
1455}
1456
1457/// Phase 216 follow-up — per-Node dispatch trampoline registered with
1458/// [`Executor::register_dispatch_slot`].
1459///
1460/// The board-side dispatch task (RTIC `__nros_run` / Embassy
1461/// `__nros_run_task`) dequeues a `nros_platform::SignaledCallback`
1462/// envelope and forwards `(cb_id, ctx_ptr)` into
1463/// [`Executor::dispatch_callback`]; that method linear-scans this
1464/// slot table and invokes every registered `on_callback` with the
1465/// owning Node's per-Node `state` blob. Each Node's
1466/// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` self-filters on its own
1467/// `CallbackId` tag set, so a slot whose Node doesn't own this
1468/// callback is a cheap no-op string compare.
1469///
1470/// The shape mirrors the per-pkg `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback`
1471/// extern "C" trampoline emitted by the `nros::node!()` macro
1472/// (see `packages/core/nros-macros/src/lib.rs` Phase 216.A.5).
1473///
1474/// # Why not `linkme`
1475///
1476/// `linkme::distributed_slice` hangs on bare-metal Cortex-M /
1477/// RISC-V because `cortex_m_rt`'s link script doesn't provide the
1478/// `__start_/__stop_` section anchors in a shape that lets the
1479/// iterator terminate (see
1480/// `packages/rmw/cffi/src/section.rs` Phase 142). Since
1481/// stm32f4 RTIC / Embassy boards are the whole point of Phase 216,
1482/// the registry uses the explicit `register()` pattern from Phase
1483/// 104.A.
1484#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1485pub struct DispatchSlot {
1486    /// Owning Node's `State` blob — produced by the macro-emitted
1487    /// `i()` and round-tripped through
1488    /// `nros::__macro::__private_node_state_into_raw`. Opaque to the
1489    /// executor.
1490    pub state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1491    /// Per-Node `extern "C"` trampoline; signature matches the
1492    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` symbol the `nros::node!()`
1493    /// macro emits.
1494    pub on_callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(
1495        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1496        cb_id_ptr: *const u8,
1497        cb_id_len: usize,
1498        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1499    ),
1500}
1501
1502// SAFETY: `DispatchSlot` carries two raw pointers (`state` + an
1503// extern "C" fn pointer). The fn pointer is `Send`/`Sync` by
1504// definition; the `state` pointer's `Send`/`Sync` story matches the
1505// owning `Executor` (which is `unsafe impl Send`). Treating the
1506// slot itself as `Send` keeps the existing `Executor` Send impl
1507// intact — see `unsafe impl Send for Executor {}` later in this
1508// file.
1509unsafe impl Send for DispatchSlot {}
1510unsafe impl Sync for DispatchSlot {}
1511
1512/// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — executor-owned component tick slot.
1513///
1514/// The layering-clean half of the W0-B `install` seam's tick fix
1515/// (phase-257 D2). A `nros`-layer `install`/`register_node_borrowed`
1516/// builds an `Arc<ComponentCell>` (the typed/poll-driven component
1517/// state) and enrolls it here via [`Executor::enroll_component`]; the
1518/// executor then drives `tick` on every enrolled slot at the tail of
1519/// each [`spin_once`](Executor::spin_once) — so `install`'d nodes
1520/// (C, C++, **and Rust owned-spin**) tick, closing the
1521/// service-client/action poll gap that the callback-`Arc`-only
1522/// lifetime left open.
1523///
1524/// Like [`DispatchSlot`] the executor only sees raw pointers + `extern
1525/// "C"` fn pointers (no `nros` dep — `nros-node` is the lower layer):
1526///
1527/// * `state` — a *leaked* `Arc<ComponentCell>` (via `Arc::into_raw`),
1528///   re-borrowed by the `nros`-side `tick`/`drop` fns. Unlike a
1529///   pub/sub/timer component (kept alive by the executor's per-entity
1530///   callback `Arc` clones), a poll-only component has no callbacks, so
1531///   the slot must own a clone of the cell — hence the paired `drop`.
1532/// * `tick` — `nros`-side `extern "C"` fn that casts `state` back to
1533///   `&ComponentCell`, casts `exec_ctx` back to `*mut Executor`, and
1534///   runs that one cell's tick (mirrors `ExecutorNodeRuntime::run_ticks`).
1535/// * `drop` — `nros`-side `extern "C"` fn run on `Executor::drop` that
1536///   reconstitutes + drops the leaked `Arc`, so the executor owns the
1537///   cell's lifetime.
1538///
1539/// Kept a SEPARATE registry from [`DispatchSlot`] on purpose: framework
1540/// dispatch (RTIC / Embassy) is interrupt-driven, name-keyed, and has no
1541/// tick/own concern — mixing the two risks that path.
1542#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1543pub struct ComponentSlot {
1544    /// Leaked `Arc<ComponentCell>` (opaque to the executor). Owned by
1545    /// this slot — dropped via `drop` on `Executor::drop`.
1546    pub state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1547    /// `nros`-side tick trampoline: `(state, exec_ctx)` where `exec_ctx`
1548    /// is `*mut Executor`. Drives one component's `tick`.
1549    pub tick: unsafe extern "C" fn(state: *mut core::ffi::c_void, exec_ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void),
1550    /// `nros`-side drop trampoline: reconstitutes + drops the leaked
1551    /// `Arc<ComponentCell>` at `state`. Run once on `Executor::drop`.
1552    pub drop: unsafe extern "C" fn(state: *mut core::ffi::c_void),
1553    /// Issue 2020 -- the level that registered the component
1554    /// (`Executor::set_registering_level` at enrol time), whose pass runs its
1555    /// `tick`; `NO_OWNING_LEVEL` on an executor whose levels do not own
1556    /// their slots, where the executor's own worker ticks every component.
1557    pub level: u8,
1558}
1559
1560// SAFETY: same story as `DispatchSlot` — two raw pointers + two extern
1561// "C" fn pointers. The `state` pointer's Send/Sync matches the owning
1562// `Executor` (`unsafe impl Send for Executor`); the fn pointers are
1563// Send/Sync by definition.
1564unsafe impl Send for ComponentSlot {}
1565unsafe impl Sync for ComponentSlot {}
1566
1567/// phase-271 — fixed capacity of the per-spin ready-sets (FIFO bitmap + EDF
1568/// heap) and the dispatch loop's upper bound. The executor's callback index is
1569/// carried in a `u64` active-mask (`1u64 << i`), so a callback table can hold at
1570/// most 64 entries regardless of per-entry sizing; the ready-sets are sized to
1571/// this ceiling (stack-transient) so any entry slice up to 64 dispatches
1572/// correctly. `EdfReadySet`'s presence bitmap independently asserts `N <= 64`.
1573pub(crate) const MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS: usize = 64;
1574
1575/// phase-509 P3 (RFC-0108 D2, its deferred re-probe question) -- whether a
1576/// slot whose backend cannot attribute an arrival (XRCE, uORB) is probed after
1577/// every callback ([`Executor::set_reprobe_each_callback`]) or once per pass.
1578///
1579/// Measured on the host (`reprobe_cost_on_an_unattributed_executor`, release
1580/// build, x86-64, `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS=32`): 32 unattributed subscriptions,
1581/// 4 ready per pass, empty callbacks. Once per pass 380-385 ns per pass;
1582/// after every callback 565-577 ns, i.e. +185-191 ns per pass, +46-48 ns per
1583/// callback, 1.65-1.71 ns per extra `has_data` (a mock's: no FFI, no
1584/// transport). The cost is one probe per unsettled slot per CALLBACK, so it
1585/// grows with slots x callbacks, and a real XRCE or uORB probe crosses the
1586/// rmw C ABI on an MCU several times slower than this host. Decided: once
1587/// per pass by default (an XRCE / uORB image keeps today's probe cost), with
1588/// the per-callback probe an opt-in. Pushed readiness (zenoh, which
1589/// attributes every arrival) joins mid-pass whatever this says, for one
1590/// atomic swap per callback.
1591pub const REPROBE_EACH_CALLBACK_DEFAULT: bool = false;
1592
1593/// Issue 1667 — the arena's allocation grain. Every region the arena hands out
1594/// starts on it and is a multiple of it, so a released region is always big
1595/// enough, and aligned enough, to hold its own free-list node.
1596pub(crate) const ARENA_GRAIN: usize = core::mem::align_of::<u64>();
1597
1598/// Issue 1667 — the smallest region the arena hands out: one free-list node
1599/// (`next`, `len`), rounded to the grain.
1600pub(crate) const ARENA_MIN_REGION: usize =
1601    (2 * core::mem::size_of::<usize>()).next_multiple_of(ARENA_GRAIN);
1602
1603/// Issue 1667 — the end of the free list.
1604const ARENA_FREE_NONE: usize = usize::MAX;
1605
1606/// Issue 1496 — one arena region, as an allocation hands it out.
1607#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1608pub(crate) struct FreedRegion {
1609    pub(crate) offset: usize,
1610    pub(crate) len: usize,
1611}
1612
1613/// Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — the slots of one executor's RAM remap table
1614/// (across all its nodes).
1615///
1616/// Issue 1971 (RFC-0107 step 1) -- the launch file's rules no longer live
1617/// here: they are one `const` table in flash every executor reads
1618/// ([`super::launch_remap`]). This table holds the RUNTIME rules: `--ros-args
1619/// -r` rules (`crate::ros_args::install_argv_remaps`) and rules a hand-written
1620/// caller declares with [`Executor::declare_remap`]. Its default is
1621/// [`crate::config::RUNTIME_REMAPS`]: 16 on a target with process arguments,
1622/// 0 on bare metal (no argv; `NROS_EXECUTOR_RUNTIME_REMAPS` restores slots).
1623pub const MAX_REMAPS: usize = crate::config::RUNTIME_REMAPS;
1624
1625/// Why [`Executor::declare_remap`] refused a rule -- never a silently dropped
1626/// routing rule.
1627#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1628pub enum RemapRefused {
1629    /// This executor has no runtime remap table: bare metal sizes it 0, since
1630    /// the launch's rules are the flash table and there is no argv. Restore
1631    /// slots with `NROS_EXECUTOR_RUNTIME_REMAPS`, or let codegen emit the rule
1632    /// into the launch table.
1633    NoRuntimeTable,
1634    /// The runtime table is full (`ExecutorSizing::remaps` slots, shared with
1635    /// `--ros-args -r` rules).
1636    TableFull,
1637    /// A string is longer than its slot (node name / namespace 64 bytes,
1638    /// `from` / `to` `MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN`).
1639    TooLong,
1640}
1641
1642impl core::fmt::Display for RemapRefused {
1643    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
1644        match self {
1645            Self::NoRuntimeTable => f.write_str(
1646                "declare_remap: this executor has no runtime remap table (0 slots: bare \
1647                 metal takes launch remaps from the flash table, nros_cpp_set_launch_remaps); \
1648                 set NROS_EXECUTOR_RUNTIME_REMAPS to restore runtime slots",
1649            ),
1650            Self::TableFull => f.write_str(
1651                "declare_remap: the runtime remap table is full (NROS_EXECUTOR_RUNTIME_REMAPS \
1652                 slots, shared with --ros-args -r rules)",
1653            ),
1654            Self::TooLong => f.write_str(
1655                "declare_remap: a name is longer than its slot (node name and namespace 64 \
1656                 bytes, from/to MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN)",
1657            ),
1658        }
1659    }
1660}
1661
1662/// Which of [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]'s two tiers a stored rule
1663/// belongs to.
1664#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1665pub(crate) enum RemapTier {
1666    /// Projected from the launch file (`declare_remap`, which the generated
1667    /// entry calls). AUTHORITATIVE, scoped to one `(name, namespace)`.
1668    Launch,
1669    /// Parsed from `--ros-args` (`crate::ros_args::install_argv_remaps`).
1670    /// FALLBACK — consulted only when no launch rule matched. Scoped to every
1671    /// node, or to the nodes of one NAME (rcl matches a `node:` prefix
1672    /// against the name alone).
1673    Argv,
1674}
1675
1676/// Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — one remap rule. `from`/`to` are stored RAW (as
1677/// written); the lookup in [`Executor::resolve_entity_name_for`] expands both
1678/// sides against the owning node's identity via `crate::names` (exact-FQN
1679/// match, no wildcards).
1680///
1681/// The table holds BOTH tiers, so each rule records which one it belongs to.
1682/// The tier is still decided at resolution, by
1683/// [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]'s two parameters, never by where a
1684/// rule sits in this table — `tier_rules` splits the table into those two
1685/// arguments. That is what keeps declaration order from deciding between the
1686/// channels: an argv rule installed before a launch rule still loses to it.
1687pub(crate) struct RemapRule {
1688    /// For [`RemapTier::Launch`]: the owning node. For [`RemapTier::Argv`]:
1689    /// the node name a `name:from:=to` rule was restricted to, or EMPTY for a
1690    /// rule that applies to every node.
1691    pub(crate) node_name: heapless::String<64>,
1692    /// For [`RemapTier::Launch`] only (normalised, `/` for root). Unused by
1693    /// argv rules, whose node prefix carries no namespace.
1694    pub(crate) namespace: heapless::String<64>,
1695    pub(crate) from: heapless::String<{ crate::names::MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN }>,
1696    pub(crate) to: heapless::String<{ crate::names::MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN }>,
1697    pub(crate) tier: RemapTier,
1698}
1699
1700impl RemapRule {
1701    /// Does this rule belong to `tier` and apply to the node `(node_name, ns)`?
1702    /// `ns` must already be normalised (`/` for root).
1703    fn applies(&self, tier: RemapTier, node_name: &str, ns: &str) -> bool {
1704        self.tier == tier
1705            && match tier {
1706                RemapTier::Launch => {
1707                    self.node_name.as_str() == node_name && self.namespace.as_str() == ns
1708                }
1709                RemapTier::Argv => {
1710                    self.node_name.is_empty() || self.node_name.as_str() == node_name
1711                }
1712            }
1713    }
1714}
1715
1716/// The rules of one tier that apply to one node, in declaration order, as the
1717/// `(from, to)` pairs [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`] takes. The ONE
1718/// place a stored table is split into the two tiers — the executor's resolver,
1719/// `NodeHandle`, and the Rust component road (through
1720/// `crate::ros_args::argv_fallback`) all read through it.
1721pub(crate) fn tier_rules<'r>(
1722    table: &'r [Option<RemapRule>],
1723    tier: RemapTier,
1724    node_name: &'r str,
1725    namespace: &'r str,
1726) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&'r str, &'r str)> + 'r {
1727    let ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
1728    table
1729        .iter()
1730        .flatten()
1731        .filter(move |r| r.applies(tier, node_name, ns))
1732        .map(|r| (r.from.as_str(), r.to.as_str()))
1733}
1734
1735/// Issue 1971 -- the two places an executor's remap rules live, read as the
1736/// two tiers of [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]:
1737///
1738/// * AUTHORITATIVE: the launch table in flash (`launch`) and, after it, any
1739///   rule a hand-written caller declared at run time (`RemapTier::Launch`
1740///   rows of `runtime`);
1741/// * FALLBACK: the `--ros-args -r` rules (`RemapTier::Argv` rows of
1742///   `runtime`).
1743///
1744/// The tier is decided by which parameter a rule is passed in, never by
1745/// where it sits, so an argv rule installed before a launch rule still loses.
1746#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1747pub(crate) struct RemapView<'r> {
1748    pub(crate) launch: &'r [super::launch_remap::LaunchRemap],
1749    pub(crate) runtime: &'r [Option<RemapRule>],
1750}
1751
1752impl<'r> RemapView<'r> {
1753    /// The authoritative rules for one node: the flash table's, then the
1754    /// runtime-declared ones.
1755    pub(crate) fn launch_rules<'a>(
1756        self,
1757        node_name: &'a str,
1758        ns: &'a str,
1759    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a str)> + 'a
1760    where
1761        'r: 'a,
1762    {
1763        super::launch_remap::launch_rules_for(self.launch, node_name, ns).chain(tier_rules(
1764            self.runtime,
1765            RemapTier::Launch,
1766            node_name,
1767            ns,
1768        ))
1769    }
1770
1771    /// The fallback (`--ros-args -r`) rules for one node.
1772    pub(crate) fn argv_rules<'a>(
1773        self,
1774        node_name: &'a str,
1775        ns: &'a str,
1776    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a str)> + 'a
1777    where
1778        'r: 'a,
1779    {
1780        tier_rules(self.runtime, RemapTier::Argv, node_name, ns)
1781    }
1782
1783    /// `resolve_name_layered` over both tiers.
1784    pub(crate) fn resolve(
1785        self,
1786        source: &str,
1787        node_name: &str,
1788        ns: &str,
1789    ) -> Result<crate::names::ResolvedName, ()> {
1790        crate::names::resolve_name_layered(
1791            source,
1792            node_name,
1793            ns,
1794            self.launch_rules(node_name, ns),
1795            self.argv_rules(node_name, ns),
1796        )
1797    }
1798}
1799
1800/// The executor's halt flag, in the one shape each configuration can hold.
1801///
1802/// Issue 1177. With an allocator it is refcounted, because `halt_flag()` hands
1803/// a caller its own handle to set from a signal handler or another thread.
1804/// Without one there is no handle to hand out -- a C caller reaches the
1805/// executor through its own pointer and calls `cancel()` directly -- so a plain
1806/// atomic is the whole requirement.
1807///
1808/// `Arc<AtomicBool>` derefs to `AtomicBool`, so every `load`/`store` below is
1809/// written once and only construction and the getter are cfg'd.
1810#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
1811pub(crate) type HaltFlag = portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>;
1812/// See [`HaltFlag`] above -- the no-allocator shape.
1813#[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
1814pub(crate) type HaltFlag = portable_atomic::AtomicBool;
1815
1816pub struct Executor<'s> {
1817    /// Issue 0656 — the ROS domain this executor's entities belong to.
1818    ///
1819    /// Retained because it was NOT: `open_in` passed `config.domain_id` into
1820    /// `RmwConfig` and dropped it, so every entity built from the executor
1821    /// (rather than from a `Node`, which keeps its own) declared on domain 0
1822    /// whatever `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` said. The value was read, printed, and then not
1823    /// used where it counts — issue 0161's shape.
1824    pub(crate) domain_id: u32,
1825    pub(crate) session: SessionStore,
1826    /// phase-271 (issue 0110) — the six sized tables are no longer inline
1827    /// arrays baked to `nros-node`'s build-time consts; they borrow
1828    /// caller-owned, per-entry-sized storage (`&'s mut` slices carved from a
1829    /// raw `[MaybeUninit<u64>]` backing by [`super::storage::carve`]). Lets a
1830    /// fat native entry and a lean embedded entry in one shared-target
1831    /// workspace each size to its own topology. `Executor` stays non-generic
1832    /// (lifetime only) so the C/C++ FFI keeps wrapping one concrete type.
1833    pub(crate) arena: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u8>],
1834    pub(crate) arena_used: usize,
1835    /// Issue 1496 / 1667 — the head of the FREE LIST: arena regions given back
1836    /// by a released entry, reused first-fit by the next allocation that fits.
1837    ///
1838    /// The list is INTRUSIVE — each free region holds its own node
1839    /// (`next`, `len`) in its first bytes — and kept in address order, so a
1840    /// release coalesces with both neighbours and nothing bounds how many holes
1841    /// there are. 1496's form was a fixed table of 8 that dropped a region when
1842    /// full and dropped any split tail under 64 B, and those bytes were gone
1843    /// for good: measured under a churning workload (issue 1667), three live
1844    /// entries leaked the whole 74 KiB arena inside 20 000 create/release
1845    /// rounds. A hole that ends at `arena_used` is given back to the bump
1846    /// pointer instead of being listed.
1847    pub(crate) arena_free_head: usize,
1848    /// Issue 1631 — the region the most recent ENTRY allocation handed out,
1849    /// waiting for `emplace_entry` to record it in the entry's
1850    /// `CallbackMeta::arena_len`. Every registration allocates its entry and
1851    /// then emplaces it, so the pair is adjacent; a registration that fails
1852    /// between them leaves a stale value that the next allocation overwrites.
1853    pub(crate) pending_region: Option<FreedRegion>,
1854    pub(crate) entries: &'s mut [Option<CallbackMeta>],
1855    /// Phase 110.B — registered scheduling contexts. Slot 0 is
1856    /// auto-populated with a `Fifo` SC at construction; every entry
1857    /// without an explicit binding maps to it via
1858    /// `sched_context_bindings`.
1859    pub(crate) sched_contexts: &'s mut [Option<super::sched_context::SchedContext>],
1860    /// Per-entry SC binding parallel to `entries`. Defaults to
1861    /// `SchedContextId(0)` (the auto-created Fifo SC).
1862    pub(crate) sched_context_bindings: &'s mut [super::sched_context::SchedContextId],
1863    /// Phase 110.E — user-space sporadic-server budget state per
1864    /// Sporadic-class SC. Slot indices match `sched_contexts`; non-
1865    /// Sporadic slots stay `None`.
1866    pub(crate) sporadic_states: &'s mut [Option<super::sched_context::SporadicState>],
1867    /// Phase 110.E.b — atomic sporadic state + opaque platform-timer
1868    /// handle for ISR-driven refill. Populated by
1869    /// `register_sporadic_timer`; dropped on Executor `Drop` via the
1870    /// stored `destroy_fn`.
1871    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
1872    pub(crate) sporadic_atomic_states: &'s mut [Option<(
1873        portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState>,
1874        OpaqueTimerHandle,
1875    )>],
1876    /// Phase 110.G — major-frame length for time-triggered dispatch.
1877    /// `0` (default) disables the TT gate entirely; non-zero enables
1878    /// gating per
1879    /// `SchedContext.tt_window_offset_us / tt_window_duration_us`.
1880    pub(crate) major_frame_us: u32,
1881    pub(crate) trigger: Trigger,
1882    pub(crate) semantics: ExecutorSemantics,
1883    /// Node name for entities created via `register_subscription`/`register_service`.
1884    /// Empty means unset — no liveliness tokens will be declared.
1885    pub(crate) node_name: heapless::String<64>,
1886    /// Phase 228.C — per-tier callback-group filter. Wildcard (register every
1887    /// callback — the single-tier degenerate case + today's behaviour) until
1888    /// [`set_active_groups`](Self::set_active_groups) names a non-empty set;
1889    /// after that this tier's executor accepts only callbacks whose
1890    /// `.callback_group()` is in it, and skips the others at registration.
1891    ///
1892    /// phase-409 — CARVED, and the wildcard is a separate flag rather than an
1893    /// `Option` around the table, because the table itself no longer lives in
1894    /// the value. "Filtering with an empty set" and "not filtering" stay
1895    /// distinguishable, which is the whole content of the old `Option`.
1896    pub(crate) active_groups: super::storage::CarvedVec<'s, super::storage::ActiveGroup>,
1897    /// Whether [`active_groups`](Self::active_groups) is a filter at all.
1898    /// `false` = wildcard (the old `None`).
1899    pub(crate) active_groups_filtering: bool,
1900    /// Node namespace (default: "/").
1901    pub(crate) namespace: heapless::String<64>,
1902    /// Phase 104.C.2 — rclcpp-style `add_node` table. Holds the
1903    /// per-Node metadata (name, namespace, rmw, locator, default
1904    /// SchedContext) for every Node attached to this Executor. The
1905    /// implicit "primary" Node (NodeId(0)) mirrors `node_name` +
1906    /// `namespace` above and is auto-populated on first use.
1907    ///
1908    /// phase-409 — CARVED. `NodeId` IS an index into this table, so the
1909    /// carved vector must keep push order and never gain a `swap_remove`.
1910    pub(crate) nodes: super::storage::CarvedVec<'s, super::node_record::NodeRecord>,
1911    /// Phase 272 (RFC-0047) — config-seeded node → sched-context bindings, keyed by the node's
1912    /// fully-qualified `(name, namespace)` pair. `NodeBuilder::build` consults this table to set a
1913    /// node's `default_sched` when no explicit `.sched()` was given. Empty ⇒ every node stays
1914    /// `SchedContextId(0)` (byte-identical to pre-272 behaviour). Sized by `MAX_NODES` (at most
1915    /// one tier per node — RFC-0047 OQ1).
1916    ///
1917    /// phase-409 — CARVED.
1918    pub(crate) node_sched_table: super::storage::CarvedVec<'s, super::storage::NodeSchedEntry>,
1919    /// Phase 273 (RFC-0047) — config-seeded per-callback-group sched bindings, keyed by the node's
1920    /// fully-qualified `(name, namespace)` pair PLUS the callback-group name. Overrides the node
1921    /// default for a callback created in that group. Empty ⇒ no per-group binding (node default
1922    /// stands). Sized by `MAX_CBS` — an upper bound on distinct callback-group bindings (you can
1923    /// never have more distinct group bindings than max callbacks).
1924    ///
1925    /// phase-409 (issue 0961) — CARVED, and it is the reason the phase exists:
1926    /// at ~168 B per slot this was `MAX_CBS` * 168 bytes INSIDE the value, so
1927    /// raising the handle limit from 14 to 36 — a fix for an unrelated failure —
1928    /// added ~3.7 KiB to the stack frame of every function that moves an
1929    /// `Executor`, and overflowed a 320 KiB part's main thread.
1930    pub(crate) group_sched_table: super::storage::CarvedVec<'s, super::storage::GroupSchedEntry>,
1931    /// Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — launch-baked per-node remap rules, keyed by
1932    /// the declaring node's `(name, namespace)` identity. Entries store the
1933    /// rule RAW (as written in launch); [`Self::resolve_entity_name`] expands
1934    /// both sides against the owning node's identity at lookup, via the shared
1935    /// `crate::names` seam (the same semantics the Rust `ExecutorSink` path
1936    /// applies). Declaration order is match order (first rule wins).
1937    /// Issue 0563 — CARVED, not inline. As a `heapless::Vec<RemapRule,
1938    /// MAX_REMAPS>` this one field was 6664 bytes of an 11632-byte `Executor`
1939    /// (57%), which is what made building an executor a ~9.3 KB stack
1940    /// temporary and overflowed the Zephyr Cortex-M main stack (issue 0552).
1941    /// It is the seventh sized table; phase-271 moved the other six here.
1942    /// `remap_len` is the fill cursor — occupied slots are `[0, remap_len)`.
1943    pub(crate) remap_table: &'s mut [Option<RemapRule>],
1944    pub(crate) remap_len: usize,
1945    /// Issue 1971 -- this executor's own launch remap table, when one was set
1946    /// on it ([`Self::set_launch_remaps`]); `None` reads the image's
1947    /// ([`super::launch_remap::launch_remaps`]), which the generated entry
1948    /// installs once before any tier is set up. A borrow of `.rodata`, never
1949    /// a copy.
1950    pub(crate) launch_remaps: Option<&'static [super::launch_remap::LaunchRemap]>,
1951    /// Phase 216 follow-up — per-Node dispatch trampoline registry.
1952    ///
1953    /// Populated by [`Executor::register_dispatch_slot`]; walked by
1954    /// [`Executor::dispatch_callback`] each time the board-side
1955    /// dispatch task hands off a `SignaledCallback` envelope.
1956    /// Sized by `MAX_NODES` because the upper-bound is one slot per
1957    /// Node pkg deployed on this executor (the same upper bound used
1958    /// by `nodes` and `extra_sessions`). `MAX_NODES` is driven by the
1959    /// `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES` build-script env var (default 4);
1960    /// boards that deploy more Node pkgs raise it at build time.

2341    /// phase-462 W4 -- the last mode request this executor saw, and the mode
2342    /// whose tables it judges by. They differ only after a request for a mode
2343    /// this executor has no table for.
2344    pub(crate) mode_seen: u16,
2345    /// phase-462 W4c -- monotonic ms of the previous mode check, the start
2346    /// of the window a request seen at this one could have waited in.
2347    pub(crate) mode_checked_ms: Option<u32>,
2348    pub(crate) mode_applied: u16,
2349    /// W3b.5 — hook invoked on `DeadlineAction::Fault` (panic when unset).
2350    pub(crate) fault_fn: Option<fn(&super::monitor::Violation)>,
2351    /// phase-503 — the reaction hook and its context: called when a
2352    /// supervised route passes its deadline (`route-deadline-runtime`), and on
2353    /// `DeadlineAction::Fault` when no `fault_fn` is set.
2354    pub(crate) reaction_hook: Option<(super::monitor::ReactionHookFn, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
2355    /// phase-509 P9b (RFC-0108 "As built in P9b") -- the lock every path that
2356    /// touches this executor takes once a second thread can reach it (one
2357    /// worker per level over one executor). `None` -- every one-level image --
2358    /// makes each guard a no-op. Read through a raw pointer by
2359    /// [`super::exec_lock::ExecGuard::acquire`], so it is written only while
2360    /// no second thread exists.
2361    pub(crate) exec_lock: Option<super::exec_lock::ExecLock>,
2362    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the callbacks running in an open window, one
2363    /// record per window, each in its pass's frame (`exec_lock::Running`).
2364    /// Read and written only under the lock; null while no window is open.
2365    pub(crate) running: *mut super::exec_lock::Running,
2366    /// Issue #515 — the spin cadence audit runs once, on the first spin
2367    /// that carries a non-zero timeout (which is where the tier's
2368    /// declared spin period becomes visible to the executor).
2369    pub(crate) spin_quantization_checked: bool,
2370    /// phase-436 W1 — the cadence the quantization audit (issue 0515) actually
2371    /// ran against. Recorded because the audit only LOGS: without this a
2372    /// regression that fed it the wrong number is invisible to a test, and
2373    /// capping the park by the timer deadline is exactly such a regression
2374    /// waiting to happen.
2375    pub(crate) spin_quantization_us: u64,
2376    /// Release jitter: worst observed lateness of a `spin_period` wake
2377    /// against its own nominal schedule, in microseconds.
2378    ///
2379    /// Issue #515 added a STATIC audit for one cause of cadence error --
2380    /// a period that is not a multiple of the spin period. Nothing measured
2381    /// the actual release instants, and `audit_spin_quantization` says so in
2382    /// as many words: "the rate is preserved and no activation is dropped,
2383    /// so every runtime rule is (correctly) silent -- the jitter stays
2384    /// invisible until someone measures cadence on target."
2385    ///
2386    /// This is that measurement, and it is the one `cyclictest` exists to
2387    /// report: the deviation between a timer's programmed wake-up and the
2388    /// instant the task actually resumed, whose MAXIMUM is the figure of
2389    /// merit for a real-time system.
2390    ///
2391    /// `spin_period` already holds both numbers -- `next_us` is the nominal
2392    /// deadline and `now_us()` the actual -- and when the loop is late it
2393    /// skips the sleep and discards the difference. That difference is the
2394    /// jitter.
2395    pub(crate) max_release_jitter_us: u64,
2396    /// Clock reading at the previous `spin_once` entry, for the interval the
2397    /// jitter is measured over. `None` until the first spin, and reset by
2398    /// `clear_release_jitter_stats` so a window starts clean.
2399    pub(crate) last_spin_entry_us: Option<u64>,
2400    /// phase-474 I11 -- the release grid of a `spin_once(timeout)` loop with
2401    /// no declared cadence. See [`ReleaseGrid`].
2402    pub(crate) grid: ReleaseGrid,
2403    /// Jitter high-water at the previous `release-jitter-runtime` check, so
2404    /// the rule reports the DELTA. Same shape as `overruns_reported` on a
2405    /// timer header, and for the same reason: a maximum that has not moved
2406    /// is the fault already reported, not a new one.
2407    pub(crate) jitter_reported_us: u64,
2408    /// phase-509 P6 (RFC-0108 D3) -- this executor's one worker: its band
2409    /// (every dispatch level), its park (RFC-0106) and its stack record. The
2410    /// fields moved here from the executor unchanged; `Executor` is the
2411    /// one-level facade over the scheduler / worker split.
2412    pub(crate) worker: super::scheduler::Worker,
2413    /// The pacing quantum the spin loop was last driven at, in microseconds.
2414    /// This is the bound the jitter rule judges against -- the caller's own
2415    /// declared cadence, so nothing further has to be declared.
2416    pub(crate) spin_nominal_us: u64,
2417    /// Cadence DECLARED by the driver, in microseconds; `0` = not declared.
2418    ///
2419    /// Takes precedence over the `spin_once` timeout when judging release
2420    /// jitter, because the two are not the same quantity. The timeout is how
2421    /// long a spin may BLOCK waiting for work; the cadence is how often the
2422    /// loop intends to come round. A driver that blocks up to 10 ms and then
2423    /// sleeps 30 ms has a 30 ms cadence and a 10 ms timeout, and judging it
2424    /// against the timeout reports a loop that is late on every single wake.
2425    pub(crate) spin_nominal_declared_us: u64,
2426    /// phase-436 A2b -- the declared cadence is met by the `spin_once` WAIT
2427    /// itself (`set_spin_nominal_wait_paced_us`), not by a sleep the caller
2428    /// adds between spins (`set_spin_nominal_us`). A wait-paced cadence runs
2429    /// on the release grid and is worth one park granule; a self-paced one is
2430    /// judged from entry to entry and is worth a microsecond.
2431    pub(crate) spin_nominal_wait_paced: bool,
2432    /// Wakes that were already past their nominal deadline, and wakes total.
2433    ///
2434    /// The maximum alone cannot distinguish one bad wake from a loop that is
2435    /// late every single cycle, and those are different faults: the first is
2436    /// a glitch, the second means the period cannot be met at all.
2437    pub(crate) late_wakes: u32,
2438    pub(crate) total_wakes: u32,
2439    /// phase-436 A2c -- late wakes whose lateness exceeds the granularity the
2440    /// measurement was made at (`release_jitter_granularity_us`). On a loop
2441    /// paced by a tick-granular park nearly every wake is late by a fraction
2442    /// of a tick, by design; `late_wakes` counts those, this does not.
2443    pub(crate) late_wakes_beyond_granule: u32,
2444    /// Issue 0514 / 1635 / phase-474 I1 -- what happens to a detected contract
2445    /// violation: the log switch, the drain-and-report hook, the image's sink,
2446    /// and the ring (CARVED, phase-409) with its total and dropped counters.
2447    /// See [`super::monitor::ViolationChannel`].
2448    pub(crate) violations: super::monitor::ViolationChannel<'s>,
2449    /// Issue 0790 — hooks that run BEFORE the session is closed, while every
2450    /// entity still works. The load-bearing half: a device releasing a bus or
2451    /// parking an actuator has to publish its final state / answer its last
2452    /// request from HERE, because after teardown it cannot.
2453    ///
2454    /// `[Option<_>; N]` rather than a `heapless::Vec`, deliberately: the handle
2455    /// a caller holds IS the slot index, so a removal must leave every other
2456    /// index where it was. A `Vec`'s `swap_remove` would silently re-point one
2457    /// live handle at a different callback, and its `remove` would re-point all
2458    /// of them. Clearing a slot to `None` also lets the next registration reuse
2459    /// it, which a fill cursor could not.
2460    pub(crate) pre_shutdown_hooks:
2461        [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2462    /// Issue 0790 — hooks that run AFTER the session is closed. rclcpp's
2463    /// `add_on_shutdown_callback` / `rclcpp::on_shutdown`. See
2464    /// [`Self::pre_shutdown_hooks`] for why this is an array.
2465    pub(crate) on_shutdown_hooks:
2466        [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2467}

2469impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
2470    /// phase-271 — assemble an executor over already-carved, caller-owned
2471    /// storage (`slices`, from [`super::storage::carve`]). Fills every
2472    /// non-storage field and reserves SC slot 0 for the default Fifo SC (carve
2473    /// left it `None`). The single builder shared by every constructor path.
2474    fn assemble(session: SessionStore, slices: super::storage::ExecutorSlices<'s>) -> Self {
2475        let super::storage::ExecutorSlices {
2476            arena,
2477            entries,
2478            sched_contexts,
2479            sched_context_bindings,
2480            sporadic_states,
2481            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2482            sporadic_atomic_states,
2483            remaps,
2484            nodes,
2485            extra_sessions,
2486            extra_session_ids,
2487            node_sched_table,
2488            dispatch_slots,
2489            component_slots,
2490            active_groups,
2491            group_sched_table,
2492            monitor_violations,
2493            alive_slots,
2494            slot_tags,
2495            params: param_slots,
2496            param_home,
2497        } = slices;
2498        // phase-382 W3' — only an executor that can build a store keeps the
2499        // carved slots; without `param-services` the region (sized by the
2500        // build, not by a feature, so the layout never depends on one) is
2501        // simply never initialised. The services' home (issue 1812) is
2502        // zero-sized without the feature.
2503        #[cfg(not(feature = "param-store"))]
2504        let _ = (param_slots, param_home);
2505        // Slot 0 = the auto-created default Fifo SC (see field doc). carve
2506        // initialised the whole table to `None`; populate the reserved slot.
2507        if let Some(slot0) = sched_contexts.first_mut() {
2508            *slot0 = Some(super::sched_context::SchedContext::default());
2509        }
2510        // phase-412 -- stamp the self-report before anything can fail. `init`
2511        // is idempotent, so an image with two executors need not decide which
2512        // one owns the record, and `note_arena_capacity` records the slice this
2513        // executor was actually handed rather than the compiled constant: the
2514        // arena's placement is the caller's choice (issue 0900), so the two can
2515        // legitimately differ and the difference is worth seeing.
2516        crate::boot_report::init();
2517        crate::boot_report::note_arena_capacity(arena.len());
2518        crate::boot_report::checkpoint(crate::boot_report::Stage::ExecutorReady);
2519        Self {
2520            // `assemble` is reached from session-only entry points that have no
2521            // config, so 0 is the floor rather than a choice; `open_in` and any
2522            // binding that knows better overwrite it via `set_domain_id`.
2523            domain_id: 0,
2524            session,
2525            arena,
2526            arena_used: 0,
2527            arena_free_head: ARENA_FREE_NONE,
2528            pending_region: None,
2529            entries,
2530            sched_contexts,
2531            sched_context_bindings,
2532            sporadic_states,
2533            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2534            sporadic_atomic_states,
2535            major_frame_us: 0,
2536            trigger: Trigger::Any,
2537            semantics: ExecutorSemantics::RclcppExecutor,
2538            node_name: heapless::String::new(),
2539            active_groups,
2540            active_groups_filtering: false,
2541            nodes,
2542            node_sched_table,
2543            group_sched_table,
2544            remap_table: remaps,
2545            remap_len: 0,
2546            launch_remaps: None,
2547            dispatch_slots,
2548            component_slots,
2549            extra_sessions,
2550            extra_session_ids,
2551            primary_rmw_name: heapless::String::new(),
2552            primary_locator: heapless::String::new(),
2553            namespace: {
2554                let mut ns = heapless::String::new();
2555                let _ = ns.push_str("/");
2556                ns
2557            },
2558            // Issue 1177 -- the only cfg the halt flag still needs. `HaltFlag`
2559            // is refcounted with an allocator and plain without one, and
2560            // nothing below this line can tell the difference.
2561            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2562            halt_flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),
2563            #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
2564            halt_flag: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
2565            spinning: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
2566            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2567            wake_flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),
2568            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2569            node_wake: super::node_wake::NodeWake::new().map(portable_atomic_util::Arc::new),
2570            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2571            wake_ctx: None,
2572            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2573            wake_cb_installed: false,
2574            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2575            has_cross_thread_waker: false,
2576            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2577            wake_membership: None,
2578            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2579            graph_change_target: None,
2580            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2581            has_async_wake: false,
2582            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2583            entity_attributed: 0,
2584            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2585            entity_recheck: 0,
2586            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2587            entity_status_polled: 0,
2588            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2589            readiness_probes: 0,
2590            // Phase 141.A.3 — alloc-mode wake state init. Constructed
2591            // eagerly (NodeWake allocation) so the runtime cb can be
2592            // installed lazily on first session without a fallible
2593            // alloc inside spin_once. `None` when the platform
2594            // provider reports the primitive unavailable (matches
2595            // the std-RTOS path's `node_wake: Option<...>`).
2596            #[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
2597            signal_fd: None,
2598            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
2599            params: None,
2600            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
2601            param_slots,
2602            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
2603            param_home,
2604            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
2605            param_store_refused: false,
2606            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
2607            declared_params: nros_params::DeclaredParams::EMPTY,
2608            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2609            sim_time_source: None,
2610            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2611            sim_time_requested: false,
2612            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2613            sim_time_stated: false,
2614            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2615            sim_time_silence: crate::time_source::SilenceWatch::new(),
2616            #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
2617            lifecycle: None,
2618            // Initialise the spin endpoint to construction time so the
2619            // very first `spin_once` credits time the caller spent
2620            // *before* it (e.g. setup, an explicit pre-spin sleep) just
2621            // like time spent between later calls.
2622            // One field, one seed now (phase-359 W10): the clock is absolute
2623            // on every flavour, so it is READ here rather than assumed to be
2624            // zero at construction. The std arm used to seed `Some(0)` because
2625            // its epoch WAS construction; with one provider that special case
2626            // is gone.
2627            last_spin_end_us: default_clock_us_fn().map(|clock| clock()),
2628            clock_us_fn: default_clock_us_fn(),
2629            consecutive_io_failures: 0,
2630            // RFC-0052 W3b.5 — a build with a wall clock gets one by default so
2631            // age monitors activate without extra wiring; a build with neither a
2632            // platform port nor a host gets `None`, and its board installs
2633            // `config.epoch_us` in `from_session_in`/`open`.
2634            //
2635            // phase-359 W10 — the cfg pair that used to be here moved into
2636            // `default_epoch_us_fn`, beside the `default_clock_us_fn` it
2637            // mirrors. (The old comment pointed at "the `not(std)` blocks
2638            // above" for the board install; those blocks are no longer
2639            // cfg-gated — the config override applies on every flavour now.)
2640            epoch_us_fn: super::types::default_epoch_us_fn(),
2641            component_frame: None,
2642            monitor_table: &[],
2643            monitor_states: [super::monitor::MonitorState::default(); super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS],
2644            age_table: &[],
2645            age_states: [super::monitor::AgeState::default(); super::monitor::MAX_AGE_MONITORS],
2646            hazard_table: &[],
2647            mode_tables: &[],
2648            mode_seen: 0,
2649            mode_checked_ms: None,
2650            mode_applied: 0,
2651            fault_fn: None,
2652            reaction_hook: None,
2653            exec_lock: None,
2654            running: core::ptr::null_mut(),
2655            spin_quantization_checked: false,
2656            reprobe_each_callback: REPROBE_EACH_CALLBACK_DEFAULT,
2657            spin_quantization_us: 0,
2658            max_release_jitter_us: 0,
2659            last_spin_entry_us: None,
2660            grid: ReleaseGrid {
2661                period_us: 0,
2662                next_us: 0,
2663                skipped: 0,
2664            },
2665            jitter_reported_us: 0,
2666            worker: super::scheduler::Worker::one_level(),
2667            spin_nominal_us: 0,
2668            spin_nominal_declared_us: 0,
2669            spin_nominal_wait_paced: false,
2670            late_wakes: 0,
2671            total_wakes: 0,
2672            late_wakes_beyond_granule: 0,
2673            violations: super::monitor::ViolationChannel::new(monitor_violations),
2674            alive_slots,
2675            slot_tags,
2676            // Issue 0790 — both phase tables start empty. An image that
2677            // registers nothing pays these `None`s and a two-slot scan at
2678            // teardown, and nothing else.
2679            pre_shutdown_hooks: [None; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2680            on_shutdown_hooks: [None; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2681        }
2682    }

2684    /// Create an owning executor over caller-supplied `backing`, sized by
2685    /// `sizing`. The core, non-generic, per-entry entry point (the `alloc`
2686    /// [`from_session`](Self::from_session) convenience leaks a default backing
2687    /// and calls this; the macro / C FFI pass an entry-sized backing).
2688    ///
2689    /// # Safety
2690    /// `backing` must be ≥ `sizing.u64_len()` words, stay alive for `'s`, and
2691    /// not be otherwise accessed while the executor lives (it aliases it).
2692    /// `sizing.cbs` must be ≤ 64 (the `u64` ready-set bitmask ceiling).
2693    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_session_in(
2694        session: session::ConcreteSession,
2695        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2696        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2697    ) -> Self {
2698        let slices = unsafe { super::storage::carve(backing, sizing) };
2699        Self::assemble(SessionStore::Owned(session), slices)
2700    }
2701
2702    /// Create a borrowing executor over caller-supplied `backing`, sized by
2703    /// `sizing`. Counterpart to [`from_session_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_in) for
2704    /// the per-tier / C model (the session is borrowed, not owned).
2705    ///
2706    /// # Safety
2707    /// - `session_ptr` must point to a valid session that outlives the executor
2708    ///   and is not moved/dropped while it exists.
2709    /// - `backing` obligations as in [`from_session_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_in).
2710    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_session_ptr_in(
2711        session_ptr: *mut session::ConcreteSession,
2712        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2713        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2714    ) -> Self {
2715        let slices = unsafe { super::storage::carve(backing, sizing) };
2716        Self::assemble(SessionStore::Borrowed(session_ptr), slices)
2717    }
2718}
