2720impl Executor<'static> {
2721    /// Create an executor from an already-opened session, using the build-time
2722    /// default sizing (`MAX_CBS`/`MAX_SC`/`ARENA_SIZE`). Convenience for
2723    /// std/alloc callers that don't size per-entry: it leaks a default-sized
2724    /// backing (executor-lifetime, one-time) and calls
2725    /// [`from_session_in`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_in). Per-entry sizing goes through
2726    /// the macro / `open_in` instead.
2727    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2728    pub fn from_session(session: session::ConcreteSession) -> Self {
2729        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
2730        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words,
2731        // `'static`, and uniquely owned by this executor.
2732        unsafe { Self::from_session_in(session, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
2733    }
2734
2735    /// [`from_session`](Self::from_session) with an [`ExecutorConfig`], so a
2736    /// caller that brings its own session can also bring its own clock.
2737    ///
2738    /// issue 0709 / issue 0687 — `from_session` takes no config, and that is
2739    /// the path the no-port population uses: it accepts any `Session`, so a
2740    /// consumer with a non-cffi backend reaches the executor through it and had
2741    /// NO way to install `clock_us`. phase-359 W10 argued the `std`-without-a-
2742    /// port clock fallbacks could go because "a caller with a clock installs it
2743    /// through `ExecutorConfig::clock_us`" — true for `open`, false here, which
2744    /// is half of why that deletion was reverted.
2745    ///
2746    /// Only the timing sources are read from `config`; identity (locator,
2747    /// domain, names) belongs to the session the caller already opened. As in
2748    /// [`open_in`](Self::open_in), a `None` field does NOT clobber the
2749    /// platform default — it means "not specified" (the bug issue 0671
2750    /// records).
2751    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2752    pub fn from_session_with(
2753        session: session::ConcreteSession,
2754        config: &super::types::ExecutorConfig<'_>,
2755    ) -> Self {
2756        let mut executor = Self::from_session(session);
2757        if let Some(clock) = config.clock_us {
2758            executor.clock_us_fn = Some(clock);
2759            executor.last_spin_end_us = Some(clock());
2760        }
2761        if let Some(epoch) = config.epoch_us {
2762            executor.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch);
2763        }
2764        executor
2765    }
2766
2767    /// Create an executor from a borrowed session pointer, default-sized. The
2768    /// `alloc` convenience wrapper over
2769    /// [`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in) — leaks a default
2770    /// backing so existing callers keep the zero-storage-arg signature.
2771    ///
2772    /// # Safety
2773    /// - `session_ptr` must point to a valid, initialized session that lives at
2774    ///   least as long as this executor.
2775    /// - The caller must not move or drop the session while the executor exists.
2776    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2777    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_session_ptr(session_ptr: *mut session::ConcreteSession) -> Self {
2778        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
2779        // SAFETY: the backing as in `from_session`; session_ptr contract
2780        // forwarded to `from_session_ptr_in`.
2781        unsafe { Self::from_session_ptr_in(session_ptr, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
2782    }
2783}
2784
2785/// phase-474 I11 -- the release grid of a `spin_once(timeout)` loop with no
2786/// declared cadence: the period it was built for (`0` = no grid yet), the next
2787/// scheduled release, and the releases skipped because the loop came back a
2788/// whole period or more after they were due (the timer `Skip` policy: the
2789/// latest due point is served once, the older ones are dropped and counted,
2790/// never released in a burst). The park is bounded by `next_us`, so a loop is
2791/// released on `anchor + k * period` instead of `period` after its previous
2792/// spin ended. Scales with no knob; named in the header-size budget.
2793#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
2794pub(crate) struct ReleaseGrid {
2795    pub(crate) period_us: u64,
2796    pub(crate) next_us: u64,
2797    pub(crate) skipped: u32,
2798}
2799
2800/// The two cadences a `period_us` timer alternates between under a `spin_us`
2801/// spin period, or `None` when the audit (issue #515) has nothing to say.
2802///
2803/// Split out of `audit_spin_quantization` so the decision can be asserted:
2804/// the audit only LOGS, so a regression in what it decides is otherwise
2805/// invisible to a test.
2806///
2807/// `None` for a period of zero, for a period that divides the spin period —
2808/// and, since issue 1321, for a timer whose activations are NOT paced by the
2809/// spin period at all. The warning's arithmetic is wall microseconds on both
2810/// sides; a `Ros` timer's activations are quantised by the `/clock` STEP, so
2811/// the sentence it would print ("activations will alternate between X and Y
2812/// us") is about nothing.
2813pub(crate) fn spin_quantization_span(
2814    clock_source: TimerClockSource,
2815    period_us: u64,
2816    spin_us: u64,
2817) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
2818    if spin_us == 0 || period_us == 0 || period_us.is_multiple_of(spin_us) {
2819        return None;
2820    }
2821    if !clock_source.remaining_is_wall_time() {
2822        return None;
2823    }
2824    let early_us = (period_us / spin_us) * spin_us;
2825    Some((early_us, early_us.saturating_add(spin_us)))
2826}
2827
2828/// phase-436 — which deadline source bounded the last park.
2829///
2830/// Attribution is what turns "why did we wake" from a guess into a number.
2831/// Recording it costs one byte per spin and is the difference between a
2832/// schedulability argument you can audit and one you have to trust.
2833#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2834#[repr(u8)]
2835pub enum WakeSourceId {
2836    /// The `spin_once` caller's own timeout — always a member of the source
2837    /// set, which is why the park is never unbounded.
2838    CallerBudget,
2839    /// A registered timer's next expiry (issue 1192).
2840    Timer,
2841    /// The backend's next internal event (lease keepalive, heartbeat,
2842    /// ACK-NACK). Folded into the same `min` as everything else rather than
2843    /// capping the budget separately upstream, so one rule decides the park
2844    /// and one attribution explains it.
2845    Session,
2846    /// A source the PLATFORM registered: a `k_poll` event set, an `epoll`
2847    /// group, a FreeRTOS queue set, a ThreadX event-flags group, or a
2848    /// bare-metal device ISR. The core never names an RTOS; it only asks each
2849    /// registered source when it will next need the executor.
2850    Platform(u8),
2851    /// phase-503 — the earliest deadline of a pending supervised route: the
2852    /// park ends there so `route-deadline-runtime` judges it on time.
2853    RouteDeadline,
2854}
2855
2856/// How many platform sources one executor can carry. A plain const, not a
2857/// sizing knob: the table is inline, so no allocator is required on the no_std
2858/// targets this seam mainly exists for.
2859pub const MAX_WAKE_SOURCES: usize = 8;
2860
2861/// phase-436 (RFC-0106 D5) — the slice a poll-only backend's transport wait is
2862/// cut into while a guard condition can signal the executor from another
2863/// thread: the worst-case latency of such a trigger, and the period at which
2864/// an otherwise idle executor re-enters the backend's `recv`.
2865#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2866pub(crate) const POLL_ONLY_WAKE_SLICE_MS: i32 = 10;
2867
2868/// When this source will next need the executor, in the executor's clock,
2869/// as microseconds FROM NOW.
2870///
2871/// `u64::MAX` means "nothing pending" — the source does not shorten the park.
2872/// That is how an ASYNC source spells itself: a socket or a DDS listener
2873/// contributes no deadline and instead breaks the park by signalling the wake
2874/// primitive, so async and deadline sources compose without a second
2875/// mechanism.
2876pub type NextDeadlineFn = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> u64;
2877
2878/// Park until `deadline_us` from now, or until something signals, whichever
2879/// comes first.
2880///
2881/// Returns `0` when woken by an event, `1` when the deadline expired, and a
2882/// negative value when this build cannot park at all.
2883///
2884/// A DEADLINE, not a duration, and that distinction is what makes bare metal
2885/// work: `nros-baremetal-common`'s own note says `wfi` with no pending
2886/// interrupt deadlocks, so a board must arm a timer compare BEFORE waiting.
2887/// A `sleep(duration)` seam cannot express that — the sleeper does not know
2888/// whether anyone armed an interrupt. `park_until(deadline)` does, because the
2889/// deadline is exactly what the compare is armed to.
2890pub type ParkUntilFn = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void, deadline_us: u64) -> i8;
2891
2892/// A registered deadline contributor.
2893#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
2894pub(crate) struct WakeSourceSlot {
2895    pub(crate) next: NextDeadlineFn,
2896    pub(crate) ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
2897}
2898
2899impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
2900    /// Phase 228.B (RFC-0015) — construct a tier task's executor that **shares**
2901    /// a session opened once by the orchestration `main()`.
2902    ///
2903    /// In the per-tier execution model `main()` opens one RMW session, then
2904    /// spawns one RTOS task per priority tier; each task calls this to get an
2905    /// [`Executor`] over the *same* session (the `Borrowed` session store — this
2906    /// executor neither owns nor closes it), registers its tier's callback
2907    /// groups, and spins. Thin alias over [`ExecutorFfi::from_session_ptr`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::from_session_ptr).
2908    ///
2909    /// # Safety
2910    /// `session` must outlive every executor/task built from it (the
2911    /// orchestration `main()` holds it and never returns / WFIs), and must not
2912    /// be mutated except through these executors' spin calls.
2913    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2914    pub unsafe fn open_with_session(session: *mut session::ConcreteSession) -> Executor<'static> {
2915        #[allow(unused_mut)]
2916        let mut exec = unsafe { Executor::<'static>::from_session_ptr(session) };
2917        // phase-436 — join the session's wake fan-out, so this tier is woken
2918        // by its arrivals instead of sleeping out its whole bound.
2919        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2920        exec.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
2921        exec
2922    }
2923
2924    /// phase-271 — per-tier borrowed-session constructor over caller-supplied,
2925    /// per-tier-sized `backing`. The sized counterpart to
2926    /// [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session): each RTOS tier task owns
2927    /// its own backing so tiers size independently.
2928    ///
2929    /// # Safety
2930    /// `session` obligations as in [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session);
2931    /// `backing`/`sizing` as in [`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in).
2932    pub(crate) unsafe fn open_with_session_in(
2933        session: *mut session::ConcreteSession,
2934        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2935        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2936    ) -> Self {
2937        #[allow(unused_mut)]
2938        let mut exec = unsafe { Self::from_session_ptr_in(session, backing, sizing) };
2939        // phase-436 — as `open_with_session`.
2940        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2941        exec.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
2942        exec
2943    }
2944
2945    /// Raw pointer to this executor's RMW session, for the per-tier model:
2946    /// the boot task opens the one session via [`Executor::open`] (the RMW
2947    /// session is a process-wide singleton — opening twice fails), then hands
2948    /// this pointer to each spawned tier task's
2949    /// [`Executor::open_with_session`]. The boot task's executor owns the
2950    /// session and outlives every borrower, so the pointer stays valid for the
2951    /// program's life. Works for both `Owned` and `Borrowed` stores.
2952    ///
2953    /// # Safety
2954    /// The returned pointer aliases `self.session`. Callers must keep `self`
2955    /// alive (not moved/dropped) for as long as any tier executor uses the
2956    /// pointer, and must only touch the session through executor spin calls
2957    /// (the RMW backend serializes concurrent access through its own locks).
2958    pub fn session_ptr(&mut self) -> *mut session::ConcreteSession {
2959        let ptr = &mut *self.session as *mut session::ConcreteSession;
2960        // phase-436 — the owner of an OWNED session claimed its wake fan-out
2961        // while this executor value could still move (inside `open*`). The
2962        // address handed out here is the one every tier is opened over, so
2963        // the entry is keyed by it from now on.
2964        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2965        if let (SessionStore::Owned(_), Some(m)) = (&self.session, self.wake_membership) {
2966            m.fanout().rekey(ptr as *mut core::ffi::c_void);
2967        }
2968        ptr
2969    }
2970
2971    /// Opaque, `Send` form of [`session_ptr`](Self::session_ptr) — the per-tier
2972    /// model hands this to each spawned tier task (it can cross the RTOS task /
2973    /// thread boundary, which a bare `*mut` cannot). See [`SessionHandle`].
2974    ///
2975    /// # Safety
2976    /// Same contract as [`session_ptr`](Self::session_ptr): `self` (the session
2977    /// owner) must outlive every executor built from the handle.
2978    pub fn session_handle(&mut self) -> SessionHandle {
2979        SessionHandle(self.session_ptr())
2980    }
2981
2982    /// Open an [`Executor`] over the session a [`SessionHandle`] refers to (the
2983    /// `Borrowed` store — neither owns nor closes it). The tier-task counterpart
2984    /// to [`session_handle`](Self::session_handle).
2985    ///
2986    /// # Safety
2987    /// The handle's session must still be alive (its owning executor not moved
2988    /// or dropped); access only through executor spin calls.
2989    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2990    pub unsafe fn open_with_session_handle(handle: SessionHandle) -> Executor<'static> {
2991        unsafe { Executor::<'static>::open_with_session(handle.0) }
2992    }
2993
2994    /// phase-271 — sized counterpart to
2995    /// [`open_with_session_handle`](Self::open_with_session_handle) (per-tier
2996    /// backing).
2997    ///
2998    /// # Safety
2999    /// As [`open_with_session_handle`](Self::open_with_session_handle) +
3000    /// [`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in).
3001    pub(crate) unsafe fn open_with_session_handle_in(
3002        handle: SessionHandle,
3003        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
3004        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
3005    ) -> Self {
3006        unsafe { Self::open_with_session_in(handle.0, backing, sizing) }
3007    }
3008
3009    /// issue 1571 — a SPAWNED tier's executor over its slot of the entry's
3010    /// [`TierExecutorBacking`](super::TierExecutorBacking) — the road every
3011    /// board's `run_tiers` takes for each tier but the boot one.
3012    ///
3013    /// The slot's TYPE is the size: it is `ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT.u64_len()`
3014    /// words and this opens with `ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT`, so the pairing is
3015    /// exact by construction and lives here, once, rather than at five boards.
3016    /// [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session) is the heap twin this
3017    /// replaced on those roads.
3018    ///
3019    /// # Safety
3020    /// `session` obligations as in [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session).
3021    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
3022    pub(crate) unsafe fn open_with_session_slot(
3023        session: *mut session::ConcreteSession,
3024        slot: &'s mut super::TierExecutorBackingSlot,
3025    ) -> Self {
3026        unsafe {
3027            Self::open_with_session_in(
3028                session,
3029                &mut slot[..],
3030                super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT,
3031            )
3032        }
3033    }
3034
3035    /// issue 1571 — [`open_with_session_slot`](Self::open_with_session_slot)
3036    /// over a [`SessionHandle`], for the boards whose tier tasks carry one.
3037    ///
3038    /// # Safety
3039    /// As [`open_with_session_handle`](Self::open_with_session_handle).
3040    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
3041    pub(crate) unsafe fn open_with_session_handle_slot(
3042        handle: SessionHandle,
3043        slot: &'s mut super::TierExecutorBackingSlot,
3044    ) -> Self {
3045        unsafe { Self::open_with_session_slot(handle.0, slot) }
3046    }
3047
3048    /// Phase 228.C — set this tier executor's active callback-group filter. The
3049    /// generated per-tier task calls this before registering nodes; afterwards
3050    /// only callbacks whose `.callback_group()` is in `groups` register here.
3051    /// An empty slice (or never calling it) leaves the wildcard — register all
3052    /// callbacks (the single-tier degenerate case + today's behaviour).
3053    pub fn set_active_groups(
3054        &mut self,
3055        groups: &[(&str, &str, &str)],
3056    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
3057        // phase-409 — the table is CARVED and reused, so clear before refilling;
3058        // the old `Option<heapless::Vec>` got a fresh empty vector each call.
3059        self.active_groups.clear();
3060        if groups.is_empty() {
3061            self.active_groups_filtering = false;
3062            return Ok(());
3063        }
3064        for (name, ns, group) in groups {
3065            // issue 1172 — this used to be `if s.push_str(g).is_ok()`, which
3066            // DROPPED an oversized group name and left the tier filtering on a
3067            // set that silently lacked it. It fails closed (the entity is never
3068            // created), so the symptom is a missing entity with nothing to read
3069            // that says why. Same contract as `declare_remap` below: too long,
3070            // or table full, is the caller's error.
3071            let key = super::storage::node_identity_hash(name, ns);
3072            let mut s = heapless::String::new();
3073            let why = if s.push_str(group).is_err() {
3074                Some(super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)
3075            } else if self.active_groups.push((key, s)).is_err() {
3076                Some(super::types::BindError::TableFull)
3077            } else {
3078                None
3079            };
3080            if let Some(why) = why {
3081                // FAIL CLOSED, and say so. Returning here with a PARTIAL table
3082                // would leave the tier filtering on a subset — the same silent
3083                // narrowing, one step later. An empty table with filtering ON
3084                // accepts NOTHING (`group_filter_accepts` matches on an empty
3085                // slice), so the tier registers no entities at all: visible in
3086                // behaviour, where a missing entry is not. The `Err` is for the
3087                // caller that can report it; the state is safe for the one that
3088                // cannot.
3089                self.active_groups.clear();
3090                self.active_groups_filtering = true;
3091                return Err(why);
3092            }
3093        }
3094        self.active_groups_filtering = true;
3095        Ok(())
3096    }
3097
3098    /// The current callback-group filter, or `None` for the wildcard.
3099    fn active_group_filter(&self) -> Option<&[super::storage::ActiveGroup]> {
3100        self.active_groups_filtering
3101            .then(|| self.active_groups.as_slice())
3102    }
3103
3104    /// Phase 228.C — whether a callback in `group` should register in this
3105    /// executor under the current filter. The wildcard accepts everything.
3106    pub fn group_active(&self, node_name: &str, node_namespace: &str, group: &str) -> bool {
3107        group_filter_accepts(
3108            self.active_group_filter(),
3109            super::storage::node_identity_hash(node_name, node_namespace),
3110            group,
3111        )
3112    }
3113
3114    /// Set the node name and namespace used for liveliness tokens.
3115    ///
3116    /// Called by `open()` to propagate config values. When `register_subscription`
3117    /// or `register_service` creates entities, these values are attached to the
3118    /// Phase 156 — record the primary session's backend identity
3119    /// (rmw name + locator) so `NodeBuilder::resolve_session_slot`
3120    /// can detect when a `.rmw(name)` matches the primary instead
3121    /// of opening a SECOND backend session against the same
3122    /// singleton (zenoh-pico's `g_session` is process-wide;
3123    /// opening twice fails). `Executor::open*` calls this
3124    /// automatically; the C surface (`rclc_executor_init`) calls
3125    /// it manually because it constructs via `from_session_ptr`
3126    /// which doesn't know the open metadata. Empty strings = "no
3127    /// primary identity tracked"; the cache check degrades to
3128    /// always-miss.
3129    pub(crate) fn set_primary_identity(&mut self, rmw_name: &str, locator: &str) {
3130        self.primary_rmw_name.clear();
3131        let _ = self.primary_rmw_name.push_str(rmw_name);
3132        self.primary_locator.clear();
3133        let _ = self.primary_locator.push_str(locator);
3134    }
3135
3136    /// `TopicInfo`/`ServiceInfo` so the zenoh backend can declare liveliness.
3137    /// Issue 0656 — set the ROS domain for entities this executor declares.
3138    ///
3139    /// For bindings that build an executor from an existing session
3140    /// (`from_session_ptr_in`), where no `ExecutorConfig` is available and the
3141    /// domain would otherwise stay at its 0 floor.
3142    pub fn set_domain_id(&mut self, domain_id: u32) {
3143        self.domain_id = domain_id;
3144    }
3145
3146    /// The ROS domain this executor declares entities on.
3147    pub fn domain_id(&self) -> u32 {
3148        self.domain_id
3149    }
3150
3151    pub fn set_node_identity(&mut self, node_name: &str, namespace: &str) {
3152        self.node_name.clear();
3153        let _ = self.node_name.push_str(node_name);
3154        if !namespace.is_empty() {
3155            self.namespace.clear();
3156            let _ = self.namespace.push_str(namespace);
3157        }
3158    }
3159
3160    // =========================================================================
3161    // Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — per-node launch remap table
3162    // =========================================================================
3163
3164    /// Record one launch `<remap from= to=/>` rule for the node identified by
3165    /// `(node_name, namespace)`. Rules are matched in declaration order (first
3166    /// wins) by [`Self::resolve_entity_name_for`]. Errors when a string
3167    /// overflows its slot or the table is at `MAX_REMAPS` — callers surface
3168    /// this rather than silently dropping a routing rule.
3169    ///
3170    /// **This declares an AUTHORITATIVE rule.** Declaration order settles
3171    /// which of two launch rules for one name wins; it is not how an argv rule
3172    /// is ranked against a launch rule. The `--ros-args` rules share this table
3173    /// but are tagged as the fallback tier, and resolution reads both tiers
3174    /// through [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`] — so an argv rule
3175    /// installed BEFORE a launch rule still loses to it.
3176    ///
3177    /// Issue 1971 -- a GENERATED entry no longer calls this: its launch rules
3178    /// are the flash table ([`super::launch_remap::set_launch_remaps`]). This
3179    /// writes the RUNTIME table, for hand-written callers; on bare metal that
3180    /// table is 0 slots by default and the call is refused by name
3181    /// ([`RemapRefused::NoRuntimeTable`]).
3182    pub fn declare_remap(
3183        &mut self,
3184        node_name: &str,
3185        namespace: &str,
3186        from: &str,
3187        to: &str,
3188    ) -> Result<(), RemapRefused> {
3189        if self.remap_table.is_empty() {
3190            return Err(RemapRefused::NoRuntimeTable);
3191        }
3192        let mut rule = RemapRule {
3193            node_name: heapless::String::new(),
3194            namespace: heapless::String::new(),
3195            from: heapless::String::new(),
3196            to: heapless::String::new(),
3197            tier: RemapTier::Launch,
3198        };
3199        let too_long = |_| RemapRefused::TooLong;
3200        rule.node_name.push_str(node_name).map_err(too_long)?;
3201        let ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
3202        rule.namespace.push_str(ns).map_err(too_long)?;
3203        rule.from.push_str(from).map_err(too_long)?;
3204        rule.to.push_str(to).map_err(too_long)?;
3205        // Same contract as the `heapless::Vec::push` this replaces: full table
3206        // is an error the caller surfaces, never a silently dropped rule.
3207        let slot = self
3208            .remap_table
3209            .get_mut(self.remap_len)
3210            .ok_or(RemapRefused::TableFull)?;
3211        *slot = Some(rule);
3212        self.remap_len += 1;
3213        Ok(())
3214    }
3215
3216    /// Resolve a source-level entity name for the node identified by
3217    /// `(node_name, namespace)`: ROS 2 name expansion (`~`/relative → FQN)
3218    /// plus this node's declared remap rules (exact-FQN match, first rule
3219    /// wins). Nodes with no rules still get expansion. Errors on an
3220    /// unexpandable name (see `crate::names::expand_name`).
3221    ///
3222    /// Two tiers, through [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]: the rules
3223    /// [`Self::declare_remap`] recorded for this node are AUTHORITATIVE (the
3224    /// generated entry declares the launch projection there), and the
3225    /// `--ros-args` rules `crate::ros_args::install_argv_remaps` put in the
3226    /// same table are the FALLBACK, consulted only when no launch rule
3227    /// matched. rcl does the same with its local and global arguments
3228    /// (`rcl_remap_topic_name`, Humble `rcl/remap.h`).
3229    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
3230    pub fn resolve_entity_name_for(
3231        &self,
3232        node_name: &str,
3233        namespace: &str,
3234        source: &str,
3235    ) -> Result<crate::names::ResolvedName, ()> {
3236        let ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
3237        self.remap_view().resolve(source, node_name, ns)
3238    }
3239
3240    /// Issue 1971 -- give this executor its own launch remap table instead of
3241    /// the image's ([`super::launch_remap::set_launch_remaps`]). A borrow of
3242    /// `.rodata`; nothing is copied.
3243    pub fn set_launch_remaps(&mut self, table: &'static [super::launch_remap::LaunchRemap]) {
3244        self.launch_remaps = Some(table);
3245    }
3246
3247    /// Both remap sources this executor resolves through: the launch table
3248    /// (flash) and the runtime table (RAM).
3249    pub(crate) fn remap_view(&self) -> RemapView<'_> {
3250        RemapView {
3251            launch: self
3252                .launch_remaps
3253                .unwrap_or_else(super::launch_remap::launch_remaps),
3254            runtime: &self.remap_table[..self.remap_len],
3255        }
3256    }
3257
3258    /// [`Self::resolve_entity_name_for`] against the executor's CURRENT node
3259    /// identity (`set_node_identity`) — the nros-c registration sites set that
3260    /// identity per node immediately before registering each entity.
3261    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
3262    pub fn resolve_entity_name(&self, source: &str) -> Result<crate::names::ResolvedName, ()> {
3263        self.resolve_entity_name_for(self.node_name.as_str(), self.namespace.as_str(), source)
3264    }

3266    // =========================================================================
3267    // Phase 272 (RFC-0047) — node-name → sched-context table
3268    // =========================================================================
3269
3270    /// Seed a config-resolved tier binding by `(name, namespace)` before the
3271    /// node is built. `NodeBuilder::build` consults this table when no
3272    /// explicit `.sched()` override is given — the table entry then wins over
3273    /// the `SchedContextId(0)` default (precedence: explicit > table > 0).
3274    ///
3275    /// Call BEFORE `node_builder(name).build()`. An existing entry for the
3276    /// same `(name, namespace)` key is overwritten (last-write wins). Overflow
3277    /// past `MAX_NODES` is an `Err`, never a dropped binding — issue 1172. An
3278    /// empty `namespace` is normalised
3279    /// to `"/"` to match what `NodeBuilder::build` computes for a root-NS node.
3280    pub fn bind_node_name_sched(
3281        &mut self,
3282        name: &str,
3283        namespace: &str,
3284        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
3285    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
3286        let norm_ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
3287        // Overwrite if there is already an entry for this (name, ns) pair.
3288        for entry in self.node_sched_table.iter_mut() {
3289            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == norm_ns {
3290                entry.2 = sc;
3291                return Ok(());
3292            }
3293        }
3294        self.push_node_entry(name, norm_ns, sc, 0)
3295    }
3296
3297    /// phase-509 P2 (RFC-0108 D2) -- seed the contract rank of the node
3298    /// `(name, namespace)` before it is built: 0 is the most urgent, as codegen
3299    /// normalises the derivation's ranks. Every callback the node registers
3300    /// then dispatches at that rank inside its sched context's bucket
3301    /// ([`Priority::dispatch_level`](super::sched_context::Priority::dispatch_level)).
3302    /// A node with no seeded rank holds 0.
3303    ///
3304    /// Shares the node-name table with [`Self::bind_node_name_sched`]: one entry
3305    /// per node carries both, so neither call disturbs the other's half. Same
3306    /// error contract: a binding that does not fit is refused, never dropped.
3307    pub fn bind_node_rank(
3308        &mut self,
3309        name: &str,
3310        namespace: &str,
3311        rank: u8,
3312    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
3313        let norm_ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
3314        for entry in self.node_sched_table.iter_mut() {
3315            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == norm_ns {
3316                entry.3 = rank;
3317                return Ok(());
3318            }
3319        }
3320        self.push_node_entry(name, norm_ns, super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0), rank)
3321    }
3322
3323    /// The rank seeded for `(name, namespace)` by [`Self::bind_node_rank`], 0
3324    /// when none was.
3325    pub(super) fn lookup_node_rank(&self, name: &str, namespace: &str) -> u8 {
3326        self.node_sched_table
3327            .iter()
3328            .find(|e| e.0.as_str() == name && e.1.as_str() == namespace)
3329            .map_or(0, |e| e.3)
3330    }
3331
3332    /// A new node-name table entry.
3333    fn push_node_entry(
3334        &mut self,
3335        name: &str,
3336        norm_ns: &str,
3337        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
3338        rank: u8,
3339    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
3340        // New entry. Too long, or table full, is an ERROR the caller surfaces
3341        // — never a dropped binding. A binding that vanishes leaves the node on
3342        // the wrong sched context with nothing to read that says so.
3343        let mut name_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
3344        let mut ns_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
3345        name_s
3346            .push_str(name)
3347            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
3348        ns_s.push_str(norm_ns)
3349            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
3350        self.node_sched_table
3351            .push((name_s, ns_s, sc, rank))
3352            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::TableFull)?;
3353        Ok(())
3354    }
3355
3356    /// Look up the seeded sched-context for `(name, namespace)`. Returns
3357    /// `None` when the table has no entry for this pair (unseed → default 0).
3358    /// `pub(super)` — visible only within the `executor` module (sibling
3359    /// `node_record` calls it from `NodeBuilder::build`).
3360    pub(super) fn lookup_node_sched(
3361        &self,
3362        name: &str,
3363        namespace: &str,
3364    ) -> Option<super::sched_context::SchedContextId> {
3365        for entry in self.node_sched_table.iter() {
3366            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == namespace {
3367                return Some(entry.2);
3368            }
3369        }
3370        None
3371    }
3372
3373    // =========================================================================
3374    // Phase 273 (RFC-0047) — per-callback-group → sched-context table
3375    // =========================================================================
3376
3377    /// Seed a config-resolved tier binding by `(name, namespace, group)` before
3378    /// entities are registered. `apply_node_default_sched` consults this table
3379    /// first (group table > node default > `SchedContextId(0)`).
3380    ///
3381    /// Call BEFORE entity creation. An existing entry for the same
3382    /// `(name, namespace, group)` key is overwritten (last-write wins). Overflow
3383    /// past `MAX_CBS` is an `Err`, never a dropped binding — issue 1172. An
3384    /// empty `namespace` is normalised to
3385    /// `"/"` to match `NodeBuilder::build`. Mirror of `bind_node_name_sched`.
3386    pub fn bind_group_sched(
3387        &mut self,
3388        name: &str,
3389        namespace: &str,
3390        group: &str,
3391        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
3392    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
3393        let norm_ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
3394        // Overwrite if there is already an entry for this (name, ns, group).
3395        for entry in self.group_sched_table.iter_mut() {
3396            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == norm_ns && entry.2.as_str() == group
3397            {
3398                entry.3 = sc;
3399                return Ok(());
3400            }
3401        }
3402        // Same contract as the two above.
3403        let mut name_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
3404        let mut ns_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
3405        let mut grp_s = heapless::String::<32>::new();
3406        name_s
3407            .push_str(name)
3408            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
3409        ns_s.push_str(norm_ns)
3410            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
3411        grp_s
3412            .push_str(group)
3413            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
3414        self.group_sched_table
3415            .push((name_s, ns_s, grp_s, sc))
3416            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::TableFull)?;
3417        Ok(())
3418    }

3420    /// Look up the seeded sched-context for `(name, namespace, group)`. Returns
3421    /// `None` when the table has no entry for this triple.
3422    fn lookup_group_sched(
3423        &self,
3424        name: &str,
3425        namespace: &str,
3426        group: &str,
3427    ) -> Option<super::sched_context::SchedContextId> {
3428        for entry in self.group_sched_table.iter() {
3429            if entry.0.as_str() == name
3430                && entry.1.as_str() == namespace
3431                && entry.2.as_str() == group
3432            {
3433                return Some(entry.3);
3434            }
3435        }
3436        None
3437    }

3439    // =========================================================================
3440    // Phase 110.B — SchedContext API
3441    // =========================================================================
3442
3443    /// Identifier of the auto-created default `Fifo`-class scheduling
3444    /// context. Every callback registered without an explicit
3445    /// [`Self::bind_handle_to_sched_context`] binds to this SC.
3446    pub fn default_sched_context_id(&self) -> super::sched_context::SchedContextId {
3447        super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0)
3448    }
3449
3450    /// Register a new scheduling context. Returns a [`SchedContextId`](crate::executor::sched_context::SchedContextId)
3451    /// callers pass to [`Self::bind_handle_to_sched_context`] to attach
3452    /// callbacks. Phase 110.B.
3453    pub fn create_sched_context(
3454        &mut self,
3455        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContext,
3456    ) -> Result<super::sched_context::SchedContextId, NodeError> {
3457        // Slot 0 is reserved for the default Fifo SC; search 1..MAX_SC.
3458        for (i, slot) in self.sched_contexts.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(1) {
3459            if slot.is_none() {
3460                *slot = Some(sc);
3461                // Phase 110.E — Sporadic-class SCs get a sibling
3462                // `SporadicState` entry that the spin_once dispatch
3463                // path consults each cycle to refill the budget at
3464                // period boundaries and skip dispatch when budget
3465                // is exhausted.
3466                if matches!(sc.class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
3467                    let budget = sc.budget_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
3468                    let period = sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
3469                    self.sporadic_states[i] =
3470                        Some(super::sched_context::SporadicState::new(budget, period));
3471                }
3472                return Ok(super::sched_context::SchedContextId(i as u8));
3473            }
3474        }
3475        Err(NodeError::NoSchedContextSlot)
3476    }

3478    /// RFC-0052 W3b.2 — wall-clock µs since the UNIX epoch, when this
3479    /// target has an epoch source (config `epoch_us`, defaulted from
3480    /// `SystemTime` on hosted configs). `None` = no wall clock; age
3481    /// monitors must not have been baked (the emitter refuses).
3482    pub fn epoch_now_us(&self) -> Option<u64> {
3483        self.epoch_us_fn.map(|f| f())
3484    }

3486    /// RFC-0052 W3b.4 — install the baked contract-monitor table. Call
3487    /// BEFORE entity creation so `create_publisher` can attach each
3488    /// contracted endpoint's counter cell. Mirrors `set_qos_overrides`:
3489    /// `&'static`, codegen-baked, empty by default.
3490    ///
3491    /// phase-496 W1 -- the executor watches at most
3492    /// [`MAX_MONITORS`](super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS) rows
3493    /// (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_MONITORS`). A generated entry cannot reach this with
3494    /// more: its table carries a compile-time assertion that names the knob,
3495    /// and the C++ installer refuses at runtime. A hand-written longer table is
3496    /// a debug-build panic naming the knob, because in release the spin loop
3497    /// would inspect only the first `MAX_MONITORS` and leave the rest silently
3498    /// unwatched.
3499    pub fn set_monitor_table(&mut self, table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec]) {
3500        if let Err(full) = super::monitor::check_table_capacity(table.len(), 0)
3501            && cfg!(debug_assertions)
3502        {
3503            panic!("set_monitor_table: {full}");
3504        }
3505        self.monitor_table = table;
3506    }
3507
3508    /// phase-496 W1 -- install BOTH baked monitor tables, or neither.
3509    ///
3510    /// The refusing installer: a table longer than this executor watches
3511    /// (`MAX_MONITORS` / `MAX_AGE_MONITORS`) is `Err`, and its `Display` names
3512    /// the knob to raise, before anything is installed. Nothing is truncated:
3513    /// the spin loop inspects only the first `MAX_*` specs, so accepting a
3514    /// longer table would boot with its tail silently unwatched. The C ABI's
3515    /// `nros_cpp_install_monitors` refuses on the same check.
3516    pub fn try_set_monitor_tables(
3517        &mut self,
3518        table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
3519        ages: &'static [super::monitor::AgeMonitorSpec],
3520    ) -> Result<(), super::monitor::MonitorTableFull> {
3521        super::monitor::check_table_capacity(table.len(), ages.len())?;
3522        self.monitor_table = table;
3523        self.age_table = ages;
3524        Ok(())
3525    }

3527    /// The installed monitor table (empty unless the entry set one).
3528    #[must_use]
3529    pub fn monitor_table(&self) -> &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec] {
3530        self.monitor_table

3572    /// [`Self::set_age_table`] install, so install those first; a guard whose
3573    /// row is absent never faults. The observer runs after the monitor rows on
3574    /// every monitor tick and reports `hazard-detected`, `hazard-reaction` and
3575    /// `hazard-recovered` on the same drain.
3576    pub fn set_hazard_table(&mut self, table: &'static [super::monitor::HazardSpec]) {

3580    /// phase-462 W4 -- install the contract's mode variants of the two monitor
3581    /// tables; entry `i` is mode `i`, and entry 0 must be the base tables
3582    /// already installed. A switch is asked for with
3583    /// [`super::monitor::request_mode`] and applied at the next spin.
3584    ///
3585    /// # Errors
3586    ///
3587    /// [`super::monitor::ModeTablesMismatch`] when an entry's tables are not the base's
3588    /// length: a variant shares the base's cells and the per-row monitor
3589    /// state by index, so a variant of another length would judge one row
3590    /// by another's requirement. Nothing is installed.
3591    pub fn set_mode_tables(
3592        &mut self,
3593        modes: &'static [super::monitor::ModeTables],
3594    ) -> Result<(), super::monitor::ModeTablesMismatch> {
3595        for (id, m) in modes.iter().enumerate() {
3596            if m.monitors.len() != self.monitor_table.len() || m.ages.len() != self.age_table.len()
3597            {
3598                return Err(super::monitor::ModeTablesMismatch {
3599                    mode: id as u16,
3600                    monitors: (m.monitors.len(), self.monitor_table.len()),
3601                    ages: (m.ages.len(), self.age_table.len()),
3602                    missing_sc: None,
3603                });
3604            }
3605            if let Some(d) = m
3606                .deadlines
3607                .iter()
3608                .find(|d| !matches!(self.sched_contexts.get(usize::from(d.sc)), Some(Some(_))))
3609            {
3610                return Err(super::monitor::ModeTablesMismatch {
3611                    mode: id as u16,
3612                    monitors: (m.monitors.len(), self.monitor_table.len()),
3613                    ages: (m.ages.len(), self.age_table.len()),
3614                    missing_sc: Some(d.sc),
3615                });
3616            }
3617        }
3618        self.mode_tables = modes;
3619        Ok(())
3620    }
3621
3622    /// The mode whose tables this executor judges by (0 = the base).
3623    #[must_use]
3624    pub fn current_mode(&self) -> u16 {
3625        self.mode_applied
3626    }
3627
3628    /// phase-462 W4 -- once per spin, before any rule runs: enter the mode the
3629    /// application asked for, if this executor has tables for it.
3630    fn update_mode(&mut self, now_us: Option<u64>) {
3631        if self.mode_tables.is_empty() {
3632            return;
3633        }
3634        // phase-462 W4c -- a request seen now arrived after the previous
3635        // check, so this gap bounds how long it waited.
3636        let now_ms = now_us.map(|us| (us / 1_000) as u32);
3637        let waited_ms = match (now_ms, self.mode_checked_ms) {
3638            (Some(now), Some(prev)) => Some(now.wrapping_sub(prev)),
3639            _ => None,
3640        };
3641        self.mode_checked_ms = now_ms;
3642        let want = super::monitor::requested_mode();
3643        if want == self.mode_seen {
3644            return;
3645        }
3646        self.mode_seen = want;
3647        match self.mode_tables.get(usize::from(want)) {
3648            Some(t) => {
3649                self.monitor_table = t.monitors;
3650                self.age_table = t.ages;
3651                for d in t.deadlines {
3652                    if let Some(Some(sc)) = self.sched_contexts.get_mut(usize::from(d.sc)) {
3653                        sc.deadline_us = super::sched_context::OptUs::from_us(d.deadline_us);
3654                    }
3655                }
3656                if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_mode_switch(t, waited_ms) {
3657                    self.violations.record(v);
3658                }
3659                self.mode_applied = want;
3660                nros_log::log_info!(
3661                    nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
3662                    "contract mode {} entered",
3663                    want
3664                );
3665            }
3666            None => nros_log::log_warn!(
3667                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
3668                "contract mode {} requested, but this executor bakes {} mode table(s); \
3669                 staying in mode {}",
3670                want,
3671                self.mode_tables.len(),
3672                self.mode_applied
3673            ),
3674        }
3675    }

3677    /// The installed hazard table (empty unless the entry set one).

3683    /// W3b.5 — override the wall-clock (epoch µs) source age monitors take
3684    /// message stamps against. Hosted builds default to `SystemTime`; a
3685    /// board with a synced RTC installs its own here (or via
3686    /// `ExecutorConfig::epoch_us`). Call BEFORE entity creation — the age
3687    /// hook captures this at `create_subscription` time.
3688    pub fn set_epoch_clock(&mut self, epoch_us: fn() -> u64) {
3689        self.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch_us);
3690    }
3691
3692    /// W3b.5 — resolve a subscription's age hook at registration time:
3693    /// exact topic match against the baked age table, only for stamped
3694    /// types (`M::STAMP_OFFSET`) and only when an epoch source exists.
3695    fn age_lookup<M: RosMessage>(&self, topic: &str) -> Option<super::arena::AgeMon> {
3696        M::STAMP_OFFSET?;
3697        let epoch = self.epoch_us_fn?;
3698        self.age_table
3699            .iter()
3700            .find(|a| a.topic == topic)
3701            .map(|a| (a.cell, epoch))
3702    }
3703
3704    /// W3b.5 — install the `DeadlineAction::Fault` hook. Without one a
3705    /// fault-class deadline miss panics (watchdog-visible stop on
3706    /// embedded targets).
3707    /// Plan one `spin_once` against the caller's intended cadence, and return
3708    /// the park budget in microseconds.
3709    ///
3710    /// phase-474 I11 -- two cases:
3711    ///
3712    /// * **No declared cadence, non-zero timeout** (the generated entries'
3713    ///   `spin_once(10)` loop, `spin`, `spin_period`): the timeout is the
3714    ///   period and the loop runs on an absolute RELEASE GRID. The budget is
3715    ///   the time to the next grid point, not a whole period from now, so the
3716    ///   previous spin's work no longer pushes every later release back. A
3717    ///   loop that comes back after its next point was due is released at
3718    ///   once, late by the difference; one that comes back a whole period or
3719    ///   more after it is released once for the LATEST due point and the
3720    ///   older ones are skipped and counted -- the timer `Skip` policy, never
3721    ///   a burst. Lateness is judged at the release (`record_grid_release`).
3722    ///   A change of timeout re-anchors the grid at this entry.
3723    /// * **A declared cadence** (`set_spin_nominal_us`, the tier loops that
3724    ///   sleep between spins themselves): unchanged. Late is
3725    ///   `(now - last_entry) - cadence`, clamped at zero, and the budget is
3726    ///   the timeout.
3727    ///
3728    /// A zero timeout claims no cadence and is skipped entirely, which keeps
3729    /// `Future::wait`-style busy spins out of the statistic and off the grid.
3730    fn record_release_jitter(&mut self, timeout: core::time::Duration) -> u64 {
3731        let timeout_us = timeout.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
3732        if !self.spin_nominal_self_paced() {
3733            if timeout_us == 0 {
3734                return 0;
3735            }
3736            let Some(now) = self.now_us() else {
3737                return timeout_us;
3738            };
3739            // phase-436 A2b -- a wait-paced declaration supplies the grid's
3740            // period; otherwise the timeout stands in for it.
3741            let period_us = if self.spin_nominal_declared_us != 0 {
3742                self.spin_nominal_declared_us
3743            } else {
3744                timeout_us
3745            };
3746            self.spin_nominal_us = period_us;
3747            if self.grid.period_us != period_us {
3748                // First periodic spin, or a new period: anchor here, so the
3749                // first park is a whole period exactly as before.
3750                self.grid.period_us = period_us;
3751                self.grid.next_us = now.saturating_add(period_us);
3752            } else if now >= self.grid.next_us.saturating_add(period_us) {
3753                // The loop came back a whole period or more after its next
3754                // release was due: serve the latest due point once and drop
3755                // the ones before it. The first dropped point is a release
3756                // that never happened, so its lateness at this moment (a
3757                // period or more) is what the jitter rule judges.
3758                let missed = (now - self.grid.next_us) / period_us;
3759                self.note_dropped_release(now - self.grid.next_us);
3760                self.grid.skipped = self
3761                    .grid
3762                    .skipped
3763                    .saturating_add(missed.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
3764                self.grid.next_us = self
3765                    .grid
3766                    .next_us
3767                    .saturating_add(missed.saturating_mul(period_us));
3768            }
3769            // The timeout still bounds the wait. With a declared period it
3770            // may be shorter than the period (a caller that passes whole
3771            // milliseconds for a 1.5 ms cadence); a wake before the grid
3772            // point is then not a release, and the next spin parks again.
3773            return self.grid.next_us.saturating_sub(now).min(timeout_us);
3774        }
3775        // phase-474 I7 -- the violation reporter's own time since the last
3776        // sample is not a late release (see `flush_violation_reports`). Taken
3777        // first, so a spin that judges nothing does not carry it forward.
3778        let report_us = core::mem::take(&mut self.violations.reports.debt_us);
3779        let nominal_us = self.spin_nominal_declared_us;
3780        let Some(now) = self.now_us() else {
3781            return timeout_us;
3782        };
3783        self.spin_nominal_us = nominal_us;
3784        if let Some(last) = self.last_spin_entry_us {
3785            let interval = now.saturating_sub(last).saturating_sub(report_us);
3786            self.total_wakes = self.total_wakes.saturating_add(1);
3787            if let Some(late) = interval.checked_sub(nominal_us)
3788                && late > 0
3789            {
3790                self.count_late_wake(late);
3791            }
3792        }
3793        self.last_spin_entry_us = Some(now);
3794        timeout_us
3795    }
3796
3797    /// phase-474 I11 -- judge a grid release, at the clock read after the
3798    /// park. A spin that wakes before its grid point (data arrived, a timer
3799    /// or another source was due first) is not a release: it dispatches and
3800    /// leaves the grid where it was. One that wakes at or after it is THE
3801    /// release of that point, late by `now - grid.next_us` (less the
3802    /// violation reporter's own time, phase-474 I7), and the grid advances by
3803    /// one period. Points the park itself overslept by a whole period are
3804    /// skipped at the next entry, not served in a burst.
3805    fn record_grid_release(&mut self, now: u64) {
3806        if self.spin_nominal_self_paced() || self.grid.period_us == 0 {
3807            return;
3808        }
3809        if now < self.grid.next_us {
3810            return;
3811        }
3812        let report_us = core::mem::take(&mut self.violations.reports.debt_us);
3813        let late = now
3814            .saturating_sub(self.grid.next_us)
3815            .saturating_sub(report_us);
3816        self.total_wakes = self.total_wakes.saturating_add(1);
3817        if late > 0 {
3818            self.count_late_wake(late);
3819        }
3820        self.grid.next_us = self.grid.next_us.saturating_add(self.grid.period_us);
3821        if now >= self.grid.next_us {
3822            // The park overslept the following point(s) too. This wake serves
3823            // one release; the points it ran past are skipped, not released
3824            // back to back on the next spins.
3825            let missed = (now - self.grid.next_us) / self.grid.period_us + 1;
3826            self.grid.skipped = self
3827                .grid
3828                .skipped
3829                .saturating_add(missed.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
3830            self.grid.next_us = self
3831                .grid
3832                .next_us
3833                .saturating_add(missed.saturating_mul(self.grid.period_us));
3834        }
3835    }
3836
3837    /// One wake that came back `late_us` (> 0) after its release was due.
3838    fn count_late_wake(&mut self, late_us: u64) {
3839        self.late_wakes = self.late_wakes.saturating_add(1);
3840        if late_us > self.release_jitter_granularity_us() {
3841            self.late_wakes_beyond_granule = self.late_wakes_beyond_granule.saturating_add(1);
3842        }
3843        if late_us > self.max_release_jitter_us {
3844            self.max_release_jitter_us = late_us;
3845        }
3846    }
3847
3848    /// A cadence the caller meets with its own sleep between spins.
3849    fn spin_nominal_self_paced(&self) -> bool {
3850        self.spin_nominal_declared_us != 0 && !self.spin_nominal_wait_paced
3851    }
3852
3853    /// The lateness of a grid release that was dropped rather than served,
3854    /// into the high-water the jitter rule reads (not into the wake counts:
3855    /// no wake happened).
3856    fn note_dropped_release(&mut self, late_us: u64) {
3857        let late = late_us.saturating_sub(core::mem::take(&mut self.violations.reports.debt_us));
3858        if late > self.max_release_jitter_us {
3859            self.max_release_jitter_us = late;
3860        }
3861    }
3862
3863    /// phase-474 I11 -- grid releases skipped since the last
3864    /// `clear_release_jitter_stats`, because the loop came back after they
3865    /// were due. Zero for a declared-cadence or zero-timeout caller.
3866    pub fn skipped_releases(&self) -> u32 {
3867        self.grid.skipped
3868    }
3869
3870    /// Release-jitter statistics from the spin loop: worst lateness in
3871    /// microseconds, the number of wakes that were already late, and the
3872    /// number of wakes total.
3873    ///
3874    /// The maximum is the figure of merit, and the ratio is what tells the
3875    /// two failures apart: one late wake in ten thousand is a glitch, ten
3876    /// thousand in ten thousand means the period cannot be met at all.
3877    ///
3878    /// Zero on a build with no clock -- `spin_period` refuses to run at all
3879    /// there (issue 0709), so there is nothing to have measured.
3880    pub fn release_jitter(&self) -> (u64, u32, u32) {
3881        (
3882            self.max_release_jitter_us,
3883            self.late_wakes,
3884            self.total_wakes,
3885        )
3886    }
3887
3888    /// phase-436 A2c -- of the `late` wakes `release_jitter` counts, those
3889    /// late by more than [`Self::release_jitter_granularity_us`].
3890    ///
3891    /// A wake is late at one microsecond past its release. A loop paced by a
3892    /// tick-granular park comes back up to a tick past it on every wake, by
3893    /// design, so `late` approaches `total` on a loop that is keeping its
3894    /// period perfectly well. This count leaves that rounding out: it is the
3895    /// lateness the measurement can actually resolve. Cleared with the rest.
3896    pub fn late_wakes_beyond_granularity(&self) -> u32 {
3897        self.late_wakes_beyond_granule
3898    }
3899
3900    /// Reset the release-jitter statistics. For monitoring code that logs
3901    /// and clears per window, so a single early outlier does not pin the
3902    /// maximum for the life of the process.
3903    pub fn clear_release_jitter_stats(&mut self) {
3904        self.max_release_jitter_us = 0;
3905        self.late_wakes = 0;
3906        self.late_wakes_beyond_granule = 0;
3907        self.total_wakes = 0;
3908        self.last_spin_entry_us = None;
3909        self.jitter_reported_us = 0;
3910        self.grid.skipped = 0;
3911    }
