3913    pub fn set_fault_handler(&mut self, f: fn(&super::monitor::Violation)) {
3914        self.fault_fn = Some(f);
3915    }
3916
3917    /// phase-503 — install the REACTION hook: `f(event, ctx)` is called on the
3918    /// spin thread when a supervised route passes its deadline
3919    /// (`route-deadline-runtime`), with the row's reaction id, row index and
3920    /// mechanism. It also stands in for [`Self::set_fault_handler`] on a
3921    /// `DeadlineAction::Fault` when no fault handler is set (reaction id 0,
3922    /// the sched-context slot as the row), so a C or C++ image has a fault
3923    /// path that does not panic. Replaces any earlier hook; `None` removes it.
3924    ///
3925    /// The hook must not block and must not re-enter this executor: it starts
3926    /// the fallback, or hands it to another thread, and returns.
3927    pub fn set_reaction_hook(
3928        &mut self,
3929        hook: Option<(super::monitor::ReactionHookFn, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
3930    ) {
3931        self.reaction_hook = hook;
3932    }
3933
3934    /// phase-509 P9b (RFC-0108 "As built in P9b") -- install the lock every
3935    /// FFI entry and every worker pass takes on this executor (`None` removes
3936    /// it). Call it while no second thread can reach the executor: a runner
3937    /// installs it before it spawns a level.
3938    pub fn set_exec_lock(&mut self, lock: Option<super::exec_lock::ExecLock>) {
3939        self.exec_lock = lock;
3940    }
3941
3942    /// phase-509 P9b -- the installed lock, if any.
3943    pub(crate) fn exec_lock(&self) -> Option<super::exec_lock::ExecLock> {
3944        self.exec_lock
3945    }
3946
3947    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- whether the callback of `slot` runs in a window
3948    /// on a thread other than the calling one. An operation on such an entry
3949    /// would race the callback, so the entry accessors answer as for a stale
3950    /// handle and cancel / reset are deferred to the end of the dispatch.
3951    /// `false` with no window open, which is every one-level image.
3952    pub(crate) fn running_elsewhere(&self, slot: usize) -> bool {
3953        if self.running.is_null() {
3954            return false;
3955        }
3956        let Some(me) = self.exec_lock.and_then(|l| l.current_thread()) else {
3957            return false;
3958        };
3959        let mut r = self.running;
3960        while !r.is_null() {
3961            // SAFETY: a record is linked only for its window and unlinked
3962            // under the lock before its frame ends (`pass`), and the caller
3963            // holds the lock.
3964            let rec = unsafe { &*r };
3965            if rec.slot == slot {
3966                return rec.thread != me;
3967            }
3968            r = rec.next;
3969        }
3970        false
3971    }
3972
3973    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- link `rec` into the open windows.
3974    ///
3975    /// # Safety
3976    /// `rec` stays alive and unmoved until [`Self::unlink_running`] removes
3977    /// it, under the lock.
3978    unsafe fn link_running(&mut self, rec: *mut super::exec_lock::Running) {
3979        // SAFETY: the caller's contract.
3980        unsafe { (*rec).next = self.running };
3981        self.running = rec;
3982    }
3983
3984    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- unlink `rec`, linked by
3985    /// [`Self::link_running`].
3986    fn unlink_running(&mut self, rec: *mut super::exec_lock::Running) {
3987        let mut at: *mut *mut super::exec_lock::Running = &mut self.running;
3988        // SAFETY: every linked record is alive (`link_running`'s contract),
3989        // and the list is touched only under the lock.
3990        unsafe {
3991            while !(*at).is_null() {
3992                if *at == rec {
3993                    *at = (*rec).next;
3994                    return;
3995                }
3996                at = &mut (**at).next;
3997            }
3998        }
3999    }
4000
4001    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the dispatch level of `slot`'s occupant: its
4002    /// sched context's bucket, and inside `Normal` its rank.
4003    fn slot_level(&self, slot: usize) -> u8 {
4004        let sc_idx = self.sched_context_bindings[slot].0 as usize;
4005        let priority = self
4006            .sched_contexts
4007            .get(sc_idx)
4008            .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
4009            .map_or(super::sched_context::Priority::Normal, |sc| sc.priority);
4010        let rank = self.slot_tags.get(slot).map_or(0, |t| t.rank);
4011        priority.dispatch_level(rank)
4012    }
4013
4014    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the slots whose dispatch level is in `band`.
4015    /// Every slot for [`super::scheduler::Band::ALL`], the one-level worker's
4016    /// band, without looking at one.
4017    fn band_slots(&self, level: u8, band: super::scheduler::Band) -> u64 {
4018        // phase-509 P9b item 4 -- levels that own their slots by
4019        // registration (a level runner): the worker of `level` runs exactly
4020        // what its level's setup registered, whatever the ranks say.
4021        if self.worker.registering_level != super::scheduler::NO_OWNING_LEVEL {
4022            let mut mask = 0u64;
4023            for i in 0..self.entries.len().min(64) {
4024                if self.entries[i].is_some()
4025                    && self.slot_tags.get(i).is_some_and(|t| t.level == level)
4026                {
4027                    mask |= 1u64 << i;
4028                }
4029            }
4030            return mask;
4031        }
4032        if band == super::scheduler::Band::ALL {
4033            return u64::MAX;
4034        }
4035        let mut mask = 0u64;
4036        for i in 0..self.entries.len().min(64) {
4037            if self.entries[i].is_some() && band.contains(self.slot_level(i)) {
4038                mask |= 1u64 << i;
4039            }
4040        }
4041        mask
4042    }
4043
4044    /// phase-509 P9b item 4 -- the callbacks registered from now on belong
4045    /// to level `level`: its worker runs them, and no other does. The first
4046    /// call switches the executor to levels that own their slots by
4047    /// registration (a level runner sets each level up in turn); until then,
4048    /// and on every image that never calls it, a worker's band of dispatch
4049    /// levels decides.
4050    pub fn set_registering_level(&mut self, level: u8) {
4051        self.worker.registering_level = level.min(super::scheduler::NO_OWNING_LEVEL - 1);
4052        // Issue 2018 -- a level's own scheduling context is set after it
4053        // becomes the registering level, never inherited from the last one.
4054        self.worker.registering_sched = 0;
4055    }
4056
4057    /// Issue 2018 (RFC-0108 As-built) -- give the registering level its own
4058    /// scheduling context: the one its tier's policy lowers to
4059    /// ([`SchedContext::from_tier_policy`](super::sched_context::SchedContext::from_tier_policy)).
4060    /// Callbacks registered from now on, until the registering level
4061    /// changes, bind to it unless a node or callback-group binding names
4062    /// another. A level's budget is then charged to that level alone, never
4063    /// to the executor's default context, which every level shares.
4064    ///
4065    /// A `Sporadic` context is created with the executor's cooperative
4066    /// budget (it skips the level's callbacks once the budget is spent, until
4067    /// the period refills it). A runner whose kernel enforces the same
4068    /// budget on the level's thread hands it to the kernel with
4069    /// [`Self::defer_budget_to_kernel`], so the budget is enforced exactly
4070    /// once.
4071    pub fn set_level_sched_context(
4072        &mut self,
4073        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContext,
4074    ) -> Result<super::sched_context::SchedContextId, NodeError> {
4075        let id = self.create_sched_context(sc)?;
4076        self.worker.registering_sched = id.0;
4077        Ok(id)
4078    }
4079
4080    /// Issue 2018 -- the kernel enforces `sc`'s budget on the level's thread
4081    /// (NuttX `SCHED_SPORADIC`, Linux `SCHED_DEADLINE`), so the executor
4082    /// stops enforcing it: the context keeps its class, budget, period and
4083    /// deadline, and its callbacks are no longer skipped for want of budget.
4084    /// One enforcer per level, with one set of numbers. `false` when `sc`
4085    /// carries no cooperative budget (nothing to hand over).
4086    pub fn defer_budget_to_kernel(&mut self, sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId) -> bool {
4087        match self.sporadic_states.get_mut(sc.0 as usize) {
4088            Some(st @ Some(_)) => {
4089                *st = None;
4090                true
4091            }
4092            _ => false,
4093        }
4094    }
4095
4096    /// Issue 2018 -- whether `sc`'s budget is enforced by this executor
4097    /// (a cooperative `Sporadic` context the kernel was not handed).
4098    pub fn enforces_budget(&self, sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId) -> bool {
4099        self.sporadic_states
4100            .get(sc.0 as usize)
4101            .is_some_and(|s| s.is_some())
4102    }
4103
4104    /// Issue 2020 -- the level that owns what is registered now, `None` until
4105    /// a level runner first calls [`Self::set_registering_level`].
4106    pub fn registering_level(&self) -> Option<u8> {
4107        (self.worker.registering_level != super::scheduler::NO_OWNING_LEVEL)
4108            .then_some(self.worker.registering_level)
4109    }
4110
4111    /// Issue 2020 -- whether a pass ticks a component (or anything else
4112    /// registered) owned by `owner`, the level recorded at registration
4113    /// (`None`: no level owned it).
4114    ///
4115    /// `band_level` is the level of a band pass ([`Self::spin_band_once`]),
4116    /// `None` for a pass of the executor's own worker. When the levels own
4117    /// their slots by registration, a band pass ticks only its level's, and
4118    /// the executor's own worker (the boot level) ticks its own level's and
4119    /// any registered before a level was set. Otherwise the executor's own
4120    /// worker ticks everything and a band pass nothing, as before levels.
4121    pub fn pass_ticks_owner(&self, band_level: Option<u8>, owner: Option<u8>) -> bool {
4122        let owning = self.worker.registering_level != super::scheduler::NO_OWNING_LEVEL;
4123        match band_level {
4124            Some(l) => owning && owner == Some(l),
4125            None => !owning || owner.is_none() || owner == Some(self.worker.level),
4126        }
4127    }
4128
4129    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the band the executor's own worker runs:
4130    /// every level by default. With band workers over the same executor
4131    /// ([`Self::spin_band_once`]), the bands must partition the levels, so
4132    /// each callback has one worker.
4133    pub fn set_worker_band(&mut self, band: super::scheduler::Band) {
4134        self.worker.band = band;
4135    }
4136
4137    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- one pass of the executor's own worker, through
4138    /// a raw pointer: `spin_once`, except that with a lock that has a thread
4139    /// identity installed ([`super::exec_lock::ExecLock::with_thread_id`]) the
4140    /// lock is released around each user callback, so other threads (band
4141    /// workers, FFI callers) reach the executor while it runs.
4142    ///
4143    /// # Safety
4144    /// `this` points at a live executor. If any other thread can reach it, a
4145    /// lock is installed and the calling thread holds it exactly once, and
4146    /// every other thread takes it before touching the executor. No reference
4147    /// to the executor is live in the caller across this call.
4148    pub unsafe fn spin_once_shared(
4149        this: *mut Self,
4150        timeout: core::time::Duration,
4151    ) -> SpinOnceResult {
4152        let mut discarded = None;
4153        // SAFETY: the caller's contract is `pass`'s.
4154        unsafe { Self::pass(this, PassMode::Shared, timeout, &mut discarded) }
4155    }
4156
4157    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- one pass of a band worker over an executor it
4158    /// shares: the readiness of `worker`'s band, then its callbacks, most
4159    /// urgent level first, the lock released around each one as in
4160    /// [`Self::spin_once_shared`]. A band pass does not park, drive the
4161    /// transport or run the executor-wide chores (parameter and lifecycle
4162    /// services, the monitors' rules): the executor's own worker does.
4163    /// Issue 2020 -- it does tick the components its level registered
4164    /// ([`Self::pass_ticks_owner`]), and the executor's own worker then does
4165    /// not.
4166    ///
4167    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 -- a worker with a waiter
4168    /// ([`super::scheduler::BandWorker::with_waiter`]) first parks, the lock
4169    /// released, for at most `timeout`: until its band's next timer is due or
4170    /// an arrival in its band signals it. Without one, `timeout` is unused
4171    /// and the pass polls.
4172    ///
4173    /// # Safety
4174    /// As [`Self::spin_once_shared`].
4175    pub unsafe fn spin_band_once(
4176        this: *mut Self,
4177        worker: &mut super::scheduler::BandWorker,
4178        timeout: core::time::Duration,
4179    ) -> SpinOnceResult {
4180        let mut discarded = None;
4181        // SAFETY: the caller's contract is `pass`'s.
4182        unsafe { Self::pass(this, PassMode::Band(worker), timeout, &mut discarded) }
4183    }
4184
4185    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 -- link `worker`'s waiter into this executor's
4186    /// arrival routing (RFC-0108 D7): an arrival attributed to a slot of its
4187    /// band then wakes it alone, an unattributed one wakes it with the rest.
4188    /// A worker with no waiter polls; this is then a no-op, as on a build
4189    /// with no arrival path. Attach each waiter to one executor, once.
4190    pub fn attach_band_worker(&mut self, worker: &super::scheduler::BandWorker) {
4191        let Some(waiter) = worker.waiter else {
4192            return;
4193        };
4194        waiter.slots.store(
4195            self.band_slots(worker.level, worker.band) as usize,
4196            portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst,
4197        );
4198        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4199        if let Some(ctx) = self.wake_ctx.as_ref() {
4200            let w = waiter as *const super::scheduler::BandWaiter as *mut _;
4201            let head = &ctx.band_waiters;
4202            let mut cur = head.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire);
4203            loop {
4204                waiter.next.store(cur, portable_atomic::Ordering::Release);
4205                match head.compare_exchange(
4206                    cur,
4207                    w,
4208                    portable_atomic::Ordering::AcqRel,
4209                    portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire,
4210                ) {
4211                    Ok(_) => break,
4212                    Err(now) => cur = now,
4213                }
4214            }
4215        }
4216    }
4217
4218    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- a band pass's prelude: check in as its level,
4219    /// read the clock, and credit its timers with the time since ITS previous
4220    /// pass. Item 3: with a waiter and a positive `timeout`, park first, with
4221    /// the lock released, until the band's next timer is due, an arrival in
4222    /// the band signals the waiter, or `timeout` passes.
4223    ///
4224    /// # Safety
4225    /// As [`Self::owned_prelude`].
4226    unsafe fn band_prelude(
4227        this: *mut Self,
4228        window_lock: Option<super::exec_lock::ExecLock>,
4229        w: &mut super::scheduler::BandWorker,
4230        timeout: core::time::Duration,
4231    ) -> (Option<u64>, u64) {
4232        // SAFETY: the caller's contract; derived again after the park.
4233        let mut s: &mut Self = unsafe { &mut *this };
4234        if let Some(waiter) = w.waiter {
4235            let mask = s.band_slots(w.level, w.band);
4236            waiter
4237                .slots
4238                .store(mask as usize, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
4239            let budget_us = timeout.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
4240            // A band timer's remainder is as of the worker's last pass; the
4241            // time since is already spent.
4242            let since_us = match (s.now_us(), w.last_spin_end_us) {
4243                (Some(now), Some(prev)) => now.saturating_sub(prev),
4244                _ => 0,
4245            };
4246            let bound_us = s
4247                .next_timer_deadline_in_us(mask)
4248                .map_or(budget_us, |t| t.saturating_sub(since_us).min(budget_us));
4249            if bound_us > 0 && !s.band_has_arrivals(mask) {
4250                let window = window_lock.map(super::exec_lock::Window::open);
4251                waiter.wait_us(bound_us);
4252                drop(window);
4253                // SAFETY: the lock is held again.
4254                s = unsafe { &mut *this };
4255            }
4256        }
4257        let now = s.now_us();
4258        super::level_liveness::LEVELS.check_in(w.level, now);
4259        match now {
4260            Some(now) => {
4261                let prev = w.last_spin_end_us.unwrap_or(now);
4262                w.last_spin_end_us = Some(now);
4263                (Some(now), now.saturating_sub(prev))
4264            }
4265            None => (None, 0),
4266        }
4267    }
4268
4269    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 -- whether an arrival for one of `mask`'s slots
4270    /// is already in the ready word (it then does not park).
4271    fn band_has_arrivals(&self, mask: u64) -> bool {
4272        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4273        if let Some(ctx) = self.wake_ctx.as_ref() {
4274            return ctx.ready.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) as u64 & mask != 0;
4275        }
4276        let _ = mask;
4277        false
4278    }
4279
4280    /// phase-503 — microseconds from now to the earliest deadline of a pending
4281    /// supervised route (0 when one is due), or `None` when none is waiting or
4282    /// the executor has no clock. A port that supervises with its own timer
4283    /// (`MECHANISM_TIMER`) re-arms it from this after each spin.
4284    pub fn route_next_due_us(&self) -> Option<u64> {
4285        // No table, no clock read: this runs on every park.
4286        if self.monitor_table.is_empty() {
4287            return None;
4288        }
4289        let clock = self.clock_us_fn?;
4290        super::monitor::route_next_due_us(self.monitor_table, clock())
4291    }
4292
4293    /// phase-503 W7 -- a [`RouteWatch`](super::monitor::RouteWatch) over this
4294    /// executor's supervised routes, which a port's timer or reaction thread
4295    /// reads from outside the spin thread: at its expiry it sees a route the
4296    /// running spin has already answered, without waiting for the spin to
4297    /// return. `None` without a monitor table or a clock. Take it after
4298    /// `set_monitor_table` and any clock change.
4299    pub fn route_watch(&self) -> Option<super::monitor::RouteWatch> {
4300        if self.monitor_table.is_empty() {
4301            return None;
4302        }
4303        let clock = self.clock_us_fn?;
4304        Some(super::monitor::RouteWatch::new(self.monitor_table, clock))
4305    }
4306
4307    /// Issue #515 — warn about periods the spin cadence cannot express.
4308    ///
4309    /// A timer fires on the first spin at or after its period elapses, so
4310    /// a period that is not an integer multiple of the executor's spin
4311    /// period lands on the spin grid instead of the declared cadence: a
4312    /// 33 ms timer on a 5 ms spin alternates 35 ms / 30 ms, mean 33.0.
4313    /// The rate is preserved and no activation is dropped, so every
4314    /// runtime rule is (correctly) silent — the jitter stays invisible
4315    /// until someone measures cadence on target.
4316    ///
4317    /// Runs ONCE, on the first spin carrying a non-zero timeout, because
4318    /// that timeout is where the tier's declared spin period becomes
4319    /// visible down here. A resolve-time diagnostic would be better
4320    /// still — the toolchain holds both numbers before the image is
4321    /// built — but this backstop needs no board or codegen change and
4322    /// catches hand-written spin loops too.
4323    /// phase-436 W1 (issue 1192) — how long the executor may park, in
4324    /// microseconds, given the caller's budget.
4325    ///
4326    /// The park used to be bounded by the caller's timeout narrowed by exactly
4327    /// one input, the BACKEND's `next_deadline_ms`. A registered timer is a
4328    /// deadline the EXECUTOR owns, and nothing let it shorten the sleep — so
4329    /// `spin_default`'s 50 ms slept straight past a 10 ms timer, and the
4330    /// activations then arrived in the burst issue 0505 describes.
4331    ///
4332    /// This is the `min` over the deadline sources phase-436 names. The
4333    /// caller's budget is always a member, so the result is never unbounded
4334    /// and never zero-by-omission: with no timers registered the budget
4335    /// stands, which keeps a long idle wait a wait rather than a poll.
4336    ///
4337    /// Distinct from issue 0515's audit, which warns that a period does not
4338    /// divide the spin grid. That takes the grid as given; this moves it.
4339    ///
4340    /// `#[cfg(test)]`-gated (matching `mod tests`'s own gate in `mod.rs`):
4341    /// production code calls `next_wake_bound_attributed_us` directly to get
4342    /// the source alongside the bound, so this `.0`-only convenience has no
4343    /// caller outside the test module and is dead code in any build that
4344    /// does not compile it (every `cargo check`/`cargo doc`, and `cargo test
4345    /// --features rmw-cffi`, which excludes `mod tests` too).
4346    #[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
4347    pub(crate) fn next_wake_bound_us(&self, budget_us: u64) -> u64 {
4348        self.next_wake_bound_attributed_us(budget_us, None).0
4349    }
4350
4351    /// phase-436 W6 — contribute a deadline source.
4352    ///
4353    /// The core never names an RTOS: a port registers `k_poll`, `epoll`, a
4354    /// queue set or a device ISR here, and the executor only ever asks "when
4355    /// will you next need me?".
4356    ///
4357    /// Refuses past capacity rather than dropping silently. A source that was
4358    /// quietly discarded would leave the executor sleeping past a deadline it
4359    /// had been told about, which is the failure this whole phase exists to
4360    /// remove.
4361    pub fn register_wake_source(
4362        &mut self,
4363        next: NextDeadlineFn,
4364        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
4365    ) -> Result<WakeSourceId, NodeError> {
4366        if self.worker.wake_source_count as usize >= MAX_WAKE_SOURCES {
4367            return Err(NodeError::ExecutorFull);
4368        }
4369        let idx = self.worker.wake_source_count as usize;
4370        self.worker.wake_sources[idx] = Some(WakeSourceSlot { next, ctx });
4371        self.worker.wake_source_count += 1;
4372        Ok(WakeSourceId::Platform(idx as u8))
4373    }
4374
4375    /// Install THE thing that blocks. Singular by nature — only one primitive
4376    /// can actually wait — so this replaces whatever was there.
4377    /// `granularity_us` is the finest park this primitive can actually
4378    /// express. The port states it because only the port knows: the ABI
4379    /// signature is not the limit — an RTOS tick is a second, coarser one, and
4380    /// a timespec primitive is a finer one.
4381    pub(crate) fn set_park_primitive(
4382        &mut self,
4383        park: ParkUntilFn,
4384        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
4385        granularity_us: u64,
4386    ) {
4387        self.worker.park_primitive = Some((park, ctx));
4388        self.worker.park_granularity_declared_us = granularity_us;
4389    }
4390
4391    /// The wake primitive a port must hand its `ParkUntilFn` as `ctx`, or NULL
4392    /// when this build has none.
4393    ///
4394    /// phase-436 W7 — a park that waits on its own fresh object is NOT
4395    /// breakable by the backend's listener, and installing one makes latency
4396    /// worse: once a port has parked, the transport drain drops to
4397    /// non-blocking, so an unbreakable park sleeps out its full deadline with
4398    /// data already waiting. Waiting on THIS object keeps the async break.
4399    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4400    pub(crate) fn wake_raw_ptr(&self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
4401        match self.node_wake.as_ref() {
4402            Some(w) => w.raw_ptr(),
4403            None => core::ptr::null_mut(),
4404        }
4405    }
4406
4407    /// phase-509 P7 (RFC-0108 D8.1) -- the level this executor runs, 0 the
4408    /// most urgent. An executor's runner sets it ([`Self::set_level`]); one it
4409    /// never set is level 0, which is every executor of a one-level image.
4410    /// It matches the generated `NROS_ENTRY_LEVEL_OF_<node>` of the nodes the
4411    /// executor hosts.
4412    pub fn level(&self) -> u8 {
4413        self.worker.level
4414    }
4415
4416    /// phase-509 P7 -- set the level this executor runs; its spins check in
4417    /// as that level. `false`, and nothing changed, at or past
4418    /// [`MAX_LEVELS`](super::MAX_LEVELS).
4419    pub fn set_level(&mut self, level: u8) -> bool {
4420        if level as usize >= super::level_liveness::MAX_LEVELS {
4421            return false;
4422        }
4423        self.worker.level = level;
4424        true
4425    }
4426
4427    /// Whether a platform park primitive is installed.
4428    pub fn has_park_primitive(&self) -> bool {
4429        self.worker.park_primitive.is_some()
4430    }
4431
4432    /// The bound and the source that produced it: the `min` over every
4433    /// deadline source, with the caller's budget as an ordinary member.
4434    ///
4435    /// The budget being a member is what makes the result never unbounded and
4436    /// never zero-by-omission, and it is why "no sources registered" needs no
4437    /// special case.
4438    pub(crate) fn next_wake_bound_attributed_us(
4439        &self,
4440        budget_us: u64,
4441        session_us: Option<u64>,
4442    ) -> (u64, WakeSourceId) {
4443        let mut best = (budget_us, WakeSourceId::CallerBudget);
4444
4445        // The backend's next internal event is a MEMBER, not a pre-cap. It was
4446        // folded into the budget upstream, which meant a park the session
4447        // actually won reported `CallerBudget` — the attribution named the
4448        // wrong source, and "why did we wake" is the question attribution
4449        // exists to answer.
4450        if let Some(s) = session_us
4451            && s < best.0
4452        {
4453            best = (s, WakeSourceId::Session);
4454        }
4455
4456        if let Some(timer_us) = self.next_timer_deadline_us()
4457            && timer_us < best.0
4458        {
4459            best = (timer_us, WakeSourceId::Timer);
4460        }
4461
4462        // phase-503 — a supervised route's deadline is the executor's own, like
4463        // a timer's: the park must end there, or a route whose output never
4464        // comes is judged only when something else wakes the loop.
4465        if let Some(due_us) = self.route_next_due_us()
4466            && due_us < best.0
4467        {
4468            best = (due_us, WakeSourceId::RouteDeadline);
4469        }
4470
4471        for (i, slot) in self.worker.wake_sources.iter().enumerate() {
4472            let Some(slot) = slot else { continue };
4473            // SAFETY: the callback and ctx were supplied together by the port
4474            // through `register_wake_source` and outlive the executor by its
4475            // contract; the call takes no ownership.
4476            let due = unsafe { (slot.next)(slot.ctx) };
4477            // `u64::MAX` is "nothing pending" — an async source spells itself
4478            // this way and breaks the park by signalling instead.
4479            if due != u64::MAX && due < best.0 {
4480                best = (due, WakeSourceId::Platform(i as u8));
4481            }
4482        }
4483
4484        best
4485    }
4486
4487    /// phase-436 — the bound the last park used, and which source won it.
4488    pub fn last_park(&self) -> (u64, WakeSourceId) {
4489        (self.worker.last_park_bound_us, self.worker.last_park_source)
4490    }
4491
4492    /// phase-436 W2 — the park the platform was actually asked for, after
4493    /// rounding the request up to an expressible value.
4494    ///
4495    /// Differs from `last_park().0` exactly when the request did not land on
4496    /// the platform's grid. Both are reported because a cadence that cannot be
4497    /// waited in must not be presented as if it were met.
4498    pub fn last_park_achieved_us(&self) -> u64 {
4499        self.worker.last_park_achieved_us
4500    }
4501
4502    /// phase-436 W3 (issue 1194) — the granularity the release-jitter
4503    /// measurement was actually made at, in microseconds.
4504    ///
4505    /// The jitter statistic is reported in microseconds, but the mechanism
4506    /// that PACES the loop decides how fine it can honestly be, and there are
4507    /// two mechanisms:
4508    ///
4509    /// * **No declared cadence** — the loop is paced by the blocking wait
4510    ///   itself, so it cannot come round more precisely than one park granule.
4511    ///   Reporting µs there is precision the wait cannot deliver.
4512    /// * **A declared cadence** (`set_spin_nominal_us`) — the caller paces
4513    ///   itself, as nros-cpp's tiers do with `platform_sleep_us` between
4514    ///   spins. That sleep is finer than the wait, so the measurement really
4515    ///   is good to a microsecond and coarsening it would understate it.
4516    ///
4517    /// Reported rather than applied: this does not change what the monitor
4518    /// judges, because silently coarsening a bound could mask real lateness.
4519    /// It says what the number is worth.
4520    pub fn release_jitter_granularity_us(&self) -> u64 {
4521        if self.spin_nominal_self_paced() {
4522            1
4523        } else {
4524            self.park_granularity_us()
4525        }
4526    }
4527
4528    /// The finest park this build can actually express, in microseconds.
4529    ///
4530    /// Comes from the INSTALLED primitive, because only the port knows. The
4531    /// exported ABI signature is not the limit in either direction (issue
4532    /// 1242):
4533    ///
4534    /// * an RTOS tick is a COARSER limit — ThreadX pins
4535    ///   `TX_TIMER_TICKS_PER_SECOND = 100`, a 10 ms tick, so a 1 ms park is not
4536    ///   achievable there however the ABI is spelled;
4537    /// * a timespec primitive is a FINER one — POSIX's `sem_timedwait` and
4538    ///   `pthread_cond_timedwait` are nanosecond-native, and only the
4539    ///   `uint32_t timeout_ms` signature floors them at a millisecond.
4540    ///
4541    /// This was a hardcoded `1_000` justified by "every `nros_platform_wake_*`
4542    /// port takes `uint32_t timeout_ms`". That was right for FreeRTOS by
4543    /// coincidence and wrong for the other two, and it made the W3 jitter
4544    /// report over-claim on ThreadX — the failure W3 exists to prevent,
4545    /// reproduced one layer below W3 in its own dependency.
4546    ///
4547    /// With nothing installed the fallback is 1 ms, which IS the honest floor
4548    /// of the `wake_wait_ms` ABI every port exports today.
4549    ///
4550    /// The declared granularity counts only while the park is USABLE. An
4551    /// executor whose backend has no live wake (XRCE, or a session whose
4552    /// callback is gone) never parks: `spin_once` waits in the transport's
4553    /// own receive instead, whose timeout is whole milliseconds. Claiming a
4554    /// POSIX park's 1 us there over-claimed the jitter report, and worse,
4555    /// rounded the bound to microseconds that the millisecond wait then
4556    /// truncated, so a sub-millisecond deadline became a non-blocking receive
4557    /// and the loop spun hot until it passed.
4558    pub fn park_granularity_us(&self) -> u64 {
4559        if self.worker.park_granularity_declared_us != 0
4560            && self.worker.park_primitive.is_some()
4561            && self.park_can_be_woken()
4562        {
4563            self.worker.park_granularity_declared_us
4564        } else {
4565            1_000
4566        }
4567    }
4568
4569    /// phase-436 — whether a park could be ended early by data arriving.
4570    ///
4571    /// A park ends on its bound or on the wake object. With a poll-only
4572    /// backend (XRCE), or a session whose wake callback is gone, nothing
4573    /// signals that object, so a park would be a blind sleep and data
4574    /// arriving mid-park would wait out the whole bound — the Phase 127.C.4
4575    /// stall (a reliable stream whose ACK lands in a session nobody drives).
4576    /// Builds without `alloc` + `rmw-cffi` have no wake callback at all and
4577    /// park as they always did.
4578    pub(crate) fn park_can_be_woken(&self) -> bool {
4579        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4580        {
4581            self.async_wake_live()
4582        }
4583        #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
4584        {
4585            true
4586        }
4587    }
4588
4589    /// Drive the primary session for `timeout_ms`, the transport-side half of
4590    /// the wait.
4591    ///
4592    /// phase-436 (RFC-0106 D5) — on a poll-only backend this wait IS the
4593    /// executor's park, and it waits inside the backend's own `recv`, which a
4594    /// guard condition triggered from another thread cannot end: the trigger
4595    /// signals the wake object and nobody is waiting on it. Measured on XRCE
4596    /// before this: a trigger 20 ms into a 100 / 500 / 1000 ms spin was
4597    /// dispatched 79 / 480 / 979 ms later, i.e. it waited out the bound. So
4598    /// when such a waker exists and nothing can wake the park, the drive is
4599    /// cut into slices of [`POLL_ONLY_WAKE_SLICE_MS`] and stops at the first
4600    /// slice that ends with the wake flag set. The latency becomes one slice;
4601    /// an executor with no cross-thread waker keeps the single blocking drive.
4602    fn drive_primary(&mut self, timeout_ms: i32) -> Result<(), ()> {
4603        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4604        if self.has_cross_thread_waker
4605            && !self.async_wake_live()
4606            && timeout_ms > POLL_ONLY_WAKE_SLICE_MS
4607        {
4608            let mut remaining = timeout_ms;
4609            while remaining > 0 {
4610                let slice = remaining.min(POLL_ONLY_WAKE_SLICE_MS);
4611                self.session.drive_io(slice).map_err(|_| ())?;
4612                remaining -= slice;
4613                if self
4614                    .wake_flag
4615                    .swap(false, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
4616                {
4617                    // Issue 1385 — consume the primitive too, or the next
4618                    // spin's wait returns at once on a signal already acted on.
4619                    if let Some(wake) = self.node_wake.as_ref() {
4620                        let _ = wake.wait_ms(0);
4621                    }
4622                    break;
4623                }
4624            }
4625            return Ok(());
4626        }
4627        self.session.drive_io(timeout_ms).map_err(|_| ())
4628    }
4629
4630    pub(crate) fn round_park_up_us(&self, requested_us: u64) -> u64 {
4631        if requested_us == 0 {
4632            return 0;
4633        }
4634        let g = self.park_granularity_us();
4635        if g <= 1 {
4636            return requested_us;
4637        }
4638        requested_us.div_ceil(g).saturating_mul(g)
4639    }
4640
4641    /// Microseconds until the soonest live timer is due, or `None` when no
4642    /// timer is pending.
4643    ///
4644    /// A timer that is cancelled, or a one-shot that already fired, owes
4645    /// nothing and must not hold the park short — otherwise the executor keeps
4646    /// waking on a deadline nobody is waiting for.
4647    ///
4648    /// So does a timer whose remainder is not WALL microseconds
4649    /// ([`TimerClockSource::remaining_is_wall_time`], issue 1321): the number
4650    /// this returns is handed to the port's park primitive, so a ROS-time
4651    /// timer's simulated remainder would be a units error — and on a paused
4652    /// `/clock` a frozen one, waking the image once per timer period forever.
4653    /// Its wake source is a `/clock` message, which reaches `drive_io` like
4654    /// any sample.
4655    ///
4656    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 -- the executor's own worker's timers: those of
4657    /// its band (every timer for the one-level worker), so it does not wake
4658    /// for a timer another band's worker runs.
4659    pub(crate) fn next_timer_deadline_us(&self) -> Option<u64> {
4660        self.next_timer_deadline_in_us(self.band_slots(self.worker.level, self.worker.band))
4661    }
4662
4663    /// phase-509 P9b item 3 -- [`Self::next_timer_deadline_us`] over the
4664    /// timers in `mask`'s slots.
4665    pub(crate) fn next_timer_deadline_in_us(&self, mask: u64) -> Option<u64> {
4666        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
4667        let mut soonest: Option<u64> = None;
4668        for (i, meta) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
4669            let Some(meta) = meta else { continue };
4670            if i < 64 && mask & (1u64 << i) == 0 {
4671                continue;
4672            }
4673            // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- not a timer running in another worker's
4674            // window: its header is that worker's while it runs, and a
4675            // running timer is not the one to wait for.
4676            if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) || Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i) {
4677                continue;
4678            }
4679            // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a `TimerEntry<F>`, whose
4680            // leading layout is `TimerHeader` — the same projection
4681            // `audit_spin_quantization` relies on.
4682            let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
4683            if header.cancelled || header.period_us == 0 {
4684                continue;
4685            }
4686            if header.oneshot && header.fired {
4687                continue;
4688            }
4689            // Issue 1321 — the park is WALL microseconds, so only a timer
4690            // whose own clock runs in them may bound it.
4691            if !header.clock_source.remaining_is_wall_time() {
4692                continue;
4693            }
4694            // Already due: the bound is zero, and no other timer can beat it.
4695            let remaining = header.period_us.saturating_sub(header.elapsed_us);
4696            soonest = Some(match soonest {
4697                Some(cur) => cur.min(remaining),
4698                None => remaining,
4699            });
4700            if remaining == 0 {
4701                break;
4702            }
4703        }
4704        soonest
4705    }
4706
4707    fn audit_spin_quantization(&mut self, spin_us: u64) {
4708        self.spin_quantized_timers(spin_us, |period_us, early_us, late_us| {
4709            nros_log::log_warn!(
4710                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
4711                "timer period {} us is not a multiple of the {} us spin period: activations will alternate between {} us and {} us (mean cadence preserved)",
4712                period_us,
4713                spin_us,
4714                early_us,
4715                late_us
4716            );
4717        });
4718    }
4719
4720    /// Each timer the executor's own worker runs whose period `spin_us`
4721    /// quantizes, as `(period_us, early_us, late_us)`. Split out of
4722    /// [`Self::audit_spin_quantization`], which only logs, so the choice of
4723    /// timers can be asserted.
4724    ///
4725    /// Issue 2050 -- only the timers in the worker's own band
4726    /// ([`Self::band_slots`], the same mask its pass dispatches from). In a
4727    /// level runner the executor's own worker is the boot level, paced at the
4728    /// boot level's spin period, while a spawned level's timers run on that
4729    /// level's band worker, whose park is bounded by its next timer deadline.
4730    /// Auditing every timer judged a 1 ms timer on a spawned level against a
4731    /// 10 ms boot spin it never ran under.
4732    pub(crate) fn spin_quantized_timers(&self, spin_us: u64, mut f: impl FnMut(u64, u64, u64)) {
4733        if spin_us == 0 {
4734            return;
4735        }
4736        let mask = self.band_slots(self.worker.level, self.worker.band);
4737        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
4738        for (i, meta) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
4739            let Some(meta) = meta.as_ref() else {
4740                continue;
4741            };
4742            if i < 64 && mask & (1u64 << i) == 0 {
4743                continue;
4744            }
4745            if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) || Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i) {
4746                continue;
4747            }
4748            // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a `TimerEntry<F>`,
4749            // whose leading layout is `TimerHeader`.
4750            let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
4751            let period_us = header.period_us;
4752            let Some((early_us, late_us)) =
4753                spin_quantization_span(header.clock_source, period_us, spin_us)
4754            else {
4755                continue;
4756            };
4757            f(period_us, early_us, late_us);
4758        }
4759    }
4760
4761    /// Issue #514 — whether the executor logs each violation as it is
4762    /// detected (the default).
4763    ///
4764    /// Turn this off in an application that reports violations its own
4765    /// way via [`Self::drain_violations`]; the ring is unaffected
4766    /// either way.
4767    pub fn set_report_violations(&mut self, enabled: bool) {
4768        self.violations.report = enabled;
4769    }
4770
4771    /// phase-474 I1 -- the drain-and-report hook: at the end of every spin,
4772    /// drain the ring and log each entry with its sequence number and the
4773    /// `total` / `dropped` counters (`contract violation #N: <rule> <fqn>
4774    /// measured=.. declared=.. (total=.. dropped=..)`).
4775    ///
4776    /// While on it REPLACES the log line at detection, so one verdict is one
4777    /// line, and an application that wanted to drain the ring itself sees an
4778    /// empty one. The generated C/C++ entries turn it on when the image sets
4779    /// `CONFIG_NROS_VIOLATION_DRAIN_REPORT` (off by default). The trace marker
4780    /// (`callback_trace::MARKER_VIOLATION`) and the SWD record do not depend
4781    /// on it: both are written at detection.
4782    pub fn set_violation_drain_report(&mut self, enabled: bool) {
4783        self.violations.drain_report = enabled;
4784    }
4785
4786    /// Issue #514 / phase-474 I1 -- violations evicted from the full ring
4787    /// before any drain took them.
4788    ///
4789    /// The ring keeps the LATEST `MAX_VIOLATIONS`, so non-zero means the
4790    /// OLDEST verdicts were lost, never the newest. (Before phase-474 a full
4791    /// ring refused the push, which kept the first verdicts since boot and
4792    /// lost every later one.)
4793    pub fn violations_dropped(&self) -> u32 {
4794        self.violations.counts.dropped
4795    }
4796
4797    /// phase-474 I1 -- contract violations this executor stored since boot
4798    /// (wrapping). The newest entry in the ring is number `violations_total()`;
4799    /// `total - dropped - pending` is how many drains have taken.
4800    pub fn violations_total(&self) -> u32 {
4801        self.violations.counts.total
4802    }

4804    /// RFC-0052 W3b.4 -- drain pending contract violations, OLDEST first.
4805    /// Draining clears the ring. Call between spins, never from a callback.
4806    pub fn drain_violations(&mut self, mut f: impl FnMut(&super::monitor::Violation)) {
4807        self.violations.drain(|_, v| f(v));
4808    }
4809
4810    /// [`Self::drain_violations`] with each entry's sequence number (1-based,
4811    /// per executor; the same number the drain-and-report line and the trace
4812    /// marker carry), so a reader can tell a gap from a quiet interval.
4813    pub fn drain_violations_numbered(&mut self, f: impl FnMut(u32, &super::monitor::Violation)) {
4814        self.violations.drain(f);
4815    }
