4817    /// phase-474 I2 -- choose when this executor's contract monitors arm,
4818    /// overriding the build default (`NROS_MONITOR_ARM_ON_CALL`,
4819    /// `NROS_MONITOR_ARM_GRACE_MS`). Call before the first spin (an
4820    /// `arm_monitors` made before it is undone by this); after the first spin
4821    /// an executor that already armed stays armed.
4822    ///
4823    /// `on_call`: wait for [`Self::arm_monitors`] or
4824    /// [`super::monitor::request_monitor_arming`] (`rclc_monitors_arm()`).
4825    /// `grace_ms`: arm anyway that long after the first spin (0 = never by
4826    /// deadline; with `on_call == false`, 0 means "at the first spin").
4827    pub fn set_monitor_arming(&mut self, on_call: bool, grace_ms: u32) {
4828        let v = &mut self.violations.counts;
4829        v.arm_on_call = on_call;
4830        v.arm_grace_ms = grace_ms;
4831        if !v.spun {
4832            // Before the first spin, "armed" is just the policy's answer (no
4833            // rule has run yet); the first spin counts the arming once.
4834            v.armed = super::monitor::MonitorArming { on_call, grace_ms }.armed_at_first_spin();
4835        }
4836    }
4837
4838    /// phase-474 I2 -- the application says its start-up is over: this
4839    /// executor's monitors start judging now. Idempotent.
4840    ///
4841    /// Judgement restarts at arming: every rate/age/silence window reopens,
4842    /// a latency or age measured before arming is discarded, the release-
4843    /// jitter statistics are cleared (so the figure after RUN is RUN's), and a
4844    /// stack low-water mark already past the declared minimum is reported
4845    /// again, because stack depth reached at start-up is a real fault, not
4846    /// start-up noise.
4847    pub fn arm_monitors(&mut self) {
4848        self.arm_now("the application armed them");
4849    }
4850
4851    /// phase-474 I2 -- whether this executor's monitors are armed.
4852    pub fn monitors_armed(&self) -> bool {
4853        self.violations.counts.armed
4854    }
4855
4856    /// phase-474 I2 -- verdicts reached before the monitors armed: counted,
4857    /// never stored, logged, sunk or traced.
4858    pub fn violations_suppressed_before_arm(&self) -> u32 {
4859        self.violations.counts.suppressed_before_arm
4860    }
4861
4862    fn arm_now(&mut self, why: &str) {
4863        if self.violations.counts.armed {
4864            return;
4865        }
4866        self.violations.counts.armed = true;
4867        for st in self.monitor_states.iter_mut() {
4868            *st = super::monitor::MonitorState::default();
4869        }
4870        for st in self.age_states.iter_mut() {
4871            *st = super::monitor::AgeState::default();
4872        }
4873        for spec in self.monitor_table.iter() {
4874            spec.cell
4875                .max_latency_us
4876                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4877        }
4878        // phase10-B3 -- a take waiting since start-up is not a route of RUN's.
4879        super::monitor::route_reset(self.monitor_table);
4880        for spec in self.age_table.iter() {
4881            spec.cell
4882                .max_age_ms
4883                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4884            spec.cell
4885                .takes
4886                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4887            spec.cell
4888                .arrivals
4889                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4890        }
4891        self.clear_release_jitter_stats();
4892        self.worker.stack_headroom_reported = usize::MAX;
4893        self.worker.stack_headroom_last_check_us = None;
4894        // Counted once per executor: here once it has spun, else by the first
4895        // spin (which counts an executor that is armed by then either way).
4896        #[cfg(nros_boot_report)]
4897        if self.violations.counts.spun {
4898            super::monitor::NROS_VIOLATION_RECORD
4899                .armed
4900                .fetch_add(1, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4901        }
4902        nros_log::log_info!(
4903            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
4904            "contract monitors armed ({}); {} verdict(s) before arming suppressed",
4905            why,
4906            self.violations.counts.suppressed_before_arm
4907        );
4908    }
4909
4910    /// phase-474 I2 -- once per spin, before any rule runs: note the first
4911    /// spin, and arm when the policy says so.
4912    fn update_monitor_arming(&mut self, now_us: Option<u64>) {
4913        // Milliseconds in a wrapping `u32`, like the silence rule's lease
4914        // (`AgeState::last_take_ms`): this state is inline in the `Executor`
4915        // value, whose size is budgeted (issue 0961).
4916        let now_ms = now_us.map(|us| (us / 1_000) as u32);
4917        let v = &mut self.violations.counts;
4918        if !v.spun {
4919            v.spun = true;
4920            v.first_spin_ms = now_ms.unwrap_or(0);
4921            if v.armed {
4922                // Armed from the start (the default), or by a call made before
4923                // the first spin: count it in the record so a reader sees how
4924                // many executors are judging.
4925                #[cfg(nros_boot_report)]
4926                super::monitor::NROS_VIOLATION_RECORD
4927                    .armed
4928                    .fetch_add(1, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
4929                return;
4930            }
4931            if (super::monitor::MonitorArming {
4932                on_call: v.arm_on_call,
4933                grace_ms: v.arm_grace_ms,
4934            })
4935            .armed_at_first_spin()
4936            {
4937                self.arm_now("at the first spin");
4938                return;
4939            }
4940        }
4941        if v.armed {
4942            return;
4943        }
4944        if super::monitor::arm_requests() != v.arm_requests_seen {
4945            self.arm_now("the application asked: rclc_monitors_arm");
4946            return;
4947        }
4948        let grace_ms = v.arm_grace_ms;
4949        if grace_ms == 0 {
4950            return;
4951        }
4952        match now_ms {
4953            Some(now) if now.wrapping_sub(v.first_spin_ms) >= grace_ms => {
4954                self.arm_now("the grace period after the first spin elapsed");
4955            }
4956            // No clock: a grace period cannot elapse, and waiting forever would
4957            // leave the image unmonitored. Arm rather than guess a duration.
4958            None if !v.arm_on_call => {
4959                self.arm_now("no clock to time the grace period");
4960            }
4961            _ => {}
4962        }
4963    }
4964
4965    /// Issue 1635 -- hand every stored violation to `sink`, beside the log line
4966    /// (issue 0514's floor) and the ring push.
4967    ///
4968    /// phase-474 I7 -- not at detection any more: the verdict is queued and
4969    /// leaves from `Executor::flush_violation_reports` at the end of a spin with
4970    /// slack, so the report never costs the dispatch it judges.
4971    ///
4972    /// Before this nothing in a generated image drained the ring, so the log
4973    /// line was the only output and `/diagnostics` stayed silent on every C
4974    /// and C++ road. A report point the RUNTIME owns reaches every road at
4975    /// once — every board's spin loop goes through the executor — where one
4976    /// per entry template would have to be rebuilt for each board runner. The
4977    /// ring is still filled, so an application (or a fixture) that drains it
4978    /// with [`Self::drain_violations`] sees exactly what it did before.
4979    /// `None` removes the sink.
4980    ///
4981    /// # Safety
4982    /// `ctx` must stay valid for every call of the sink until it is replaced
4983    /// or this executor is dropped (see [`super::monitor::ViolationSink`]).
4984    pub unsafe fn set_violation_sink(
4985        &mut self,
4986        sink: Option<(super::monitor::ViolationSink, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
4987    ) {
4988        self.violations.sink = sink.map(|(f, ctx)| (f, ctx as usize));
4989        if self.violations.sink.is_none() {
4990            // Nothing is left to send them to.
4991            self.violations.reports.pending.clear();
4992            self.violations.reports.since_us = None;
4993        }
4994    }
4995
4996    /// phase-474 I7 -- hand the queued verdicts to the sink, if this is a slot
4997    /// for it. Called at the end of every spin, after its dispatches and its
4998    /// rules, so the report never runs inside the tick being judged.
4999    ///
5000    /// A slot is a spin end whose next timer is due no sooner than the last
5001    /// report took (`ReportQueue::last_cost_us`; 0 before the first report, so
5002    /// the first goes at the first spin end with no timer already due), or
5003    /// any spin end once the oldest pending verdict has waited
5004    /// [`REPORT_DEFER_MAX_US`](super::monitor::REPORT_DEFER_MAX_US). Without a
5005    /// clock there is nothing to measure slack with, so every spin end is a
5006    /// slot. The sink takes as many as it coalesces into one message; the rest
5007    /// wait for the next slot.
5008    ///
5009    /// The time the sink takes is the reporter's own and is stated by
5010    /// [`Self::violation_report_cost_us`]; the release-jitter rule does not
5011    /// charge it to the spin's cadence (it is not a late release of any
5012    /// application work), which is what used to turn one verdict into a
5013    /// `release-jitter-runtime` verdict of its own on the safety island.
5014    pub(crate) fn flush_violation_reports(&mut self) {
5015        let Some((sink, ctx)) = self.violations.sink else {
5016            return;
5017        };
5018        if self.violations.reports.pending.is_empty() {
5019            return;
5020        }
5021        let now = self.now_us();
5022        if let Some(now) = now {
5023            let since = *self.violations.reports.since_us.get_or_insert(now);
5024            let overdue = now.saturating_sub(since) >= super::monitor::REPORT_DEFER_MAX_US;
5025            let cost = self.violations.reports.last_cost_us as u64;
5026            let slack = match self.next_timer_deadline_us() {
5027                None => true,
5028                Some(remaining) => remaining > 0 && remaining >= cost,
5029            };
5030            if !slack && !overdue {
5031                return;
5032            }
5033        }
5034        // SAFETY: `Executor::set_violation_sink`'s contract -- `ctx` is valid
5035        // for every call until the sink is replaced or the executor dropped.
5036        let taken = unsafe {
5037            sink(
5038                ctx as *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5039                &self.violations.reports.pending[..],
5040            )
5041        };
5042        let q = &mut self.violations.reports;
5043        if taken == 0 {
5044            // The sink counted its failure; drop the oldest so a report that
5045            // can never be sent does not stall the queue. It stays in the ring
5046            // and the record.
5047            q.pending.remove(0);
5048            q.failed = q.failed.saturating_add(1);
5049        } else {
5050            let n = taken.min(q.pending.len());
5051            for _ in 0..n {
5052                q.pending.remove(0);
5053            }
5054        }
5055        q.since_us = None;
5056        if let (Some(t0), Some(t1)) = (now, self.now_us()) {
5057            let q = &mut self.violations.reports;
5058            let cost = t1.saturating_sub(t0);
5059            q.last_cost_us = cost.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32;
5060            q.max_cost_us = q.max_cost_us.max(q.last_cost_us);
5061            q.debt_us = q.debt_us.saturating_add(cost);
5062        }
5063    }
5064
5065    /// phase-474 I7 -- what handing verdicts to the violation sink has cost
5066    /// this executor: `(last_us, max_us, pending, overflowed)`. `overflowed`
5067    /// counts verdicts evicted from the report queue by newer ones before a
5068    /// slot came (they are still in the ring and the SWD record).
5069    pub fn violation_report_cost_us(&self) -> (u32, u32, usize, u32) {
5070        let q = &self.violations.reports;
5071        (q.last_cost_us, q.max_cost_us, q.pending.len(), q.overflowed)
5072    }
5073
5074    /// THE monotonic-µs read. phase-359 W4 — every consumer goes through here.
5075    ///
5076    /// Before this there were FIVE spellings of "what time is it": this one,
5077    /// `last_spin_end: Instant`, and two ad-hoc `static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant>`
5078    /// blocks — plus `PlatformClock`, which nothing called because `Executor` is
5079    /// deliberately non-generic and the trait's methods are associated fns.
5080    ///
5081    /// `None` means no clock is available (no_std with no injected hook).
5082    /// Callers must degrade, not guess: a missing clock is why the sporadic
5083    /// refill and the major-frame phase behaved differently on no_std.
5084    fn now_us(&mut self) -> Option<u64> {
5085        self.clock_us_fn.map(|clock| clock())
5086    }
5087
5088    /// Run the rate/latency/age checks over the baked tables (single
5089    /// branch each when empty).
5090    fn run_contract_monitors(&mut self) {
5091        if !self.monitor_table.is_empty()
5092            && let Some(now_us) = self.now_us()
5093        {
5094            {
5095                for (i, spec) in self
5096                    .monitor_table
5097                    .iter()
5098                    .take(super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS)
5099                    .enumerate()
5100                {
5101                    if let Some(v) =
5102                        super::monitor::check_rate(spec, &mut self.monitor_states[i], now_us)
5103                    {
5104                        self.violations.record(v);
5105                    }
5106                    if let Some(v) =
5107                        super::monitor::check_latency(spec, &mut self.monitor_states[i])
5108                    {
5109                        self.violations.record(v);
5110                    }
5111                }
5112            }
5113        }
5114        if !self.age_table.is_empty() {
5115            // phase-462 W2 -- the age loop needs the clock now: `silence-runtime`
5116            // judges how long an endpoint has taken NOTHING, and `None` (a
5117            // build with no clock) makes that rule abstain rather than guess.
5118            // Read before the loop because the borrow of `age_states` below
5119            // outlives the `&mut self` the reader wants.
5120            let now_us = self.now_us();
5121            for (i, spec) in self
5122                .age_table
5123                .iter()
5124                .take(super::monitor::MAX_AGE_MONITORS)
5125                .enumerate()
5126            {
5127                if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_age(spec, &mut self.age_states[i], now_us) {
5128                    self.violations.record(v);
5129                }
5130            }
5131        }
5132        // phase-462 W3b -- the hazard observer reads the verdict STATE the rows
5133        // above just updated, so it runs after them and on the same tick.
5134        if !self.hazard_table.is_empty()
5135            && let Some(now_us) = self.now_us()
5136        {
5137            let now_ms = (now_us / 1_000) as u32;
5138            // phase-462 W3c -- a detected hazard whose reacting path states a
5139            // `safe_state` asks the reaction hook to start it, once per
5140            // detection. Not before arming: a start-up verdict is only
5141            // counted (phase-474 I2), and it starts nothing either.
5142            let hook = self.reaction_hook.filter(|_| self.violations.counts.armed);
5143            let violations = &mut self.violations;
5144            for (row, spec) in self.hazard_table.iter().enumerate() {
5145                super::monitor::check_hazard(
5146                    spec,
5147                    self.monitor_table,
5148                    &self.monitor_states,
5149                    &self.age_states,
5150                    now_ms,
5151                    |v| {
5152                        if v.rule == "hazard-detected" && spec.reaction_id != 0 {
5153                            call_hazard_reaction(hook, spec, row, &v);
5154                        }
5155                        violations.record(v);
5156                    },
5157                );
5158            }
5159        }
5160        self.check_route_deadlines();
5161    }
5162
5163    /// phase-503 — `route-deadline-runtime`: every pending supervised route
5164    /// past `take + route_deadline_ms` is reported (once until a route is
5165    /// within budget again) and its reaction requested through the hook.
5166    /// Runs right after the park, whose bound includes the earliest due time
5167    /// ([`WakeSourceId::RouteDeadline`]), so a route whose output never comes
5168    /// is judged within one park granule of its deadline. A callback that does
5169    /// not return holds this check too: that is `MECHANISM_TIMER`'s case.
5170    fn check_route_deadlines(&mut self) {
5171        let table = self.monitor_table;
5172        if table.is_empty() || !super::monitor::route_deadline_active(table) {
5173            return;
5174        }
5175        let Some(now_us) = self.now_us() else {
5176            return;
5177        };
5178        // Start-up is not RUN (phase-474 I2): before arming a verdict is only
5179        // counted, and no reaction is requested for it either.
5180        let hook = self.reaction_hook.filter(|_| self.violations.counts.armed);
5181        let violations = &mut self.violations;
5182        super::monitor::route_overdue(table, now_us, |row, v, first| {
5183            call_route_reaction(hook, table, row, &v);
5184            if first {
5185                violations.record(v);
5186            }
5187        });
5188    }
5189
5190    /// Issue #505 — report activations dropped by
5191    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::Skip`](super::arena::TimerOverrunPolicy)
5192    /// since the last check.
5193    ///
5194    /// Unlike the rate/age/latency rules this needs no baked spec table:
5195    /// every periodic timer counts its own overruns, and a dropped
5196    /// activation is a contract failure for any declared period. It runs
5197    /// on the same tick so violations land in the same ring the entry
5198    /// glue drains.
5199    /// Declare the minimum stack headroom this executor's thread must keep,
5200    /// in bytes. `0` (the default) disables the `stack-headroom-runtime`
5201    /// rule.
5202    ///
5203    /// Set by the entry that spawned the thread, because it is the only
5204    /// party that knows what stack it handed over: the executor never sees
5205    /// `stack_bytes`, and no portable query returns a task's total stack, so
5206    /// neither an absolute floor nor a percentage can be inferred here.
5207    /// Declare how often this executor's loop intends to come round, in
5208    /// microseconds. `0` (the default) falls back to the `spin_once` timeout.
5209    ///
5210    /// Needed because a driver's pacing and its blocking bound are separate
5211    /// numbers. nros-cpp's tier loops sleep `spin_period_us` between spins but
5212    /// pass a fixed 10 ms timeout, so the release-jitter rule judged every
5213    /// tier against 10 ms regardless of what the contract declared -- too lax
5214    /// for a 1 ms tier and far too strict for a 30 ms one.
5215    ///
5216    /// This also says the CALLER paces the loop (a sleep finer than the
5217    /// park), so the measurement is reported at 1 us. A loop paced by the
5218    /// `spin_once` wait itself declares with
5219    /// [`Self::set_spin_nominal_wait_paced_us`] instead.
5220    pub fn set_spin_nominal_us(&mut self, us: u64) {
5221        self.spin_nominal_declared_us = us;
5222        self.spin_nominal_wait_paced = false;
5223    }
5224
5225    /// phase-436 A2b -- declare the loop's cadence, in microseconds, for a
5226    /// loop paced by the `spin_once` wait itself. `0` withdraws it.
5227    ///
5228    /// [`Self::set_spin_nominal_us`] couples two facts: the period to judge
5229    /// against, and that the caller paces the loop with its own sleep. A loop
5230    /// like `for (;;) spin_once(period_ms)` has the first without the second.
5231    /// Declaring through the coupled setter would report its jitter at 1 us
5232    /// when the park it waits on is tick-granular (issue 1194's failure); not
5233    /// declaring at all makes the timeout the period, which is wrong whenever
5234    /// the timeout is not the period (a cadence that is not whole
5235    /// milliseconds, or one raised to a floor).
5236    ///
5237    /// Here the cadence is the period of the release grid that a
5238    /// `spin_once(timeout)` loop already runs on, and the timeout stays a
5239    /// bound on each wait. The jitter is judged at grid releases and reported
5240    /// at the park granularity.
5241    pub fn set_spin_nominal_wait_paced_us(&mut self, us: u64) {
5242        self.spin_nominal_declared_us = us;
5243        self.spin_nominal_wait_paced = us != 0;
5244    }
5245
5246    pub fn set_min_stack_headroom_bytes(&mut self, bytes: usize) {
5247        self.worker.min_stack_headroom_bytes = bytes;
5248        // phase-436 E4 — a new bound is checked on the next spin, not up to an
5249        // interval later.
5250        self.worker.stack_headroom_last_check_us = None;
5251        // phase-436 E3 — `check_stack_headroom_rule` treats a 0 from the port as
5252        // "not instrumented" and skips, which is right for the rule and wrong
5253        // for the reader: an armed rule that can never judge reports nothing,
5254        // exactly like one that judged and found the stack healthy. Ask the
5255        // port once, here. Entries set the bound at boot on the thread it
5256        // describes, so the answer is about the right stack and the warning
5257        // lands once per tier, next to the tier's other boot lines.
5258        // phase-436 E5 -- "does the port answer at all?" needs one byte, not
5259        // the whole unused region the full query would scan.
5260        self.worker.stack_headroom_blind =
5261            bytes != 0 && nros_platform_api::stack_unused_bytes_upto(1) == 0;
5262        if self.worker.stack_headroom_blind {
5263            nros_log::log_warn!(
5264                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
5265                "stack-headroom-runtime: a {} B minimum is set but this port reports no stack \
5266                 data, so the rule will never check (Zephyr: enable CONFIG_INIT_STACKS)",
5267                bytes
5268            );
5269        }
5270    }
5271
5272    /// phase-436 E3 — whether `stack-headroom-runtime` is armed on a port that
5273    /// cannot measure, and so will never report a violation.
5274    ///
5275    /// `true` means the rule's silence is not evidence of headroom. Zephyr
5276    /// answers only with `CONFIG_INIT_STACKS && CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO`;
5277    /// POSIX never does.
5278    pub fn stack_headroom_blind(&self) -> bool {
5279        self.worker.stack_headroom_blind
5280    }
5281
5282    /// Report a spin thread that has come closer to the end of its stack
5283    /// than `set_min_stack_headroom_bytes` allows.
5284    ///
5285    /// Runs on the same tick as the other rules and feeds the same ring.
5286    /// Queries the port at most once per `STACK_HEADROOM_CHECK_INTERVAL_US`
5287    /// (phase-436 E4): on a painted Zephyr stack the full query scans every
5288    /// unused byte, so an every-spin query put that scan inside the control
5289    /// loop. Since E5 the query is capped at the declared minimum, so a scan
5290    /// reads at most that many bytes.
5291    /// Nothing at all when no minimum was declared.
5292    fn check_stack_headroom_rule(&mut self) {
5293        if self.worker.min_stack_headroom_bytes == 0 {
5294            return;
5295        }
5296        self.worker.stack_headroom_spins_since_check = self
5297            .worker
5298            .stack_headroom_spins_since_check
5299            .saturating_add(1);
5300        let now_us = self.now_us();
5301        if !super::monitor::stack_headroom_check_due(
5302            now_us,
5303            self.worker.stack_headroom_last_check_us,
5304            self.worker.stack_headroom_spins_since_check,
5305        ) {
5306            return;
5307        }
5308        self.worker.stack_headroom_last_check_us = Some(now_us.unwrap_or(0));
5309        self.worker.stack_headroom_spins_since_check = 0;
5310        self.worker.stack_headroom_checks = self.worker.stack_headroom_checks.saturating_add(1);
5311        // phase-436 E5 -- the CAPPED query. The rule only asks whether
5312        // `min_stack_headroom_bytes` are unused, and a port that scans for
5313        // paint answers that by reading those bytes alone. Below the cap the
5314        // answer is the exact headroom, which is what a breach reports, so
5315        // no second, full scan is needed. E4's throttle still applies.
5316        let unused =
5317            nros_platform_api::stack_unused_bytes_upto(self.worker.min_stack_headroom_bytes);
5318        // 0 means the port does not instrument stacks, not that the stack is
5319        // full. Reporting a violation there would be a fault invented from an
5320        // absence of data.
5321        if unused == 0 {
5322            return;
5323        }
5324        if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_stack_headroom(
5325            unused,
5326            self.worker.min_stack_headroom_bytes,
5327            &mut self.worker.stack_headroom_reported,
5328        ) {
5329            self.violations.record(v);
5330        }
5331    }
5332
5333    /// AUTOSAR-style ALIVE supervision: report a SchedContext that produced
5334    /// no dispatch at all over a full window while declaring a period.
5335    ///
5336    /// Every other rule here fires when something happens and is wrong. This
5337    /// one fires when nothing happens, which is the failure a watchdog
5338    /// exists for and the one `rate-hierarchy-runtime` cannot see: that rule
5339    /// counts publishes on an endpoint, so a callback that stops firing while
5340    /// its topic is published from elsewhere leaves it satisfied.
5341    fn check_alive_supervision(&mut self) {
5342        let Some(now_us) = self.now_us() else {
5343            // No clock, no windows. Silence here is honest: the rule cannot
5344            // tell a stalled context from a fast one without time.
5345            return;
5346        };
5347        let n = self.alive_slots.len().min(self.sched_contexts.len());
5348        for i in 0..n {
5349            let period_us = match self.sched_contexts[i].as_ref() {
5350                Some(sc) => sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get() as u64).unwrap_or(0),
5351                None => continue,
5352            };
5353            let slot = &mut self.alive_slots[i];
5354            if let Some(v) =
5355                super::monitor::check_alive(period_us, slot.dispatches, &mut slot.state, now_us)
5356            {
5357                self.violations.record(v);
5358            }
5359        }
5360    }
5361
5362    /// Issue #515 — report a spin wake a whole period late.
5363    ///
5364    /// Runs on the same tick as `check_timer_overruns` and feeds the same
5365    /// ring, so the entry glue drains it with the other rules and no caller
5366    /// needs to know this one exists. Like that rule it needs no spec table:
5367    /// the bound is the spin period the caller already passes in.
5368    fn check_release_jitter_rule(&mut self) {
5369        let (max_us, _late, _total) = self.release_jitter();
5370        let period_us = self.spin_nominal_us;
5371        if let Some(v) =
5372            super::monitor::check_release_jitter(max_us, &mut self.jitter_reported_us, period_us)
5373        {
5374            self.violations.record(v);
5375        }
5376    }
5377
5378    fn check_timer_overruns(&mut self) {
5379        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
5380        for i in 0..self.entries.len() {
5381            let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref() else {
5382                continue;
5383            };
5384            // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- a timer whose callback runs in another
5385            // worker's window is that worker's to touch; its overrun is
5386            // reported by the next pass that finds it idle.
5387            if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) || Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i) {
5388                continue;
5389            }
5390            // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a `TimerEntry<F>`,
5391            // which shares its leading layout with `TimerHeader`. The
5392            // baseline lives in the header too, so this needs no state
5393            // parallel to `entries` (whose capacity is a runtime slice
5394            // length, not a const).
5395            let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
5396            if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_timer_overrun(
5397                header.overruns,
5398                &mut header.overruns_reported,
5399                0,
5400            ) {
5401                self.violations.record(v);
5402            }
5403        }
5404    }
5405
5406    /// RFC-0052 / phase-296 W3a — replace the DEFAULT scheduling context
5407    /// (slot 0, the SC every unbound callback dispatches through).
5408    ///
5409    /// The run_tiers model runs one Executor per tier, so a tier-wide
5410    /// scheduling policy (`[tiers.<t>] class/budget_us/period_us` and the
5411    /// TT window) is exactly "this executor's default SC". Boards call
5412    /// this once, before entity creation; explicit per-handle/per-group
5413    /// bindings still take precedence (they never resolve to slot 0).
5414    ///
5415    /// Sporadic-class SCs get the same sibling `SporadicState` the
5416    /// `create_sched_context` path builds, so budget refill/exhaustion
5417    /// applies to the default queue too.
5418    pub fn set_default_sched_context(&mut self, sc: super::sched_context::SchedContext) {
5419        self.sched_contexts[0] = Some(sc);
5420        if matches!(sc.class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
5421            let budget = sc.budget_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
5422            let period = sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
5423            self.sporadic_states[0] =
5424                Some(super::sched_context::SporadicState::new(budget, period));
5425        } else {
5426            self.sporadic_states[0] = None;
5427        }
5428    }
5429
5430    /// Bind a registered callback to a scheduling context. The next
5431    /// `spin_once` cycle dispatches the callback through that SC's
5432    /// queue (FIFO bitmap or EDF heap). Phase 110.B.
5433    pub fn bind_handle_to_sched_context(
5434        &mut self,
5435        handle: HandleId,
5436        sc_id: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
5437    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
5438        let i = self.live_slot(handle);
5439        if i >= self.entries.len() {
5440            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
5441        }
5442        if self.entries[i].is_none() {
5443            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
5444        }
5445        let sc_idx = sc_id.0 as usize;
5446        if sc_idx >= self.sched_contexts.len() || self.sched_contexts[sc_idx].is_none() {
5447            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
5448        }
5449        self.sched_context_bindings[i] = sc_id;
5450        Ok(())
5451    }
5452
5453    /// Phase 110.G — enable time-triggered dispatch by setting the
5454    /// executor's major-frame length. Once set, every `spin_once`
5455    /// cycle gates dispatch through each entry's bound SC's
5456    /// `tt_window_offset_us` / `tt_window_duration_us` fields:
5457    /// dispatch only fires when the current monotonic time falls
5458    /// inside the window `[off, off + duration) mod major_frame`.
5459    ///
5460    /// `major_frame_us = 0` disables the TT gate (default state).
5461    /// Setting a non-zero major frame after callbacks are already
5462    /// registered is allowed — TT gates take effect on the next
5463    /// `spin_once` cycle.
5464    pub fn register_time_triggered_dispatcher(&mut self, major_frame_us: u32) {
5465        self.major_frame_us = major_frame_us;
5466    }
5467
5468    /// Phase 110.G — apply a declarative cyclic schedule.
5469    ///
5470    /// One-shot helper that wraps the underlying primitives:
5471    /// validates the schedule (`major_frame > 0`, no overlapping
5472    /// windows, every window fits inside the major frame), sets the
5473    /// executor's major-frame length, then materialises one
5474    /// `SchedContext` per window with `class = TimeTriggered` +
5475    /// the window's offset / duration. Returns the per-window
5476    /// [`SchedContextId`](crate::executor::sched_context::SchedContextId) array so callers can immediately
5477    /// `bind_handle_to_sched_context(handle, sc_id)` for their
5478    /// subscription / timer handles.
5479    ///
5480    /// `N` is the schedule's *declared* maximum window count;
5481    /// `schedule.window_count` gates how many SCs are actually
5482    /// created. Unused trailing slots return
5483    /// `SchedContextId::default()` (sentinel — callers must respect
5484    /// `window_count`).
5485    pub fn apply_time_triggered_schedule<const N: usize>(
5486        &mut self,
5487        schedule: &super::sched_context::TimeTriggeredSchedule<N>,
5488    ) -> Result<
5489        [super::sched_context::SchedContextId; N],
5490        super::sched_context::TimeTriggeredScheduleError,
5491    > {
5492        schedule.validate()?;
5493        self.major_frame_us = schedule.major_frame_us;
5494        // SC slot 0 is the auto-created default; reusing it as a
5495        // sentinel for unused trailing slots is safe because the
5496        // caller respects `schedule.window_count`.
5497        let mut ids: [super::sched_context::SchedContextId; N] =
5498            [super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0); N];
5499        for (i, window) in schedule.windows[..schedule.window_count].iter().enumerate() {
5500            // TT is not a scheduling class (phase-482 W6 deleted the
5501            // `SchedClass::TimeTriggered` variant): it is a per-SC *window gate* on top of
5502            // the existing class-based dispatch (Fifo here keeps
5503            // the EDF / Sporadic budgets out of the picture for
5504            // pure cyclic schedules). The window-gate fields set
5505            // below are what `spin_once`'s 110.G runtime gate
5506            // actually reads.
5507            let sc = super::sched_context::SchedContext {
5508                tt_window_offset_us: super::sched_context::OptUs::from_us(window.offset_us),
5509                tt_window_duration_us: super::sched_context::OptUs::from_us(window.duration_us),
5510                ..super::sched_context::SchedContext::new_fifo()
5511            };
5512            ids[i] = self.create_sched_context(sc).map_err(|_| {
5513                super::sched_context::TimeTriggeredScheduleError::WindowCountOverflow
5514            })?;
5515        }
5516        Ok(ids)
5517    }
5518
5519    /// Phase 110.E.b — register an ISR-driven refill timer for an
5520    /// already-created Sporadic SC. The caller invokes their
5521    /// platform's `PlatformTimer::create_periodic` with the returned
5522    /// `Arc<AtomicSporadicState>` as `user_data` and the
5523    /// `atomic_sporadic_refill_thunk` as the callback, then hands
5524    /// the resulting platform handle to this method via
5525    /// `OpaqueTimerHandle::new(handle, destroy_fn)`.
5526    ///
5527    /// The Executor stores both the Arc and the handle so Drop can
5528    /// clean them up. Calling this on a non-Sporadic SC returns
5529    /// `Err(InvalidSchedContextBinding)`.
5530    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
5531    pub fn register_sporadic_timer(
5532        &mut self,
5533        sc_id: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
5534        timer: OpaqueTimerHandle,
5535    ) -> Result<portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState>, NodeError>
5536    {
5537        let i = sc_id.0 as usize;
5538        if i >= self.sched_contexts.len() {
5539            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
5540        }
5541        let sc = self.sched_contexts[i]
5542            .as_ref()
5543            .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
5544        if !matches!(sc.class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
5545            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
5546        }
5547        let budget = sc.budget_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
5548        let period = sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
5549        let state = portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState::new(
5550            budget, period,
5551        ));
5552        self.sporadic_atomic_states[i] = Some((portable_atomic_util::Arc::clone(&state), timer));
5553        Ok(state)
5554    }
5555
5556    /// Inspect a registered scheduling context. Phase 110.B.
5557    pub fn sched_context(
5558        &self,
5559        sc_id: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
5560    ) -> Option<&super::sched_context::SchedContext> {
5561        self.sched_contexts.get(sc_id.0 as usize)?.as_ref()

5629    /// Issue #52 — install the baked QoS-override table on one node. Every
5630    /// entity created on it AFTERWARDS folds the matching `(topic, role)`
5631    /// entries into its QoS, before the backend-compat check — so an override
5632    /// the active RMW cannot honour still errors loudly rather than silently
5633    /// downgrading.
5634    ///
5635    /// Called by the generated entry (`nros::main!` → the register seam) right
5636    /// after the node is created and before the component declares entities.
5637    /// Unknown `node_id` is a no-op.
5638    pub fn set_node_qos_overrides(
5639        &mut self,
5640        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
5641        overrides: &'static [super::node_record::QoSOverrideCode],
5642    ) {
5643        if let Some(r) = self.nodes.get_mut(node_id.index()) {
5644            r.qos_overrides = overrides;
5645        }
5646    }

5648    /// Phase 104.C.3 — resolve a session-slot index to a mutable
5649    /// session reference. Slot 0 = the Executor's primary session;
5650    /// slots 1..=N = the `extra_sessions` vec opened by
5651    /// `node_builder.rmw(name)` calls that named a backend
5652    /// different from the primary.
5653    pub(crate) fn session_at_mut(&mut self, idx: u8) -> Option<&mut session::ConcreteSession> {
5654        if idx == 0 {
5655            Some(&mut *self.session)
5656        } else {
5657            self.extra_sessions.get_mut((idx - 1) as usize)
5658        }
5659    }
5660
5661    /// [`Self::session_at_mut`] plus a shared borrow of the remap table, for
5662    /// building a [`NodeHandle`] — which needs both at once, and gets them
5663    /// here as two disjoint field borrows rather than through two `&mut self`
5664    /// calls the borrow checker could not split.
5665    pub(crate) fn session_and_remaps_at_mut(
5666        &mut self,
5667        idx: u8,
5668    ) -> Option<(&mut session::ConcreteSession, RemapView<'_>)> {
5669        let remaps = RemapView {
5670            launch: self
5671                .launch_remaps
5672                .unwrap_or_else(super::launch_remap::launch_remaps),
5673            runtime: &self.remap_table[..self.remap_len],
5674        };
5675        let session = if idx == 0 {
5676            Some(&mut *self.session)
5677        } else {
5678            self.extra_sessions.get_mut((idx - 1) as usize)
5679        };
5680        session.map(|s| (s, remaps))
5681    }

5683    /// Phase 104.C.9.b — resolve the per-Node session for direct
5684    /// entity creation paths (C++ FFI publisher / subscription /
5685    /// service that bypass the `register_*_on` arena dispatch).
5686    /// Returns `None` when `node_id` is out of range or the Node's
5687    /// `session_idx` lands outside the executor's session table.
5688    pub(crate) fn node_session_mut(
5689        &mut self,
5690        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
5691    ) -> Option<&mut session::ConcreteSession> {
5692        let session_idx = self.nodes.get(node_id.index())?.session_idx;
5693        self.session_at_mut(session_idx)
5694    }
