5696    /// Phase 189.M1 — create a typed publisher bound to a node's session.
5697    /// Backs `node.publisher(t).typed::<M>().build()` on the
5698    /// executor-borrowing [`Node`](super::node::Node); the returned
5699    /// handle is owned and outlives the `Node`.
5700    pub fn create_publisher_on<M: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw>(
5701        &mut self,
5702        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
5703        topic_name: &str,
5704        qos: QoSProfile,
5705    ) -> Result<crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedPublisher<M>, NodeError> {
5706        // RFC-0088 / phase-421 W1 — the message's declared format must be the
5707        // one the linked backend speaks. Universal: the const lives on
5708        // `RosMessage`, which `MessageForRmw` requires under every backend.
5709        crate::format_check::assert_message_format::<M>();
5710        // Phase 212.K.7.6.b — register `M`'s cyclonedds descriptor before
5711        // creating the underlying publisher handle. No-op for other RMWs.
5712        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<M>()?;
5713        let handle = self.create_raw_publisher_handle_on(
5714            node_id,
5715            topic_name,
5716            <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
5717            <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
5718            qos,
5719        )?;
5720        // RFC-0052 W3b.4 — attach the contracted endpoint's counter cell.
5721        let monitor = self
5722            .monitor_table
5723            .iter()
5724            .find(|m| m.topic == topic_name)
5725            .map(|m| m.cell);
5726        Ok(crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedPublisher {
5727            handle,
5728            event_regs: crate::executor::handles::empty_event_regs(),
5729            monitor,
5730            epoch: self.epoch_us_fn,
5731            _phantom: PhantomData,
5732        })
5733    }
5734
5735    /// Phase 189.M1 — create a generic (type-erased) publisher bound to a
5736    /// node's session. Backs `node.publisher(t).generic(ty, hash).build()`;
5737    /// the bridge re-publishes through this handle on the dest session.
5738    pub fn create_publisher_raw_on(
5739        &mut self,
5740        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
5741        topic_name: &str,
5742        type_name: &str,
5743        type_hash: &str,
5744        qos: QoSProfile,
5745    ) -> Result<crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedRawPublisher, NodeError> {
5746        let handle =
5747            self.create_raw_publisher_handle_on(node_id, topic_name, type_name, type_hash, qos)?;
5748        Ok(crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedRawPublisher {
5749            handle,
5750            arena: crate::executor::handles::TxArena::new(),
5751            event_regs: crate::executor::handles::empty_event_regs(),
5752            // Issue 1676 — attach the contracted endpoint's counter cell by
5753            // exact topic match against the installed table, the rule
5754            // `NodeHandle::create_publisher` applies. This is the publisher
5755            // the Rust component road creates, so without it no contracted
5756            // Rust publisher was ever counted.
5757            monitor: self.publisher_monitor_cell(topic_name),
5758        })
5759    }
5760
5761    /// Shared prelude for the publisher-on-node paths: resolve the node's
5762    /// identity + session slot, build the [`TopicInfo`], validate QoS, and
5763    /// create the backend publisher handle. Mirrors
5764    /// `register_subscription_buffered_raw_on`'s session resolution so a
5765    /// bridge's source sub + dest pub agree on topic construction.
5766    fn create_raw_publisher_handle_on(
5767        &mut self,
5768        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
5769        topic_name: &str,
5770        type_name: &str,
5771        type_hash: &str,
5772        qos: QoSProfile,
5773    ) -> Result<session::RmwPublisher, NodeError> {
5774        let (node_name, ns, session_idx, overrides) = {
5775            let r = self
5776                .nodes
5777                .get(node_id.index())
5778                .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
5779            (
5780                r.name.clone(),
5781                r.namespace.clone(),
5782                r.session_idx,
5783                r.qos_overrides,
5784            )
5785        };
5786        // Issue #52 — fold the node's baked overrides for this topic BEFORE
5787        // `validate_against`, so an override the backend cannot honour errors
5788        // loudly instead of being silently dropped.
5789        let qos = super::node_record::apply_qos_override_codes(
5790            qos,
5791            topic_name,
5792            nros_rmw::QoSOverrideRole::Publisher,
5793            overrides,
5794        );
5795        let mut topic = TopicInfo::new(topic_name, type_name, type_hash)
5796            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
5797            .with_namespace(&ns);
5798        if !node_name.is_empty() {
5799            topic = topic.with_node_name(&node_name);
5800        }
5801        // issue 1608 -- the publisher half of the declared-QoS check, before
5802        // validation so a policy the contract raises this publisher to is one
5803        // the backend is asked about. See `declared_qos::honour_publisher`.
5804        let qos = crate::declared_qos::honour_publisher(topic.type_name, topic.name, qos)?;
5805        let session = self
5806            .session_at_mut(session_idx)
5807            .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
5808        super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
5809            &qos,
5810            Session::supported_qos_policies(session),
5811            "publisher",
5812            topic_name,
5813        )?;
5814        session
5815            .create_publisher(&topic, qos)
5816            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::PublisherCreationFailed))
5817    }
5818
5819    /// Phase 124.B.1 — install the executor's wake callback onto the
5820    /// primary session. Best-effort: backends that don't override
5821    /// `Session::set_wake_callback` (poll-only XRCE, bare-metal)
5822    /// ignore the call and continue to be drained on the executor's
5823    /// deadline-bound cv-wait boundary.
5824    ///
5825    /// `pub` for issue 1385, and for the same reason
5826    /// [`set_primary_identity`](Self::set_primary_identity) is: the three
5827    /// `Executor::open*` paths call this automatically, and a binding that
5828    /// builds its executor over a session it BORROWS
5829    /// ([`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in)) reaches none of
5830    /// them, so it has to call it itself. `rclc_executor_init` is that
5831    /// binding, and until 1385 it did not — leaving `has_async_wake` false
5832    /// for the life of every C executor on every backend.
5833    ///
5834    /// Pairs with `clear_wake_signal`, which the
5835    /// executor runs from `close()` and from `drop`. A caller that installs
5836    /// owes nothing further: the teardown is the executor's.
5837    ///
5838    /// phase-436 — the backend's slot holds a `WakeFanout`
5839    /// and this executor JOINS it, so every executor over one session is woken
5840    /// by an arrival: the boot executor and each spawned tier
5841    /// (`open_with_session*` now installs too), or several C executors over
5842    /// one support context. Idempotent. If the fan-out pool is exhausted the
5843    /// executor installs its own context directly, as before; if the entry's
5844    /// member table is full it joins nothing and reads as having no async
5845    /// wake, so it never parks on a wake nobody will signal.
5846    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
5847    pub(crate) fn install_wake_signal_on_primary(&mut self) {
5848        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
5849        if self.wake_membership.is_some() {
5850            return;
5851        }
5852        let ctx = self.wake_ctx_ptr();
5853        let key = self.session_ptr() as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
5854        let supports = self.session.supports_wake_callback();
5855        let fanout = match super::wake_fanout::find(key) {
5856            Some(f) => Some(f),
5857            None => super::wake_fanout::claim(key).inspect(|f| {
5858                f.set_live(supports);
5859                // SAFETY: the context is a `static` pool entry, valid for the
5860                // program's life; `clear_wake_signal` takes the callback off
5861                // before returning the entry to the pool.
5862                unsafe {
5863                    self.session
5864                        .set_wake_callback(Some(nros_rmw_fanout_wake_cb), f.as_ctx());
5865                }
5866            }),
5867        };
5868        match fanout {
5869            Some(f) => {
5870                if let Some(m) = f.join(ctx) {
5871                    self.wake_membership = Some(m);
5872                    // Issue 1385 — this executor now owes a teardown: leaving
5873                    // the fan-out (and, for the session's owner or its last
5874                    // member, taking the callback off the backend).
5875                    self.wake_cb_installed = true;
5876                }
5877            }
5878            None => {
5879                // SAFETY: `ctx` points at executor-owned wake state that
5880                // outlives the installation and is cleared by
5881                // `clear_wake_signal` on `close()`/drop.
5882                unsafe {
5883                    self.session
5884                        .set_wake_callback(Some(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb), ctx);
5885                }
5886                self.wake_cb_installed = true;
5887                if supports {
5888                    self.has_async_wake = true;
5889                }
5890            }
5891        }
5892    }
5893
5894    /// phase-436 — does an arrival on any of this executor's sessions signal
5895    /// its wake object? Through the primary's fan-out (live until the
5896    /// session's owner takes the callback down), or a direct install on the
5897    /// primary or an extra session.
5898    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
5899    pub(crate) fn async_wake_live(&self) -> bool {
5900        self.has_async_wake || self.wake_membership.is_some_and(|m| m.is_live())
5901    }
5902
5903    /// Phase 124.B.1 — install the wake callback onto an extra
5904    /// session opened by `node_builder.rmw(...)`. Called from
5905    /// `NodeBuilder::build()` right after `extra_sessions.push(...)`.
5906    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
5907    pub(crate) fn install_wake_signal_on_extra(&mut self, idx: usize) {
5908        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
5909        let ctx = self.wake_ctx_ptr();
5910        if let Some(s) = self.extra_sessions.get_mut(idx) {
5911            // SAFETY: same executor-owned wake state as the primary session;
5912            // the extra session is owned by this executor.
5913            unsafe {
5914                s.set_wake_callback(Some(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb), ctx);
5915            }
5916            // Issue 1385 — as on the primary.
5917            self.wake_cb_installed = true;
5918            if s.supports_wake_callback() {
5919                self.has_async_wake = true;
5920            }
5921        }
5922    }
5923
5924    /// Issue 1385 — the teardown half of `install_wake_signal_on_*`, and the
5925    /// obligation `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`'s own SAFETY comment has asserted
5926    /// since phase 124: *"Executor::drop must clear the callback via
5927    /// `set_wake_callback(None, _)` on all sessions before dropping
5928    /// wake_ctx"*. Nothing did. The string `set_wake_callback(None` occurred
5929    /// exactly once in the tree — in that comment.
5930    ///
5931    /// The context the backend holds is `Arc::as_ptr(&self.wake_ctx)`, freed
5932    /// with this executor. Leaving it installed is a dangling callback the
5933    /// backend may invoke from a worker thread or an ISR. On the Rust `open*`
5934    /// paths the session is `SessionStore::Owned` and dies in the same drop,
5935    /// so the window is narrow; on the C path it is arbitrary —
5936    /// `rclc_executor_fini` drops the executor and zero-fills `_opaque` while
5937    /// the session lives on in `rclc_support_t` until `rclc_support_fini`.
5938    ///
5939    /// Clears the primary and every extra session, then latches off, so
5940    /// `close()` followed by drop clears once.
5941    ///
5942    /// Only fires when THIS executor installed (see
5943    /// `install_wake_signal_on_primary`). Executors sharing one session were
5944    /// last-writer-wins on the backend's single slot until phase-436: the first
5945    /// to tear down cleared the other's wake. The slot now holds a wake
5946    /// fan-out, so a member's teardown is leaving it, and the callback comes
5947    /// off the backend only with the session's owner or its last member.
5948    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
5949    pub(crate) fn clear_wake_signal(&mut self) {
5950        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
5951        if !self.wake_cb_installed {
5952            return;
5953        }
5954        self.wake_cb_installed = false;
5955        // phase-436 — a fan-out member leaves first; the callback comes off
5956        // the backend only when the session's OWNER leaves (the session dies
5957        // with it) or the last member does. A membership from an entry the
5958        // owner already released is a no-op, and must not touch the entry's
5959        // next tenant.
5960        let take_off_primary = match self.wake_membership.take() {
5961            Some(m) => {
5962                let fanout = m.fanout();
5963                let current = m.is_current();
5964                m.leave(nros_platform_api::yield_now);
5965                let owned = matches!(self.session, SessionStore::Owned(_));
5966                if current && (owned || fanout.member_count() == 0) {
5967                    // SAFETY: as below; the entry is released only after the
5968                    // backend can no longer start a callback on it.
5969                    unsafe { self.session.set_wake_callback(None, core::ptr::null_mut()) };
5970                    fanout.release(nros_platform_api::yield_now);
5971                }
5972                false
5973            }
5974            None => true,
5975        };
5976        // SAFETY: clearing takes no context, and both sessions are still live
5977        // here — this runs BEFORE `Session::close` in `close()` and before the
5978        // session field is dropped in `Drop`.
5979        unsafe {
5980            if take_off_primary {
5981                self.session.set_wake_callback(None, core::ptr::null_mut());
5982            }
5983            for s in self.extra_sessions.iter_mut() {
5984                s.set_wake_callback(None, core::ptr::null_mut());
5985            }
5986        }
5987        self.has_async_wake = false;
5988    }
5989
5990    /// phase-467 Row 8 — hand the PRIMARY session a graph-change target it may
5991    /// trigger from a worker thread, and take ownership of that target.
5992    ///
5993    /// The install half of the pair; [`clear_graph_change_signal`] is the
5994    /// other and the executor owes it. `guard` is CLONED, so the caller keeps
5995    /// its own handle to the same arena flag — that is the whole point: the
5996    /// pointer the backend receives is the executor's box, never the caller's
5997    /// storage. Issue 1385 is the same hazard on the wake slot, found after
5998    /// the fact; this is the shape that cannot reach it.
5999    ///
6000    /// PRIMARY only, deliberately. A graph is a property of a session, and the
6001    /// extra sessions of `node_builder.rmw(...)` each have their own — feeding
6002    /// several into one guard would make "the graph changed" unattributable
6003    /// while costing the caller the ability to ask which. A caller wanting a
6004    /// second backend's graph asks that session for its own.
6005    ///
6006    /// Returns `Err(Unsupported)` from a backend with no graph. A previously
6007    /// installed target is retired first, so an executor never has two.
6008    ///
6009    /// [`clear_graph_change_signal`]: Self::clear_graph_change_signal
6010    ///
6011    /// `pub(crate)`, not `pub`: the public verb is
6012    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`], which does the probe, the
6013    /// registration and this in the one order that cannot hand back a guard
6014    /// nothing fires. Exposing the install alone would let a caller reach the
6015    /// second step without the first.
6016    ///
6017    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`]: Self::register_graph_change_guard_on
6018    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
6019    pub(crate) fn install_graph_change_guard(
6020        &mut self,
6021        guard: &GuardCondition,
6022    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
6023        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
6024        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
6025        let boxed = alloc::boxed::Box::new(guard.clone());
6026        let ptr = (&*boxed) as *const GuardCondition as *const core::ffi::c_void;
6027        // SAFETY: `ptr` names heap storage this executor owns and which
6028        // `clear_graph_change_signal` retires from the backend before it is
6029        // freed. `GuardCondition` is `Send + Sync` and its `trigger()` is a
6030        // relaxed store plus the runtime wake hook, which is what a foreign
6031        // thread is allowed to do here.
6032        let rc = unsafe {
6033            self.session
6034                .set_graph_change_callback(Some(nros_rmw_runtime_graph_change_cb), ptr)
6035        };
6036        match rc {
6037            Ok(()) => {
6038                self.graph_change_target = Some(boxed);
6039                Ok(())
6040            }
6041            // `boxed` drops here, and nothing holds its pointer: the backend
6042            // either refused or failed, so there is no installed callback to
6043            // retire first.
6044            Err(e) => Err(NodeError::Transport(e)),
6045        }
6046    }
6047
6048    /// phase-467 Row 8 — can the primary session deliver a graph-change edge?
6049    ///
6050    /// Asked by CLEARING, which is the one probe that costs nothing and cannot
6051    /// lie: a backend with no graph answers `Unsupported` to a `None` install
6052    /// just as it does to a real one, and an idempotent clear on a backend
6053    /// that HAS a graph is a no-op. Nullity of the vtable slot cannot answer
6054    /// it — `rust_adapter.rs` fills the slot for every Rust backend whether or
6055    /// not that backend overrides the trait method, which
6056    /// `check-rmw-slot-producers`'s own report says in as many words.
6057    ///
6058    /// The caller is `register_graph_change_guard_on`, which asks BEFORE it
6059    /// consumes an executor handle slot, so an unsupported backend costs
6060    /// nothing and the caller is never handed a guard nothing fires.
6061    /// `pub(crate)` for the same reason the install is: asking costs a CLEAR,
6062    /// so a caller that asks and then does nothing has silently retired a live
6063    /// target. The public verb asks once, on the caller's behalf.
6064    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
6065    pub(crate) fn supports_graph_change_callback(&mut self) -> bool {
6066        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
6067        // Retire whatever is installed first — the probe IS a clear, so doing
6068        // it without this would silently drop a live target.
6069        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
6070        // SAFETY: a `None` install takes no context and installs nothing.
6071        unsafe {
6072            self.session
6073                .set_graph_change_callback(None, core::ptr::null())
6074                .is_ok()
6075        }
6076    }
6077
6078    /// phase-467 Row 8 — the teardown half of
6079    /// [`install_graph_change_guard`](Self::install_graph_change_guard), and
6080    /// the reason that install cannot recreate issue 1385.
6081    ///
6082    /// Order is the whole content: tell the backend to stop FIRST, then drop
6083    /// the box it was pointing at. Reversed, the window between the free and
6084    /// the clear is exactly 1385's dangling callback — and on the C path that
6085    /// window is arbitrary, because the session outlives the executor.
6086    ///
6087    /// Latched on `graph_change_target.is_some()`, not on a separate flag: the
6088    /// box IS the record of having installed, so `close()` followed by drop
6089    /// clears once and an executor that never installed clears nothing. That
6090    /// is the same predicate `clear_wake_signal` needs a bool for only because
6091    /// its context is shared with `signal_fd()` and every guard condition.
6092    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
6093    pub(crate) fn clear_graph_change_signal(&mut self) {
6094        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
6095        if self.graph_change_target.is_none() {
6096            return;
6097        }
6098        // SAFETY: clearing takes no context, and the session is still live
6099        // here — this runs BEFORE `Session::close` in `close()` and before the
6100        // session field is dropped in `Drop`.
6101        unsafe {
6102            let _ = self
6103                .session
6104                .set_graph_change_callback(None, core::ptr::null());
6105        }
6106        // Only now. The backend has been told, so nothing can be holding this
6107        // pointer when it is freed.
6108        self.graph_change_target = None;
6109    }
6110
6111    /// Phase 124.B.2 — opaque context pointer the runtime wake
6112    /// callback receives. Encodes `(flag, mu, cv)` as a borrowed
6113    /// `&WakeCtx` reference; the callback decodes via
6114    /// `*const WakeCtx`.
6115    ///
6116    /// Lifetime: tied to the Executor instance. WakeCtx storage
6117    /// lives inside Executor (lazy-allocated on first install), so
6118    /// the pointer stays valid as long as the Executor is.
6119    /// Phase 124.B.7.c — POSIX signal-handler-safe wake fd.
6120    ///
6121    /// Returns a Linux `eventfd` that callers (typically POSIX
6122    /// signal handlers) can `write(fd, &1u64, 8)` to from any
6123    /// context, including signal handlers. A runtime-owned worker
6124    /// thread reads the fd and signals `wake_cv`, unblocking
6125    /// `spin_once`.
6126    ///
6127    /// The worker thread is spawned lazily on first call and
6128    /// joined on Executor drop. Linux-only and gated behind
6129    /// `feature = "signal-fd-wake"`; binaries that don't install
6130    /// signal handlers shouldn't enable it.
6131    ///
6132    /// Returns the raw fd. The Executor retains ownership; do not
6133    /// `close()` it from the caller.
6134    #[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", feature = "rmw-cffi", target_os = "linux"))]
6135    /// phase-359 W10 — was `std::io::Result`. Same values, an error type that
6136    /// does not require `std`.
6137    pub fn signal_fd(&mut self) -> Result<core::ffi::c_int, NodeError> {
6138        let ctx_ptr = self.wake_ctx_ptr() as *const WakeCtx;
6139        if self.signal_fd.is_none() {
6140            self.signal_fd = Some(WakeSignalFd::new(ctx_ptr)?);
6141        }
6142        Ok(self.signal_fd.as_ref().expect("just set").fd())
6143    }
6144
6145    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
6146    fn wake_ctx_ptr(&mut self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
6147        if self.wake_ctx.is_none() {
6148            self.wake_ctx = Some(portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(WakeCtx::new(
6149                self.wake_flag.clone(),
6150                self.node_wake.clone(),
6151            )));
6152        }
6153        let arc = self.wake_ctx.as_ref().expect("just set");
6154        portable_atomic_util::Arc::as_ptr(arc) as *mut core::ffi::c_void
6155    }
6156
6157    /// Phase 104.C.4 — apply a Node's default SchedContext to a
6158    /// freshly-registered handle. Called from every `_inner`
6159    /// register variant after the entry slot is committed. No-op
6160    /// when `node_id` is None (legacy path), when the Node is
6161    /// out of range, or when the Node's `default_sched` is the
6162    /// auto-created Fifo slot (0) which matches the executor's
6163    /// default binding already.
6164    ///
6165    /// Phase 273 (RFC-0047) — extends with an optional `group` name.
6166    /// Precedence: **group table > node default > no binding** (SC 0).
6167    /// When `group` is `Some(g)`, consults `group_sched_table` first;
6168    /// if no entry exists for `(name, namespace, g)` falls back to the
6169    /// node's `default_sched`. When `group` is `None` the group table
6170    /// is not consulted (unchanged phase-272 path).
6171    ///
6172    /// Handles can still override per-call via
6173    /// `bind_handle_to_sched_context(handle, sc_id)` post-register.
6174    pub(crate) fn apply_node_default_sched(
6175        &mut self,
6176        slot: usize,
6177        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
6178        group: Option<&str>,
6179    ) {
6180        let Some(id) = node_id else { return };
6181        // Copy name, namespace, and default_sched out so the borrow on
6182        // `self.nodes` is released before the immutable `lookup_group_sched`
6183        // borrow and the mutable `sched_context_bindings` write below.
6184        let (name, namespace, node_sc, rank) = {
6185            let Some(rec) = self.nodes.get(id.index()) else {
6186                return;
6187            };
6188            (
6189                rec.name.clone(),
6190                rec.namespace.clone(),
6191                rec.default_sched,
6192                rec.rank,
6193            )
6194        };
6195        // phase-509 P2 -- the entry dispatches at its node's rank, whatever
6196        // sched context it ends up bound to.
6197        if let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get_mut(slot) {
6198            tag.rank = rank;
6199        }
6200        // Phase 273: group table > node default.
6201        let sc = match group {
6202            Some(g) => self
6203                .lookup_group_sched(name.as_str(), namespace.as_str(), g)
6204                .unwrap_or(node_sc),
6205            None => node_sc,
6206        };
6207        if sc.0 == 0 {
6208            return;
6209        }
6210        if slot >= self.entries.len() {
6211            return;
6212        }
6213        let sc_idx = sc.0 as usize;
6214        if sc_idx >= self.sched_contexts.len() || self.sched_contexts[sc_idx].is_none() {
6215            return;
6216        }
6217        self.sched_context_bindings[slot] = sc;
6218    }
6219
6220    /// Phase 104.C.3.2 — scoped Node-handle access. The closure
6221    /// receives a [`NodeHandle`](crate::executor::NodeHandle) bound to the
6222    /// requested [`NodeId`](crate::executor::NodeId)'s
6223    /// session + identity. Use the standard `Node::create_publisher`,
6224    /// `create_subscription`, etc. APIs inside.
6225    ///
6226    /// rclcpp-aligned bridge pattern:
6227    ///
6228    /// ```ignore
6229    /// let node_in = exec.node_builder("ingress").rmw("zenoh").build()?;
6230    /// let node_out = exec.node_builder("egress").rmw("xrce").build()?;
6231    ///
6232    /// let pub_out = exec.with_node(node_out, |n| {
6233    ///     n.create_publisher::<Int32>("/fwd")
6234    /// })??;
6235    ///
6236    /// exec.with_node(node_in, |n| {
6237    ///     n.create_subscription_buffered::<Int32, _, 1024>(
6238    ///         "/src", qos(), move |m| { let _ = pub_out.publish(m); }
6239    ///     )
6240    /// })??;
6241    /// ```
6242    ///
6243    /// The closure can return any type; double-`?` unwraps the
6244    /// outer `Result<R, NodeError>` from `with_node` and the inner
6245    /// result returned by the closure.
6246    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.d — flat-Result variant of
6247    /// [`with_node`](Self::with_node). When the closure already
6248    /// returns `Result<R, NodeError>`, this avoids the double-`?`:
6249    ///
6250    /// ```ignore
6251    /// // Without `with_node_try`:
6252    /// let pub_ = exec.with_node(id, |n| n.create_publisher(...))??;
6253    ///
6254    /// // With `with_node_try`:
6255    /// let pub_ = exec.with_node_try(id, |n| n.create_publisher(...))?;
6256    /// ```
6257    pub fn with_node_try<R>(
6258        &mut self,
6259        id: super::node_record::NodeId,
6260        f: impl FnOnce(&mut NodeHandle<'_>) -> Result<R, NodeError>,
6261    ) -> Result<R, NodeError> {
6262        self.with_node(id, f)?
6263    }
6264
6265    pub fn with_node<R>(
6266        &mut self,
6267        id: super::node_record::NodeId,
6268        f: impl FnOnce(&mut NodeHandle<'_>) -> R,
6269    ) -> Result<R, NodeError> {
6270        let (name, ns, session_idx) = {
6271            let r = self
6272                .nodes
6273                .get(id.index())
6274                .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
6275            (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
6276        };
6277        let monitors = self.monitor_table;
6278        let age_monitors = self.age_table;
6279        let epoch = self.epoch_us_fn;
6280        let domain_id = self.domain_id;
6281        let (session, remaps) = self
6282            .session_and_remaps_at_mut(session_idx)
6283            .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
6284        // SAFETY: short-lived scoped reference. `Node::new` takes
6285        // `&mut ConcreteSession`; lifetime is bound to this fn's
6286        // body via the closure's borrow of `node`.
6287        // issue 0801 (second half) — the executor's domain, NOT a literal 0.
6288        // 429d5a581 fixed the ELEVEN arena `TopicInfo`s and left the THREE
6289        // `NodeHandle::new` sites, so an entity created through a node HANDLE
6290        // (`with_node`, `node`, `node_on`) still declared on domain 0 while the
6291        // arena path declared on the configured one. Same split the issue is
6292        // about, one constructor over: `loan_e2e` publishes through a handle and
6293        // subscribes through the arena, so it delivered on domain 0 and on
6294        // nothing else.
6295        let mut node = NodeHandle::new(name, ns, session, remaps, domain_id);
6296        // RFC-0052 W3b.4/.5 — seed the baked monitor tables so contracted
6297        // publishers/subscribers attach their cells without entry glue.
6298        node.set_monitors(monitors);
6299        node.set_age_monitors(age_monitors, epoch);
6300        Ok(f(&mut node))
6301    }
6302
6303    /// Find a registered executor node by final name and namespace.
6304    pub fn node_id_by_name(
6305        &self,
6306        name: &str,
6307        namespace: &str,
6308    ) -> Option<super::node_record::NodeId> {
6309        self.nodes
6310            .iter()
6311            .enumerate()
6312            .find(|(_, node)| node.name.as_str() == name && node.namespace.as_str() == namespace)
6313            .map(|(index, _)| super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(index as u8))
6314    }
6315
6316    /// Create a node on this executor.
6317    ///
6318    /// Registers the node in the executor's table, deduplicating on
6319    /// `(name, namespace)` — phase-376 W5/B1.
6320    ///
6321    /// # This is `rclrs::Executor::create_node`
6322    ///
6323    /// phase-427 W10 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled"). Same name, same
6324    /// place in the sequence — `Context` → executor → node — so a ported rclrs
6325    /// `main` lands here unchanged:
6326    ///
6327    /// ```ignore
6328    /// let context = nros::Context::default_from_env()?;
6329    /// let mut executor = context.create_executor()?;
6330    /// let mut node = executor.create_node("talker")?;
6331    /// ```
6332    ///
6333    /// Two differences from upstream, both structural and both named in the
6334    /// ledger row (`rust:Executor::create_node`): ours takes `&mut self`,
6335    /// because the node is registered in the executor's compile-time-sized
6336    /// table rather than allocated, and it hands back a borrowing
6337    /// [`NodeHandle`] rather than an `Arc<Node>`, because there is no
6338    /// allocator. Neither is silent — the compiler names both.
6339    ///
6340    /// The name comes from HERE, not from
6341    /// [`ExecutorConfig::node_name`](crate::ExecutorConfig::node_name), whose
6342    /// builder spelling is deprecated for exactly this reason: one executor
6343    /// holds several named nodes (RFC-0047), so a name on the session config
6344    /// can only ever describe the first of them.
6345    ///
6346    /// Until 2026-08-24 this path registered NOTHING. It built a `NodeHandle`
6347    /// and returned it, so `node_id_by_name` could not find a node the caller
6348    /// had just created, and two calls with one name handed out two handles the
6349    /// executor had never heard of. `create_node_on_with_domain` had the dedup
6350    /// (phase-267 added it there when N bridge endpoints overflowed the table);
6351    /// the plain path never got it.
6352    ///
6353    /// That is a prerequisite for the `create_node` vtable slot, whose contract
6354    /// is that the runtime calls it ONCE per distinct `(name, namespace)`:
6355    /// without a registry to check, the runtime would call it once per
6356    /// `create_node` and every backend would need its own dedup — which is the
6357    /// registry the slot exists to delete (zenoh's `ensure_node_liveliness`
6358    /// linear-scans `per_node_liveliness` for exactly this reason).
6359    ///
6360    /// The table is bounded by `MAX_NODES` (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES`, default
6361    /// 4), so a caller creating a fifth DISTINCT node now gets
6362    /// `NodeError::NodeTableFull` where it previously got a handle. That is the
6363    /// bound doing its job: a node the executor does not know about cannot
6364    /// carry a sched context, a QoS override, or a graph identity. Repeated
6365    /// calls with the SAME name are free.
6366    ///
6367    /// phase-515 R2 -- takes rclrs's `impl IntoNodeOptions`: a bare name
6368    /// (`create_node("talker")`) or a [`NodeOptions`](crate::NodeOptions)
6369    /// (`create_node("talker".namespace("/robot"))`). Here the options'
6370    /// DEFAULTS mean "the executor's": namespace `/` places the node in the
6371    /// executor's own namespace and domain `0` on its own session, as a bare
6372    /// name always did. A non-default value is applied, so an explicit `/`
6373    /// under an executor configured with another namespace, or an explicit
6374    /// domain 0 under another domain, is not expressible here; open a node on
6375    /// another domain with [`create_node_on_with_domain`](Self::create_node_on_with_domain).
6376    pub fn create_node<'o>(
6377        &mut self,
6378        options: impl crate::IntoNodeOptions<'o>,
6379    ) -> Result<super::node::Node<'_, 's>, NodeError> {
6380        let options = options.into_node_options();
6381        let name = options.name;
6382        if name.len() > 64 {
6383            return Err(NodeError::NameTooLong);
6384        }
6385        let namespace = (options.namespace != "/").then_some(options.namespace);
6386        // Dedup against the namespace the node lands in -- the executor's
6387        // own when none is named, which is what `node_builder` gives it.
6388        // phase-483 W2: this returns THE node type (`Node`, re-exported as
6389        // `nros::Node`), the same handle `node_mut` gives a component, where
6390        // it used to return a session-borrowing `NodeHandle` with a different
6391        // method set.
6392        let lookup_ns = match namespace {
6393            Some(ns) => heapless::String::<64>::try_from(ns).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?,
6394            None => self.namespace.clone(),
6395        };
6396        let id = match self.node_id_by_name(name, lookup_ns.as_str()) {
6397            Some(id) => id,
6398            None => {
6399                let mut builder = self.node_builder(name);
6400                if let Some(ns) = namespace {
6401                    builder = builder.namespace(ns);
6402                }
6403                if options.domain_id != 0 {
6404                    builder = builder.domain_id(options.domain_id);
6405                }
6406                builder.build()?
6407            }
6408        };
6409        Ok(super::node::Node::new(self, id))
6410    }
6411
6412    /// Phase 128.F.2 — bridge-mode node factory. Registers a Node
6413    /// bound to the named RMW backend by opening (or reusing) an
6414    /// extra session via `node_builder().rmw(rmw).build()`, then
6415    /// returns a [`NodeHandle`](crate::executor::NodeHandle) borrowing that
6416    /// session. Use when the
6417    /// binary intentionally links more than one backend and a Node
6418    /// must speak a specific one.
6419    ///
6420    /// The single-backend common case should keep using
6421    /// [`create_node`](Self::create_node) — this entry costs an
6422    /// extra session lookup and serves no purpose when only one
6423    /// backend is registered.
6424    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
6425    pub fn create_node_on(
6426        &mut self,
6427        name: &str,
6428        rmw: &str,
6429    ) -> Result<super::node::Node<'_, 's>, NodeError> {
6430        self.create_node_on_with_domain(name, rmw, None, None)
6431    }
6432
6433    /// Like [`create_node_on`](Self::create_node_on) but pins the extra
6434    /// session's domain id. Required for a multi-domain config-driven bridge:
6435    /// an extra RMW session's participant domain follows the **node builder's**
6436    /// `domain_id` (`resolve_session_slot` → `domain_id.unwrap_or(0)`), NOT the
6437    /// `SessionSpec`'s — so without this an egress on a non-zero domain silently
6438    /// opens on domain 0 and never matches its receiver (phase-267 issue 0109).
6439    /// `None` domain preserves the legacy domain-0 default. `locator` pins the
6440    /// extra session's address — REQUIRED for an agent-based backend (xrce: the
6441    /// Micro-XRCE-DDS Agent addr) whose session can't be opened locator-less;
6442    /// `None` keeps the rmw-default (cyclonedds is domain-discovered, no locator).
6443    pub fn create_node_on_with_domain(
6444        &mut self,
6445        name: &str,
6446        rmw: &str,
6447        domain_id: Option<u32>,
6448        locator: Option<&str>,
6449    ) -> Result<super::node::Node<'_, 's>, NodeError> {
6450        if name.len() > 64 {
6451            return Err(NodeError::NameTooLong);
6452        }
6453        // Reuse an existing Node of this name rather than growing the node table
6454        // (phase-267 non-flat): a config-driven bridge calls this once per bridge
6455        // ENDPOINT, and the same session node (`s0`/`s1`) recurs across every
6456        // `[[bridge]]`. Without dedup, N bridges push 2N records and overflow
6457        // `MAX_NODES`. Names are unique per session in a generated bridge config,
6458        // so matching by name is unambiguous.
6459        let id = if let Some(i) = self.nodes.iter().position(|n| n.name.as_str() == name) {
6460            super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(i as u8)
6461        } else {
6462            let mut builder = self.node_builder(name).rmw(rmw);
6463            if let Some(d) = domain_id {
6464                builder = builder.domain_id(d);
6465            }
6466            if let Some(loc) = locator {
6467                builder = builder.locator(loc);
6468            }
6469            builder.build()?
6470        };
6471        Ok(super::node::Node::new(self, id))
6472    }

6474    /// Drive transport I/O (poll network, dispatch callbacks).
6475    #[allow(dead_code)]
6476    pub(crate) fn drive_io(&mut self, timeout_ms: i32) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
6477        self.session
6478            .drive_io(timeout_ms)
6479            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::PollFailed))
6480    }
6481
6482    /// Close the underlying session, running the shutdown hooks around it.
6483    ///
6484    /// Issue 0790. The order is the feature:
6485    ///
6486    /// 1. every registered PRE-shutdown hook, while the session is still open
6487    ///    and every entity still works — this is where a node publishes a final
6488    ///    state, answers a last request, parks an actuator or releases a bus;
6489    /// 2. the session close;
6490    /// 3. every registered ON-shutdown hook.
6491    ///
6492    /// A hook runs EXACTLY ONCE: each phase table is emptied before its first
6493    /// hook is invoked, so a second `close()` — or the [`Drop`] sweep after one
6494    /// — finds nothing left to run. Step 2 runs even
6495    /// if a pre-shutdown hook was registered and step 3 even if the close
6496    /// failed — a hook cannot strand the session, and a dead session must not
6497    /// strand the hooks.
6498    ///
6499    /// # This is a CLEAN-STOP facility and nothing more
6500    ///
6501    /// A watchdog reset, a hard fault or a panic does not come through here, so
6502    /// these hooks do not run then. Nothing in a fixed static table can promise
6503    /// otherwise, and an API that implied it would be worse than none: hardware
6504    /// that must be safe across an abnormal stop needs a hardware answer (a
6505    /// pull-down, a watchdog-driven output disable), not a callback.
6506    pub fn close(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
6507        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre);
6508        // Issue 1385 — hand the callback back BEFORE closing the session that
6509        // holds it. `close()` leaves the executor alive, so without this a
6510        // later `set_wake_callback` from the drop sweep would reach a session
6511        // the backend has already torn down.
6512        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
6513        self.clear_wake_signal();
6514        // phase-467 Row 8 — the same obligation on the graph-change slot, and
6515        // it has to be discharged in the same place for the same reason.
6516        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
6517        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
6518        let result = self
6519            .session
6520            .close()
6521            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed));
6522        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post);
6523        result
6524    }
6525
6526    /// Register a hook to run BEFORE the session is closed (issue 0790).
6527    ///
6528    /// rclcpp's `Context::add_pre_shutdown_callback`. Returns the handle
6529    /// [`Self::remove_pre_shutdown_callback`] takes, or
6530    /// [`NodeError::ShutdownCallbacksFull`] when the phase table is full —
6531    /// raise `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS` (default 2) at build time.
6532    ///
6533    /// # Safety
6534    /// `callback` must be safe to invoke exactly once with `context`, and
6535    /// `context` must stay valid until the hook runs or is removed. The hook
6536    /// runs on whichever task calls [`Self::close`] (or drops the executor),
6537    /// which is not necessarily the task that registered it.
6538    pub(crate) unsafe fn add_pre_shutdown_callback(
6539        &mut self,
6540        callback: super::types::ShutdownCallbackFn,
6541        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6542    ) -> Result<super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle, NodeError> {
6543        Self::claim_shutdown_slot(
6544            &mut self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
6545            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre,
6546            callback,
6547            context,
6548        )
6549    }
6550
6551    /// Register a hook to run AFTER the session is closed (issue 0790).
6552    ///
6553    /// rclcpp's `Context::add_on_shutdown_callback` / `rclcpp::on_shutdown`.
6554    /// Entities are gone by the time it runs, so anything that needs the wire
6555    /// belongs in [`Self::add_pre_shutdown_callback`] instead.
6556    ///
6557    /// # Safety
6558    /// Same contract as [`Self::add_pre_shutdown_callback`].
6559    pub(crate) unsafe fn add_on_shutdown_callback(
6560        &mut self,
6561        callback: super::types::ShutdownCallbackFn,
6562        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6563    ) -> Result<super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle, NodeError> {
6564        Self::claim_shutdown_slot(
6565            &mut self.on_shutdown_hooks,
6566            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post,
6567            callback,
6568            context,
6569        )
6570    }
6571
6572    /// Remove a pre-shutdown hook. `true` if `handle` named a live one.
6573    ///
6574    /// rclcpp's `Context::remove_pre_shutdown_callback`, and `bool` for the
6575    /// same reason: "it was not there" is an ordinary answer (the hook may
6576    /// already have run), not an error. A handle issued for the OTHER phase
6577    /// returns `false` and removes nothing — that is what the phase tag in
6578    /// [`ShutdownCallbackHandle`] buys.
6579    ///
6580    /// [`ShutdownCallbackHandle`]: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle
6581    pub(crate) fn remove_pre_shutdown_callback(
6582        &mut self,
6583        handle: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle,
6584    ) -> bool {
6585        Self::release_shutdown_slot(
6586            &mut self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
6587            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre,
6588            handle,
6589        )
6590    }
6591
6592    /// Remove an on-shutdown hook. See [`Self::remove_pre_shutdown_callback`].
6593    pub(crate) fn remove_on_shutdown_callback(
6594        &mut self,
6595        handle: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle,
6596    ) -> bool {
6597        Self::release_shutdown_slot(
6598            &mut self.on_shutdown_hooks,
6599            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post,
6600            handle,
6601        )
6602    }
6603
6604    /// How many hooks are currently registered for `phase`. Diagnostic /
6605    /// test surface, and what a "did my registration land?" assertion reads.
6606    pub fn shutdown_callback_count(&self, phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase) -> usize {
6607        let table = match phase {
6608            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre => &self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
6609            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post => &self.on_shutdown_hooks,
6610        };
6611        table.iter().flatten().count()
6612    }
6613
6614    /// Claim the first free slot of a phase table.
6615    fn claim_shutdown_slot(
6616        table: &mut [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>],
6617        phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase,
6618        callback: super::types::ShutdownCallbackFn,
6619        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6620    ) -> Result<super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle, NodeError> {
6621        for (index, slot) in table.iter_mut().enumerate() {
6622            if slot.is_some() {
6623                continue;
6624            }
6625            let handle = super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle::new(phase, index)
6626                .ok_or(NodeError::ShutdownCallbacksFull)?;
6627            *slot = Some(super::types::ShutdownHook { callback, context });
6628            return Ok(handle);
6629        }
6630        Err(NodeError::ShutdownCallbacksFull)
6631    }
6632
6633    /// Clear a slot of a phase table, rejecting a handle from the other phase.
6634    fn release_shutdown_slot(
6635        table: &mut [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>],
6636        phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase,
6637        handle: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle,
6638    ) -> bool {
6639        if handle.phase() != Some(phase) {
6640            return false;
6641        }
6642        match table.get_mut(handle.index()) {
6643            Some(slot) => slot.take().is_some(),
6644            None => false,
6645        }
6646    }
6647
6648    /// Run — and consume — every hook registered for `phase`, in registration
6649    /// order.
6650    ///
6651    /// The table is EMPTIED BEFORE the first callback runs, not slot by slot as
6652    /// the loop walks it, and both halves of that matter:
6653    ///
6654    /// * "exactly once" becomes a property of the table rather than of the
6655    ///   caller — a second `close()`, or the `Drop` sweep after one, finds
6656    ///   nothing left to run;
6657    /// * the `&mut self` borrow ENDS before any foreign code is invoked. A hook
6658    ///   is an `extern "C" fn` that may hold a raw pointer back to this
6659    ///   executor (the C and C++ shims hand out exactly that), so a hook that
6660    ///   registers or removes another one must not be running inside a live
6661    ///   `&mut` into the table it is touching.
6662    pub(crate) fn run_shutdown_hooks(&mut self, phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase) {
6663        let table = match phase {
6664            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre => &mut self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
6665            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post => &mut self.on_shutdown_hooks,
6666        };
6667        // `ShutdownHook` is `Copy` (a fn pointer and a raw pointer), so this is
6668        // a register-width move of a table whose default size is two slots —
6669        // not a reason to keep the borrow open across the calls.
6670        let hooks = *table;
6671        *table = [None; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS];
6672        for hook in hooks.iter().flatten() {
6673            // SAFETY: the `add_*_shutdown_callback` caller promised `callback`
6674            // is safe to invoke once with `context`, and that `context` stays
6675            // valid until the hook runs or is removed. This is that one call,
6676            // and the table is already cleared so it cannot happen again.
6677            unsafe {
6678                (hook.callback)(hook.context);
6679            }
6680        }
6681    }

6683    /// Phase 216 follow-up — register a per-Node dispatch trampoline.
6684    ///
6685    /// The board-side Entry pkg (or the macro-emitted
6686    /// `register_dispatch(executor)` wrapper, once wired) calls this
6687    /// once per deployed Node pkg, handing in the
6688    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` symbol + the Node's per-pkg
6689    /// `state` blob. [`Executor::dispatch_callback`] then linear-scans
6690    /// the registered slots when the dispatch task hands off a
6691    /// `SignaledCallback`.
6692    ///
6693    /// Returns `Err(())` when the registry is full (`MAX_NODES`
6694    /// entries — raise via `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES` at build time).
6695    ///
6696    /// # Safety
6697    ///
6698    /// `state` must outlive the executor (the typical shape is a
6699    /// `*mut State` produced by
6700    /// `nros::__macro::__private_node_state_into_raw` from the
6701    /// macro-emitted `i()`; that pointer's lifetime IS the
6702    /// `Executor`'s by construction). `on_callback` must be safe to
6703    /// invoke with `(state, cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len, ctx)` matching the
6704    /// per-Node `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` ABI emitted by the
6705    /// `nros::node!()` macro (Phase 216.A.5).
6706    #[doc(hidden)]
6707    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
6708    pub fn register_dispatch_slot(
6709        &mut self,
6710        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6711        on_callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(
6712            *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6713            *const u8,
6714            usize,
6715            *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6716        ),
6717    ) -> Result<(), ()> {
6718        self.dispatch_slots
6719            .push(DispatchSlot { state, on_callback })
6720            .map_err(|_| ())
6721    }

6723    /// Phase 216 follow-up — current registered dispatch-slot count.

6726    pub fn dispatch_slot_count(&self) -> usize {
6727        self.dispatch_slots.len()
6728    }

6730    /// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — enroll a component into the executor-owned
6731    /// tick registry. Called by `nros`'s `install`/`register_node_borrowed`
6732    /// after it builds the `Arc<ComponentCell>`: `state` is the leaked
6733    /// `Arc<ComponentCell>` (the slot takes ownership), `tick`/`drop` are the
6734    /// `nros`-side trampolines (see `ComponentSlot`). The slot's `tick`
6735    /// runs at the tail of every [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once); its `drop`
6736    /// runs once on `Executor::drop`. Issue 2020 -- on an executor whose
6737    /// levels own their slots, the component belongs to the registering
6738    /// level, and only that level's pass ticks it.
6739    ///
6740    /// Returns `Err(())` when the registry is full (`MAX_NODES` — raise via
6741    /// `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES` at build time). On error the caller still
6742    /// owns `state` (the slot was not stored) and must drop it.
6743    ///
6744    /// # Safety
6745    /// `state` must be a `*mut` produced by leaking the component cell the
6746    /// `tick`/`drop` trampolines expect (an `Arc<ComponentCell>` via
6747    /// `Arc::into_raw` in the canonical `nros` caller), and must remain valid
6748    /// until the matching `drop` runs. `tick` must be safe to invoke with
6749    /// `(state, exec_ctx = *mut Executor)` each spin; `drop` must be safe to
6750    /// invoke exactly once with `state`.
6751    #[doc(hidden)]
6752    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
6753    pub unsafe fn enroll_component(
6754        &mut self,
6755        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
6756        tick: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void, *mut core::ffi::c_void),
6757        drop: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
6758    ) -> Result<(), ()> {
6759        let level = self.worker.registering_level;
6760        self.component_slots
6761            .push(ComponentSlot {
6762                state,
6763                tick,
6764                drop,
6765                level,
6766            })
6767            .map_err(|_| ())
6768    }

6770    /// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — current enrolled component-slot count.

6773    pub fn component_slot_count(&self) -> usize {
6774        self.component_slots.len()
6775    }

6777    /// issue #140 — the enrolled components' opaque `state` pointers, in enroll
6778    /// order. Each is the *leaked* `Arc<ComponentCell>` `enroll_component` was
6779    /// handed (see `ComponentSlot::state`); the `nros` layer re-borrows them
6780    /// to fold per-component dispatch counters into
6781    /// `observed_callback_counts` — install-seam components
6782    /// (`register_node_borrowed`) live ONLY here, not in
6783    /// `ExecutorNodeRuntime::components`, so the hosted-spin counts read zero
6784    /// without this surface.
6785    #[doc(hidden)]
6786    pub fn enrolled_component_states(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = *mut core::ffi::c_void> + '_ {
6787        self.component_slots.iter().map(|slot| slot.state)
6788    }
6789
6790    /// Phase 216 final dispatch hook — stable entry point the
6791    /// framework's dispatch task (RTIC `__nros_run` /
6792    /// Embassy `__nros_run_task`) calls for each `SignaledCallback`
6793    /// envelope it dequeues from the board-side SPSC / Embassy
6794    /// channel.
6795    ///
6796    /// ## Signature shape
6797    ///
6798    /// `nros-node` sits below `nros` in the dep graph, so the typed
6799    /// `nros::CallbackId<'_>` / `nros::CallbackCtx<'_>` types
6800    /// referenced in the Phase 216 design notes cannot appear in the
6801    /// signature here. The macro emit translates the dequeued
6802    /// envelope to the layer-clean `(cb_id: &str, ctx: *mut c_void)`
6803    /// pair before calling this method; the per-Node `on_callback`
6804    /// trampoline ABI (Phase 216.A.5,
6805    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback(state, cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len,
6806    /// ctx)`) uses the same untyped shape on the other side of the
6807    /// fence, so the round-trip stays type-consistent.
6808    ///
6809    /// ## Body — linear scan of the dispatch registry
6810    ///
6811    /// Each registered `DispatchSlot` holds an
6812    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` fn pointer + the owning Node's
6813    /// `state` blob. The macro-emitted trampoline body
6814    /// `match`es on `CallbackId` tags the Node declared and is a
6815    /// no-op for non-matching `cb_id`s — at most one Node per
6816    /// `cb_id` actually acts, the rest are cheap string-compare
6817    /// no-ops. This mirrors the strategy
6818    /// `ExecutorNodeRuntime::dispatch_callback` uses in
6819    /// `packages/api/nros/src/node_runtime.rs:470`.
6820    ///
6821    /// ## What's NOT auto-wired today
6822    ///
6823    /// The `nros::node!()` macro doesn't yet emit a
6824    /// `register_dispatch(executor)` wrapper that pushes the per-pkg
6825    /// `(state, on_callback)` into this registry. Until that wiring
6826    /// lands (Phase 216 follow-up — see commit msg), downstream
6827    /// consumers (board's `init_hardware`, or the codegen-emitted
6828    /// `run_plan`) must call
6829    /// [`Executor::register_dispatch_slot`] explicitly with the
6830    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` symbol + a `state` blob from
6831    /// the macro-emitted `i()`.
6832    //
6833    // `ctx` is an opaque FFI cookie forwarded verbatim to each slot's
6834    // `on_callback`; this fn never dereferences it (the registered callback
6835    // does, under the `register_dispatch_slot` safety contract), so it is sound
6836    // to call from safe code.
6837    #[doc(hidden)]
6838    #[allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]
6839    pub fn dispatch_callback(&mut self, cb_id: &str, ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
6840        let cb_id_ptr = cb_id.as_ptr();
6841        let cb_id_len = cb_id.len();
6842        // Snapshot pointer + length to avoid an outstanding borrow
6843        // across the unsafe fn calls below; each `DispatchSlot` is
6844        // `Copy`, so iterating by value sidesteps any aliasing
6845        // worry the borrow checker would flag if a slot's
6846        // `on_callback` re-entered the executor.
6847        for slot in self.dispatch_slots.iter().copied() {
6848            // SAFETY: caller of `register_dispatch_slot` guaranteed
6849            // `state` outlives the executor + `on_callback` matches
6850            // the per-Node `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` ABI;
6851            // `cb_id_ptr`/`cb_id_len` describe the live `&str` the
6852            // caller passed in.
6853            unsafe {
6854                (slot.on_callback)(slot.state, cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len, ctx);
6855            }
6856        }
6857    }

6890    /// phase-381 W4 — every node on the graph, with its namespace.
6891    ///
6892    /// `visit(name, namespace, enclave)` is called once per node and returns
6893    /// `false` to stop early. A VISITOR rather than a returned collection
6894    /// because there is no allocator at this layer and the graph has no bound
6895    /// the caller can know; peak extra memory is one entry. Every string is
6896    /// BORROWED for the duration of the call.
6897    ///
6898    /// `enclave` is `None` where the backend does not track one, which is what
6899    /// lets one call answer both `rmw_get_node_names` and
6900    /// `rmw_get_node_names_with_enclaves`.
6901    ///
6902    /// **This reports what has already been DISCOVERED, and never blocks.** The
6903    /// first call after startup legitimately sees a partial graph — the backend
6904    /// keeps a standing query fed by `spin`, so the view fills in over
6905    /// successive calls. Code that waits for a peer should poll, not call once
6906    /// and conclude. An empty result is "nobody seen yet", never "nobody
6907    /// exists".
6908    ///
6909    /// `Err(Transport(Unsupported))` from a backend with no graph — distinct
6910    /// from an empty graph, deliberately.
6911    pub fn get_node_names(
6912        &mut self,
6913        visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&str, &str, Option<&str>) -> bool,
6914    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
6915        use nros_rmw::Session;
6916        self.session
6917            .get_node_names(visit)
6918            .map_err(NodeError::Transport)
6919    }

7100    /// phase-444 — block until at least `count` publishers are visible on
7101    /// `topic_name`, or `timeout` elapses. Upstream's `rcl_wait_for_publishers`.
7102    ///
7103    /// Returns `Ok(true)` when the graph showed at least `count` inside the
7104    /// budget, `Ok(false)` on timeout. The startup-ordering primitive one
7105    /// entity kind over from [`EmbeddedServiceClient::wait_for_service`](super::handles::EmbeddedServiceClient::wait_for_service),
7106    /// and built the same way: a spin on a discovery read, so other
7107    /// subscriptions and timers keep making progress while it waits.
7108    ///
7109    /// **This is the one blocking member of the graph family, and it does not
7110    /// weaken the family's contract — it composes it.** The query underneath
7111    /// ([`count_publishers`](Self::count_publishers)) still reports only what
7112    /// has been DISCOVERED and still never blocks; what waits is this loop,
7113    /// and it waits by POLLING that query. RFC-0021 is the rule that governs
7114    /// it, and that rule does not forbid blocking: it requires a blocking
7115    /// helper to take an executor and drive it, which is what makes the
7116    /// timeout reliable on a single-threaded transport and what makes the
7117    /// reentrancy visible at the call site.
7118    ///
7119    /// **`Unsupported` is propagated IMMEDIATELY, not waited out** — and this
7120    /// is the one place it deliberately differs from `wait_for_service`, which
7121    /// treats a backend that cannot answer as "keep waiting" and reports
7122    /// `Ok(false)` at the deadline (issue 1087). That is right for a service
7123    /// probe, where not-yet-answerable is a transient. It is wrong here: a
7124    /// backend with no graph (XRCE) can never answer, so spending the budget
7125    /// to return `Ok(false)` would report "no publishers appeared" for a
7126    /// backend that cannot see publishers at all — collapsing "cannot tell
7127    /// you" into "not there", which is exactly the distinction RFC-0036 exists
7128    /// to keep and which every other method in this family promises to keep.
7129    ///
7130    /// `count == 0` is satisfied immediately and without asking the backend —
7131    /// including on a backend with no graph, because "at least zero" is true
7132    /// of every graph and needs no discovery to establish.
7133    pub fn wait_for_publishers(
7134        &mut self,
7135        topic_name: &str,
7136        count: usize,
7137        timeout: core::time::Duration,
7138    ) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
7139        self.wait_for_endpoints(true, topic_name, count, timeout)
7140    }
7141
7142    /// phase-444 — block until at least `count` subscribers are visible on
7143    /// `topic_name`. Upstream's `rcl_wait_for_subscribers`. See
7144    /// [`wait_for_publishers`](Self::wait_for_publishers) for the contract,
7145    /// and for why `Unsupported` returns rather than waits.
7146    pub fn wait_for_subscribers(
7147        &mut self,
7148        topic_name: &str,
7149        count: usize,
7150        timeout: core::time::Duration,
7151    ) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
7152        self.wait_for_endpoints(false, topic_name, count, timeout)
7153    }
7154
7155    /// The one loop both `wait_for_*` verbs run — a shared helper rather than
7156    /// a second spelling, because the pair differs only in which counter it
7157    /// polls and a copied loop is how the two drift.
7158    fn wait_for_endpoints(
7159        &mut self,
7160        publishers: bool,
7161        topic_name: &str,
7162        count: usize,
7163        timeout: core::time::Duration,
7164    ) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
7165        if count == 0 {
7166            return Ok(true);
7167        }
7168        // `?`, not a swallow: a backend that cannot see the graph says so now.
7169        if self.count_endpoints(publishers, topic_name)? >= count {
7170            return Ok(true);
7171        }
7172        let spin_interval =
7173            core::time::Duration::from_millis(super::handles::DEFAULT_SPIN_INTERVAL_MS);
7174        let max_spins =
7175            (timeout.as_millis() as u64 / super::handles::DEFAULT_SPIN_INTERVAL_MS).max(1);
7176        let mut budget = super::handles::WaitBudget::new(max_spins, timeout);
7177        loop {
7178            self.spin_once(budget.next_spin_interval(spin_interval));
7179            if self.count_endpoints(publishers, topic_name)? >= count {
7180                return Ok(true);
7181            }
7182            if !budget.tick() {
7183                return Ok(false);
7184            }
7185        }
7186    }
7187
7188    /// Which counter a `wait_for_*` polls. Keeps the boolean's meaning in ONE
7189    /// place instead of at both call sites.
7190    fn count_endpoints(&mut self, publishers: bool, topic_name: &str) -> Result<usize, NodeError> {
7191        if publishers {
7192            self.count_publishers(topic_name)
7193        } else {
7194            self.count_subscribers(topic_name)
7195        }
7196    }

7198    /// Get a mutable reference to an action client core in the arena by entry index.
7199    ///
7200    /// # Safety
7201    /// The caller must ensure that `entry_index` refers to an `ActionClientRawArenaEntry`.
7202    #[doc(hidden)]
7203    pub(crate) unsafe fn action_client_core_mut(
7204        &mut self,
7205        entry_index: usize,
7206    ) -> Option<&mut super::action_core::ActionClientCore> {
7207        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
7208        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::ActionClient) {
7209            return None;
7210        }
7211        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7212        unsafe {
7213            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(meta.offset)
7214                as *mut super::arena::ActionClientRawArenaEntry<
7215                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
7216                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
7217                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
7218                >;
7219            Some(&mut (*entry_ptr).core)
7220        }
7221    }

7226    /// entry. The default reply buffer size is assumed because the C API
7227    /// always uses the default — the entry was registered via
7228    /// `register_service_client_raw_sized::<DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE>`.
7229    ///
7230    /// # Safety
7231    /// `entry_index` must refer to a `ServiceClientRawArenaEntry`.
7232    pub(crate) unsafe fn service_client_entry_mut(
7233        &mut self,

7235    ) -> Option<&mut super::arena::ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<{ crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE }>>
7236    {

7238        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::ServiceClient) {

7240        }
7241        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;

7251    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
7252    // issue 1437 / phase-444 — the ARENA half of the granted-QoS read-back.
7253    //
7254    // An entity registered with a callback lives in the executor arena, and
7255    // the C / C++ handle the user holds is then bookkeeping: its inline
7256    // storage is untouched and the only identity it carries is the entry
7257    // index. So an accessor that reads the user's own storage answers for
7258    // the POLL road and returns an absence on the CALLBACK road — which is
7259    // the road a ported `rclcpp` node takes, i.e. the common one. These
7260    // three close that reach.
7261    //
7262    // Each reads the entry's HANDLE and nothing else, which is why one
7263    // function per kind serves every entry SHAPE of that kind: every arena
7264    // entry is `#[repr(C)]` with its handle as the first field (12
7265    // subscription shapes, 2 service-server, 2 service-client), so
7266    // `arena_base + offset` IS the handle pointer whatever buffer sizes and
7267    // callback types the shape was monomorphised with.
7268    // `service_client_entry_mut` above has to name ONE shape because it
7269    // reaches past the handle; these do not, and that is the whole
7270    // difference. `arena::tests::every_arena_entry_begins_with_its_handle`
7271    // pins the invariant.
7272
7273    /// The `RmwSubscriber` of an arena-registered subscription, by entry index.
7274    ///
7275    /// `None` when `entry_index` names no entry, or names one that is not a
7276    /// subscription.
7277    ///
7278    /// # Safety
7279    /// `entry_index` must be an index this executor handed out. The borrow is
7280    /// valid only while the arena is not re-entered.
7281    #[doc(hidden)]
7282    pub(crate) unsafe fn subscription_handle(
7283        &self,
7284        entry_index: usize,
7285    ) -> Option<&session::RmwSubscriber> {
7286        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
7287        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription) {
7288            return None;
7289        }
7290        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
7291        // SAFETY: `meta.offset` is inside the arena by construction, and every
7292        // subscription entry shape begins with its `RmwSubscriber`.
7293        Some(unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const session::RmwSubscriber) })
7294    }
7295
7296    /// [`Executor::subscription_handle`], mutably — issue 1972: registering a
7297    /// status-event callback (`Subscription::register_event_callback`) takes
7298    /// `&mut`, and the C API's subscription is arena-owned.
7299    ///
7300    /// Issue 2060 — taking it also makes the readiness scan probe this
7301    /// subscription's `has_data` on every pass, where its backend polls the
7302    /// status events (see `entity_status_polled`).
7303    ///
7304    /// # Safety
7305    /// See [`Executor::subscription_handle`]; in addition no other borrow of
7306    /// the same entry may be live.
7307    #[doc(hidden)]
7308    pub(crate) unsafe fn subscription_handle_mut(
7309        &mut self,
7310        entry_index: usize,
7311    ) -> Option<&mut session::RmwSubscriber> {
7312        let slot = self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?;
7313        let meta = self.entries.get(slot)?.as_ref()?;
7314        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription) {
7315            return None;
7316        }
7317        let offset = meta.offset;
7318        // Issue 2060 — `&mut` to an arena subscriber's handle exists to
7319        // register a status-event callback, and those events are polled from
7320        // `has_data`: from now on the scan asks it every pass, not only after
7321        // an arrival. Marked before the registration is known to succeed; a
7322        // refused one costs one cheap probe per pass, a missed mark costs the
7323        // event.
7324        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7325        if slot < super::entity_wake::SLOTS {
7326            self.entity_status_polled |= 1u64 << slot;
7327        }
7328        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7329        // SAFETY: as `subscription_handle`; `&mut self` makes the borrow unique.
7330        Some(unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut session::RmwSubscriber) })
7331    }
7332
7333    /// The `RmwServiceServer` of an arena-registered service, by entry index.
7334    ///
7335    /// # Safety
7336    /// See [`Executor::subscription_handle`].
7337    #[doc(hidden)]
7338    pub(crate) unsafe fn service_server_handle(
7339        &self,
7340        entry_index: usize,
7341    ) -> Option<&session::RmwServiceServer> {
7342        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
7343        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Service) {
7344            return None;
7345        }
7346        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
7347        // SAFETY: as above; every service-server entry shape begins with its
7348        // `RmwServiceServer`.
7349        Some(unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const session::RmwServiceServer) })
7350    }

7352    /// The `RmwServiceClient` of an arena-registered client, by entry index.
7353    ///
7354    /// # Safety
7355    /// See [`Executor::subscription_handle`].
7356    #[doc(hidden)]
7357    pub(crate) unsafe fn service_client_handle(
7358        &self,
7359        entry_index: usize,
7360    ) -> Option<&session::RmwServiceClient> {
7361        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
7362        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::ServiceClient) {
7363            return None;
7364        }
7365        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
7366        // SAFETY: as above; both service-client entry shapes begin with their
7367        // `RmwServiceClient` — the typed one through `ServiceClientSendHeader`,
7368        // itself `#[repr(C)]` and handle-first.
7369        Some(unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const session::RmwServiceClient) })

7375    /// callbacks. Defaults to [`Trigger::AnyReady`](crate::Trigger).

7380    /// Set the executor data communication semantics.
7381    ///
7382    /// Choose between `Direct` (process in place) and `LET`
7383    /// (snapshot-then-process) semantics. See [`ExecutorSemantics`].
7384    pub fn set_semantics(&mut self, semantics: ExecutorSemantics) {

7388    /// Set the invocation mode for a specific handle.
7389    ///
7390    /// Controls whether the callback fires on every spin
7391    /// ([`Always`](InvocationMode::Always)) or only when new data
7392    /// arrives ([`OnNewData`](InvocationMode::OnNewData), the default).
7393    pub fn set_invocation(&mut self, id: HandleId, mode: InvocationMode) {
