7400    // ========================================================================
7401    // Arena-based callback registration
7402    // ========================================================================
7403
7404    /// Arena bytes claimed by registered entities so far.
7405    ///
7406    /// EXACT, not a worst case: the arena is a bump allocator and every
7407    /// `arena_alloc` charges `size_of::<T>()`, so nothing is reserved per slot.
7408    /// `ARENA_SIZE` itself is derived the other way — every slot budgeted at
7409    /// the ActionClient worst case — which is issue 0900, and this accessor is
7410    /// how an image can find out what it actually needs.
7411    pub fn arena_used(&self) -> usize {
7412        self.arena_used
7413    }
7414
7415    /// Total arena bytes this executor was given.
7416    ///
7417    /// The arena is a borrowed slice; where its storage lives is the caller's
7418    /// choice, not a property of this type. Three answers are real — a `.bss`
7419    /// static (the C/C++ entries, and the `alloc` constructors since phase-392
7420    /// W6), the heap (those constructors' fallback), and a stack-declared
7421    /// `rclc_executor_t`. See `super::backing` and `report_arena_headroom`.
7422    pub fn arena_capacity(&self) -> usize {
7423        self.arena.len()
7424    }
7425
7426    /// Bump-allocate space for `T` in the arena. Returns the byte offset.
7427    pub(crate) fn arena_alloc<T>(&mut self) -> Result<usize, NodeError> {
7428        // Issue 1667 — every region is grain-aligned and at least one free-list
7429        // node long, so it can be listed when it is released.
7430        let align = core::mem::align_of::<T>().max(ARENA_GRAIN);
7431        let size = Self::arena_region_len(core::mem::size_of::<T>());
7432        if let Some((offset, granted)) = self.arena_take_freed(size, align) {
7433            crate::boot_report::note_alloc(size, self.arena_used);
7434            self.note_entry_region(offset, granted);
7435            return Ok(offset);
7436        }
7437        let aligned_offset = (self.arena_used + align - 1) & !(align - 1);
7438        let new_used = aligned_offset + size;
7439        if new_used > self.arena.len() {
7440            // issue 0900 — `BufferTooSmall` is returned by a dozen other paths,
7441            // so on a target where a return code is all you get, arena
7442            // exhaustion is indistinguishable from a message that did not fit.
7443            return Err(self.arena_exhausted(
7444                core::any::type_name::<T>(),
7445                size,
7446                new_used - self.arena.len(),
7447            ));
7448        }
7449        self.arena_used = new_used;
7450        crate::boot_report::note_alloc(size, new_used);
7451        self.note_entry_region(aligned_offset, size);
7452        Ok(aligned_offset)
7453    }
7454
7455    /// Issue 1631 — remember the region an ENTRY allocation handed out, for
7456    /// `emplace_entry` to record. Only the two entry allocators call this; a
7457    /// callback capture rides inside the entry's trailing region (phase-476
7458    /// W0), so it is part of what they record.
7459    fn note_entry_region(&mut self, offset: usize, len: usize) {
7460        self.pending_region = Some(FreedRegion { offset, len });
7461    }
7462
7463    /// Issue 1667 — the length a region of `len` requested bytes occupies:
7464    /// rounded up to the grain, and never shorter than a free-list node.
7465    const fn arena_region_len(len: usize) -> usize {
7466        let len = len.next_multiple_of(ARENA_GRAIN);
7467        if len < ARENA_MIN_REGION {
7468            ARENA_MIN_REGION
7469        } else {
7470            len
7471        }
7472    }
7473
7474    /// Bytes a callback CAPTURE takes in an entry's trailing region: its length
7475    /// rounded up to the arena's `u64` grain. 0 for no capture.
7476    ///
7477    /// phase-476 W0 — a capture used to be a SEPARATE arena allocation
7478    /// (`stow_capture` over `arena_alloc_bytes`), which `release_entry` never
7479    /// gave back: it frees exactly the region `emplace_entry` recorded, and that
7480    /// was the entry's. Placing the capture at the END of the entry's own
7481    /// trailing region puts it inside the recorded region, so releasing the
7482    /// entry releases its capture.
7483    pub(crate) fn capture_trailing_len(capture: Option<&[u8]>) -> usize {
7484        match capture {
7485            Some(b) if !b.is_empty() => b.len().next_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<u64>()),
7486            _ => 0,
7487        }
7488    }
7489
7490    /// Copy a caller's callback CAPTURE to arena offset `at` and return the
7491    /// context pointer the entry should dispatch with — phase-456 W1, made a
7492    /// runtime length by W8, made part of the entry's region by phase-476 W0.
7493    ///
7494    /// `context` is one pointer. That carries a C++ `[this]` capture and not a
7495    /// `[this, state]` (two) or a `[obj, method]` (three, because a
7496    /// pointer-to-member-function is two words on the Itanium ABI) — the
7497    /// distribution phase-442 W0 measured over this tree and the porting corpus.
7498    /// So the capture lives in the arena beside the registration that uses it:
7499    /// arena bytes never move once allocated, and the returned pointer is into
7500    /// them rather than into anything of the caller's, so the C++ side keeps
7501    /// nothing.
7502    ///
7503    /// `at` must start [`capture_trailing_len`](Self::capture_trailing_len)
7504    /// bytes the caller's entry allocation reserved for it. `None` and an empty
7505    /// slice both mean "no capture", and both give the caller's own `context`
7506    /// straight back, which is every pre-W1 caller.
7507    pub(crate) fn place_capture(
7508        &mut self,
7509        at: usize,
7510        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
7511        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
7512    ) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
7513        let bytes = match capture {
7514            Some(b) if !b.is_empty() => b,
7515            _ => return context,
7516        };
7517        debug_assert!(at + bytes.len() <= self.arena.len());
7518        // SAFETY: the caller's entry allocation reserved
7519        // `capture_trailing_len(capture)` bytes at `at` for exactly this, and
7520        // `bytes` is a caller slice that cannot alias the arena (the arena is
7521        // borrowed mutably by `self` for the whole call).
7522        unsafe {
7523            let dst = (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(at);
7524            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), dst, bytes.len());
7525            dst as *mut core::ffi::c_void
7526        }
7527    }
7528
7529    /// Bump-allocate space for `T` plus `trailing_bytes` extra bytes.
7530    ///
7531    /// Returns `(entry_offset, trailing_offset)`. The trailing region starts
7532    /// immediately after `T` (aligned to 8 bytes).
7533    pub(crate) fn arena_alloc_with_trailing<T>(
7534        &mut self,
7535        trailing_bytes: usize,
7536    ) -> Result<(usize, usize), NodeError> {
7537        let align = core::mem::align_of::<T>().max(ARENA_GRAIN);
7538        let entry_size = core::mem::size_of::<T>();
7539        // Issue 1496 — a released region that holds the entry AND its trailing
7540        // region is reused whole. The trailing region keeps its rule: it starts
7541        // on a `u64` boundary after the entry, so the request is sized by that.
7542        let u64_align = core::mem::align_of::<u64>();
7543        let whole = Self::arena_region_len(entry_size.next_multiple_of(u64_align) + trailing_bytes);
7544        if let Some((entry_offset, granted)) = self.arena_take_freed(whole, align) {
7545            let trailing_offset = (entry_offset + entry_size).next_multiple_of(u64_align);
7546            crate::boot_report::note_alloc(whole, self.arena_used);
7547            self.note_entry_region(entry_offset, granted);
7548            return Ok((entry_offset, trailing_offset));
7549        }
7550        let entry_offset = self.arena_used.next_multiple_of(align);
7551        // Trailing region starts on an 8-byte (u64) boundary after the entry.
7552        let trailing_offset =
7553            (entry_offset + entry_size).next_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<u64>());
7554        // Issue 1667 — the region ends on the grain and is at least a node.
7555        let new_used = entry_offset + whole;
7556        debug_assert!(new_used >= trailing_offset + trailing_bytes);
7557        if new_used > self.arena.len() {
7558            // This path reported NOTHING until phase-412's self-report went in,
7559            // while its sibling `arena_alloc` has named the knob since issue
7560            // 0900. Half of arena exhaustion was therefore silent -- and it is
7561            // the half carrying buffered subscriptions and action entries,
7562            // which is what an island image actually allocates.
7563            return Err(self.arena_exhausted(
7564                core::any::type_name::<T>(),
7565                new_used - entry_offset,
7566                new_used - self.arena.len(),
7567            ));
7568        }
7569        self.arena_used = new_used;
7570        crate::boot_report::note_alloc(new_used - entry_offset, new_used);
7571        self.note_entry_region(entry_offset, new_used - entry_offset);
7572        Ok((entry_offset, trailing_offset))
7573    }
7574
7575    /// The ONE exhaustion path every arena allocator goes through — issues
7576    /// 0900, 1036, 1496.
7577    ///
7578    /// It names the knob (`report_arena_exhausted`), writes the first failure
7579    /// and its shortfall to the boot record (the only channel a console-less
7580    /// board has), says whether the failure is a SHAPE problem rather than a
7581    /// size one (released regions that together hold the request, none of
7582    /// which alone does), and — where the image asked for it — halts through
7583    /// the platform's fatal hook, so the record survives instead of the board
7584    /// running on with an entity missing. Three spellings of this existed, and
7585    /// the `_with_trailing` one reported nothing until phase-412.
7586    fn arena_exhausted(&self, entity: &'static str, request: usize, shortfall: usize) -> NodeError {
7587        super::arena::report_arena_exhausted(
7588            entity,
7589            shortfall,
7590            self.arena_used,
7591            self.arena.len(),
7592            self.arena_released(),
7593            request,
7594        );
7595        crate::boot_report::note_alloc_failed(request, shortfall);
7596        super::arena::arena_exhaustion_is_fatal();
7597        NodeError::BufferTooSmall
7598    }
7599
7600    /// Issue 1667 — read the free-list node at `offset`: `(next, len)`.
7601    fn arena_hole(&self, offset: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
7602        // SAFETY: `offset` is a listed free region: in bounds, grain-aligned and
7603        // at least `ARENA_MIN_REGION` long, written by `arena_set_hole`.
7604        unsafe {
7605            let p = (self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8).add(offset) as *const usize;
7606            (p.read_unaligned(), p.add(1).read_unaligned())
7607        }
7608    }
7609
7610    /// Issue 1667 — write the free-list node at `offset`.
7611    fn arena_set_hole(&mut self, offset: usize, next: usize, len: usize) {
7612        debug_assert!(len >= ARENA_MIN_REGION && offset + len <= self.arena.len());
7613        // SAFETY: as `arena_hole`; the region is free, so nothing else reads it.
7614        unsafe {
7615            let p = (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(offset) as *mut usize;
7616            p.write_unaligned(next);
7617            p.add(1).write_unaligned(len);
7618        }
7619    }
7620
7621    /// Point `prev`'s node (or the head, for `ARENA_FREE_NONE`) at `next`.
7622    fn arena_link(&mut self, prev: usize, next: usize) {
7623        if prev == ARENA_FREE_NONE {
7624            self.arena_free_head = next;
7625        } else {
7626            let (_, len) = self.arena_hole(prev);
7627            self.arena_set_hole(prev, next, len);
7628        }
7629    }
7630
7631    /// Issue 1496 / 1667 — first-fit over the free list. Returns the offset and
7632    /// the length GRANTED, which is the request plus any tail too short to list
7633    /// on its own: that tail belongs to the allocation, so its release gives it
7634    /// back. A hole whose alignment slack would be too short to list is skipped
7635    /// rather than split, for the same reason — no byte is ever orphaned.
7636    fn arena_take_freed(&mut self, size: usize, align: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
7637        let mut prev = ARENA_FREE_NONE;
7638        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
7639        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
7640            let (next, len) = self.arena_hole(cur);
7641            let start = cur.next_multiple_of(align);
7642            let head = start - cur;
7643            let fits = start + size <= cur + len;
7644            if fits && (head == 0 || head >= ARENA_MIN_REGION) {
7645                let tail = cur + len - (start + size);
7646                let granted = if tail < ARENA_MIN_REGION {
7647                    size + tail
7648                } else {
7649                    size
7650                };
7651                // What stays listed: the head slack, the tail, both, or neither.
7652                let mut after = next;
7653                if tail >= ARENA_MIN_REGION {
7654                    let t = start + size;
7655                    self.arena_set_hole(t, after, tail);
7656                    after = t;
7657                }
7658                if head > 0 {
7659                    self.arena_set_hole(cur, after, head);
7660                } else {
7661                    self.arena_link(prev, after);
7662                }
7663                return Some((start, granted));
7664            }
7665            prev = cur;
7666            cur = next;
7667        }
7668        None
7669    }
7670
7671    /// Issue 1496 / 1667 — give a region back. It is inserted in address order
7672    /// and coalesced with both neighbours, so a loop that frees what it
7673    /// allocated returns the arena to the shape it had; a hole that then ends
7674    /// at `arena_used` is handed back to the bump pointer.
7675    pub(crate) fn arena_release(&mut self, offset: usize, len: usize) {
7676        debug_assert!(len >= ARENA_MIN_REGION && len.is_multiple_of(ARENA_GRAIN));
7677        // `pprev` -> `prev` -> [offset] -> `cur`, in address order.
7678        let mut pprev = ARENA_FREE_NONE;
7679        let mut prev = ARENA_FREE_NONE;
7680        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
7681        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE && cur < offset {
7682            pprev = prev;
7683            prev = cur;
7684            cur = self.arena_hole(cur).0;
7685        }
7686        let (mut start, mut size) = (offset, len);
7687        let mut next = cur;
7688        if next != ARENA_FREE_NONE && start + size == next {
7689            let (after, next_len) = self.arena_hole(next);
7690            size += next_len;
7691            next = after;
7692        }
7693        if prev != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
7694            let (_, prev_len) = self.arena_hole(prev);
7695            if prev + prev_len == start {
7696                start = prev;
7697                size += prev_len;
7698                // `prev` is absorbed: link from ITS predecessor.
7699                prev = pprev;
7700            }
7701        }
7702        if start + size == self.arena_used {
7703            // The top of the arena: give it back to the bump pointer.
7704            self.arena_used = start;
7705            self.arena_link(prev, next);
7706            return;
7707        }
7708        self.arena_set_hole(start, next, size);
7709        self.arena_link(prev, start);
7710    }
7711
7712    /// Issue 1496 — bytes released back to the arena and not yet reused.
7713    /// Bytes handed back to the bump pointer are not counted: `arena_used`
7714    /// already went down by them.
7715    pub fn arena_released(&self) -> usize {
7716        let mut total = 0;
7717        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
7718        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
7719            let (next, len) = self.arena_hole(cur);
7720            total += len;
7721            cur = next;
7722        }
7723        total
7724    }
7725
7726    /// Issue 1667 — how many separate holes the free list holds. For tests and
7727    /// diagnostics.
7728    pub fn arena_holes(&self) -> usize {
7729        let mut count = 0;
7730        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
7731        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
7732            count += 1;
7733            cur = self.arena_hole(cur).0;
7734        }
7735        count
7736    }
7737
7738    /// Issue 1496 — RELEASE one callback entry: drop the entry in place (its
7739    /// RMW handles' `Drop`s destroy the backend entities, so nothing stays
7740    /// advertised), free its callback slot, and give its arena bytes back for
7741    /// reuse. `false`, touching nothing, when `index` is not a live entry of
7742    /// `kind`.
7743    ///
7744    /// Issue 1631 — the bytes released are the ones `emplace_entry` RECORDED
7745    /// from the allocator (`CallbackMeta::arena_len`), entry and trailing
7746    /// region together. 1496's form took the size from the caller, which had
7747    /// to restate the concrete entry type — impossible for a buffered
7748    /// subscription (its trailing region is sized at runtime) or a timer (its
7749    /// closure type is the registering crate's).
7750    ///
7751    /// # Safety
7752    /// No handle naming `index` may be used afterwards: the slot and its bytes
7753    /// go to the next registration.
7754    pub(crate) unsafe fn release_entry(&mut self, index: usize, kind: EntryKind) -> bool {
7755        let live = self
7756            .entries
7757            .get(index)
7758            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
7759            .is_some_and(|m| m.kind == kind);
7760        if !live {
7761            return false;
7762        }
7763        // Issue 1667 — the entry's own callback is running (it, or something it
7764        // called, asked for this release). Mark it and let `finish_dispatch` do
7765        // the release when the callback returns. The handle stops resolving
7766        // now, so a second request answers `false` and nothing dispatches it.
7767
7768        if let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(index)
7769            && tag.flags() & super::types::SlotTag::IN_FLIGHT != 0
7770        {
7771            let was = tag.set(super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING);
7772            return was & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING == 0;
7773        }
7774        // phase-397 W2 — the slot's next occupant arms (or not) on its own.
7775        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7776        if index < super::entity_wake::SLOTS {
7777            self.entity_attributed &= !(1u64 << index);
7778            self.entity_recheck &= !(1u64 << index);
7779            self.entity_status_polled &= !(1u64 << index);
7780        }
7781        let Some(meta) = self.entries[index].take() else {
7782            return false;
7783        };
7784        // SAFETY: the entry was written by its registration and not yet
7785        // dropped; `drop_fn` matches its concrete type.
7786        unsafe {
7787            let data_ptr = (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(meta.offset);
7788            (meta.drop_fn)(data_ptr);
7789        }
7790        // The entry's binding goes; the CONTEXT's budget state stays. It is
7791        // indexed by sched context, not by entry slot, and other entries may
7792        // still be bound to it: clearing `sporadic_states[index]` here dropped
7793        // the budget of whichever context shared the released slot's number.
7794        self.sched_context_bindings[index] = super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0);
7795        // phase10-B3 -- a released trigger subscription stops starting routes.
7796        if matches!(kind, EntryKind::Subscription) {
7797            super::monitor::route_unbind(self.monitor_table, index);
7798            super::monitor::deadline_unbind(self.age_table, index);
7799        }
7800        if let Some(len) = meta.arena_len.get() {
7801            self.arena_release(meta.offset, len);
7802        }
7803        if let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get_mut(index) {
7804            tag.owner = 0;
7805            tag.rank = 0;
7806            tag.reset_flags();
7807        }
7808        true
7809    }
7810
7811    /// Issue 1667 — mark `slot`'s callback as running, so a release it requests
7812    /// is deferred rather than dropping the entry under it.
7813    #[inline]
7814    fn begin_dispatch(slot_tags: &[super::types::SlotTag], slot: usize) {
7815        if let Some(tag) = slot_tags.get(slot) {
7816            tag.set(super::types::SlotTag::IN_DISPATCH);
7817        }
7818    }
7819
7820    /// Issue 1705 — `slot`'s entry is not to be touched by the spin thread
7821    /// this pass: its release is pending (it is never dispatched again), or
7822    /// (phase-509 P9b item 2) its callback is running, in another worker's
7823    /// window or below this pass on the same stack. So one callback never
7824    /// runs twice at once, and a pass never probes or sweeps an entry whose
7825    /// callback another thread is in.
7826    #[inline]
7827    fn slot_held(slot_tags: &[super::types::SlotTag], slot: usize) -> bool {
7828        slot_tags.get(slot).is_some_and(|t| {
7829            t.flags() & (super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING | super::types::SlotTag::IN_FLIGHT)
7830                != 0
7831        })
7832    }
7833
7834    /// phase-509 P3 (RFC-0108 D2) -- after a callback, merge what became
7835    /// ready while it ran into this pass's ready set, so the next pick is
7836    /// from the set as it is now.
7837    ///
7838    /// - An attributed slot's arrival (its bit in the ready word) joins.
7839    /// - With [`Self::set_reprobe_each_callback`], a slot that cannot be
7840    ///   attributed is probed (`has_data`) and joins when it has data.
7841    /// - A slot the pass already `settled` (queued, dispatched or held back by
7842    ///   a gate) does not join: it runs at most once per pass. An arrival for
7843    ///   one is kept for the next pass's scan.
7844    /// - A slot whose context gates its dispatch (a sporadic budget, a
7845    ///   time-triggered window) waits for the next pass, where the scan
7846    ///   applies the gate.
7847    fn merge_mid_pass(
7848        &mut self,
7849        fifo: &mut super::ready_set::RankedFifoSet<{ MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS }>,
7850        edf: &mut super::ready_set::BucketedEdfSet<
7851            { super::sched_context::Priority::COUNT },
7852            { MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS },
7853        >,
7854        settled: &mut u64,
7855        arena_ptr: *mut u8,
7856        band_mask: u64,
7857    ) {
7858        let mut fresh: u64 = 0;
7859        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7860        let attributed = self.entity_attributed;
7861        #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
7862        let attributed: u64 = 0;
7863        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7864        {
7865            // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- this band's arrivals only.
7866            let arrived = self
7867                .wake_ctx
7868                .as_ref()
7869                .map_or(0, |ctx| take_band_bits(&ctx.ready, band_mask))
7870                & attributed;
7871            // Kept for the next pass: its scan asks `has_data` (the bit has
7872            // left the word, and its wake already ended no park early).
7873            self.entity_recheck |= arrived & *settled;
7874            fresh |= arrived & !*settled;
7875        }
7876        if self.reprobe_each_callback {
7877            let mut probes: u32 = 0;
7878            for (i, meta) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
7879                let bit = 1u64 << i;
7880                let Some(meta) = meta else { continue };
7881                if (*settled | attributed | fresh) & bit != 0
7882                    || band_mask & bit == 0
7883                    || matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer | EntryKind::GuardCondition)
7884                    || matches!(meta.invocation, InvocationMode::Always)
7885                    || Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i)
7886                {
7887                    continue;
7888                }
7889                probes = probes.wrapping_add(1);
7890                // SAFETY: as the readiness scan's probe: `meta.offset` is this
7891                // live entry's arena slot, and `has_data` only reads it.
7892                if unsafe { (meta.has_data)(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const u8) } {
7893                    fresh |= bit;
7894                }
7895            }
7896            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7897            {
7898                self.readiness_probes = self.readiness_probes.wrapping_add(probes);
7899            }
7900            #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
7901            let _ = probes;
7902        }
7903        if fresh == 0 {
7904            return;
7905        }
7906        if !self.age_table.is_empty() {
7907            super::monitor::credit_arrivals(self.age_table, fresh);
7908        }
7909        let mut rest = fresh;
7910        while rest != 0 {
7911            let i = rest.trailing_zeros() as usize;
7912            let bit = 1u64 << i;
7913            rest &= !bit;
7914            if self.entries.get(i).is_none_or(|e| e.is_none()) || Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i)
7915            {
7916                #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7917                {
7918                    self.entity_recheck |= bit & attributed;
7919                }
7920                continue;
7921            }
7922            let sc_idx = self.sched_context_bindings[i].0 as usize;
7923            let sc = self.sched_contexts.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref());
7924            let class = sc.map_or(super::sched_context::SchedClass::Fifo, |sc| sc.class);
7925            let priority = sc.map_or(super::sched_context::Priority::Normal, |sc| sc.priority);
7926            let windowed = self.major_frame_us > 0
7927                && sc.is_some_and(|sc| sc.tt_window_duration_us.get().is_some());
7928            if matches!(class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) || windowed {
7929                #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7930                {
7931                    self.entity_recheck |= bit & attributed;
7932                }
7933                continue;
7934            }
7935            let is_edf = matches!(class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Edf);
7936            let job = super::types::ActiveJob {
7937                sort_key: if is_edf {
7938                    sc.and_then(|sc| sc.deadline_us.get())
7939                        .map_or(u32::MAX, |nz| nz.get())
7940                } else {
7941                    i as u32
7942                },
7943                desc_idx: i as super::types::DescIdx,
7944            };
7945            if is_edf {
7946                let _ = edf.insert_into(priority.index(), job);
7947            } else {
7948                let rank = self.slot_tags.get(i).map_or(0, |t| t.rank);
7949                let _ = fifo.insert_at(priority.dispatch_level(rank), job);
7950            }
7951            *settled |= bit;
7952            // As the scan does: a ready attributed slot is asked again next
7953            // spin, since one dispatch may leave data behind.
7954            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
7955            {
7956                self.entity_recheck |= bit & attributed;
7957            }
7958        }
7959    }
7960
7961    /// Issue 1667 — `slot`'s callback has returned. Complete a release it
7962    /// requested while running.
7963    fn finish_dispatch(&mut self, slot: usize) {
7964        let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(slot) else {
7965            return;
7966        };
7967        // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- a cancel or reset deferred behind this
7968        // callback first, while the entry is still marked running.
7969        if tag.flags()
7970            & (super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING | super::types::SlotTag::RESET_PENDING)
7971            != 0
7972        {
7973            self.apply_deferred_timer_op(slot);
7974        }
7975        let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(slot) else {
7976            return;
7977        };
7978        let was = tag.clear(super::types::SlotTag::IN_DISPATCH);
7979        if was & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING != 0 {
7980            self.complete_deferred_release(slot);
7981        }
7982    }
7983
7984    /// Issue 1667 / 1705 — finish a release that was deferred while a dispatch
7985    /// of the entry was in flight, if none is any more. A no-op while one still
7986    /// is: `reap_deferred_releases` retries.
7987    fn complete_deferred_release(&mut self, slot: usize) {
7988        let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(slot) else {
7989            return;
7990        };
7991        let f = tag.flags();
7992        if f & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING == 0
7993            || f & super::types::SlotTag::IN_FLIGHT != 0
7994        {
7995            return;
7996        }
7997        if let Some(kind) = self
7998            .entries
7999            .get(slot)
8000            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
8001            .map(|m| m.kind)
8002        {
8003            // SAFETY: the release was requested through a generation-checked
8004            // handle, and `resolve_handle` has refused the slot since; no
8005            // dispatch holds the entry (`IN_FLIGHT` is clear).
8006            let _ = unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, kind) };
8007        }
8008    }
8009
8010    /// Issue 1705 — complete every deferred release whose last dispatch has
8011    /// finished. `finish_dispatch` completes one deferred behind a callback
8012    /// on the spin thread when it returns; this is the backstop at the top
8013    /// of every `spin_once` (it served the retired OS-priority worker pool,
8014    /// whose worker could not touch the executor, phase-509 P11).
8015    pub(crate) fn reap_deferred_releases(&mut self) {
8016        for slot in 0..self.slot_tags.len() {
8017            if self.slot_tags[slot].flags() & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING != 0 {
8018                self.complete_deferred_release(slot);
8019            }
8020        }
8021    }
8022
8023    /// Issue 1631 — release a SUBSCRIPTION entry, whatever registration shape
8024    /// made it (typed, raw, in-place, buffered, with-info). See
8025    /// `release_entry` (crate-private): the entry is dropped, so its
8026    /// subscriber leaves the graph; its slot and arena bytes are reused by the
8027    /// next registration. `false`, touching nothing, when `handle` is not a
8028    /// live subscription.
8029    ///
8030    /// # Safety
8031    /// No copy of `handle` may be used afterwards — the slot is handed to the
8032    /// next registration, which may be of any kind.
8033    pub(crate) unsafe fn release_subscription(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
8034        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
8035            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::Subscription) },
8036            None => false,
8037        }
8038    }
8039
8040    /// Issue 1631 — release a TIMER entry; the timer's callback (and anything
8041    /// its closure captured) is dropped and never fires again. As
8042    /// [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
8043    ///
8044    /// # Safety
8045    /// As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
8046    pub(crate) unsafe fn release_timer(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
8047        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
8048            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::Timer) },
8049            None => false,
8050        }
8051    }

8053    /// Issue 1631 — release a SERVICE SERVER entry; the server leaves the
8054    /// graph. As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
8055    ///
8056    /// # Safety
8057    /// As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
8058    pub(crate) unsafe fn release_service(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
8059        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
8060            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::Service) },

8062        }

8065    /// Issue 1631 — release a SERVICE CLIENT entry; the client leaves the
8066    /// graph and any reply it was waiting for is abandoned with it. As
8067    /// [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
8068    ///
8069    /// # Safety
8070    /// As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
8071    pub(crate) unsafe fn release_service_client(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
8072        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
8073            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::ServiceClient) },
