9599    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.a — Node-aware variant of
9600    /// [`register_service`](Self::register_service).
9601    pub fn register_service_on<Svc, F>(
9602        &mut self,
9603        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
9604        service_name: &str,
9605        callback: F,
9606    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9607    where
9608        Svc: RosService + 'static,
9609        Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
9610        Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
9611        F: FnMut(&Svc::Request) -> Svc::Reply + 'static,
9612    {
9613        self.register_service_sized_on::<
9614            Svc,
9615            F,
9616            { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
9617            { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
9618        >(node_id, service_name, QoSProfile::services_default(), callback)
9619    }
9620
9621    // ========================================================================
9622    // Timer registration
9623    // ========================================================================
9624
9625    /// The ONE timer registration in the tree (phase-430 W4).
9626    ///
9627    /// Every timer verb — the four `Executor::register_timer*` entry points
9628    /// below, `Node::create_timer_in_group` / `create_timer_on_clock*`, the
9629    /// declarative `nros::Node` timer, and the C/C++ FFI that lower to them —
9630    /// constructs its arena entry HERE. Until W4 there were four copies of this
9631    /// body differing only in `oneshot`, `clock_source` and whether the sched
9632    /// binding was applied, and phase-425's clock axis reached exactly one of
9633    /// them; that is how a `nros::main!` component could declare a timer but
9634    /// not a ROS-time one.
9635    ///
9636    /// `node_id` / `group` feed `apply_node_default_sched` (phase 273: group
9637    /// table > node default > SC 0). `node_id == None` is the legacy unscoped
9638    /// path and makes that call a no-op.
9639    pub(crate) fn register_timer_entry<F>(
9640        &mut self,
9641        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
9642        period: TimerDuration,
9643        source: TimerClockSource,
9644        oneshot: bool,
9645        group: Option<&str>,
9646        callback: F,
9647    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9648    where
9649        F: FnMut() + 'static,
9650    {
9651        let mut callback = callback;
9652        self.register_timer_entry_with(
9653            node_id,
9654            period,
9655            source,
9656            oneshot,
9657            true,
9658            group,
9659            None,
9660            core::ptr::null_mut(),
9661            move |_| move |_: &TimerCallInfo| callback(),
9662        )
9663    }
9664
9665    /// [`register_timer_entry`](Self::register_timer_entry), with a CAPTURE
9666    /// the arena holds — phase-476 W2.
9667    ///
9668    /// The callback is BUILT after the allocation, by `make`, from the context
9669    /// pointer the entry should dispatch with: `place_capture`'s copy of
9670    /// `capture` when there is one, otherwise `context` unchanged. That is what
9671    /// lets the capture ride in the timer entry's own trailing region (so a
9672    /// release frees it) while the closure that reads it is still a plain
9673    /// `TimerEntry<F>`.
9674    ///
9675    /// Issue 1974 — the stored callback takes the dispatcher's
9676    /// [`TimerCallInfo`]; a plain `FnMut()` is adapted by ignoring it, so there
9677    /// is one entry type and one dispatch whichever flavour the caller wrote.
9678    /// `autostart == false` builds the entry CANCELLED (rcl's
9679    /// `rcl_timer_init2(..., autostart = false)`): it never fires until
9680    /// [`reset_timer`](Self::reset_timer) starts it.
9681    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
9682    pub(crate) fn register_timer_entry_with<F, M>(
9683        &mut self,
9684        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
9685        period: TimerDuration,
9686        source: TimerClockSource,
9687        oneshot: bool,
9688        autostart: bool,
9689        group: Option<&str>,
9690        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
9691        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
9692        make: M,
9693    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9694    where
9695        F: FnMut(&TimerCallInfo) + 'static,
9696        M: FnOnce(*mut core::ffi::c_void) -> F,
9697    {
9698        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
9699        let capture_len = Self::capture_trailing_len(capture);
9700        // No capture keeps the exact pre-W2 allocation, so a timer that captures
9701        // nothing costs what it always did.
9702        let (offset, context) = if capture_len == 0 {
9703            (self.arena_alloc::<TimerEntry<F>>()?, context)
9704        } else {
9705            let (offset, at) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<TimerEntry<F>>(capture_len)?;
9706            (offset, self.place_capture(at, capture, context))
9707        };
9708        let callback = make(context);
9709
9710        unsafe {
9711            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
9712            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut TimerEntry<F>;
9713            core::ptr::write(
9714                entry_ptr,
9715                TimerEntry {
9716                    period_us: period.as_micros(),
9717                    elapsed_us: 0,
9718                    overruns: 0,
9719                    overruns_reported: 0,
9720                    oneshot,
9721                    fired: false,
9722                    cancelled: !autostart,
9723                    overrun_policy: TimerOverrunPolicy::default(),
9724                    clock_source: source,
9725                    // Seeded HERE rather than on the first poll: a zero would
9726                    // make the first delta the whole epoch, which `Skip` would
9727                    // then coalesce into one immediate activation and `CatchUp`
9728                    // into a replay burst of ~10^9 periods. `Steady` reads no
9729                    // clock at all, so its seed is 0 and is never read.
9730                    last_clock_ns: source.now_ns(),
9731                    callback,
9732                },
9733            );
9734        }
9735
9736        let meta = CallbackMeta {
9737            offset,
9738            kind: EntryKind::Timer,
9739            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
9740            try_process: timer_try_process::<F>,
9741            has_data: always_ready,
9742            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
9743            invocation: InvocationMode::Always,
9744            drop_fn: drop_entry::<TimerEntry<F>>,
9745        };
9746        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::TimerPeriod(period.as_micros()));
9747        // Phase 273 — apply group sched binding (group > node default > SC 0).
9748        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
9749        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
9750    }
9751
9752    /// Register a repeating timer callback.
9753    ///
9754    /// The callback fires every `period` milliseconds during [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once).
9755    /// The timer delta is approximated by the `timeout_ms` argument to `spin_once`.
9756    pub fn register_timer<F>(
9757        &mut self,
9758        period: TimerDuration,
9759        callback: F,
9760    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9761    where
9762        F: FnMut() + 'static,
9763    {
9764        self.register_timer_entry(
9765            None,
9766            period,
9767            TimerClockSource::Steady,
9768            false,
9769            None,
9770            callback,
9771        )
9772    }
9773
9774    /// Register a repeating timer driven by a CLOCK rather than by the spin
9775    /// delta — phase-425 W4, the shape rclcpp spells
9776    /// `create_timer(node, clock, period, cb)`.
9777    ///
9778    /// [`register_timer`](Self::register_timer) is the wall timer: it consumes
9779    /// the executor's monotonic spin delta and no simulator can slow it down.
9780    /// This one reads `source` on every poll and advances by the difference, so
9781    /// a [`TimerClockSource::Ros`] timer follows `/clock` — it stops while the
9782    /// simulator is paused, halves with a bag replayed at 0.5x, and restarts
9783    /// its period on a backwards jump instead of stalling for the length of it.
9784    ///
9785    /// With no `/clock` source installed, a `Ros` timer reads system time and
9786    /// behaves like a wall timer with NTP steps, which is the same fallback
9787    /// `rclcpp::Clock` has: a node written for simulation still runs standalone.
9788    ///
9789    /// The node-level spellings of this are `Node::create_timer_on_clock`
9790    /// and the declarative `DeclaredNode::create_timer_on_clock` (phase-430 W4);
9791    /// all of them reach `register_timer_entry`, which is the only place a
9792    /// timer entry is built.
9793    pub fn register_timer_on_clock<F>(
9794        &mut self,
9795        period: TimerDuration,
9796        source: TimerClockSource,
9797        callback: F,
9798    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9799    where
9800        F: FnMut() + 'static,
9801    {
9802        self.register_timer_entry(None, period, source, false, None, callback)
9803    }
9804
9805    /// Register a one-shot timer callback.
9806    ///
9807    /// The callback fires once after `delay` milliseconds, then becomes inert.
9808    pub fn register_timer_oneshot<F>(
9809        &mut self,
9810        delay: TimerDuration,
9811        callback: F,
9812    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9813    where
9814        F: FnMut() + 'static,
9815    {
9816        self.register_timer_entry(None, delay, TimerClockSource::Steady, true, None, callback)
9817    }
9818
9819    /// phase-476 W2 — register a timer whose callback is a C function pointer
9820    /// and whose CAPTURE the arena holds: the `nros-cpp` road for a C++
9821    /// lambda, the timer twin of
9822    /// [`add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture`](Self::add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture).
9823    ///
9824    /// `capture`'s bytes are copied into the timer entry's trailing region and
9825    /// `callback` is called with a pointer to that copy, so the caller keeps
9826    /// nothing — which is what lets the C++ side hand back a two-word handle
9827    /// instead of a heap cell the node had to keep alive. Releasing the timer
9828    /// releases the capture with it.
9829    ///
9830    /// `source` picks the clock: [`TimerClockSource::Steady`] is the wall timer
9831    /// that advances with the spin delta.
9832    ///
9833    /// `capture_drop`, when given, is called with the same pointer when the
9834    /// entry is dropped (released, or the executor torn down), BEFORE its bytes
9835    /// go back to the arena. A C++ capture is a callable that may own something
9836    /// (a `std::shared_ptr`, a `std::string`), and its bytes were MOVED here by
9837    /// copy, so this is the only place its destructor can run.
9838    pub(crate) fn register_timer_c_capturing(
9839        &mut self,
9840        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
9841        period: TimerDuration,
9842        source: TimerClockSource,
9843        callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
9844        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
9845        capture_drop: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
9846    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
9847        self.register_timer_entry_with(
9848            node_id,
9849            period,
9850            source,
9851            false,
9852            true,
9853            None,
9854            capture,
9855            core::ptr::null_mut(),
9856            move |ctx| {
9857                let held = super::arena::CapturedCallback {
9858                    callback,
9859                    guard: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
9860                        ctx,
9861                        drop: capture_drop,
9862                    },
9863                };
9864                move |_: &TimerCallInfo| held.call()
9865            },
9866        )
9867    }
9868
9869    /// [`register_timer_c_capturing`](Self::register_timer_c_capturing) with
9870    /// the dispatcher's [`TimerCallInfo`] handed to the C callback, a callback
9871    /// group, and rcl's `autostart` — issue 1974, the road a C++
9872    /// `TimerInfoCallbackType` lambda and `create_wall_timer(..., autostart)`
9873    /// take.
9874    ///
9875    /// `I` is the FFI's own `#[repr(C)]` mirror of the info struct (the C++
9876    /// header is generated without includes, so it cannot name this crate's
9877    /// type); it is built from the executor's `TimerCallInfo` by `From` on each
9878    /// activation — a copy of two words, never a second computation.
9879    ///
9880    /// `autostart == false` registers the timer cancelled; `reset_timer`
9881    /// starts it. `group` binds it as `register_timer_on` does.
9882    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
9883    pub(crate) fn register_timer_c_capturing_with_info<I>(
9884        &mut self,
9885        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
9886        period: TimerDuration,
9887        source: TimerClockSource,
9888        autostart: bool,
9889        group: Option<&str>,
9890        callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(*const I, *mut core::ffi::c_void),
9891        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
9892        capture_drop: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
9893    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
9894    where
9895        I: From<TimerCallInfo> + 'static,
9896    {
9897        self.register_timer_entry_with(
9898            node_id,
9899            period,
9900            source,
9901            false,
9902            autostart,
9903            group,
9904            capture,
9905            core::ptr::null_mut(),
9906            move |ctx| {
9907                let guard = super::arena::CaptureGuard {
9908                    ctx,
9909                    drop: capture_drop,
9910                };
9911                move |info: &TimerCallInfo| {
9912                    // Borrow the WHOLE guard: a closure naming only `guard.ctx`
9913                    // would capture that `Copy` field alone and let the guard
9914                    // (whose `Drop` runs the capture's destructor) die here.
9915                    let guard = &guard;
9916                    let ffi_info = I::from(*info);
9917                    // SAFETY: the registrant's contract — `callback` reads its
9918                    // capture through the pointer it is given, and the info
9919                    // pointer is valid for the duration of the call.
9920                    unsafe { callback(&ffi_info, guard.ctx) }
9921                }
9922            },
9923        )
9924    }

9926    /// Register a repeating timer whose callback receives the dispatcher's

10019    /// The kept C-FFI subscription core (Phase 189.M2.b): registers a
10020    /// raw `RawSubscriptionCallback` fn-ptr + `context` against an
10021    /// optional node's session. The Rust ergonomic surface is the
10022    /// `node.subscription(t)` builder (closures); this is the single
10023    /// primitive the `nros-c` thin wrapper lowers to. `node_id == None`
10024    /// is the legacy single-node path.
10025    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10026    pub(crate) fn add_arena_subscription_c_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
10027        &mut self,
10028        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10029        topic_name: &str,
10030        type_name: &str,
10031        type_hash: &str,
10032        qos: QoSProfile,
10033        callback: RawSubscriptionCallback,
10034        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
10035        group: Option<&str>,
10036        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
10037    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10038        self.add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture::<RX_BUF>(
10039            node_id,
10040            topic_name,
10041            type_name,
10042            type_hash,
10043            qos,
10044            callback,
10045            context,
10046            group,
10047            rx_buffer_hint,
10048            None,
10049            None,
10050        )
10051    }
10052
10053    /// The same registration, with the caller's CAPTURE held by the arena —
10054    /// phase-456 W1.
10055    ///
10056    /// `context` is one pointer, which carries a C++ `[this]` capture and not a
10057    /// `[this, state]` or a `[obj, method]`. When `capture` is `Some`, its
10058    /// bytes are copied into the arena and `context` is repointed at that copy,
10059    /// so the caller keeps nothing and nothing the caller owns is referenced
10060    /// after this returns. When it is `None` the behaviour is exactly the
10061    /// pre-existing one, which is why the plain entry point above is a wrapper
10062    /// rather than a second implementation.
10063    ///
10064    /// **phase-456 W8 changed two things here.** The capture is a RUNTIME
10065    /// length — see `Self::place_capture` — so there is no constant the C++
10066    /// side has to match and no `BufferTooSmall` reachable only by drifting
10067    /// from it. And this path now reaches the in-place dispatch that the Rust
10068    /// typed path has had since phase-231: `RawSubscriptionCallback` is
10069    /// `(const uint8_t*, size_t, void*)`, so the backend's borrowed receive
10070    /// slot IS the argument, and a C or C++ subscription on zenoh or XRCE
10071    /// claims no receive region at all.
10072    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10073    pub(crate) fn add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture<const RX_BUF: usize>(
10074        &mut self,
10075        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10076        topic_name: &str,
10077        type_name: &str,
10078        type_hash: &str,
10079        qos: QoSProfile,
10080        callback: RawSubscriptionCallback,
10081        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
10082        group: Option<&str>,
10083        // phase-402 W2 / issue 0896 — bytes the caller expects to receive; 0 =
10084        // no opinion. A size-classing backend (zenoh-pico) routes on this, and
10085        // a subscription that states nothing takes the SMALL class whatever its
10086        // message type. The C path had no way to say it until the options
10087        // struct existed.
10088        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
10089        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
10090        // phase-476 W2 — called on the arena's copy of `capture` when the entry
10091        // is dropped; see `CaptureGuard`. `None` when the capture owns nothing.
10092        capture_drop: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
10093    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10094        // phase-403 W3/W5 -- size the arena slot from the TYPE, not from the
10095        // image-wide default. `rx_buffer_hint` already arrives here (phase-402
10096        // routed it to the backend's payload class and stopped); spending it on
10097        // the allocation as well is what makes the buffer per-type.
10098        //
10099        // This is the whole saving on the raw path. `RX_BUF` is
10100        // DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE, so every slot -- publishers and timers included --
10101        // was charged the largest subscription's buffer. Measured on
10102        // mr-canhubk344: 36 handles at the correct 2052-byte bound wanted a
10103        // 242096-byte arena of a 77968-byte region; only 13 of those handles
10104        // receive anything.
10105        //
10106        // 0 keeps the old behaviour, and it means "this CALLER stated nothing"
10107        // rather than "this type is unbounded" -- an unbounded type is a build
10108        // error now, so a zero here is a caller that did not ask, never a type
10109        // that could not answer.
10110        let slot_bytes = if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
10111            rx_buffer_hint
10112        } else {
10113            RX_BUF
10114        };
10115
10116        let SubscriptionOpen {
10117            slot,
10118            handle,
10119            qos,
10120            in_place,
10121            slot_bytes,
10122        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
10123            node_id,
10124            topic_name,
10125            type_name,
10126            type_hash,
10127            qos,
10128            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
10129            slot_bytes,
10130            // phase-456 W8 — `RawSubscriptionCallback` takes borrowed bytes and
10131            // a context, which is exactly what `process_raw_in_place` hands it.
10132            in_place_capable: true,
10133        })?;
10134
10135        // The capture is placed AFTER the backend call and BEFORE either entry
10136        // is written, so both dispatch shapes get the same context and a failed
10137        // `create_subscription` costs no arena bytes. phase-476 W0 — it rides
10138        // at the end of the entry's own trailing region, so releasing the entry
10139        // gives it back.
10140        let capture_len = Self::capture_trailing_len(capture);
10141
10142        if in_place {
10143            let (entry_offset, capture_at) =
10144                self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry>(capture_len)?;
10145            let context = self.place_capture(capture_at, capture, context);
10146            unsafe {
10147                let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10148                let entry_ptr =
10149                    arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry;
10150                core::ptr::write(
10151                    entry_ptr,
10152                    super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry {
10153                        handle,
10154                        callback,
10155                        context,
10156                        capture: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
10157                            ctx: context,
10158                            drop: capture_drop,
10159                        },
10160                    },
10161                );
10162            }
10163            let meta = CallbackMeta {
10164                offset: entry_offset,
10165                kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
10166                arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10167                try_process: super::arena::sub_inplace_raw_c_try_process,
10168                has_data: super::arena::sub_inplace_raw_c_has_data,
10169                pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10170                invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10171                drop_fn: drop_entry::<super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry>,
10172            };
10173            self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
10174            // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
10175            // SAFETY: a `super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry` was written at `entry_offset` just above.
10176            unsafe {
10177                self.arm_entry_wake::<super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry>(
10178                    slot,
10179                    entry_offset,
10180                    |e, w| nros_rmw::Subscription::register_waker(&e.handle, w),
10181                )
10182            };
10183            self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
10184            return Ok(self.handle_for(slot));
10185        }
10186
10187        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, slot_bytes);
10188
10189        // The ring first, then the capture on the next `u64` boundary after it.
10190        let ring_len = trailing_bytes.next_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<u64>());
10191        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
10192            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<SubBufferedRawCEntry>(ring_len + capture_len)?;
10193        let context = self.place_capture(trailing_offset + ring_len, capture, context);
10194
10195        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
10196
10197        let buffer = if qos.depth <= 1 {
10198            BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes) })
10199        } else {
10200            BufferStrategy::Ring(unsafe { SpscRing::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes, qos.depth as usize) })
10201        };
10202
10203        unsafe {
10204            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10205            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut SubBufferedRawCEntry;
10206            core::ptr::write(
10207                entry_ptr,
10208                SubBufferedRawCEntry {
10209                    handle,
10210                    buffer,
10211                    callback,
10212                    context,
10213                    capture: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
10214                        ctx: context,
10215                        drop: capture_drop,
10216                    },
10217                },
10218            );
10219        }
10220
10221        let meta = CallbackMeta {
10222            offset: entry_offset,
10223            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
10224            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10225            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_c_try_process,
10226            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_c_has_data,
10227            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10228            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10229            drop_fn: drop_entry::<SubBufferedRawCEntry>,
10230        };
10231        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
10232        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
10233        // SAFETY: a `SubBufferedRawCEntry` was written at `entry_offset` just above.
10234        unsafe {
10235            self.arm_entry_wake::<SubBufferedRawCEntry>(slot, entry_offset, |e, w| {
10236                nros_rmw::Subscription::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
10237            })
10238        };
10239        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
10240        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
10241    }
10242
10243    /// phase-417 W5.a (RFC-0089 stage 5) — the TYPED C-FFI subscription core:
10244    /// the same registration as [`Self::add_arena_subscription_c_callback`],
10245    /// plus caller-owned message storage and the erased deserialiser for its
10246    /// type, so the callback receives a DESERIALISED message instead of CDR
10247    /// bytes.
10248    ///
10249    /// This is the Rust half of rclc's
10250    /// `rclc_executor_add_subscription(executor, subscription, msg, callback,
10251    /// invocation)`. rclc has no allocator on that path either — it makes the
10252    /// CALLER own the storage, which is exactly what `msg` is here. The C
10253    /// ledger recorded our byte-oriented delivery as forced by "no allocator";
10254    /// the compared surface operates under the same constraint, so the reason
10255    /// was false and the divergence was avoidable (issue 1022 / W-C3).
10256    ///
10257    /// The raw path is untouched and stays: a byte-oriented subscriber is a
10258    /// legitimate thing to want, and this is additive.
10259    ///
10260    /// # Contract on failure
10261    /// If `deserialize` returns non-zero the callback is **not** invoked, the
10262    /// sample is dropped, `try_process` reports
10263    /// `TransportError::DeserializationError` (so it lands in
10264    /// `SpinOnceResult::subscription_errors`), and a rate-limited `nros_log`
10265    /// error names the length and the return code. A message that does not fit
10266    /// the caller's storage arrives here as exactly that failure: both the
10267    /// bounded-string and bounded-sequence decoders refuse rather than
10268    /// truncate, so there is no silent short read.
10269    ///
10270    /// # Safety
10271    /// `msg` must point to storage of the type `deserialize` writes, valid for
10272    /// as long as the subscription is registered. Nothing here drops it.
10273    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10274    pub(crate) unsafe fn add_arena_subscription_c_typed_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
10275        &mut self,
10276        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10277        topic_name: &str,
10278        type_name: &str,
10279        type_hash: &str,
10280        qos: QoSProfile,
10281        msg: core::ptr::NonNull<core::ffi::c_void>,
10282        deserialize: RawMessageDeserializeFn,
10283        callback: TypedSubscriptionCallback,
10284        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
10285        group: Option<&str>,
10286        // Same meaning as on the raw path: bytes the caller expects to receive,
10287        // 0 = no opinion. A typed caller normally HAS an answer — the generated
10288        // `<Msg>_RX_MAX_SERIALIZED_SIZE` — which is why the C entry point takes
10289        // it rather than defaulting.
10290        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
10291    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10292        let SubscriptionOpen {
10293            slot,
10294            handle,
10295            qos,
10296            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
10297            ..
10298        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
10299            node_id,
10300            topic_name,
10301            type_name,
10302            type_hash,
10303            qos,
10304            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
10305            // phase-403 W3/W5, unchanged: the hint sizes the arena slot, and 0
10306            // means "this caller stated nothing", never "this type is zero
10307            // bytes".
10308            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
10309                rx_buffer_hint
10310            } else {
10311                RX_BUF
10312            },
10313            // The callback receives the caller's DESERIALISED storage, written
10314            // by `deserialize` from the sample's bytes, so borrowed bytes would
10315            // be enough and this shape could take the in-place row. It does not
10316            // yet: `SubBufferedTypedCEntry` also owns the `msg` pointer and the
10317            // deserialiser, so an in-place twin is a second entry type rather
10318            // than a flag, and phase-456 W8's acceptance is the RAW C path.
10319            // Stated here rather than left blank because a `false` nobody wrote
10320            // down is what this whole item is about.
10321            in_place_capable: false,
10322        })?;
10323
10324        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, rx_bytes);
10325
10326        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
10327            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<SubBufferedTypedCEntry>(trailing_bytes)?;
10328
10329        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
10330
10331        let buffer = if qos.depth <= 1 {
10332            BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, rx_bytes) })
10333        } else {
10334            BufferStrategy::Ring(unsafe { SpscRing::init(buf_ptr, rx_bytes, qos.depth as usize) })
10335        };
10336
10337        unsafe {
10338            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10339            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut SubBufferedTypedCEntry;
10340            core::ptr::write(
10341                entry_ptr,
10342                SubBufferedTypedCEntry {
10343                    handle,
10344                    buffer,
10345                    msg: msg.as_ptr(),
10346                    deserialize,
10347                    callback,
10348                    context,
10349                },
10350            );
10351        }
10352
10353        let meta = CallbackMeta {
10354            offset: entry_offset,
10355            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
10356            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10357            try_process: sub_buffered_typed_c_try_process,
10358            has_data: sub_buffered_typed_c_has_data,
10359            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10360            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10361            drop_fn: drop_entry::<SubBufferedTypedCEntry>,
10362        };
10363        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
10364        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
10365        // SAFETY: a `SubBufferedTypedCEntry` was written at `entry_offset` just above.
10366        unsafe {
10367            self.arm_entry_wake::<SubBufferedTypedCEntry>(slot, entry_offset, |e, w| {
10368                nros_rmw::Subscription::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
10369            })
10370        };
10371        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
10372        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
10373    }

10375    /// Issue 2036 — register a raw subscription whose closure receives each
10376    /// sample's [`MessageInfo`](nros_core::MessageInfo) (`None` from a backend
10377    /// that reports none): the raw twin of the typed `with_info` path, for a
10378    /// caller that deserializes itself. Backs the C++
10379    /// `(const M&, const rclcpp::MessageInfo&)` subscription callback
10380    /// (`nros_cpp_subscription_register_message_info`).
10381    ///
10382    /// `rx_buffer_hint` sizes both the backend's payload class and the arena
10383    /// slot, as on [`add_arena_subscription_c_info_callback`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::add_arena_subscription_c_info_callback);
10384    /// 0 falls back to `DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE`.
10385    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10386    pub fn add_arena_subscription_msg_info_closure<F>(
10387        &mut self,
10388        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10389        topic_name: &str,
10390        type_name: &str,
10391        type_hash: &str,
10392        qos: QoSProfile,
10393        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
10394        callback: F,
10395    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
10396    where
10397        F: FnMut(&[u8], Option<&nros_core::MessageInfo>) + 'static,
10398    {
10399        type Entry<F> = SubBufferedRawMsgInfoEntry<F>;
10400
10401        let SubscriptionOpen {
10402            slot,
10403            handle,
10404            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
10405            ..
10406        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
10407            node_id,
10408            topic_name,
10409            type_name,
10410            type_hash,
10411            qos,
10412            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
10413            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
10414                rx_buffer_hint
10415            } else {
10416                crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE
10417            },
10418            // The metadata comes with a COPYING take (`take_serialized_with_info`).
10419            in_place_capable: false,
10420        })?;
10421
10422        let (offset, trailing_offset) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry<F>>(rx_bytes)?;
10423        unsafe {
10424            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10425            let buffer = super::arena::TrailingBuf::init(arena_ptr.add(trailing_offset), rx_bytes);
10426            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry<F>;
10427            core::ptr::write(
10428                entry_ptr,
10429                Entry {
10430                    handle,
10431                    buffer,
10432                    callback,
10433                },
10434            );
10435        }
10436
10437        let meta = CallbackMeta {
10438            offset,
10439            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
10440            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10441            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_msg_info_try_process::<F>,
10442            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_msg_info_has_data::<F>,
10443            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10444            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10445            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<F>>,
10446        };
10447        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
10448        // SAFETY: an `Entry<F>` was written at `offset` just above.
10449        unsafe {
10450            self.arm_entry_wake::<Entry<F>>(slot, offset, |e, w| {
10451                nros_rmw::Subscription::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
10452            })
10453        };
10454        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
10455        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
10456    }
10457
10458    /// Phase 189.M3.4 — register a raw C-fn-ptr subscription whose callback
10459    /// also receives the sample's wire **attachment**
10460    /// ([`RawSubscriptionInfoCallback`]: `(data, len, attachment, att_len,
10461    /// context)`) — the C analog of the Rust
10462    /// `node.subscription(t).generic(..).message_info()` builder. Backs the C
10463    /// FFI `rclc_executor_add_subscription_raw_with_info`. Flat per-entry
10464    /// payload + attachment buffers (cap `RAW_INFO_ATT_CAP`);
10465    /// one sample per `spin_once`.
10466    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10467    pub(crate) fn add_arena_subscription_c_info_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
10468        &mut self,
10469        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10470        topic_name: &str,
10471        type_name: &str,
10472        type_hash: &str,
10473        qos: QoSProfile,
10474        callback: RawSubscriptionInfoCallback,
10475        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
10476        // phase-408 W5a/W5b — bytes the caller expects to receive; 0 = no
10477        // opinion. It now buys BOTH halves: the BACKEND's payload size-class
10478        // routing (W5a, below) and the ARENA slot (W5b, further down). `RX_BUF`
10479        // survives only as the fallback for a caller that states nothing, which
10480        // is exactly its role on the plain C path.
10481        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
10482    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10483        type Entry = SubBufferedRawInfoCEntry;
10484
10485        let SubscriptionOpen {
10486            slot,
10487            handle,
10488            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
10489            ..
10490        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
10491            node_id,
10492            topic_name,
10493            type_name,
10494            type_hash,
10495            qos,
10496            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
10497            // phase-408 W5b — the hint sizes the ARENA too, not just the
10498            // backend's size class. 0 still means "this caller stated nothing",
10499            // so `RX_BUF` -- `DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE` at every call site -- is what
10500            // it falls back to, and an unhinted registration claims the same
10501            // bytes it always did.
10502            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
10503                rx_buffer_hint
10504            } else {
10505                RX_BUF
10506            },
10507            // Carries the wire attachment — see the Rust `_raw_info_on` twin.
10508            in_place_capable: false,
10509        })?;
10510
10511        let (offset, trailing_offset) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry>(rx_bytes)?;
10512        unsafe {
10513            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10514            let buf = super::arena::TrailingBuf::init(arena_ptr.add(trailing_offset), rx_bytes);
10515            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry;
10516            core::ptr::write(
10517                entry_ptr,
10518                Entry {
10519                    handle,
10520                    buffer: buf,
10521                    att: [0u8; super::arena::RAW_INFO_ATT_CAP],
10522                    callback,
10523                    context,
10524                },
10525            );
10526        }
10527
10528        let meta = CallbackMeta {
10529            offset,
10530            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
10531            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10532            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_info_c_try_process,
10533            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_info_c_has_data,
10534            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10535            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10536            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry>,
10537        };
10538        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
10539        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
10540        // SAFETY: a `Entry` was written at `offset` just above.
10541        unsafe {
10542            self.arm_entry_wake::<Entry>(slot, offset, |e, w| {
10543                nros_rmw::Subscription::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
10544            })
10545        };
10546        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
10547        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
10548    }
10549
10550    /// Phase 269 W3 — register a raw C-fn-ptr subscription whose callback
10551    /// ALSO surfaces the sample's E2E integrity status (CRC + sequence gap/dup)
10552    /// alongside the CDR bytes — the C/C++ component-callback analog of Rust's
10553    /// `register_subscription_buffered_raw_safety_on` (`FnMut(&[u8], &IntegrityStatus)`).
10554    ///
10555    /// The executor validates the sample via `take_validated` and unpacks the
10556    /// [`nros_rmw::IntegrityStatus`] into three plain scalars (gap, duplicate,
10557    /// crc_valid) before calling `callback`. This avoids introducing a
10558    /// cbindgen-visible struct at the executor layer; the C/C++ headers pack them
10559    /// back into their local integrity-status typedef.
10560    ///
10561    /// Requires the `safety-e2e` feature. Backed by `SubBufferedRawSafetyCEntry`.
10562    #[cfg(feature = "safety-e2e")]
10563    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10564    pub(crate) fn add_arena_subscription_c_validated_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
10565        &mut self,
10566        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10567        topic_name: &str,
10568        type_name: &str,
10569        type_hash: &str,
10570        qos: QoSProfile,
10571        callback: super::types::RawSubscriptionSafetyCallback,
10572        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
10573        // phase-408 W5a/W5b — bytes the caller expects to receive; 0 = no
10574        // opinion. It now buys BOTH halves: the BACKEND's payload size-class
10575        // routing (W5a, below) and the ARENA slot (W5b, further down). `RX_BUF`
10576        // survives only as the fallback for a caller that states nothing, which
10577        // is exactly its role on the plain C path.
10578        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
10579    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10580        use super::arena::{
10581            SubBufferedRawSafetyCEntry, TrailingBuf, sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_has_data,
10582            sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_try_process,
10583        };
10584        type Entry = SubBufferedRawSafetyCEntry;
10585
10586        let SubscriptionOpen {
10587            slot,
10588            handle,
10589            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
10590            ..
10591        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
10592            node_id,
10593            topic_name,
10594            type_name,
10595            type_hash,
10596            qos,
10597            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
10598            // phase-408 W5b — same as the info sibling: one flat slot in the
10599            // trailing region, sized from the hint, `RX_BUF` only as the
10600            // stated-nothing fallback.
10601            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
10602                rx_buffer_hint
10603            } else {
10604                RX_BUF
10605            },
10606            // Carries the integrity status, which comes from `take_validated`.
10607            in_place_capable: false,
10608        })?;
10609
10610        let (offset, trailing_offset) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry>(rx_bytes)?;
10611        unsafe {
10612            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10613            let buf = TrailingBuf::init(arena_ptr.add(trailing_offset), rx_bytes);
10614            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry;
10615            core::ptr::write(
10616                entry_ptr,
10617                Entry {
10618                    handle,
10619                    buffer: buf,
10620                    callback,
10621                    context,
10622                },
10623            );
10624        }
10625
10626        let meta = CallbackMeta {
10627            offset,
10628            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
10629            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10630            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_try_process,
10631            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_has_data,
10632            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10633            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10634            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry>,
10635        };
10636        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
10637        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
10638        // SAFETY: a `Entry` was written at `offset` just above.
10639        unsafe {
10640            self.arm_entry_wake::<Entry>(slot, offset, |e, w| {
10641                nros_rmw::Subscription::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
10642            })
10643        };
10644        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
10645        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
10646    }

10752            qos,
10753            callback,
10754            core::ptr::null_mut(),
10755            capture,

10757        )

10764    /// ([`ServiceTrait::request_info`](nros_rmw::ServiceTrait::request_info)),
10765    /// all zeros when it reported none.
10766    ///
10767    /// One entry point for every registration shape: `node_id` as
10768    /// `register_service_raw_sized_on` (or `None`), and `capture` as
10769    /// `register_service_raw_capturing` (or `None`, with `context`
10770    /// passed through instead).

10786    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {

10800    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10801    fn register_service_raw_sized_inner<
10802        const REQ_BUF: usize,
10803        const REPLY_BUF: usize,
10804        C: super::arena::RawServiceDispatch,
10805    >(
10806        &mut self,
10807        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10808        service_name: &str,
10809        service_type: &str,
10810        service_hash: &str,
10811        qos: QoSProfile,
10812        callback: C,
10813        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
10814        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
10815        capture_drop: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
10816    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10817        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
10818        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match node_id {
10819            Some(id) => {
10820                let r = self
10821                    .nodes
10822                    .get(id.index())
10823                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
10824                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
10825            }
10826            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
10827        };
10828        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, service_type, service_hash)
10829            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
10830            .with_namespace(&ns);
10831        if !node_name.is_empty() {
10832            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
10833        }
10834        let handle = {
10835            let session = self
10836                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
10837                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
10838            // Phase 193.5 — validate against the backend's supported policies
10839            // (no silent downgrade); request/reply effectively requires RELIABLE.
10840            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
10841                &qos,
10842                session.supported_qos_policies(),
10843                "service",
10844                service_name,
10845            )?;
10846            session
10847                .create_service(&info, qos)
10848                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?
10849        };
10850
10851        // phase-488 — a capture rides at the end of the entry's own region, as
10852        // a subscription's does, so releasing the entry gives it back. No
10853        // capture keeps `arena_alloc`, so a C caller's arena use does not move.
10854        let capture_len = Self::capture_trailing_len(capture);
10855        let (offset, context) = if capture_len == 0 {
10856            (
10857                self.arena_alloc::<SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>>()?,
10858                context,
10859            )
10860        } else {
10861            let (offset, capture_at) =
10862                self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>>(capture_len)?;
10863            (offset, self.place_capture(capture_at, capture, context))
10864        };
10865
10866        unsafe {
10867            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
10868            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>;
10869            core::ptr::write(
10870                entry_ptr,
10871                SrvRawEntry {
10872                    handle,
10873                    req_buffer: [0u8; REQ_BUF],
10874                    reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
10875                    callback,
10876                    context,
10877                    capture: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
10878                        ctx: context,
10879                        drop: capture_drop,
10880                    },
10881                },
10882            );
10883        }
10884
10885        let meta = CallbackMeta {
10886            offset,
10887            kind: EntryKind::Service,
10888            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
10889            try_process: srv_raw_try_process::<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>,
10890            has_data: srv_raw_has_data::<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>,
10891            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
10892            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
10893            drop_fn: drop_entry::<SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>>,
10894        };
10895        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
10896        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
10897        // SAFETY: a `SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>` was written at `offset` just above.
10898        unsafe {
10899            self.arm_entry_wake::<SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF, C>>(slot, offset, |e, w| {
10900                nros_rmw::ServiceTrait::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
10901            })
10902        };
10903        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
10904        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
10905    }

10987    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10988    fn register_service_client_raw_sized_inner<const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
10989        &mut self,
10990        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
10991        service_name: &str,

10993        service_hash: &str,
10994        qos: QoSProfile,

10997    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
10998        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
10999        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match node_id {
11000            Some(id) => {
11001                let r = self
11002                    .nodes
11003                    .get(id.index())
11004                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
11005                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
11006            }
11007            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
11008        };
11009        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, service_type, service_hash)
11010            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
11011            .with_namespace(&ns);
11012        if !node_name.is_empty() {
11013            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
11014        }
11015        let handle = {
11016            let session = self
11017                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
11018                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
11019            // Phase 193.5 — validate against the backend's supported policies
11020            // (no silent downgrade); request/reply effectively requires RELIABLE.
11021            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
11022                &qos,
11023                session.supported_qos_policies(),
11024                "client",
11025                service_name,
11026            )?;
11027            session
11028                .create_client(&info, qos)
11029                .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ServiceClientCreationFailed))?
11030        };
11031
11032        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>>()?;
11033        unsafe {
11034            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11035            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>;
11036            core::ptr::write(
11037                entry_ptr,
11038                ServiceClientRawArenaEntry {
11039                    handle,
11040                    reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
11041                    pending: false,
11042                    reply_ready: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
11043                    callback,
11044                    context,
11045                    sequences: super::arena::ClientSequences::new(),
11046                },
11047            );
11048        }
11049
11050        let meta = CallbackMeta {
11051            offset,
11052            kind: EntryKind::ServiceClient,
11053            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
11054            try_process: service_client_raw_try_process::<REPLY_BUF>,
11055            has_data: always_ready,
11056            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
11057            invocation: InvocationMode::Always,
11058            drop_fn: drop_entry::<ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>>,
11059        };
11060        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
11061        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
11062        // SAFETY: a `ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>` was written at `offset` just above.
11063        unsafe {
11064            self.arm_entry_wake::<ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>>(slot, offset, |e, w| {
11065                nros_rmw::ClientTrait::register_waker(&e.handle, w)
11066            })
11067        };
11068        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
11069        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
11070    }
11071
11072    /// RFC-0041 / Phase 239.1 — register a **typed callback** service client.
11073    /// The reply is eager-drained at `spin_once` and dispatched to `callback` as
11074    /// a deserialized `Svc::Reply`. Returns the scheduling [`HandleId`] and a
11075    /// `*mut` to the arena entry's send header (used to build the typed
11076    /// [`ServiceClientCallback`](super::handles::ServiceClientCallback)).
11077    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
11078    pub(crate) fn register_service_client_callback<Svc, F, const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
11079        &mut self,
11080        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
11081        service_name: &str,
11082        service_type: &str,
11083        service_hash: &str,
11084        qos: QoSProfile,
11085        callback: F,
11086    ) -> Result<(HandleId, *mut ServiceClientSendHeader<REPLY_BUF>), NodeError>
11087    where
11088        Svc: nros_core::RosService + 'static,
11089        F: FnMut(&Svc::Reply) + 'static,
11090    {
11091        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
11092        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match node_id {
11093            Some(id) => {
11094                let r = self
11095                    .nodes
11096                    .get(id.index())
11097                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
11098                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
11099            }
11100            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
11101        };
11102        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, service_type, service_hash)
11103            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
11104            .with_namespace(&ns);
11105        if !node_name.is_empty() {
11106            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
11107        }
11108        let handle = {
11109            let session = self
11110                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
11111                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
11112            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
11113                &qos,
11114                session.supported_qos_policies(),
11115                "client",
11116                service_name,
11117            )?;
11118            session
11119                .create_client(&info, qos)
11120                .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ServiceClientCreationFailed))?
11121        };
11122
11123        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>>()?;
11124        let hdr_ptr = unsafe {
11125            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11126            let entry_ptr =
11127                arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>;
11128            core::ptr::write(
11129                entry_ptr,
11130                ServiceClientCallbackEntry {
11131                    hdr: ServiceClientSendHeader {
11132                        handle,
11133                        reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
11134                        pending: false,
11135                        reply_ready: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
11136                        sequences: super::arena::ClientSequences::new(),
11137                    },
11138                    callback,
11139                    _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
11140                },
11141            );
11142            &mut (*entry_ptr).hdr as *mut ServiceClientSendHeader<REPLY_BUF>
11143        };
11144
11145        let meta = CallbackMeta {
11146            offset,
11147            kind: EntryKind::ServiceClient,
11148            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
11149            try_process: service_client_callback_try_process::<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>,
11150            has_data: always_ready,
11151            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
11152            invocation: InvocationMode::Always,
11153            drop_fn: drop_entry::<ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>>,
11154        };
11155        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
11156        // phase-397 W2 — this entry's arrivals mark its slot and wake this executor.
11157        // SAFETY: a `ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>` was written at `offset` just above.
11158        unsafe {
11159            self.arm_entry_wake::<ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>>(
11160                slot,
11161                offset,
11162                |e, w| nros_rmw::ClientTrait::register_waker(&e.hdr.handle, w),
11163            )
11164        };
11165        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
11166        Ok((self.handle_for(slot), hdr_ptr))
11167    }

11169    // ========================================================================
11170    // Guard condition registration
11171    // ========================================================================
11172
11173    /// Register a guard condition with a callback, on no particular node.
11174    ///
11175    /// Returns both the [`HandleId`] for trigger configuration and a
11176    /// [`GuardCondition`] for triggering from other threads.
11177    ///
11178    /// **This is the ours-only PRIMITIVE, not the verb a user reaches for.**
11179    /// phase-417 W4.e settled that the NODE owns a guard condition in all three
11180    /// languages, so the spelling an application writes is
11181    /// [`Node::create_guard_condition`](crate::executor::Node::create_guard_condition)
11182    /// — which is this function with a node bound, so the guard inherits that
11183    /// node's `SchedContext` like every other entity the node creates. This one
11184    /// stays because the executor is what owns the arena the flag lives in, and
11185    /// because an image with no node at all (a bare `Executor::open` plus a
11186    /// wake source) still has to be able to make one.
11187    pub fn register_guard_condition<F>(
11188        &mut self,
11189        callback: F,
11190    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
11191    where
11192        F: FnMut() + 'static,
11193    {
11194        self.register_guard_condition_on(None, callback)
11195    }
11196
11197    /// The node-bound form of [`register_guard_condition`](Self::register_guard_condition)
11198    /// — phase-417 W4.e.
11199    ///
11200    /// `node_id == None` is the legacy nodeless path and behaves exactly as
11201    /// `register_guard_condition` always did. With a node, the registered slot
11202    /// takes that node's default `SchedContext`, which is what "the node owns
11203    /// it" has to mean for a callback that shares one executor with every other
11204    /// tier in the image (RFC-0047).
11205    pub fn register_guard_condition_on<F>(
11206        &mut self,
11207        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
11208        callback: F,
11209    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
11210    where
11211        F: FnMut() + 'static,
11212    {
11213        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
11214        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<GuardConditionEntry<F>>()?;
11215
11216        unsafe {
11217            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11218            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut GuardConditionEntry<F>;
11219            core::ptr::write(
11220                entry_ptr,
11221                GuardConditionEntry {
11222                    flag: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
11223                    callback,
11224                },
11225            );
11226
11227            // Create a handle pointing to the flag in the arena
11228            let flag_ptr = &(*entry_ptr).flag as *const portable_atomic::AtomicBool;
11229            #[allow(unused_mut)]
11230            let mut guard_handle = GuardCondition::new(flag_ptr);
11231            // Phase 124.B.5 — wire the wake callback so trigger()
11232            // also signals the executor's wake_cv.
11233            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
11234            {
11235                let ctx = self.wake_ctx_ptr();
11236                guard_handle.set_wake_cb(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb, ctx);
11237                self.has_cross_thread_waker = true;
11238            }
11239
11240            let meta = CallbackMeta {
11241                offset,
11242                kind: EntryKind::GuardCondition,
11243                arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
11244                try_process: guard_try_process::<F>,
11245                has_data: guard_has_data::<F>,
11246                pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
11247                invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
11248                drop_fn: drop_entry::<GuardConditionEntry<F>>,
11249            };
11250            self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Slot("guard", slot));
11251            self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
11252
11253            Ok((self.handle_for(slot), guard_handle))
11254        }
11255    }
11256
11257    /// phase-467 Row 8 — a guard condition the BACKEND triggers when the ROS
11258    /// graph changes. Upstream's `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition`, under
11259    /// this project's guard-condition shape.
11260    ///
11261    /// **The verb is upstream's, the shape is ours, and the difference is
11262    /// stated rather than silent.** `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition`
11263    /// RETURNS a borrowed handle to a guard the node owns, which the caller
11264    /// then adds to a wait set. RFC-0018/0019 forbids returning an owned
11265    /// handle across the C seam, we decline wait sets (RFC-0002: one executor
11266    /// per RTOS task), and a guard condition here is created into CALLER
11267    /// storage with its callback bound at creation. So this CREATES one —
11268    /// exactly as [`register_guard_condition_on`] does — and differs from it
11269    /// only in who pulls the trigger.
11270    ///
11271    /// Order matters and is the reason this is one verb rather than two. The
11272    /// backend is asked whether it HAS a graph before a handle slot is
11273    /// consumed, so a caller on XRCE or uORB gets `Unsupported` and an
11274    /// unchanged executor, never a guard condition nothing will ever fire.
11275    ///
11276    /// [`register_guard_condition_on`]: Self::register_guard_condition_on
11277    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
11278    pub fn register_graph_change_guard_on<F>(
11279        &mut self,
11280        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
11281        callback: F,
11282    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
11283    where
11284        F: FnMut() + 'static,
11285    {
11286        // The probe FIRST — see the doc comment. `supports_*` asks by
11287        // clearing, which is idempotent and costs nothing.
11288        if !self.supports_graph_change_callback() {
11289            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported));
11290        }
11291        let (handle_id, guard) = self.register_guard_condition_on(node_id, callback)?;
11292        self.install_graph_change_guard(&guard)?;
11293        Ok((handle_id, guard))
11294    }
11295
11296    /// The nodeless form of
11297    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`](Self::register_graph_change_guard_on),
11298    /// for an image with a session and no node — the same pairing
11299    /// [`register_guard_condition`](Self::register_guard_condition) has.
11300    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
11301    pub fn register_graph_change_guard<F>(
11302        &mut self,
11303        callback: F,
11304    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
11305    where
11306        F: FnMut() + 'static,
11307    {
11308        self.register_graph_change_guard_on(None, callback)
11309    }
11310
11311    /// The same two verbs on a build with no `rmw-cffi` backend seam, or no
11312    /// allocator — they REFUSE rather than disappear.
11313    ///
11314    /// The cfg'd-out spelling was the first shape and it was wrong in a way
11315    /// `just check fast` cannot see: `rclc_node_get_graph_guard_condition` is
11316    /// a C ABI symbol and calls this unconditionally, so a feature
11317    /// combination without the seam stopped `nros-c` from COMPILING
11318    /// (`check-build`'s `workspace-features`, which is the lane that unifies
11319    /// nothing and therefore sees each combination as a user would).
11320    ///
11321    /// Refusing is also the honest answer rather than a compile fix. The
11322    /// graph-change edge is installed on a SESSION through the backend seam;
11323    /// without that seam there is no backend to install it on, and the
11324    /// executor-owned target needs an allocator for the box the backend holds
11325    /// a pointer to. `Unsupported` is what a caller gets from a backend with
11326    /// no graph too, so the C entry point answers `RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED` in
11327    /// both cases and a ported program sees one behaviour, not two.
11328    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
11329    pub fn register_graph_change_guard_on<F>(
11330        &mut self,
11331        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
11332        callback: F,
11333    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
11334    where
11335        F: FnMut() + 'static,
11336    {
11337        let _ = (node_id, callback);
11338        Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported))
11339    }
11340
11341    /// The nodeless form on a build with no backend seam — see
11342    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`](Self::register_graph_change_guard_on).
11343    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
11344    pub fn register_graph_change_guard<F>(
11345        &mut self,
11346        callback: F,
11347    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
11348    where
11349        F: FnMut() + 'static,
11350    {
11351        self.register_graph_change_guard_on(None, callback)
11352    }

11354    // ========================================================================
11355    // Timer control methods
11356    // ========================================================================
11357
11358    /// Cancel a timer. A cancelled timer will not fire but still accumulates
11359    /// elapsed time. The timer can be restarted with [`reset_timer()`](Self::reset_timer).
11360    ///
11361    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- while the timer's callback runs in another
11362    /// thread's window, the cancel is recorded and applied when it returns.
11363    pub fn cancel_timer(&mut self, id: HandleId) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
11364        if self.defer_timer_op(id, super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING)? {
11365            return Ok(());
11366        }
11367        let meta = self
11368            .entries
11369            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11370            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11371            .ok_or(NodeError::BufferTooSmall)?;
11372        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
11373            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
11374        }
11375        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11376        // SAFETY: meta.offset points to a valid TimerEntry<F> which shares
11377        // layout with TimerHeader for its initial fields (both #[repr(C)]).
11378        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
11379        header.cancelled = true;
11380        Ok(())
11381    }
11382
11383    /// Reset a timer. Clears the cancelled state and resets the elapsed time
11384    /// to zero, so the timer starts a fresh period.
11385    ///
11386    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- deferred like [`Self::cancel_timer`].
11387    pub fn reset_timer(&mut self, id: HandleId) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
11388        if self.defer_timer_op(id, super::types::SlotTag::RESET_PENDING)? {
11389            return Ok(());
11390        }
11391        let meta = self
11392            .entries
11393            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11394            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11395            .ok_or(NodeError::BufferTooSmall)?;
11396        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
11397            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
11398        }
11399        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11400        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
11401        header.cancelled = false;
11402        header.elapsed_us = 0;
11403        // Issue 1974 — a CLOCK timer advances by `now - last_clock_ns`, and a
11404        // cancelled timer is not polled, so its last reading is from when it
11405        // was cancelled (or, for `autostart = false`, registered). Without a
11406        // re-seed the first poll after this reset would credit the whole
11407        // cancelled interval as one step and fire at once — "a fresh period"
11408        // would hold for wall timers only. `Steady` reads no clock; its seed
11409        // stays 0 and is never read.
11410        header.last_clock_ns = header.clock_source.now_ns();
11411        Ok(())
11412    }
11413
11414    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- record a cancel (`op` = `CANCEL_PENDING`) or a
11415    /// reset (`RESET_PENDING`) of the timer `id` when its callback runs in
11416    /// another thread's window, and answer `true`; `false` when it is not,
11417    /// and the caller applies the operation now. The later of the two wins.
11418    fn defer_timer_op(&mut self, id: HandleId, op: u8) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
11419        let Some(slot) = self.resolve_handle(id) else {
11420            return Ok(false);
11421        };
11422        if !self.running_elsewhere(slot) {
11423            return Ok(false);
11424        }
11425        if !self.entries[slot]
11426            .as_ref()
11427            .is_some_and(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))
11428        {
11429            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
11430        }
11431        let tag = &self.slot_tags[slot];
11432        tag.clear(super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING | super::types::SlotTag::RESET_PENDING);
11433        tag.set(op);
11434        Ok(true)
11435    }
11436
11437    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- apply the cancel or reset deferred while the
11438    /// timer in `slot` ran (`defer_timer_op`). Under the lock, its callback
11439    /// returned.
11440    fn apply_deferred_timer_op(&mut self, slot: usize) {
11441        let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(slot) else {
11442            return;
11443        };
11444        let was =
11445            tag.clear(super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING | super::types::SlotTag::RESET_PENDING);
11446        if was & (super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING | super::types::SlotTag::RESET_PENDING) == 0
11447        {
11448            return;
11449        }
11450        let id = self.handle_for(slot);
11451        if was & super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING != 0 {
11452            let _ = self.cancel_timer(id);
11453        } else {
11454            let _ = self.reset_timer(id);
11455        }
11456    }
11457
11458    /// Check if a timer is cancelled.
11459    ///
11460    /// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- a cancel or reset still pending behind the
11461    /// timer's running callback is the answer, as if it had applied.
11462    pub fn timer_is_canceled(&self, id: HandleId) -> bool {
11463        if let Some(slot) = self.resolve_handle(id)
11464            && self.running_elsewhere(slot)
11465        {
11466            let f = self.slot_tags[slot].flags();
11467            if f & super::types::SlotTag::CANCEL_PENDING != 0 {
11468                return true;
11469            }
11470            if f & super::types::SlotTag::RESET_PENDING != 0 {
11471                return false;
11472            }
11473        }
11474        // `resolve_handle`, not `live_slot`: a running callback's dispatch
11475        // never writes `cancelled` (only `cancel_timer` / `reset_timer` do,
11476        // and they are deferred while it runs elsewhere), so the flag is read
11477        // as a plain field, through a raw pointer, with no reference to the
11478        // entry the callback holds.
11479        let meta = match self
11480            .entries
11481            .get(self.resolve_handle(id).unwrap_or(usize::MAX))
11482            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11483        {
11484            Some(m) if matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer) => m,
11485            _ => return false,
11486        };
11487        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11488        // SAFETY: `meta.offset` is this live entry's slot inside the arena.
11489        let header = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader };
11490        // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot starts with its `TimerHeader`;
11491        // see above for why the read races no write.
11492        unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*header).cancelled).read() }
11493    }
11494
11495    /// Get the period of a timer in milliseconds (truncated — see
11496    /// [`Self::timer_period_us`]), or `None` if the handle is not a
11497    /// valid timer.
11498    pub fn timer_period_ms(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u64> {
11499        let meta = self
11500            .entries
11501            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11502            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11503            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
11504        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11505        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
11506        Some(header.period_us / 1000)
11507    }
11508
11509    /// Get the period of a timer in microseconds, or `None` if the
11510    /// handle is not a valid timer.
11511    pub fn timer_period_us(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u64> {
11512        let meta = self
11513            .entries
11514            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11515            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11516            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
11517        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11518        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_ms`.
11519        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
11520        Some(header.period_us)
11521    }
11522
11523    /// Which clock advances this timer, or `None` if the handle is not a valid
11524    /// timer.
11525    ///
11526    /// issue 1975 — the state `rclcpp::TimerBase::get_clock()` reports. The
11527    /// header field is the one `arena::timer_try_process` reads, so the answer
11528    /// is the dispatcher's own rather than a copy a wrapper kept beside it: a
11529    /// wall timer answers [`TimerClockSource::Steady`], a clock timer the
11530    /// source it was registered with.
11531    pub fn timer_clock_source(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<TimerClockSource> {
11532        let meta = self
11533            .entries
11534            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11535            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11536            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
11537        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11538        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
11539        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
11540        Some(header.clock_source)
11541    }
11542
11543    /// Swap a registered timer's period, in microseconds, returning the one
11544    /// it had — or `None` if the handle is not a valid timer.
11545    ///
11546    /// `TimerHeader::period_us` is the number `arena::timer_try_process`
11547    /// compares `elapsed_us` against, so this writes the period the
11548    /// DISPATCHER honours rather than a second copy of it (RFC-0019). The C
11549    /// entry point `rcl_timer_exchange_period` also keeps
11550    /// `rcl_timer_t::period_ns` in step, because that field is the
11551    /// registration input a later `rclc_executor_add_timer` would re-read.
11552    ///
11553    /// `elapsed_us` is deliberately NOT rewound, which is rcl's own behaviour:
11554    /// `rcl_timer_exchange_period` swaps the period and touches nothing else,
11555    /// so a timer shortened below its accumulated elapsed time becomes ready
11556    /// at once and one lengthened past it simply waits longer. A caller that
11557    /// wants the new period to start fresh calls
11558    /// [`reset_timer`](Self::reset_timer) after it.
11559    ///
11560    /// phase-417 W5.c — the Rust half of `c:timer_exchange_period`, the last
11561    /// timer row the C ledger filed as `gap`. The answer lives here and only
11562    /// the spelling lives in the wrapper, the same split
11563    /// [`timer_elapsed_us`](Self::timer_elapsed_us) made.
11564    pub(crate) fn exchange_timer_period_us(
11565        &mut self,
11566        id: HandleId,
11567        new_period_us: u64,
11568    ) -> Option<u64> {
11569        let offset = self
11570            .entries
11571            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11572            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11573            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?
11574            .offset;
11575        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11576        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
11577        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
11578        let old_period_us = header.period_us;
