11579        header.period_us = new_period_us;
11580        Some(old_period_us)
11581    }
11582
11583    /// Set a timer's overrun policy (issue #505). Timers default to
11584    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::Skip`]; switch to
11585    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::CatchUp`] for timers whose every activation
11586    /// is a unit of work that must not be lost.
11587    pub fn set_timer_overrun_policy(
11588        &mut self,
11589        id: HandleId,
11590        policy: TimerOverrunPolicy,
11591    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
11592        let meta = self
11593            .entries
11594            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11595            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11596            .ok_or(NodeError::BufferTooSmall)?;
11597        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
11598            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
11599        }
11600        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11601        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `cancel_timer`.
11602        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
11603        header.overrun_policy = policy;
11604        Ok(())
11605    }
11606
11607    /// Periods this timer missed and dropped under
11608    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::Skip`] (issue #505), or `None` if the handle
11609    /// is not a valid timer.
11610    ///
11611    /// Monotonic and saturating. A growing count is the on-target signal
11612    /// that a tier is not keeping up with its declared cadence — the
11613    /// symptom an external observer would otherwise have to infer by
11614    /// differencing timestamps.
11615    pub fn timer_overruns(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u32> {
11616        let meta = self
11617            .entries
11618            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11619            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11620            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
11621        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11622        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
11623        Some(header.overruns)
11624    }
11625
11626    /// Microseconds accumulated since this timer last fired, or `None` if the
11627    /// handle is not a valid timer.
11628    ///
11629    /// This is `TimerHeader::elapsed_us` — the SAME counter
11630    /// `arena::timer_try_process` compares against the period and rewinds on
11631    /// every activation, so it is the executor's own answer rather than a
11632    /// second one derived from a clock. `None` is not "zero elapsed": a caller
11633    /// that cannot tell them apart reports a timer that has just fired and a
11634    /// handle that is not a timer identically.
11635    ///
11636    /// phase-417 W5.c — added because the state was already here and nothing
11637    /// exposed it, which is why `c:timer_get_time_since_last_call` and
11638    /// `c:timer_is_ready` were both filed as gaps. The C forwarders
11639    /// (`rcl_timer_get_time_since_last_call`, `nros_timer_is_ready`) read
11640    /// this; RFC-0019 puts the answer in Rust and only the spelling in the
11641    /// wrapper.
11642    pub(crate) fn timer_elapsed_us(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u64> {
11643        let meta = self
11644            .entries
11645            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11646            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11647            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
11648        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11649        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
11650        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
11651        Some(header.elapsed_us)
11652    }
11653
11654    /// Would this timer fire on the next dispatch pass? `None` if the handle
11655    /// is not a valid timer.
11656    ///
11657    /// The predicate is `arena::timer_try_process`'s own guard, in the same
11658    /// order: a cancelled timer is never ready, a one-shot that already fired
11659    /// is never ready again, and otherwise readiness is `elapsed >= period`.
11660    /// Keeping the two in one shape is the point — a readiness answer that
11661    /// disagrees with the dispatcher is worse than no answer at all.
11662    pub(crate) fn timer_is_ready(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<bool> {
11663        let meta = self
11664            .entries
11665            .get(self.live_slot(id))
11666            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
11667            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
11668        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
11669        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
11670        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
11671        if header.cancelled || (header.oneshot && header.fired) {
11672            return Some(false);
11673        }
11674        Some(header.elapsed_us >= header.period_us)
11675    }
11676
11677    /// Nanoseconds until this timer next fires — NEGATIVE when it is overdue.
11678    /// `None` if the handle is not a valid timer.
11679    ///
11680    /// phase-417 G6. THE computation, and it has to be: rcl's own pair are
11681    /// `next_call_time` and `next_call_time - now`, so upstream cannot have
11682    /// them disagree either. Before this it lived in `nros-c`
11683    /// (`remaining_period_ns` + `time_until_next_call_ns_of`), and the C++
11684    /// half of `cpp:Timer::time_until_trigger` would have been a second
11685    /// derivation of the same subtraction in a second crate — the shape
11686    /// CLAUDE.md's "fix the CLASS, add ONE shared helper rather than a second
11687    /// spelling" rule names. `nros-c` forwards here now; so does `nros-cpp`.
11688    ///
11689    /// **The unit is nanoseconds and the RESOLUTION is microseconds.** The
11690    /// arena's timer accounting is microsecond-based (issue #505), so this is a
11691    /// microsecond quantity scaled by 1000. The unit is rcl's; the resolution
11692    /// is ours.
11693    ///
11694    /// Saturating rather than wrapping: `period_us` and `elapsed_us` are both
11695    /// `u64`, so their difference in nanoseconds can leave `i64` in either
11696    /// direction, and a wrap would turn "overdue by a lot" into "due in a
11697    /// long time" — the sign is the whole answer here.
11698    pub fn timer_time_until_next_call_ns(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<i64> {
11699        let period_us = self.timer_period_us(id)?;
11700        let elapsed_us = self.timer_elapsed_us(id)?;
11701        let delta_ns = (period_us as i128 - elapsed_us as i128).saturating_mul(1_000);
11702        Some(if delta_ns > i64::MAX as i128 {
11703            i64::MAX
11704        } else if delta_ns < i64::MIN as i128 {
11705            i64::MIN
11706        } else {
11707            delta_ns as i64
11708        })
11709    }
11710
11711    // ========================================================================
11712    // spin_once (three-phase: readiness -> trigger -> dispatch)
11713    // ========================================================================
11714
11715    /// Drive I/O and dispatch registered callbacks once.
11716    ///
11717    /// Three-phase execution:
11718    /// 1. **Readiness scan** — query each handle's `has_data()`.
11719    /// 2. **Trigger evaluation** — check if the executor-level trigger passes.
11720    /// 3. **Dispatch** — invoke callbacks according to their `InvocationMode`.
11721    ///
11722    /// Returns a [`SpinOnceResult`] with counts of processed items and errors.
11723    ///
11724    /// # Arguments
11725    /// * `timeout` — upper bound on the I/O wait. Saturated at
11726    ///   `i32::MAX` ms (~24 days) for the underlying transport call.
11727    ///
11728    /// Phase 84.D7: unified on `core::time::Duration`. The previous
11729    /// `timeout_ms: i32` signature had a latent footgun where
11730    /// `spin_once(-1)` silently froze timers while still polling I/O;
11731    /// `Duration` has no negative sentinel.
11732    /// Consecutive `drive_io` failures on the primary session (issue 0324).
11733    ///
11734    /// `0` means the last drive succeeded. A value that keeps climbing across
11735    /// spins is a session that is no longer doing I/O — router gone, lease
11736    /// expired, socket closed — which otherwise presents as a node that spins
11737    /// `Ok(())` forever while publishing nowhere and firing no callbacks.
11738    ///
11739    /// Transient failures happen, so a single non-zero reading is not a fault;
11740    /// a threshold (say, "more than a few consecutive spins") is the useful
11741    /// signal. Extra (bridge / multi-domain) sessions are best-effort and are
11742    /// deliberately NOT counted here.
11743    pub(crate) fn session_io_failures(&self) -> u32 {
11744        self.consecutive_io_failures
11745    }
11746
11747    /// Whether the primary session drove I/O successfully on the last spin.
11748    ///
11749    /// Convenience over [`ExecutorFfi::session_io_failures`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::session_io_failures) for the common
11750    /// "is my transport alive?" check.
11751    pub fn session_io_healthy(&self) -> bool {
11752        self.consecutive_io_failures == 0
11753    }
11754
11755    /// Drive I/O once, then dispatch EVERY callback that is ready — the tick
11756    /// primitive the rest of the family is built from.
11757    ///
11758    /// OURS-ONLY (RFC-0089): rclcpp's `spin_once` executes the NEXT ready item
11759    /// and has no timeout; rclpy's is `spin_once(node, timeout_sec)`. Ours is a
11760    /// blocking wait with a budget, which an RTOS task that must not spin-poll
11761    /// needs and which neither upstream has a verb for. What it DOES when work
11762    /// is ready is rclcpp's `spin_some` — the whole ready set, one pass
11763    /// (RFC-0002 §3) — so [`spin_some`](Self::spin_some) is the drain verb and
11764    /// this is the waiting one.
11765    ///
11766    /// `timeout` is the upper bound on the I/O wait. Since phase-436 W2 it is
11767    /// carried in MICROSECONDS all the way to the park (issue 1193 — an
11768    /// `as_millis()` here truncated `from_micros(500)` to `0`, and a zero
11769    /// timeout selects the non-blocking path, so a sub-millisecond `spin()`
11770    /// was a 100 % CPU loop with no warning); the conversion to whatever the
11771    /// platform primitive accepts happens once, at the park, and rounds UP.
11772    /// `Duration` has no negative sentinel, which is what the pre-phase-84
11773    /// `timeout_ms: i32` signature used to silently mean "freeze the timers
11774    /// and poll I/O forever".
11775    pub fn spin_once(&mut self, timeout: core::time::Duration) -> SpinOnceResult {
11776        let mut discarded = None;
11777        self.spin_once_capturing(timeout, &mut discarded)
11778    }
11779
11780    /// [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once), plus the FIRST failing callback's
11781    /// error.
11782    ///
11783    /// phase-427 — [`SpinOnceResult`] counts errors and drops their values,
11784    /// and `SpinOnceResult` is `Copy`, so widening it to carry a
11785    /// (non-`Copy`, `alloc`-variant-bearing) [`TransportError`] would change a
11786    /// public type every consumer copies. The value is needed in exactly one
11787    /// place — `SpinOptions::stop_on_first_error`, where `spin` has to return
11788    /// the first error rather than a count — so it is threaded out through an
11789    /// out-parameter that lives in the caller's frame. Nothing is added to
11790    /// `Executor`, so a no-alloc image pays nothing for it.
11791    ///
11792    /// `first_error` is written at most once: subsequent failures in the same
11793    /// pass are counted in the result and their values dropped, exactly as
11794    /// before.
11795    fn spin_once_capturing(
11796        &mut self,
11797        timeout: core::time::Duration,
11798        first_error: &mut Option<TransportError>,
11799    ) -> SpinOnceResult {
11800        // SAFETY: `self` is exclusive for the whole call, and an owned pass
11801        // never releases the executor's lock (`PassMode::Owned`), so nothing
11802        // else reaches the executor while it runs.
11803        unsafe { Self::pass(self, PassMode::Owned, timeout, first_error) }
11804    }
11805
11806    /// One pass, over a raw executor pointer (phase-509 P9b item 2, RFC-0108
11807    /// "As built in P9b"). See [`PassMode`]: an owned pass is the
11808    /// `spin_once` every image ran before; a shared pass releases the
11809    /// executor's lock around each user callback, and a band pass runs one
11810    /// worker's band.
11811    ///
11812    /// No `&mut Self` lives across a callback window: `s` is re-derived from
11813    /// `this` after each one, and nothing borrowed from the executor before a
11814    /// window is used after it.
11815    ///
11816    /// # Safety
11817    /// `this` points at a live executor. For `PassMode::Owned`, nothing else
11818    /// reaches it for the call. Otherwise the executor's lock is installed and
11819    /// held exactly once by the calling thread, and every other thread that
11820    /// reaches the executor takes the lock first.
11821    unsafe fn pass(
11822        this: *mut Self,
11823        mut mode: PassMode<'_>,
11824        timeout: core::time::Duration,
11825        first_error: &mut Option<TransportError>,
11826    ) -> SpinOnceResult {
11827        // SAFETY: the caller's contract; re-derived after every window.
11828        #[allow(unused_mut)]
11829        let mut s: &mut Self = unsafe { &mut *this };
11830        // Issue 1705 — releases deferred behind a dispatch that has since
11831        // finished are completed here, before this pass looks at the entries.
11832        s.reap_deferred_releases();
11833        // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the lock this pass releases around each
11834        // user callback (and, item 3, around its park): only a shared or band
11835        // pass, and only when the lock can tell the callback's thread from
11836        // the others. `None` -- an owned pass, or no lock -- runs the whole
11837        // pass under the caller's hold.
11838        let window_lock = match mode {
11839            PassMode::Owned => None,
11840            _ => s.exec_lock.filter(|l| l.opens_windows()),
11841        };
11842        // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the owned and shared passes run the
11843        // executor's own worker's prelude (sim time, services, jitter, the
11844        // park, the transport drive); a band pass runs its own clock and
11845        // (item 3) its own park.
11846        //
11847        // SAFETY: the caller's contract is the preludes'; `s` is not used
11848        // across the call and is derived again after it.
11849        let (now_us_this_spin, delta_us) = match &mut mode {
11850            PassMode::Band(w) => unsafe { Self::band_prelude(this, window_lock, w, timeout) },
11851            _ => unsafe { Self::owned_prelude(this, window_lock, timeout) },
11852        };
11853        // SAFETY: the prelude returns holding the lock again.
11854        s = unsafe { &mut *this };
11855        // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- this pass's band (every level for the
11856        // one-level worker) and its slots. The scan, the sweep and the drain
11857        // see only these, so a worker never takes another band's work.
11858        let (level, band) = match &mode {
11859            PassMode::Band(w) => (w.level, w.band),
11860            _ => (s.worker.level, s.worker.band),
11861        };
11862        let band_mask = s.band_slots(level, band);
11863        let is_band_pass = matches!(mode, PassMode::Band(_));
11864        let window_thread = window_lock.and_then(|l| l.current_thread()).unwrap_or(0);
11865
11866        let arena_ptr = s.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
11867
11868        // Phase 1: Readiness scan (Phase 110.A.b — backed by FifoReadySet).
11869        //
11870        // `bits` carries data-readiness only (used by trigger eval +
11871        // by `InvocationMode::OnNewData`). `always_mask` carries the
11872        // `InvocationMode::Always` entries that fire regardless of
11873        // data presence. The dispatcher drains `bits | always_mask`
11874        // after the trigger passes. phase-509 P2 -- in dispatch-level
11875        // order (the sched context's bucket, and inside `Normal` the
11876        // node's rank), registration order (lowest bit first) among
11877        // equals, so an image whose nodes hold one rank is bit-identical
11878        // to the pre-refactor `for (i, meta) in entries.iter().enumerate()`
11879        // loop.
11880        let mut bits: u64 = 0;
11881        let mut count: usize = 0;
11882        let mut non_timer_mask: u64 = 0;
11883        let mut always_mask: u64 = 0;
11884
11885        // phase-397 W3 (RFC-0084) — an ATTRIBUTED slot's readiness is pushed,
11886        // not probed. Its arrivals set its bit in the ready word (W2), so the
11887        // bit is read and `has_data` is not called. Three cases still ask:
11888        //
11889        // - a slot in `entity_recheck`, which may hold data no arrival will
11890        //   announce again (see the field);
11891        // - a subscription with a status-event callback (issue 2060,
11892        //   `entity_status_polled`), whose backend polls those events there;
11893        // - a slot whose backend cannot attribute (XRCE, uORB, a timer, a
11894        //   guard condition), exactly as before.
11895        //
11896        // The bit means the data ARRIVED, not that it is still PRESENT: an
11897        // arrival that races a drain may dispatch to an empty queue, and every
11898        // `try_process` already answers `Ok(false)` to that. A bit cleared
11899        // before its dispatch would lose a message; one that over-reports
11900        // costs one empty call.
11901        //
11902        // The word is taken AFTER the wait and the drive above, so it holds
11903        // every arrival that ended this spin's park, including those a
11904        // single-threaded backend delivered inside `drive_io`. One that lands
11905        // after the take stays in the word and has signalled the wake, so the
11906        // next spin does not park on it.
11907        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
11908        let (attributed, arrived, recheck) = {
11909            let attributed = s.entity_attributed;
11910            // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- only this band's arrivals: another
11911            // band's bits stay in the word for its worker.
11912            let arrived = s
11913                .wake_ctx
11914                .as_ref()
11915                .map_or(0, |ctx| take_band_bits(&ctx.ready, band_mask));
11916            let recheck = s.entity_recheck & band_mask;
11917            s.entity_recheck &= !band_mask;
11918            // Issue 2060 — a slot whose status events are polled from
11919            // `has_data` is asked every pass, like a recheck that never
11920            // drains. It is folded in AFTER the clear, so it never leaks into
11921            // `entity_recheck` and leaves the moment its entry is released.
11922            let recheck = recheck | (s.entity_status_polled & band_mask);
11923            (attributed, arrived & attributed, recheck & attributed)
11924        };
11925        #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
11926        let (attributed, arrived, recheck) = (0u64, 0u64, 0u64);
11927        // Attributed slots the scan could not settle (held mid-dispatch).
11928        let mut carry: u64 = 0;
11929        let mut probes: u32 = 0;
11930
11931        for (i, meta) in s.entries.iter().enumerate() {
11932            let Some(meta) = meta else { continue };
11933            let bit = 1u64 << i;
11934            if band_mask & bit == 0 {
11935                continue;
11936            }
11937            if Self::slot_held(s.slot_tags, i) {
11938                carry |= (arrived | recheck) & bit;
11939                continue;
11940            }
11941            {
11942                let pushed = attributed & bit != 0;
11943                let ready = if pushed && arrived & bit != 0 {
11944                    true
11945                } else if pushed && recheck & bit == 0 {
11946                    false
11947                } else {
11948                    probes = probes.wrapping_add(1);
11949                    let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const u8 };
11950                    unsafe { (meta.has_data)(data_ptr) }
11951                };
11952                if ready {
11953                    bits |= bit;
11954                }
11955                if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer | EntryKind::GuardCondition) {
11956                    non_timer_mask |= 1u64 << i;
11957                }
11958                if matches!(meta.invocation, InvocationMode::Always) {
11959                    always_mask |= 1u64 << i;
11960                }
11961                count += 1;
11962            }
11963        }
11964        // Every attributed slot that was ready is asked again next spin: a
11965        // dispatch takes what one call takes, and a trigger that does not
11966        // pass dispatches nothing, so either may leave data behind.
11967        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
11968        {
11969            s.entity_recheck |= carry | (bits & attributed);
11970            s.readiness_probes = s.readiness_probes.wrapping_add(probes);
11971        }
11972        #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
11973        let _ = (carry, probes);
11974
11975        // phase-462 W5b — an armed deadline row's arrival evidence.
11976        if bits != 0 && !s.age_table.is_empty() {
11977            super::monitor::credit_arrivals(s.age_table, bits);
11978        }
11979
11980        let snapshot = ReadinessSnapshot { bits, count };
11981
11982        // Phase 2: Trigger evaluation
11983        let trigger_passes = match &s.trigger {
11984            Trigger::Any => bits & non_timer_mask != 0 || non_timer_mask == 0,
11985            Trigger::All => bits & non_timer_mask == non_timer_mask,
11986            Trigger::One(id) => snapshot.is_ready(*id),
11987            Trigger::AllOf(set) => snapshot.all_ready(*set),
11988            Trigger::AnyOf(set) => snapshot.any_ready(*set),
11989            Trigger::Always => true,
11990            Trigger::Predicate(f) => f(&snapshot),
11991            Trigger::RawPredicate { callback, context } => {
11992                // Convert ReadinessSnapshot bitmask to a bool array for the C callback
11993                let mut ready_array = [false; 64];
11994                for (i, slot) in ready_array
11995                    .iter_mut()
11996                    .enumerate()
11997                    .take(snapshot.count.min(64))
11998                {
11999                    *slot = snapshot.bits & (1u64 << i) != 0;
12000                }
12001                // SAFETY: The callback and context are provided by the C API caller.
12002                // The ready_array is valid for snapshot.count elements.
12003                unsafe { callback(ready_array.as_ptr(), snapshot.count, *context) }
12004            }
12005        };
12006
12007        if !trigger_passes {
12008            // Timers still need delta accumulation even when trigger doesn't pass
12009            //
12010            // phase-8 — `.enumerate()` (rather than a bare `.flatten()`) because
12011            // `try_process` now carries the entry's slot index for the callback
12012            // trace hooks. This sweep FIRES timer callbacks, so it is a real
12013            // dispatch path and must attribute them like the drain below does.
12014            //
12015            // phase-474 I6 -- and it must TIME them like the drain does. This
12016            // is the path every timer takes on a node that also subscribes
12017            // (the default `Trigger::Any` fails whenever no subscription has
12018            // a sample), and it measured nothing, so `max-latency-runtime`
12019            // never judged a timer path: the safety island's 250 ms overrun of
12020            // a 206 ms path stored no verdict. One clock read before and one
12021            // after each timer's `try_process`, only when a latency contract
12022            // exists and a clock is injected; the publish-count snapshot is a
12023            // fixed array on the stack, nothing allocates. The measured span
12024            // is callback entry to exit, as in the drains; release jitter is
12025            // `release-jitter-runtime`'s.
12026            let mon_table = s.monitor_table;
12027            // phase10-B3 -- the route rule reads the same clock and snapshot:
12028            // a timer tick is where a sampled route's output is published.
12029            let lat_clock = s.clock_us_fn.filter(|_| {
12030                mon_table.iter().any(|m| m.max_latency_ms > 0)
12031                    || super::monitor::route_active(mon_table)
12032            });
12033            for i in 0..s.entries.len() {
12034                let Some(meta) = s.entries[i].as_ref() else {
12035                    continue;
12036                };
12037                if matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer)
12038                    && band_mask & (1u64 << i) != 0
12039                    && !Self::slot_held(s.slot_tags, i)
12040                {
12041                    let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) };
12042                    let try_process = meta.try_process;
12043                    let counts_before = snapshot_pub_counts(mon_table, lat_clock.is_some());
12044                    let start_us = lat_clock.map(|c| c());
12045                    Self::begin_dispatch(s.slot_tags, i);
12046                    // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the callback window: see the
12047                    // drain below.
12048                    let mut rec = super::exec_lock::Running {
12049                        slot: i,
12050                        thread: window_thread,
12051                        next: core::ptr::null_mut(),
12052                    };
12053                    let window = window_lock.map(|l| {
12054                        // SAFETY: `rec` outlives the window and is unlinked
12055                        // under the lock right after it.
12056                        unsafe { s.link_running(&mut rec) };
12057                        super::exec_lock::Window::open(l)
12058                    });
12059                    // phase-463 W7 -- the host profile times this sweep too:
12060                    // it is the path every timer of a node that also
12061                    // subscribes takes (see above), so missing it measured
12062                    // the talker's timer at zero invocations.
12063                    //
12064                    // The OFF arm is the original `let _ =`, untouched, and
12065                    // that is MEASURED rather than tidy: every binding tried
12066                    // in its place (`let _p`, `let p; drop(p)`) moved
12067                    // `spin_once_capturing` by 49-64 B in the Zephyr image
12068                    // (phase-463 W5 I3c). Hence the second `unsafe` block,
12069                    // recorded in the unsafe census.
12070                    #[cfg(not(feature = "profile-mode"))]
12071                    let _ = unsafe { try_process(data_ptr, delta_us, i as u8) };
12072                    #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
12073                    {
12074                        super::profile::dispatch_begin(arena_ptr as usize, i);
12075                        let processed = unsafe { try_process(data_ptr, delta_us, i as u8) };
12076                        super::profile::dispatch_end(matches!(processed, Ok(true)));
12077                    }
12078                    // Read before the lock is taken back, so a wait for it
12079                    // is not counted as the callback's latency.
12080                    let swept_end_us = start_us.and(lat_clock).map(|c| c());
12081                    if let Some(w) = window {
12082                        drop(w);
12083                        // SAFETY: the lock is held again; nothing borrowed
12084                        // from the executor before the window is used after.
12085                        s = unsafe { &mut *this };
12086                        s.unlink_running(&mut rec);
12087                    }
12088                    if let (Some(end_us), Some(t0)) = (swept_end_us, start_us) {
12089                        let elapsed_us = end_us.saturating_sub(t0).min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32;
12090                        attribute_latency(mon_table, true, &counts_before, elapsed_us);
12091                        let hook = s.reaction_hook.filter(|_| s.violations.counts.armed);
12092                        let violations = &mut s.violations;
12093                        super::monitor::route_judge(
12094                            mon_table,
12095                            &counts_before,
12096                            end_us,
12097                            |row, v, record, react| {
12098                                if react {
12099                                    call_route_reaction(hook, mon_table, row, &v);
12100                                }
12101                                if record {
12102                                    violations.record(v)
12103                                }
12104                            },
12105                        );
12106                    }
12107                    s.finish_dispatch(i);
12108                }
12109            }
12110
12111            // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the executor-wide chores below are the
12112            // executor's own worker's. Issue 2020 -- the band's own
12113            // components' ticks are the band's.
12114            if is_band_pass {
12115                // SAFETY: the pass's contract; `s` is not used after it.
12116                unsafe { Self::tick_components(this, Some(level)) };
12117                return SpinOnceResult::new();
12118            }
12119
12120            // Parameter services live outside the arena and must be processed
12121            // regardless of trigger state, otherwise ROS 2 param queries time out.
12122            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
12123            {
12124                #[allow(unused_mut)] // only the services add to it
12125                let mut handled = 0usize;
12126                #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
12127                if let Some(params) = &mut s.params {
12128                    {
12129                        let crate::param_store::ParamState {
12130                            server,
12131                            services,
12132                            buffers,
12133                            staged,
12134                            ..
12135                        } = &mut **params;
12136                        // phase-426 W3 — one set per node; every set is pumped,
12137                        // because `ros2 param list` addresses each node's own
12138                        // six and a set nobody polls times out.
12139                        //
12140                        // Issue 1270 -- all of them through ONE buffer pair.
12141                        // Issue 1271 -- a request that got no reply is logged
12142                        // inside, once per service; there is no error to drop.
12143                        if let Some(buffers) = buffers {
12144                            for set in services.iter_mut() {
12145                                handled += set.process(server, staged, buffers);
12146                            }
12147                        }
12148                    }
12149                }
12150                // phase-425 W3b — a `ros2 param set … use_sim_time true` arrives
12151                // through this path.
12152                s.note_param_services_ran(handled);
12153            }
12154
12155            // Same treatment for lifecycle services — `ros2 lifecycle get`
12156            // must succeed even when no callbacks fired this tick.
12157            //
12158            // Issue 1587 — `process` also drains the state machine's
12159            // announcement queue onto `~/transition_event`, so a transition
12160            // triggered from application code between two spins (autostart is
12161            // the common one) reaches a watching supervisor here.
12162            // SAFETY: see the matching invariant on the later call site.
12163            #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
12164            if let Some(lc) = &mut s.lifecycle {
12165                let _ = unsafe { lc.process() };
12166            }
12167
12168            // phase-474 I7 -- an idle spin is the natural slot for the queued
12169            // reports.
12170            s.flush_violation_reports();
12171
12172            return SpinOnceResult::new();
12173        }
12174
12175        // Phase 2.5: LET pre-sample (only when LogicalExecutionTime)
12176        //
12177        // Sample all subscription data into entry buffers BEFORE dispatching
12178        // any callbacks. This ensures all callbacks in this cycle see a
12179        // consistent snapshot of data from the same point in time.
12180        // Services are NOT pre-sampled (request-reply is sequential).
12181        if matches!(s.semantics, ExecutorSemantics::LogicalExecutionTime) {
12182            for (i, meta) in s.entries.iter().enumerate() {
12183                let Some(meta) = meta else { continue };
12184                if matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription)
12185                    && band_mask & (1u64 << i) != 0
12186                    && !Self::slot_held(s.slot_tags, i)
12187                {
12188                    let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) };
12189                    unsafe { (meta.pre_sample)(data_ptr) };
12190                }
12191            }
12192        }
12193
12194        // Phase 3: Dispatch (Phase 110.C — bucketed by SC.priority).
12195        //
12196        // Two ready-set families, each split across `Priority::COUNT`
12197        // buckets (Critical / Normal / BestEffort). Per-entry SC
12198        // `class` selects FIFO bitmap vs EDF heap; SC `priority`
12199        // selects the bucket within. Drain order:
12200        //   for each bucket in priority order (Critical first):
12201        //     drain EDF heap (deadline-priority), then FIFO bitmap
12202        //     (registration-order)
12203        // Default workloads — every entry on the auto-default Fifo SC
12204        // (Normal priority) — populate only `fifo[Normal]`, so
12205        // dispatch order is bit-identical to 110.B.b for those.
12206        const NB: usize = super::sched_context::Priority::COUNT;
12207        let mut result = SpinOnceResult::new();
12208        // phase-509 P2 (RFC-0108 D2) -- the FIFO half is ordered by dispatch
12209        // level: a bucket's reserved level, or `1 + rank` inside `Normal`, the
12210        // rank being the one the entry's node was seeded with. Equal levels
12211        // keep registration order, so an image with one rank is unchanged.
12212        let mut fifo: super::ready_set::RankedFifoSet<{ MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS }> =
12213            super::ready_set::RankedFifoSet::new();
12214        let mut edf: super::ready_set::BucketedEdfSet<NB, { MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS }> =
12215            super::ready_set::BucketedEdfSet::new();
12216        let active_mask = bits | always_mask;
12217
12218        // Phase 110.E — refill any Sporadic SC budgets at period
12219        // boundaries before deciding what to dispatch this cycle.
12220        // Refill is polled (not ISR-driven) — coarse but correct
12221        // upper-bound bandwidth limiter.
12222        // phase-359 W4 — was `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` with NO no_std arm, so
12223        // polled Sporadic budgets never refilled on embedded: they exhausted
12224        // once and stayed exhausted. That was a consequence of "no clock on
12225        // no_std", which is false whenever a `clock_us` hook is injected. Now it
12226        // runs on either flavour when a clock exists, and is skipped when none
12227        // does — identical to today's behaviour in that case.
12228        if let Some(now_us) = now_us_this_spin {
12229            let now_ms = now_us / 1000;
12230            // issue 0736 — REFILL only. This used to also charge the cycle's
12231            // `delta_us` as the per-SC consumption estimate ("worst-case
12232            // attribution", pending a higher-precision clock hook). That hook
12233            // landed, and the attribution was not merely coarse: `delta_us` is
12234            // the wall-clock gap between spins, not CPU the callbacks spent, so
12235            // wherever the gap exceeds the budget the SC is exhausted on every
12236            // spin regardless of what it ran. Consumption is charged from
12237            // measured callback runtime in `consume_dispatch_runtime_us`.
12238            for slot in s.sporadic_states.iter_mut().flatten() {
12239                let _ = slot.refill(now_ms);
12240            }
12241        }
12242
12243        for i in 0..s.entries.len() {
12244            if active_mask & (1u64 << i) == 0 {
12245                continue;
12246            }
12247            let sc_idx = s.sched_context_bindings[i].0 as usize;
12248            let sc_class_priority_deadline = s
12249                .sched_contexts
12250                .get(sc_idx)
12251                .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
12252                .map(|sc| {
12253                    (
12254                        sc.class,
12255                        sc.priority.index(),
12256                        sc.deadline_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
12257                    )
12258                });
12259            let (sc_class, bucket, deadline_us) = sc_class_priority_deadline.unwrap_or((
12260                super::sched_context::SchedClass::Fifo,
12261                super::sched_context::Priority::Normal.index(),
12262                u32::MAX,
12263            ));
12264            // Phase 110.E — Sporadic SC dispatch is suppressed when
12265            // its budget is exhausted. Atomic path (110.E.b PlatformTimer
12266            // refill) takes precedence when registered; polled path
12267            // (cycle-level delta_us attribution) handles the unregistered
12268            // case. Either way, exhausted budget skips dispatch.
12269            if matches!(sc_class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
12270                #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12271                let atomic_has_budget = s
12272                    .sporadic_atomic_states
12273                    .get(sc_idx)
12274                    .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
12275                    .map(|(state, _)| state.has_budget());
12276                #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
12277                let atomic_has_budget: Option<bool> = None;
12278                let has_budget = match atomic_has_budget {
12279                    Some(b) => b,
12280                    None => s
12281                        .sporadic_states
12282                        .get(sc_idx)
12283                        .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
12284                        .map(|s| s.budget_remaining_us > 0)
12285                        .unwrap_or(true),
12286                };
12287                if !has_budget {
12288                    // issue 0736 — keep the TIMER'S CLOCK honest even while the
12289                    // budget gates its dispatch.
12290                    //
12291                    // A timer's `elapsed_us` only advances inside
12292                    // `timer_try_process`, which is reached only when the entry
12293                    // is DISPATCHED, and each dispatch is handed just THIS
12294                    // cycle's `delta_us`. So every cycle skipped here was
12295                    // dropped from the timer's sense of time: it did not fire,
12296                    // it did not learn that its period had passed, and — because
12297                    // the overrun counter is driven by that same `elapsed_us` —
12298                    // it did not count the activation it missed.
12299                    //
12300                    // That is why the throttle was invisible. Measured on
12301                    // nuttx-arm/rust: ~238 activations lost against ~40
12302                    // reported, so five in six missed firings were unaccounted
12303                    // ANYWHERE. The tier ran at a quarter of its declared rate
12304                    // and the only honest signal was the delivery count itself.
12305                    //
12306                    // Advancing the clock here does not dispatch anything and
12307                    // does not defeat the budget. It makes the entry's own
12308                    // accounting independent of whether the executor CHOSE to
12309                    // run it, which is the property every "did this meet its
12310                    // declaration?" question needs, and it lets the existing
12311                    // `Skip` policy count the backlog and the existing
12312                    // `timer-overrun-runtime` rule report it.
12313                    if let Some(meta) = s.entries[i].as_ref()
12314                        && matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer)
12315                    {
12316                        // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a
12317                        // `TimerEntry<F>`, whose leading layout IS
12318                        // `TimerHeader` — the same cast the overrun reporter
12319                        // one screen up already relies on.
12320                        let header =
12321                            unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
12322                        // Issue 1321 — on the TIMER'S clock, not the
12323                        // executor's. This line read
12324                        // `header.elapsed_us += delta_us`, which is wall
12325                        // microseconds: for a `Ros` timer that advanced a
12326                        // simulated-time counter by wall time, so a paused
12327                        // `/clock` no longer paused the timer — the one
12328                        // property a ROS-time timer has. Unbounded, unlike
12329                        // 1321's park bound, because it can fire a callback
12330                        // that no clock step earned.
12331                        super::arena::timer_advance_without_dispatch(header, delta_us);
12332                    }
12333                    // issue 0736 — a budget skip used to be a bare `continue`,
12334                    // which is the silent-drop shape 0737 gated one layer out:
12335                    // the entry is simply not dispatched and nothing anywhere
12336                    // says so, so a permanently starved tier is
12337                    // indistinguishable from an idle one. It took a hand-run
12338                    // 45 s image and a per-executor probe to learn that this
12339                    // line was skipping 96 % of one tier's spins.
12340                    // The rolling window catches a budget that THROTTLES; the
12341                    // streak below catches one that starves outright. issue
12342                    // 0736 needed both: the measured case skipped ~3 spins in
12343                    // 4 without ever reaching a streak, so the tier ran at a
12344                    // quarter of its declared rate in silence.
12345                    if let Some((skips, total)) = s
12346                        .sporadic_states
12347                        .get_mut(sc_idx)
12348                        .and_then(|st| st.as_mut())
12349                        .and_then(|st| st.take_budget_window())
12350                    {
12351                        nros_log::log_warn!(
12352                            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
12353                            "sporadic budget throttled sched context {}: {} of the last {} dispatch opportunities were skipped for want of budget. The declared budget_us/period_us cannot sustain this tier's callbacks on this target.",
12354                            sc_idx,
12355                            skips,
12356                            total
12357                        );
12358                    }
12359                    if let Some(streak) = s
12360                        .sporadic_states
12361                        .get_mut(sc_idx)
12362                        .and_then(|st| st.as_mut())
12363                        .and_then(|st| st.note_budget_skip())
12364                    {
12365                        nros_log::log_warn!(
12366                            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
12367                            "sporadic budget exhausted for {} consecutive spins (sched context {}): its callbacks are not being dispatched. Either the callback runtime exceeds the declared budget_us per period_us, or the declaration is unsatisfiable on this target.",
12368                            streak,
12369                            sc_idx
12370                        );
12371                    }
12372                    continue;
12373                }
12374                // Phase 110.E.b follow-up — per-callback runtime
12375                // accounting (replaces this cycle-level attribution)
12376                // is applied at dispatch time below via
12377                // `consume_dispatch_runtime_us`. We only update the
12378                // polled-path `SporadicState` (no_std fallback) here
12379                // because the atomic path now records actual
12380                // wall-clock per-callback runtime. The
12381                // `delta_us` over-attribution that previously hit the
12382                // atomic state was a worst-case bandwidth limiter;
12383                // per-callback measurement is strictly tighter.
12384                #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
12385                {
12386                    let _ = sc_idx; // polled-state path lives in
12387                    // `sporadic_states`; this branch is a no-op when
12388                    // the atomic path is enabled.
12389                }
12390            }
12391            // Phase 110.G — TT window gate, orthogonal to class.
12392            // Skips dispatch when the SC has a TT window AND the
12393            // current monotonic time is outside it. Both gates apply
12394            // independently — a Sporadic SC with a TT window must
12395            // pass both.
12396            if s.major_frame_us > 0 {
12397                let sc_opt = s.sched_contexts.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref());
12398                if let Some(sc) = sc_opt {
12399                    let off = sc.tt_window_offset_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(0);
12400                    let dur = sc
12401                        .tt_window_duration_us
12402                        .get()
12403                        .map(|nz| nz.get())
12404                        .unwrap_or(0);
12405                    if dur > 0 {
12406                        // Compute current phase within the major
12407                        // frame using the accumulated `delta_us` clock
12408                        // (std-only precise; no_std uses `delta_us`
12409                        // approximation from spin cadence).
12410                        // phase-359 W4 — the shared read. The no_std arm used
12411                        // to be `now_us = delta_us`, i.e. a per-spin INTERVAL
12412                        // used as an absolute phase clock, which the comment
12413                        // above called an approximation. It is now the real
12414                        // clock when one is injected, and falls back to the old
12415                        // approximation only when none is.
12416                        let now_us = now_us_this_spin.unwrap_or(delta_us);
12417                        let phase = (now_us % s.major_frame_us as u64) as u32;
12418                        let in_window = if off + dur <= s.major_frame_us {
12419                            phase >= off && phase < off + dur
12420                        } else {
12421                            // Window wraps the major frame boundary.
12422                            let end = (off as u64 + dur as u64) % s.major_frame_us as u64;
12423                            phase >= off || (phase as u64) < end
12424                        };
12425                        if !in_window {
12426                            continue;
12427                        }
12428                    }
12429                }
12430            }
12431            let is_edf = matches!(sc_class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Edf);
12432            let job = super::types::ActiveJob {
12433                sort_key: if is_edf { deadline_us } else { i as u32 },
12434                desc_idx: i as super::types::DescIdx,
12435            };
12436            if is_edf {
12437                let _ = edf.insert_into(bucket, job);
12438            } else {
12439                let rank = s.slot_tags.get(i).map_or(0, |t| t.rank);
12440                let level = super::sched_context::Priority::from_index(bucket).dispatch_level(rank);
12441                // phase-509 P6 / P9b item 2 -- the scan saw only this pass's
12442                // band, so nothing it queued is another band's.
12443                debug_assert!(
12444                    s.worker.registering_level != super::scheduler::NO_OWNING_LEVEL
12445                        || band.contains(level)
12446                );
12447                let _ = fifo.insert_at(level, job);
12448            }
12449        }
12450        // phase-509 P3 -- every slot this pass has already settled: queued
12451        // above, or held back by a gate (budget, window, worker). A slot in
12452        // it never joins the pass again, so each entry runs at most once per
12453        // pass (a timer's clock advances by one `delta_us` per pass, and a
12454        // callback that readies itself cannot hold the pass forever).
12455        let mut settled: u64 = active_mask;
12456        // phase-509 P3 -- the LET semantics dispatch the pass's snapshot,
12457        // sampled before any callback ran; nothing joins it mid-pass.
12458        // A trigger narrower than "any" (`One`, `AllOf`, a predicate) chose
12459        // this pass's work from the scan; it stays the scan's.
12460        let repick = !matches!(s.semantics, ExecutorSemantics::LogicalExecutionTime)
12461            && matches!(s.trigger, Trigger::Any | Trigger::Always);
12462
12463        // SAFETY: each `desc_idx` we pop was set above only when the
12464        // corresponding `entries[i]` slot was `Some`; no Executor
12465        // mutation happens between that scan and this dispatch.
12466        let mut dispatch_one = |meta: &CallbackMeta,
12467                                desc_idx: usize,
12468                                arena_ptr: *mut u8,
12469                                delta_us: u64,
12470                                result: &mut SpinOnceResult| {
12471            // Phase 141.B.2 — capture T1 at subscription dispatch
12472            // entry. Probe pairs it with the most recent T0 from
12473            // `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb` (std + alloc variants)
12474            // and pushes `T1 - T0` onto the ring buffer 141.C
12475            // drains. No-op when the probe feature is off or
12476            // no cycle reader is installed. Other entry kinds
12477            // (Service / Timer / GuardCondition) skip the probe
12478            // because the 141 acceptance is specifically
12479            // wake-to-subscription-dispatch latency.
12480            #[cfg(feature = "wake-latency-probe")]
12481            if matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription) {
12482                super::wake_probe::on_dispatch();
12483            }
12484            let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) };
12485            // phase-8 — `desc_idx` is the entry slot index, threaded through so
12486            // the leaf hooks in `arena.rs` can name the callback they bracket.
12487            // `MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS` is 64 (enforced by the `u64` ready-set
12488            // bitmask), so the `as u8` cannot truncate a live slot.
12489            // phase-463 W7 — time the dispatch and attribute its publishes
12490            // (host `profile-mode` only). ONE call site for both builds, so no
12491            // second `unsafe` block; the binding is the only change an RTOS
12492            // image sees, and its loadable bytes measured identical (phase-463
12493            // W5 I3c, Zephyr cpp/talker).
12494            #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
12495            super::profile::dispatch_begin(arena_ptr as usize, desc_idx);
12496            let processed = unsafe { (meta.try_process)(data_ptr, delta_us, desc_idx as u8) };
12497            #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
12498            super::profile::dispatch_end(matches!(processed, Ok(true)));
12499            match processed {
12500                Ok(true) => match meta.kind {
12501                    EntryKind::Subscription => result.subscriptions_processed += 1,
12502                    EntryKind::Service
12503                    | EntryKind::ServiceClient
12504                    | EntryKind::ActionServer
12505                    | EntryKind::ActionClient => result.services_handled += 1,
12506                    EntryKind::Timer => result.timers_fired += 1,
12507                    EntryKind::GuardCondition => {}
12508                },
12509                Ok(false) => {}
12510                Err(e) => {
12511                    // phase-427 — the first one is kept, the rest are counted.
12512                    // `stop_on_first_error` is what reads it; when nobody
12513                    // asked, the `Option` is a local the optimiser drops.
12514                    if first_error.is_none() {
12515                        *first_error = Some(e);
12516                    }
12517                    match meta.kind {
12518                        EntryKind::Subscription => result.subscription_errors += 1,
12519                        EntryKind::Service
12520                        | EntryKind::ServiceClient
12521                        | EntryKind::ActionServer
12522                        | EntryKind::ActionClient => result.service_errors += 1,
12523                        EntryKind::Timer | EntryKind::GuardCondition => {}
12524                    }
12525                }
12526            }
12527        };
12528
12529        // Phase 110.E.b follow-up — per-callback runtime accounting
12530        // for Sporadic SCs. Wall-clock-measure each dispatch and
12531        // consume the elapsed microseconds from the bound SC's
12532        // atomic budget. This replaces the cycle-level over-
12533        // attribution that previously charged the FULL `delta_us`
12534        // against every Sporadic SC regardless of which entries
12535        // actually fired — accurate per-callback measurement is the
12536        // shape the design doc's per-callback runtime acceptance
12537        // calls out.
12538        //
12539        // phase-359 W10 — this was `feature = "std"`-gated, because it "needs a
12540        // `core::time::Instant`-equivalent monotonic clock ... until a
12541        // board-side monotonic-microsecond accessor lands". That accessor
12542        // landed: `now_us()` reads the platform monotonic counter on every
12543        // flavour. So per-callback sporadic accounting is no longer something
12544        // only a hosted build gets, and the no_std fallback to polled
12545        // `SporadicState` cycle deltas is no longer the only option on target.
12546        let consume_dispatch_runtime_us =
12547            |desc_idx: usize,
12548             elapsed_us: u32,
12549             sched_context_bindings: &[super::sched_context::SchedContextId],
12550             sched_contexts: &[Option<super::sched_context::SchedContext>],
12551             sporadic_states: &mut [Option<super::sched_context::SporadicState>],
12552             alive_slots: &mut [super::monitor::AliveSlot],
12553             #[cfg(feature = "alloc")] sporadic_atomic_states: &[Option<(
12554                portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState>,
12555                OpaqueTimerHandle,
12556            )>]| {
12557                let sc_idx = sched_context_bindings[desc_idx].0 as usize;
12558                // Alive supervision counts EVERY dispatch, before the class
12559                // gate below: a Fifo or time-triggered context can fall
12560                // silent exactly as a sporadic one can, and the rule that
12561                // notices must not be scoped to the class that happens to
12562                // carry a budget.
12563                if let Some(slot) = alive_slots.get_mut(sc_idx) {
12564                    slot.dispatches = slot.dispatches.wrapping_add(1);
12565                }
12566                let sc_class = sched_contexts
12567                    .get(sc_idx)
12568                    .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
12569                    .map(|sc| sc.class)
12570                    .unwrap_or(super::sched_context::SchedClass::Fifo);
12571                if !matches!(sc_class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
12572                    return;
12573                }
12574                #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12575                if let Some((state, _)) =
12576                    sporadic_atomic_states.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
12577                {
12578                    state.consume(elapsed_us);
12579                    // Unconditional, unlike the overrun record below: the
12580                    // budget is sized FROM this number, so it has to exist
12581                    // before the budget is right rather than only after it
12582                    // is wrong.
12583                    state.record_exec(elapsed_us);
12584                    // Phase 110.E.b — overrun detection. Cooperative
12585                    // single-thread can't preempt a runaway callback,
12586                    // so post-dispatch wall-clock comparison delivers
12587                    // the same observable signal as the design's
12588                    // oneshot-IRQ-and-cancel pattern, without needing
12589                    // a separate timer per SC. `budget_capacity_us` is
12590                    // the per-period budget the SC was sized against;
12591                    // any callback exceeding that has run past its
12592                    // bandwidth allotment.
12593                    if elapsed_us > state.budget_capacity_us {
12594                        state.record_overrun(elapsed_us - state.budget_capacity_us);
12595                    }
12596                }
12597                // issue 0736 — the POLLED state is charged unconditionally,
12598                // and it is the one that matters: `has_budget` prefers the
12599                // atomic state only when a refill timer was registered, which
12600                // no board or entry does. Before this, the alloc arm charged a
12601                // state nothing populated and the no_std arm discarded the
12602                // measurement outright (`let _ = (sc_idx, elapsed_us)`), so no
12603                // shipped image recorded per-callback runtime anywhere — while
12604                // the comment above claimed it did.
12605                if let Some(state) = sporadic_states.get_mut(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_mut()) {
12606                    state.consume(elapsed_us);
12607                }
12608            };
12609
12610        // W3b.5 — post-dispatch contract checks. `lat_active` gates the
12611        // per-dispatch publish-count snapshot (attribution of dispatch
12612        // elapsed time to monitored publishers whose counter advanced);
12613        // `dl_active` gates elapsed measurement for deadline actions. The third
12614        // term used to be `cfg!(feature = "std")` — "std measures anyway for
12615        // the sporadic path" — which made a COMPILE-TIME flavour stand in for
12616        // "is there a clock". It is now the runtime question it always was.
12617        let mon_table = s.monitor_table;
12618        let lat_active = mon_table.iter().any(|m| m.max_latency_ms > 0);
12619        let dl_active = s.sched_contexts.iter().flatten().any(|sc| {
12620            sc.deadline_us.is_some()
12621                && !matches!(
12622                    sc.deadline_action,
12623                    super::sched_context::DeadlineAction::Ignore
12624                )
12625        });
12626        let mon_clock = s.clock_us_fn;
12627        // phase10-B3 -- the route rule needs the clock and the publish-count
12628        // snapshot, and nothing else; without a clock it judges nothing.
12629        let route_on = mon_clock.is_some() && super::monitor::route_active(mon_table);
12630        // phase-503 -- a late supervised route reacts at completion too; not
12631        // before the monitors are armed (phase-474 I2), as after the park.
12632        let route_hook = s.reaction_hook.filter(|_| s.violations.counts.armed);
12633        let counts_on = lat_active || route_on;
12634        // phase-359 W4 — one predicate, no cfg block. `cfg!` is an expression,
12635        // so the flavour difference stays a value instead of a branch: std
12636        // measures unconditionally because the sporadic runtime accounting
12637        // below (itself std-only) consumes the result, which is exactly what
12638        // the comment above described and what the four-arm sites encoded.
12639        let measure_us = counts_on || dl_active || mon_clock.is_some();
12640        // phase-359 W4 — ONE hoisted µs reader for the per-dispatch latency
12641        // measurement below. Hoisted because `now_us()` takes `&mut self` and
12642        // the dispatch loop already holds borrows; the std arm copies the epoch
12643        // (a `Copy` `Instant`) so reading inside the loop touches no `self`.
12644        // This is the last cfg pair in the timing path: the two call sites it
12645        // serves each had FOUR arms (start + elapsed, per flavour).
12646        let read_us = move || mon_clock.map(|c| c()).unwrap_or(0);
12647        // Deferred deadline-miss violations (the loop body holds an
12648        // immutable borrow of `s.entries`, so the ring is fed after).
12649        let mut deadline_misses: heapless::Vec<
12650            super::monitor::Violation,
12651            { super::monitor::MAX_VIOLATIONS },
12652        > = heapless::Vec::new();
12653        // SCs whose remaining callbacks this cycle are skipped
12654        // (`DeadlineAction::Skip`) — bitmask over SC slots.
12655        let mut skipped_scs: u64 = 0;
12656
12657        // For each priority bucket (Critical → Normal → BestEffort),
12658        // drain EDF first then FIFO so an EDF callback in this bucket
12659        // beats a FIFO peer at the same priority, but no lower-priority
12660        // entry runs while a higher-priority bucket has work pending.
12661        // Strict static priority across buckets; non-preemptive within
12662        // an in-flight callback (see Phase 110.D).
12663        // phase-509 P3 (RFC-0108 D2) -- one pick at a time. Each pick is the
12664        // most urgent queued job (bucket by bucket: EDF heap, then the ranked
12665        // FIFO's levels), and after each callback the ready set is merged
12666        // with what became ready while it ran, so an urgent callback made
12667        // ready by a less urgent one runs before the rest of the pass. Was a
12668        // drain of the scan's snapshot, bucket by bucket.
12669        loop {
12670            let mut next = None;
12671            for bucket in 0..NB {
12672                if let Some(job) = edf.pop_from(bucket) {
12673                    next = Some(job);
12674                    break;
12675                }
12676                let (level_lo, level_hi) =
12677                    super::sched_context::Priority::from_index(bucket).level_range();
12678                if let Some(job) = fifo.pop_in(level_lo, level_hi) {
12679                    next = Some(job);
12680                    break;
12681                }
12682            }
12683            let Some(job) = next else { break };
12684            let i = job.desc_idx as usize;
12685            let sc_idx = s.sched_context_bindings[i].0 as usize;
12686            if sc_idx < 64 && skipped_scs & (1u64 << sc_idx) != 0 {
12687                continue; // W3b.5 DeadlineAction::Skip containment
12688            }
12689            if let Some(meta) = s.entries[i]
12690                && !Self::slot_held(s.slot_tags, i)
12691            {
12692                let counts_before = snapshot_pub_counts(mon_table, counts_on);
12693                // Measured only when a consumer wants it, matching the
12694                // no_std arm this replaces — the std arm used to measure
12695                // unconditionally.
12696                let start_us = measure_us.then(read_us);
12697                let took_before = result.subscriptions_processed;
12698                Self::begin_dispatch(s.slot_tags, i);
12699                // phase-509 P9b item 2 (RFC-0108 "As built in P9b") -- the
12700                // callback window. With a lock that can tell threads apart,
12701                // a shared or band pass gives it for the callback, so a more
12702                // urgent worker (or an FFI caller) reaches the executor
12703                // while this callback runs. What crosses the window is a
12704                // copy of the entry's meta and its pinned arena address; the
12705                // running mark (`begin_dispatch`) keeps every other pass off
12706                // the entry and defers its release, and `rec` names this
12707                // thread as the one running it. `s` is derived again after.
12708                let mut rec = super::exec_lock::Running {
12709                    slot: i,
12710                    thread: window_thread,
12711                    next: core::ptr::null_mut(),
12712                };
12713                let window = window_lock.map(|l| {
12714                    // SAFETY: `rec` outlives the window and is unlinked under
12715                    // the lock right after it.
12716                    unsafe { s.link_running(&mut rec) };
12717                    super::exec_lock::Window::open(l)
12718                });
12719                dispatch_one(&meta, i, arena_ptr, delta_us, &mut result);
12720                let end_us = start_us.map(|_| read_us());
12721                if let Some(w) = window {
12722                    drop(w);
12723                    // SAFETY: the lock is held again; nothing borrowed from
12724                    // the executor before the window is used after.
12725                    s = unsafe { &mut *this };
12726                    s.unlink_running(&mut rec);
12727                }
12728                let elapsed_us: Option<u32> = start_us
12729                    .zip(end_us)
12730                    .map(|(t0, t1)| t1.saturating_sub(t0))
12731                    .map(|d| d.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
12732                // phase10-B3 -- a subscription dispatch takes its sample
12733                // first, so the dispatch start is the take.
12734                if route_on && let (Some(t0), Some(t1)) = (start_us, end_us) {
12735                    if result.subscriptions_processed != took_before {
12736                        super::monitor::route_take(mon_table, i, t0);
12737                    }
12738                    super::monitor::route_judge(
12739                        mon_table,
12740                        &counts_before,
12741                        t1,
12742                        |row, v, record, react| {
12743                            if react {
12744                                call_route_reaction(route_hook, mon_table, row, &v);
12745                            }
12746                            if record {
12747                                let _ = deadline_misses.push(v);
12748                            }
12749                        },
12750                    );
12751                }
12752                if let Some(elapsed_us) = elapsed_us {
12753                    consume_dispatch_runtime_us(
12754                        i,
12755                        elapsed_us,
12756                        &s.sched_context_bindings[..],
12757                        &s.sched_contexts[..],
12758                        &mut s.sporadic_states[..],
12759                        &mut s.alive_slots[..],
12760                        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12761                        &s.sporadic_atomic_states[..],
12762                    );
12763                }
12764                if let Some(elapsed_us) = elapsed_us {
12765                    attribute_latency(mon_table, lat_active, &counts_before, elapsed_us);
12766                    check_deadline_miss(
12767                        s.sched_contexts.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref()),
12768                        sc_idx,
12769                        elapsed_us,
12770                        &mut deadline_misses,
12771                        &mut skipped_scs,
12772                        s.fault_fn,
12773                        s.reaction_hook,
12774                    );
12775                }
12776                s.finish_dispatch(i);
12777            }
12778            if repick {
12779                s.merge_mid_pass(&mut fifo, &mut edf, &mut settled, arena_ptr, band_mask);
12780            }
12781        }
12782
12783        // W3b.5 — feed deferred deadline misses into the violation ring.
12784        for v in deadline_misses {
12785            s.violations.record(v);
12786        }
12787        // phase-509 P9b item 2 -- the rules and the executor-wide chores
12788        // below are the executor's own worker's. Issue 2020 -- the band's
12789        // own components' ticks are the band's.
12790        if is_band_pass {
12791            // SAFETY: the pass's contract; `s` is not used after it.
12792            unsafe { Self::tick_components(this, Some(level)) };
12793            return result;
12794        }
12795
12796        // Issue #505 — same ring, same cycle. This runs AFTER dispatch,
12797        // unlike the windowed rate/age/latency rules at the top of the
12798        // spin: the activations it reports were dropped by the dispatch
12799        // that just happened, and a tier that is stalling should not have
12800        // to wait for the next spin to say so.
12801        s.check_timer_overruns();
12802        s.check_release_jitter_rule();
12803        s.check_stack_headroom_rule();
12804        s.check_alive_supervision();
12805        // phase-474 I7 -- the queued /diagnostics reports, after this spin's
12806        // dispatches and rules, when the next timer leaves room for them.
12807        s.flush_violation_reports();
12808        // phase-474 I1 -- the opt-in drain-and-report hook, after every rule of
12809        // this spin has had its say.
12810        s.violations.drain_and_report();
12811
12812        // Process parameter services (outside the arena)
12813        #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
12814        #[allow(unused_mut)] // only the services add to it
12815        let mut handled = 0usize;
12816        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
12817        if let Some(params) = &mut s.params {
12818            {
12819                let crate::param_store::ParamState {
12820                    server,
12821                    services,
12822                    buffers,
12823                    staged,
12824                    ..
12825                } = &mut **params;
12826                // phase-426 W3 -- one set per node; see the sibling site above,
12827                // including why nothing here can discard an error (1270/1271).
12828                if let Some(buffers) = buffers {
12829                    for set in services.iter_mut() {
12830                        let n = set.process(server, staged, buffers);
12831                        result.services_handled += n;
12832                        handled += n;
12833                    }
12834                }
12835            }
12836        }
12837        #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
12838        s.note_param_services_ran(handled);
12839
12840        // Process lifecycle services (outside the arena).
12841        //
12842        // SAFETY: `change_state` dispatches a user-supplied C callback through a
12843        // raw function pointer stored in `LifecyclePollingNodeCtx`. The caller
12844        // of `register_lifecycle_services` guarantees the callback/context pair
12845        // stays live for as long as the executor (see that method's docs).
12846        #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
12847        if let Some(lc) = &mut s.lifecycle {
12848            if let Ok(n) = unsafe { lc.process() } {
12849                result.services_handled += n;
12850            }
12851        }
12852
12853        // Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — executor-owned component tick pass.
12854        // Mirrors `ExecutorNodeRuntime::run_ticks`: after the transport +
12855        // callbacks have been pumped, drive each enrolled component's `tick`
12856        // (service-client/action poll, etc.). `exec_ctx` hands the component
12857        // the whole executor as a raw `*mut Executor` so its tick can
12858        // reborrow it (the same disjoint-field raw-ptr pattern run_ticks
12859        // uses). Index-iterate over `Copy` slots so no borrow of
12860        // `s.component_slots` is held while `tick` runs (which aliases
12861        // `self` through `exec_ctx`).
12862        //
12863        // Issue 2020 -- only the components this pass's level owns.
12864        // SAFETY: the pass's contract; `s` is not used after the call.
12865        unsafe { Self::tick_components(this, None) };
12866
12867        result
12868    }
12869
12870    /// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) -- the component tick pass at the tail of a
12871    /// pass: each enrolled component's `tick` (service-client polls,
12872    /// action-server completion and feedback), with the whole executor as
12873    /// `exec_ctx`. Issue 2020 -- only the components the pass's level owns
12874    /// ([`Self::pass_ticks_owner`]): `band_level` is a band pass's level,
12875    /// `None` for the executor's own worker.
12876    ///
12877    /// The lock stays held across every tick, as it always was: a component
12878    /// is ticked by one level's thread only, and never by two at once.
12879    ///
12880    /// # Safety
12881    /// As [`Self::pass`], called with the lock held (when installed) and no
12882    /// reference to the executor live in the caller.
12883    unsafe fn tick_components(this: *mut Self, band_level: Option<u8>) {
12884        let exec_ctx = this as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
12885        let mut i = 0;
12886        loop {
12887            // SAFETY: re-derived after each tick, which aliases the executor
12888            // through `exec_ctx`; the slot is copied out, so no borrow of
12889            // `component_slots` is outstanding during the call.
12890            let s: &Self = unsafe { &*this };
12891            let Some(slot) = s.component_slots.get(i).copied() else {
12892                break;
12893            };
12894            i += 1;
12895            let owner = (slot.level != super::scheduler::NO_OWNING_LEVEL).then_some(slot.level);
12896            if !s.pass_ticks_owner(band_level, owner) {
12897                continue;
12898            }
12899            // SAFETY: `slot.state` is the leaked cell the matching `tick`
12900            // expects (enrolled via `enroll_component`); `exec_ctx` is a live
12901            // `*mut Executor`.
12902            unsafe { (slot.tick)(slot.state, exec_ctx) };
12903        }
12904    }
12905
12906    /// The executor's own worker's prelude to a pass: everything
12907    /// `spin_once` did before its readiness scan. Returns the pass's clock
12908    /// read and the elapsed time its timers are credited.
12909    /// # Safety
12910    /// As [`Self::pass`]; `window_lock` is the pass's (`None` for an owned
12911    /// pass), and with it the calling thread holds the lock exactly once.
12912    unsafe fn owned_prelude(
12913        this: *mut Self,
12914        window_lock: Option<super::exec_lock::ExecLock>,
12915        timeout: core::time::Duration,
12916    ) -> (Option<u64>, u64) {
12917        // SAFETY: the caller's contract; re-derived after every window.
12918        #[allow(unused_mut)]
12919        let mut s: &mut Self = unsafe { &mut *this };
12920        // phase-509 P7 (RFC-0108 D8.2) -- this level is alive: it reached a
12921        // spin. A level stuck in a callback stops checking in, which is what
12922        // the image's watchdog feed (`take_every_level_alive`) waits on.
12923        let now = s.now_us();
12924        super::level_liveness::LEVELS.check_in(s.worker.level, now);
12925        // phase-436 W2 (issue 1193) — the budget is carried in MICROSECONDS.
12926        // This was `as_millis()`, which truncates: `from_micros(500)` became
12927        // `0`, and a zero timeout selects the non-blocking path — so a
12928        // sub-millisecond `spin()` was a 100 % CPU loop with no warning. The
12929        // conversion to whatever the platform primitive accepts happens once,
12930        // at the park, and rounds UP. The budget itself is `grid_budget_us`
12931        // below (phase-474 I11).
12932
12933        // phase-425 W3b — bring the `/clock` subscription in line with
12934        // `use_sim_time`. One bool comparison in the settled case; the work only
12935        // happens on a transition, or while a request is waiting for its first
12936        // node to exist.
12937        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
12938        {
12939            #[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
12940            s.settle_builder_reserved_parameters();
12941            s.reconcile_ros_time_source();
12942        }
12943
12944        // phase-426 W3 — attach the six parameter services to any node that
12945        // does not have them yet. Same reason as the reconcile above: the
12946        // request routinely arrives before there is a node to publish under
12947        // (`nros::main!` emits `apply_param_services` ahead of its per-node
12948        // `register` calls, by design). One length comparison once settled.
12949        //
12950        // Issue 1271 -- a failure is LOGGED, once, rather than discarded. On
12951        // Cyclone this fails on every spin with `Transport(Unsupported)`
12952        // (issue 1268), and with the result dropped "this node has no
12953        // parameter services" was a fact nothing on the image stated.
12954        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
12955        if s.parameter_services_pending()
12956            && let Err(e) = s.reconcile_parameter_services()
12957        {
12958            s.report_parameter_service_reconcile_failure(e);
12959        }
12960
12961        // Release jitter, measured HERE rather than in `spin_period`, because
12962        // this is the function every driver goes through.
12963        //
12964        // The first version instrumented `spin_period` only, and that was the
