12965        // same mistake issue 0736 records one layer down: a measurement placed
12966        // on a path no shipped image takes. `nros-cpp`'s tier trampoline paces
12967        // itself with a `spin_once` loop at `spin_period_us` (see its
12968        // `run_components` docs, step 4), so `spin_period` is not what the C++
12969        // entry -- and therefore not what the Zephyr lane -- actually calls.
12970        // The field recorded zero forever while claiming to measure cadence.
12971        //
12972        // `timeout` is the caller's intended pacing quantum: `spin_period`
12973        // passes its period, and the generated entries pass 10 ms. phase-474
12974        // I11 -- with no declared cadence it is the period of an absolute
12975        // release grid, and the park budget is the time to the next grid
12976        // point (see `record_release_jitter`); the release is judged after the
12977        // park, against the grid (`record_grid_release`). A zero timeout means
12978        // "poll, no cadence claimed", so it is neither judged nor gridded.
12979        let grid_budget_us = s.record_release_jitter(timeout);
12980
12981        // issue 0900 — one-shot advisory when the arena is far larger than what
12982        // registered. First spin rather than "end of registration", because
12983        // there is no such point: an app may register lazily.
12984        super::arena::maybe_report_arena_headroom(s.arena_used, s.arena.len());
12985
12986        // phase-412 -- the same moment, recorded where a board with no log sink
12987        // can still be asked. Reaching this stage is the positive result the
12988        // advisory above cannot deliver on the island: registration completed.
12989        crate::boot_report::checkpoint(crate::boot_report::Stage::FirstSpin);
12990
12991        // Phase 110.0 — the backend's next internal-event deadline (lease
12992        // keepalive, heartbeat, ACK-NACK timeout, ...). Default backend impl
12993        // returns `None`, so this contributes nothing unless the active
12994        // backend opts in.
12995        //
12996        // phase-436 W6 — a CANDIDATE now, not a pre-cap. Folding it into the
12997        // budget here meant a park the session won was attributed to
12998        // `CallerBudget`, so the one number that explains a wake named the
12999        // wrong source.
13000        let session_us = s
13001            .session
13002            .next_deadline_ms()
13003            .map(|next| (next as u64).saturating_mul(1000));
13004
13005        // phase-436 W1 (issue 1192) — and by the next TIMER deadline, which is
13006        // the one class of deadline the executor itself owns. Before this the
13007        // park was bounded by the caller's budget narrowed only by the
13008        // BACKEND's next event, so `spin_default`'s 50 ms slept straight past
13009        // a registered 10 ms timer.
13010        //
13011        // Attribution is recorded here rather than derived later: this is the
13012        // only point where the losing candidates are still in hand.
13013        let (park_bound_us, park_source) =
13014            s.next_wake_bound_attributed_us(grid_budget_us, session_us);
13015        s.worker.last_park_bound_us = park_bound_us;
13016        s.worker.last_park_source = park_source;
13017        // phase-436 W2 (issue 1193) — round UP to what the primitive can
13018        // express. The old `as_millis()` truncated, so a sub-millisecond
13019        // request became a zero park: the non-blocking path, a busy loop.
13020        let park_achieved_us = s.round_park_up_us(park_bound_us);
13021        s.worker.last_park_achieved_us = park_achieved_us;
13022
13023        // phase-436 W6 — a port that installed a park primitive does its
13024        // waiting HERE, on the bound every source agreed on, and the transport
13025        // is then drained non-blockingly.
13026        //
13027        // This is the path bare metal needs: `park_until(deadline)` can arm a
13028        // timer compare before `wfi`, which `sleep(duration)` cannot express —
13029        // and `nros-baremetal-common` notes that `wfi` with no pending
13030        // interrupt deadlocks, so arming first is not optional there.
13031        //
13032        // Additive by construction: with no primitive installed this is a
13033        // no-op and every existing port keeps the behaviour it has.
13034        // phase-436 — park only when something can END the park early. A
13035        // park ends on the bound or on the wake object; with a poll-only
13036        // backend (XRCE), or a session whose wake callback is gone, nothing
13037        // signals that object, so the park would be a blind sleep and data
13038        // arriving mid-park would wait out the whole bound — the Phase
13039        // 127.C.4 stall (a reliable stream whose ACK lands in a session nobody
13040        // drives). Those executors keep the receive-blocking wait below.
13041        let park_can_be_woken = s.park_can_be_woken();
13042        // phase-509 P9b item 3 -- a shared pass parks with the lock released
13043        // (a window), so the band workers run while the executor's own
13044        // worker waits. Nothing borrowed from the executor crosses it.
13045        let parked = match s.worker.park_primitive {
13046            Some((park, ctx)) if park_achieved_us > 0 && park_can_be_woken => {
13047                let _window = window_lock.map(super::exec_lock::Window::open);
13048                // SAFETY: `park` and `ctx` were supplied together by the port
13049                // through `set_park_primitive` and outlive the executor by its
13050                // contract.
13051                //
13052                // phase-436 — a negative answer is "cannot park": the ABI's
13053                // own contract, and what a Rust-implemented port's trait
13054                // default returns at once. Counting that as a park would
13055                // drop the drain below to non-blocking and spin hot, so the
13056                // spin falls back to the wait it would have had uninstalled.
13057                (unsafe { park(ctx, park_achieved_us) }) >= 0
13058            }
13059            _ => false,
13060        };
13061
13062        // Having already waited, the transport drain must not block again —
13063        // otherwise the park and the drive would sum, and the cadence would be
13064        // up to twice what was asked. Same trap as passing a period to
13065        // `spin_once` instead of declaring it (#648).
13066        // SAFETY: the lock is held again (the window, if any, has closed).
13067        s = unsafe { &mut *this };
13068        let timeout_ms = if parked {
13069            0
13070        } else {
13071            (park_achieved_us / 1000).min(i32::MAX as u64) as i32
13072        };
13073
13074        // Wall-clock-accurate timer accumulation. Measure real time
13075        // since the previous `spin_once` exited (or, on the first call,
13076        // since `drive_io` started). Two failure modes the requested
13077        // `timeout_ms` doesn't capture:
13078        //  1. `drive_io` returns early — e.g. zenoh-pico's condvar wakes
13079        //     on data arrival, well under 1 ms.
13080        //  2. The caller spends time outside `spin_once` (explicit sleep,
13081        //     ROS-2 cooperative scheduling, etc.) and that time should
13082        //     still count toward timers.
13083        // Crediting the requested timeout to timers in either case ticks
13084        // them faster than wall-clock — observed as a 30 Hz control loop
13085        // overshooting to >200 Hz under sustained traffic. Carry the
13086        // sub-ms remainder across calls so precision is preserved.
13087        // phase-359 W4 — the spin-ENTRY read, one spelling. Kept distinct from
13088        // the post-IO read below because the first spin's delta is measured from
13089        // entry; collapsing them would make that delta 0 on the first call only.
13090        let spin_start_us = s.now_us();
13091
13092        // phase-474 I2 -- arm the monitors when the policy says start-up is over,
13093        // before any rule of this spin can judge.
13094        s.update_monitor_arming(spin_start_us);
13095        // phase-462 W4 -- and switch to the requested mode's tables, before
13096        // any rule of this spin judges by them.
13097        s.update_mode(spin_start_us);
13098
13099        // RFC-0052 W3b.4 — contract monitors tick once per spin (window
13100        // logic inside; single branch when the baked table is empty).
13101        s.run_contract_monitors();
13102
13103        // Phase 104.C.6 — shared executor wake. Swap-and-clear the
13104        // wake flag; if it was set before this `spin_once` entered,
13105        // skip the blocking wait on the primary session and poll
13106        // every session non-blockingly. Lets a wake signal from any
13107        // thread (or, post-104.C.6.b, any backend's vtable hook)
13108        // pre-empt whichever session the executor would otherwise
13109        // sleep on. Cost on the no-wake path is one atomic swap.
13110        // phase-359 W10 — ONE swap, at `alloc` scope.
13111        //
13112        // This was `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` while the alloc wait arm did its
13113        // own swap further down. Merging the two arms made that two swaps of
13114        // one flag per spin, the first consuming what the second tested, so the
13115        // arm would have read `was_woken == false` forever. Deleting the outer
13116        // one instead broke a different thing: `wake_flag` is `alloc`-gated and
13117        // "spin_once consumes the wake flag" is an invariant of every alloc
13118        // build, but the merged arm only runs with `rmw-cffi` — so a
13119        // `std`-without-`rmw-cffi` build stopped clearing it, which
13120        // `test_wake_cleared_each_spin` catches. It belongs here, at the scope
13121        // of the field it reads.
13122        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13123        #[allow(unused_variables)]
13124        let was_woken = s.wake_flag.swap(false, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
13125
13126        // Phase 124.B.4 — condvar-blocked wait.
13127        //
13128        // RT contract:
13129        //  * cv.wait_timeout_while: bounded by `timeout_ms`.
13130        //    Predicate is O(1) — one atomic swap + Instant::now.
13131        //    No allocation. PI-mutex consideration: wake_mu held
13132        //    only during predicate check (microseconds);
13133        //    contended worst-case = notify_all execution time
13134        //    (~10s of µs).
13135        //  * Backend's `set_wake_callback`-installed cb is called
13136        //    on async data arrival from its transport-notify path
13137        //    (worker thread, ISR-safe variant via 124.B.7). The
13138        //    runtime cb writes wake_flag + signals wake_cv,
13139        //    unblocking this loop sub-poll-period.
13140        //  * Poll-only backends (XRCE, bare-metal) leave the slot
13141        //    NULL; the cv wait still fires on its deadline, then
13142        //    drive_io(0) drains whatever the backend's internal
13143        //    poll has buffered. Equivalent to their pre-124
13144        //    behaviour minus the blocking wait inside drive_io.
13145        //
13146        // Lost-wakeup safe: SeqCst flag write happens-before
13147        // notify, and the waiter checks the flag under wake_mu in
13148        // the predicate. If wake fires between drain and cv.wait
13149        // entry, the predicate sees flag=true on first eval and
13150        // exits immediately.
13151        // Phase 130.4 — only sleep in the wake wait when a backend actually
13152        // installed `set_wake_callback`. Poll-only backends (XRCE) leave the
13153        // vtable slot NULL → `has_async_wake == false` →
13154        // drive_io for the caller's full timeout instead of sleeping in a
13155        // never-signaled wait that starves reliable retransmission (Phase
13156        // 127.C.4 root cause: the server's `send_response` flushes 100 ms once,
13157        // then a blind `wait_ms(100)` sleeps with zero session activity, so the
13158        // agent's ACK arrives into a stalled session and reliable redelivery
13159        // never fires).
13160        //
13161        // Phase 248 (C2) — which primitive is a RUNTIME choice from the
13162        // platform vtable's wake probe, not a compile-time per-RTOS `cfg`:
13163        // `node_wake.is_some()` means `nros_platform_wake_*` is linked and
13164        // `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb` signals it on transport arrival.
13165        // phase-359 W10 — ONE arm. This was a `std` arm and an `alloc` arm with
13166        // the same body: block on the platform wake primitive when a backend
13167        // installed the callback and nothing has woken us yet, else drive the
13168        // transport for the caller's full timeout. They stopped differing when
13169        // the condvar fallback was deleted — the std arm's `else` branch had
13170        // already become "drive for the full timeout", which is what the alloc
13171        // arm always did — so keeping two was keeping a fork that agreed.
13172        // phase-417 W4.e — the FIRST arm is what the swap-and-clear above says
13173        // it is for, and it was missing: a wake that landed BETWEEN two spins
13174        // set the flag, and this expression then took the `else` and drove the
13175        // transport for the caller's FULL timeout, so the pending work waited
13176        // out the very budget the wake exists to cut short. Measured with a
13177        // guard condition triggered from another thread just before a 400 ms
13178        // spin: 400 ms to dispatch, against 50 ms for the same trigger issued
13179        // while the spin was already parked in `wait_ms`. Being woken means
13180        // there IS work, so the right timeout is 0 — poll every session
13181        // non-blockingly and go dispatch it, which is what the comment at the
13182        // swap has claimed since Phase 104.C.6.
13183        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
13184        let primary_drive_timeout_ms = {
13185            if was_woken {
13186                // Issue 1385 — drain the wake PRIMITIVE too.
13187                //
13188                // `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb` sets both halves of one signal:
13189                // the flag, and the platform primitive. The swap above
13190                // consumed the flag and this arm returns without entering the
13191                // wait, so a primitive left posted makes the NEXT spin's
13192                // `wait_ms` return instantly on a signal already acted on —
13193                // that spin does not wait at all, and whatever it should have
13194                // waited for is dispatched a whole spin late.
13195                //
13196                // `wait_ms(0)` is the non-blocking take: every port's wait is a
13197                // deadline (`sem_timedwait`, `k_sem_take`, `xSemaphoreTake`),
13198                // so zero means "take it if it is there", never "wait
13199                // forever".
13200                //
13201                // Measured, not reasoned: with the C executor installing a
13202                // callback (the other half of 1385), an arrival taken by this
13203                // arm left the spin after it returning in 0 ms where it owed
13204                // 60 ms of waiting — which is what `node_guard_condition.c`'s
13205                // mid-spin case caught, and what `executor_backend_wake.c`'s
13206                // second lower bound now pins. Latent until then only because
13207                // no C spin had ever entered the wait arm.
13208                if let Some(wake) = s.node_wake.as_ref() {
13209                    let _ = wake.wait_ms(0);
13210                }
13211                0
13212            } else if s.async_wake_live()
13213                && let Some(wake) = s.node_wake.as_ref()
13214            {
13215                // phase-436 — after a park this wait has a zero timeout and
13216                // the park has already waited on this same object, so it is a
13217                // second syscall that can only time out. Measured on a native
13218                // tier: one extra futex wait per iteration, doubling the idle
13219                // context switches. A signal that lands between the park's
13220                // return and here stays posted and ends the next park at once,
13221                // which costs one spin and loses nothing.
13222                if !parked {
13223                    // phase-509 P9b item 3 -- the wait is a window too: the
13224                    // wake object is the executor's (`Arc`, set at open and
13225                    // never replaced), reached through a raw pointer.
13226                    let wake: *const super::node_wake::NodeWake = &**wake;
13227                    let _window = window_lock.map(super::exec_lock::Window::open);
13228                    // SAFETY: the object outlives the executor's open window.
13229                    let _ = unsafe { &*wake }.wait_ms(timeout_ms as u32);
13230                }
13231                // SAFETY: the lock is held again.
13232                s = unsafe { &mut *this };
13233                // Drain any flag the cb set while we were waiting.
13234                let _ = s.wake_flag.swap(false, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
13235                0
13236            } else {
13237                // No wake primitive linked, or a poll-only backend: drive the
13238                // transport for the full timeout. It still BLOCKS — in the
13239                // transport's own recv — which is where every flavour ended up
13240                // anyway.
13241                timeout_ms
13242            }
13243        };
13244
13245        // std builds without rmw-cffi (mock-session tests, future alternative
13246        // backends) keep the original "drive_io is non-blocking" assumption.
13247        // `std` implies `alloc`, so this is the only std configuration the arm
13248        // above does not cover.
13249        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
13250        let primary_drive_timeout_ms = 0;
13251
13252        // no_std without (alloc + rmw-cffi) keeps the legacy
13253        // full-timeout drive_io call.
13254        #[cfg(all(
13255            not(feature = "alloc"),
13256            not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))
13257        ))]
13258        let primary_drive_timeout_ms = timeout_ms;
13259
13260        // issue 0324 — the primary session's I/O result is TRACKED, not
13261        // discarded. See `consecutive_io_failures` for why this is a counter
13262        // rather than an early return.
13263        match s.drive_primary(primary_drive_timeout_ms) {
13264            Ok(()) => s.consecutive_io_failures = 0,
13265            Err(_) => s.consecutive_io_failures = s.consecutive_io_failures.saturating_add(1),
13266        }
13267        for extra in s.extra_sessions.iter_mut() {
13268            // Best-effort BY DESIGN: extra sessions are bridge / multi-domain
13269            // attachments, and one of them failing must not stall the primary
13270            // spin. The old code expressed this the same way it expressed the
13271            // primary's discarded error — identically — so the intent was
13272            // invisible. It is now the only `let _ =` of the two.
13273            let _ = extra.drive_io(0);
13274        }
13275
13276        // phase-359 W4 — ONE clock read per spin, shared by the delta below and
13277        // every consumer further down. Replaces the std/no_std delta pair AND
13278        // two ad-hoc `static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant>` blocks that each kept
13279        // their own std-only epoch.
13280        let now_us_this_spin = s.now_us();
13281        // phase-474 I11 -- the release instant is the end of the park, so it
13282        // is judged on this read, before any dispatch of this spin.
13283        if let Some(now) = now_us_this_spin {
13284            s.record_grid_release(now);
13285        }
13286
13287        // Same rule on both flavours: measure elapsed when a clock exists, else
13288        // credit the REQUESTED timeout. That fallback was previously reachable
13289        // only on no_std; on std `Instant` always answered. It stays unreachable
13290        // on std for the same reason — `now_us()` is infallible there — so this
13291        // is one expression, not a behaviour change.
13292        let delta_us = match now_us_this_spin {
13293            Some(now) => {
13294                let prev = s
13295                    .last_spin_end_us
13296                    .unwrap_or_else(|| spin_start_us.unwrap_or(now));
13297                s.last_spin_end_us = Some(now);
13298                now.saturating_sub(prev)
13299            }
13300            None => (timeout_ms as u64).saturating_mul(1000),
13301        };
13302
13303        // phase-430 W1 — the silence watch is credited the SAME `delta_us` the
13304        // wall timers below are, which is the whole of its unit argument: the
13305        // diagnostic arrives after as much time as this image's own wall timers
13306        // believe has passed, on whatever clock it actually has.
13307        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13308        s.note_sim_time_silence(delta_us);
13309
13310        if !s.spin_quantization_checked && timeout_ms > 0 {
13311            s.spin_quantization_checked = true;
13312            // The TIER's declared cadence, not the capped park bound. Since
13313            // phase-436 W1 the two differ whenever a timer is due sooner than
13314            // the budget, and auditing the cap would compare the timer period
13315            // against itself — an exact multiple every time, so issue 0515's
13316            // warning would go silent on precisely the images that have a
13317            // timer to quantize. `spin_nominal_us` is the declared cadence
13318            // (`set_spin_nominal_us`, else the caller's timeout), recorded at
13319            // the top of this spin before any capping.
13320            s.spin_quantization_us = s.spin_nominal_us;
13321            s.audit_spin_quantization(s.spin_quantization_us);
13322        }
13323        (now_us_this_spin, delta_us)
13324    }
13325
13326    /// Drive I/O and dispatch callbacks forever — the body of an RTOS task.
13327    ///
13328    /// EXTENSION (RFC-0089). Not a rename of upstream's `spin`: the `!` is the
13329    /// point. A bare-metal entry has no shutdown source to return TO, and
13330    /// declaring that lets the compiler drop the epilogue and lets the caller
13331    /// write it as the last expression of a `-> !` task body with no
13332    /// `unreachable!()`. [`spin`](Self::spin) is the verb that can end, and it
13333    /// is upstream's.
13334    ///
13335    /// phase-427 — was `spin(Duration) -> !`, which squatted on rclrs's name
13336    /// with a different contract (a ported `executor.spin(SpinOptions)` line
13337    /// had to be renamed by hand, the one edit on the tutorial's happy path
13338    /// that no real difference forced). `spin_default()` went with it: it named
13339    /// a 50 ms poll interval and had zero call sites, and the interval is now
13340    /// [`SpinOptions::poll_interval`], defaulting to
13341    /// [`DEFAULT_SPIN_POLL_INTERVAL`](super::types::DEFAULT_SPIN_POLL_INTERVAL).
13342    ///
13343    /// **Envelope.** Only `poll_interval` and `stop_on_first_error` can mean
13344    /// anything here; `timeout`, `only_next` and `max_callbacks` are ENDING
13345    /// conditions and this verb does not end. Passing one is a caller error and
13346    /// says so at `LOG_ERR` on entry rather than being quietly dropped — a
13347    /// discarded ending condition is precisely the "compiles and differs" case
13348    /// RFC-0089 exists to make loud, and a `-> !` signature has no other
13349    /// channel. `stop_on_first_error` likewise cannot RETURN the error; it
13350    /// logs it and keeps spinning, because a task body has nowhere to put it.
13351    ///
13352    /// ```ignore
13353    /// let mut executor = Executor::open(&config)?;
13354    /// executor.register_subscription::<Int32, _>("/topic", |msg| { /* ... */ })?;
13355    /// executor.spin_forever(SpinOptions::default()); // never returns
13356    /// ```
13357    pub fn spin_forever(&mut self, opts: SpinOptions) -> ! {
13358        if opts.timeout.is_some() || opts.only_next || opts.max_callbacks.is_some() {
13359            nros_log::log_error!(
13360                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
13361                "spin_forever: an ending condition (timeout / only_next / max_callbacks) \
13362                 was supplied to a verb that never returns and is being IGNORED \
13363                 -- use `Executor::spin` for a loop that can end"
13364            );
13365        }
13366        let poll = opts.poll_interval;
13367        let report_errors = opts.stop_on_first_error;
13368        loop {
13369            let mut first_error = None;
13370            self.spin_once_capturing(poll, &mut first_error);
13371            if report_errors && let Some(e) = first_error {
13372                nros_log::log_error!(
13373                    nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
13374                    "spin_forever: a callback failed ({:?}); `stop_on_first_error` cannot \
13375                     end a `-> !` loop, so this is a report, not a stop",
13376                    e
13377                );
13378            }
13379        }
13380    }
13381
13382    /// Drive I/O and dispatch callbacks asynchronously.
13383    ///
13384    /// Runs forever, yielding between poll cycles so that other async tasks
13385    /// (e.g., [`Promise`](super::handles::Promise)) can make progress.
13386    ///
13387    /// Uses only `core::future` — no external async runtime dependency.
13388    ///
13389    /// ADOPT-BOUNDED against rclrs's
13390    /// `spin_async(SpinOptions) -> impl Future<Output = Vec<RclrsError>>`:
13391    ///
13392    /// * **It never returns and reports no errors** — the output is `!`, and it
13393    ///   takes no `SpinOptions`. To stop, `select` it against the thing you are
13394    ///   waiting for (pattern 1 below).
13395    /// * **It does not sleep on RMW I/O.** Each cycle is `spin_once(1 ms)` and then
13396    ///   a yield that wakes itself before returning `Pending`, so any runtime that
13397    ///   honours wakes polls it again at once. It is CPU-bound by construction;
13398    ///   the 1 ms `spin_once` budget is its only wait. Do not read `async` as idle.
13399    ///
13400    /// # Usage patterns
13401    ///
13402    /// ```ignore
13403    /// // Pattern 1: select with a promise (embassy-futures)
13404    /// use embassy_futures::select::{select, Either};
13405    /// let promise = client.call(&req)?;
13406    /// let Either::Second(reply) = select(executor.spin_async(), promise).await
13407    ///     else { unreachable!() };
13408    ///
13409    /// // Pattern 2: manual polling (no async runtime)
13410    /// let mut promise = client.call(&req)?;
13411    /// loop {
13412    ///     executor.spin_once(core::time::Duration::from_millis(10));
13413    ///     if let Ok(Some(r)) = promise.take() { break r; }
13414    /// }
13415    /// ```
13416    pub async fn spin_async(&mut self) -> ! {
13417        loop {
13418            self.spin_once(core::time::Duration::from_millis(1));
13419            core::future::poll_fn::<(), _>(|cx| {
13420                cx.waker().wake_by_ref();
13421                core::task::Poll::Pending
13422            })
13423            .await;
13424        }
13425    }
13426
13427    /// Execute the work that is ready NOW and return — rclcpp's
13428    /// `Executor::spin_some(max_duration)`.
13429    ///
13430    /// ADOPT-BOUNDED (RFC-0089). Upstream's drain verb: collect what is ready,
13431    /// execute it, come back. It never waits for new work — that is
13432    /// [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once), which takes a budget and blocks on the
13433    /// transport until it expires.
13434    ///
13435    /// **Envelope, two ways it is weaker than rclcpp's:**
13436    ///
13437    /// * rclcpp collects the ready set ONCE and executes it. One
13438    ///   `spin_once(0)` here is already that whole set (RFC-0002 §3), so this
13439    ///   would be a single call — except a callback may enqueue work for
13440    ///   another entity, which rclcpp's `spin_all` re-collects and its
13441    ///   `spin_some` leaves for the next call. Ours re-drains until a pass does
13442    ///   NO work, which is `spin_all`'s answer, because the alternative is
13443    ///   work sitting in the arena until someone spins again. Bounded by
13444    ///   `max`, so a callback that feeds itself cannot wedge the caller.
13445    /// * `max` is checked BETWEEN passes, never inside one, so it is a floor on
13446    ///   when this returns and not a ceiling: a single long callback overruns
13447    ///   it. There is no preemption here to make it a ceiling.
13448    ///
13449    /// `max` of [`Duration::ZERO`](core::time::Duration::ZERO) means no limit —
13450    /// rclcpp's own default — and is the spelling a build with no clock must
13451    /// use. A non-zero `max` on a clockless build is an ERROR rather than an
13452    /// unbounded drain (issue 0709, the same rule as `spin`'s `timeout`).
13453    ///
13454    /// The `Result` is about that PRECONDITION and nothing else. A failed
13455    /// callback is counted in each pass's `SpinOnceResult` and does not end the
13456    /// drain, matching `spin`'s default (`SpinOptions::stop_on_first_error` is
13457    /// `false`); rclcpp's `spin_some` returns `void` and reports callback
13458    /// failures nowhere at all.
13459    ///
13460    /// # Example
13461    ///
13462    /// ```ignore
13463    /// // Drain the ready set, then get on with the caller's own work.
13464    /// executor.spin_some(core::time::Duration::ZERO)?;
13465    /// ```
13466    pub fn spin_some(&mut self, max: core::time::Duration) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
13467        let bounded = !max.is_zero();
13468        let start_us = self.now_us();
13469        if bounded && start_us.is_none() {
13470            nros_log::log_error!(
13471                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
13472                "spin_some: a max duration was requested but this build has no clock \
13473                 - install one with `ExecutorConfig::clock_us`, or pass \
13474                 `Duration::ZERO` for rclcpp's unbounded default (issue 0709)"
13475            );
13476            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
13477        }
13478        let max_us = max.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
13479
13480        // No `enter_spin_loop` here, deliberately: `is_spinning` answers "a
13481        // blocking loop is running that a peer's `cancel()` has to reach", and
13482        // this verb returns on its own. Raising the flag for the length of a
13483        // drain would make a `cancel()` from another task look acted-upon when
13484        // nothing was waiting for it.
13485        loop {
13486            let result = self.spin_once(core::time::Duration::ZERO);
13487            if !result.any_work() {
13488                break;
13489            }
13490            if bounded
13491                && let (Some(start), Some(now)) = (start_us, self.now_us())
13492                && now.saturating_sub(start) >= max_us
13493            {
13494                break;
13495            }
13496        }
13497        Ok(())
13498    }
13499
13500    // ========================================================================
13501    // spin_one_period (no_std)
13502    // ========================================================================
13503
13504    /// Process one iteration and return remaining sleep time.
13505    ///
13506    /// This is `no_std` compatible — the caller is responsible for the actual
13507    /// delay using platform-specific sleep.
13508    ///
13509    /// # Arguments
13510    /// * `period_ms` - Target period in milliseconds
13511    /// * `elapsed_ms` - Time elapsed since last call (used for timer ticking)
13512    ///
13513    /// # Example
13514    ///
13515    /// ```ignore
13516    /// loop {
13517    ///     let r = executor.spin_one_period(10, elapsed_ms);
13518    ///     platform_sleep_ms(r.remaining_ms);
13519    /// }
13520    /// ```
13521    pub fn spin_one_period(&mut self, period_ms: u64, elapsed_ms: u64) -> SpinPeriodPollingResult {
13522        let result = self.spin_once(core::time::Duration::from_millis(elapsed_ms));
13523        SpinPeriodPollingResult {
13524            work: result,
13525            remaining_ms: period_ms.saturating_sub(elapsed_ms),
13526        }
13527    }
13528}
13529
13530// ============================================================================
13531// Parameter services (cfg param-services)
13532// ============================================================================
13533
13534#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
13535impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
13536    /// Register the 6 ROS 2 parameter services for this node.
13537    ///
13538    /// Creates service servers for `get_parameters`, `set_parameters`,
13539    /// `set_parameters_atomically`, `list_parameters`, `describe_parameters`,
13540    /// and `get_parameter_types`.
13541    ///
13542    /// The service names follow the ROS 2 convention: `/{namespace}/{node_name}/{suffix}`.
13543    /// For the default namespace `/`, this becomes `/{node_name}/{suffix}` (e.g.
13544    /// `/sentinel/list_parameters`).
13545    ///
13546    /// Parameter services are stored outside the arena and don't consume
13547    /// callback slots.
13548    ///
13549    /// Issue 2023 — every node served this way also PUBLISHES
13550    /// `/parameter_events` (`rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterEvent`), rclcpp's and
13551    /// rclrs's default: a start-up event, then one event per declare, set and
13552    /// undeclare. One VOLATILE publisher per executor
13553    /// ([`PARAM_EVENT_PUBLISHERS`](crate::parameter_services::PARAM_EVENT_PUBLISHERS)).
13554    /// A node opts out with
13555    /// [`disable_parameter_events_on`](Self::disable_parameter_events_on)
13556    /// (rclc's `notify_changed_over_dds = false`).
13557    ///
13558    /// # Example
13559    ///
13560    /// ```ignore
13561    /// let config = ExecutorConfig::from_env().node_name("talker");
13562    /// let mut executor = Executor::open(&config)?;
13563    /// executor.register_parameter_services()?;
13564    /// executor.declare_parameter("start_value", ParameterValue::Integer(0));
13565    /// ```
13566    pub fn register_parameter_services(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
13567        // Issue 1706 -- six services over a store that does not exist would
13568        // answer every request with "not declared"; say what went wrong
13569        // instead (`report_parameter_store_refused` has named the size).
13570        if !self.ensure_parameter_store() {
13571            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
13572        }
13573        if let Some(params) = &mut self.params {
13574            params.requested = true;
13575        }
13576        // phase-426 W3 — with no node yet, RECORD the request and stop. The
13577        // reconcile's no-node fallback publishes under the executor's own
13578        // identity, and taking it here would pin node 0 to that name before the
13579        // node that IS node 0 has been built — which is the pre-W3 behaviour
13580        // this work item exists to remove. Every generated entry arrives in
13581        // exactly this state (`apply_param_services` runs ahead of the per-node
13582        // `register` calls, by design), so the fallback belongs on the spin
13583        // path, where "no node" has stopped being merely "not yet".
13584        if self.nodes.is_empty() {
13585            return Ok(());
13586        }
13587        self.reconcile_parameter_services()
13588    }
13589
13590    /// phase-426 W3 — is there a node whose six services are not up yet?
13591    ///
13592    /// The cheap half of the reconcile, kept separate so `spin_once` can test
13593    /// it without carrying the reconcile's frame (see below).
13594    #[inline]
13595    pub(crate) fn parameter_services_pending(&self) -> bool {
13596        self.params.as_deref().is_some_and(|p| {
13597            p.requested
13598                && p.services.len() < self.nodes.len().max(1)
13599                // Issue 1268 — a failure that cannot change is not pending
13600                // work. This used to retry six `create_service` calls on EVERY
13601                // spin, for the life of an image that would never serve them,
13602                // and the result was discarded; 1271 made it say so once, which
13603                // left the retrying. An explicit
13604                // `register_parameter_services()` still tries, because that is
13605                // a caller asking rather than the spin guessing.
13606                && p.reconcile_failure.as_ref().is_none_or(|f| !f.permanent)
13607        })
13608    }
13609
13610    /// Issue 1271 -- say, once, that the parameter services could not be
13611    /// created, instead of discarding the result on every spin.
13612    ///
13613    /// The spin keeps retrying (a node registered later, or a transport that
13614    /// comes up late, may still succeed); this only decides whether anyone is
13615    /// told. Cold and out of line: it formats, and `spin_once`'s frame must
13616    /// not carry that.
13617    #[cold]
13618    #[inline(never)]
13619    fn report_parameter_service_reconcile_failure(&mut self, e: NodeError) {
13620        let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() else {
13621            return;
13622        };
13623        if params.reconcile_failure_reported {
13624            return;
13625        }
13626        params.reconcile_failure_reported = true;
13627        // Issue 1268 — name the node and the service. "could not be created
13628        // ({:?})" named neither, so a reader could not tell a name too long for
13629        // one node from a backend that will serve none of the six.
13630        let (node_fqn, service, permanent) = match params.reconcile_failure.as_ref() {
13631            Some(f) => (f.node_fqn.as_str(), f.service, f.permanent),
13632            None => ("<unknown node>", "<unknown service>", false),
13633        };
13634        nros_log::log_error!(
13635            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
13636            "parameter services could not be created for node {} at service {}: {:?}. \
13637             `ros2 param` cannot reach {} of this image's {} node(s). {} (issues 1271, 1268).",
13638            node_fqn,
13639            service,
13640            e,
13641            self.nodes.len().max(1) - params.services.len(),
13642            self.nodes.len().max(1),
13643            if permanent {
13644                "Not retrying: this failure cannot change without a rebuild."
13645            } else {
13646                "Retrying on every spin; logged once."
13647            }
13648        );
13649    }
13650
13651    /// phase-426 W3 — publish one set of six under every node that does not
13652    /// have one yet.
13653    ///
13654    /// **Why a reconcile and not a registration.** `nros::main!` emits
13655    /// `apply_param_services` BEFORE its per-node `register` calls, by design:
13656    /// the store has to exist when each component cell captures it. So at the
13657    /// moment the request is made the node table is EMPTY and there is no FQN
13658    /// to publish under — registering there is how the six ended up pinned to
13659    /// the executor's own identity in the first place. The request is recorded
13660    /// and satisfied here, at the head of every spin, exactly as
13661    /// `reconcile_ros_time_source` does for `use_sim_time` and for the same
13662    /// reason.
13663    ///
13664    /// **An executor with no registered node still gets one set**, under its
13665    /// own `node_name`/`namespace` and keyed `NodeId::PRIMARY` — the identity
13666    /// [`declare_parameter`](Self::declare_parameter) writes to. That is the
13667    /// pre-W3 behaviour, preserved for the direct-API images that never call
13668    /// `node_builder` (`param-chatter-talker` is one), and it is keyed the same
13669    /// as the first node record, so a node registered later inherits the set
13670    /// rather than getting a second one under a different name.
13671    ///
13672    /// Cheap in the settled case: one length comparison — but the FRAME is not
13673    /// cheap, so it is `inline(never)` and the spin site tests
13674    /// [`parameter_services_pending`](Self::parameter_services_pending) first.
13675    /// Building one set used to materialise six `EmbeddedServiceServer`s by
13676    /// value (2 x `PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE` each, ~48 KiB at the 4096
13677    /// default) before they were boxed; inlined into `spin_once` that landed
13678    /// on every spin frame whether or not the branch was taken. Issue 1270
13679    /// took the buffers out of the set -- one pair per executor, allocated on
13680    /// the heap directly -- but the set still carries six backend handles and
13681    /// a name, so the frame stays out of `spin_once`. Issue 0756's rule one
13682    /// call up — a parameter-service frame does not fit an embedded thread
13683    /// stack, and `test_open_threaded_spawn_and_halt` died with a bare SIGSEGV
13684    /// the first time this was reachable from the spin path.
13685    #[inline(never)]
13686    pub(crate) fn reconcile_parameter_services(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
13687        let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref() else {
13688            return Ok(());
13689        };
13690        if !params.requested {
13691            return Ok(());
13692        }
13693        // The nodes wanted, minus the ones already served. Collected first
13694        // because building a set borrows `self.session` mutably while
13695        // `self.nodes` / `self.params` are still borrowed by the scan.
13696        let want = self.nodes.len().max(1);
13697        if params.services.len() >= want {
13698            return Ok(());
13699        }
13700        let mut todo: heapless::Vec<
13701            (u8, heapless::String<64>, heapless::String<64>),
13702            { crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS },
13703        > = heapless::Vec::new();
13704        for index in 0..want {
13705            let key = nros_params::NodeKey::new(index as u8);
13706            if params.services.iter().any(|set| set.param_node() == key) {
13707                continue;
13708            }
13709            let (name, namespace) = match self.nodes.get(index) {
13710                Some(record) => (record.name.clone(), record.namespace.clone()),
13711                // No node table entry: the executor's own implicit primary
13712                // identity, which is what `NodeId::PRIMARY` means.
13713                None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone()),
13714            };
13715            if todo.push((index as u8, name, namespace)).is_err() {
13716                return Err(NodeError::NodeTableFull);
13717            }
13718        }
13719        // Issue 1270 -- the ONE buffer pair every set is answered through,
13720        // allocated with the first set so an image that declares parameters
13721        // and serves none pays nothing for it. `params` is `Some` here: the
13722        // scan above returned early otherwise.
13723        // Issue 1812 -- a carved home hands its pair over with the state, so
13724        // this is reached only on the heap fallback.
13725        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut()
13726            && params.buffers.is_none()
13727        {
13728            // Issue 1551 — an exhausted heap is an error this fn returns, not
13729            // an abort through libstd's OOM hook.
13730            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13731            {
13732                params.buffers = Some(
13733                    crate::parameter_services::ParamServiceBuffers::try_with_capacity(
13734                        crate::parameter_services::param_service_buffer_bytes(),
13735                    )
13736                    .ok_or(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc))?,
13737                );
13738            }
13739            #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
13740            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
13741        }
13742        for (index, name, namespace) in todo {
13743            let servers = match self.build_parameter_service_set(
13744                nros_params::NodeKey::new(index),
13745                &name,
13746                &namespace,
13747            ) {
13748                Ok(servers) => servers,
13749                Err((e, service)) => {
13750                    // Issue 1268 — keep WHAT failed and WHERE, for the one log
13751                    // line, and decide once whether retrying could ever help.
13752                    // `Unsupported` from the transport is a property of the
13753                    // build (the backend has no descriptor for the
13754                    // `rcl_interfaces` types), so a later spin asks the same
13755                    // question and gets the same answer.
13756                    let permanent = matches!(e, NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported));
13757                    if let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() {
13758                        let mut node_fqn = heapless::String::<256>::new();
13759                        if let Ok(fqn) = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(&name, &namespace) {
13760                            let _ = node_fqn.push_str(fqn.as_str());
13761                        }
13762                        params.reconcile_failure =
13763                            Some(crate::parameter_services::ParamServiceReconcileFailure {
13764                                node_fqn,
13765                                service,
13766                                permanent,
13767                            });
13768                    }
13769                    return Err(e);
13770                }
13771            };
13772            // Issue 1812 -- the set lives INLINE in the (carved) state now, not
13773            // in a box of its own.
13774            // Issue 0745 — PRESERVE an already-initialized store: launch-param
13775            // seeding may have run before any node existed (services can't be
13776            // registered that early). Overwriting here would wipe the seeds.
13777            match &mut self.params {
13778                Some(params) => params
13779                    .services
13780                    .push(servers)
13781                    .map_err(|_| NodeError::NodeTableFull)?,
13782                None => {
13783                    // Issue 0756 — see new_param_state: never build a ParamState
13784                    // by value, it does not fit an embedded thread stack.
13785                    // Issue 1706 -- the store is fallible; the refusal is
13786                    // reported once by `ensure_parameter_store`'s spelling.
13787                    if self.param_store_refused {
13788                        return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
13789                    }
13790                    let Some(mut state) = Self::new_param_state(
13791                        core::mem::take(&mut self.param_slots),
13792                        core::mem::take(&mut self.param_home),
13793                    ) else {
13794                        self.param_store_refused = true;
13795                        report_parameter_store_refused();
13796                        return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
13797                    };
13798                    state.requested = true;
13799                    let _ = state.services.push(servers);
13800                    self.params = Some(state);
13801                }
13802            }
13803            // phase-430 W2 — "declare `use_sim_time` on EVERY node, as rclcpp
13804            // does", said where the nodes finally exist. This is the only place
13805            // that knows the full set: `ensure_parameter_store` runs before any
13806            // node record does, so it can only seed the implicit PRIMARY, and
13807            // the further nodes an image composes onto one executor arrive
13808            // later. Seeding as each set of six goes up keeps the two in step —
13809            // the parameter is declared on exactly the nodes a
13810            // `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true` can reach.
13811            //
13812            // Idempotent by construction: `declare` refuses a name the node
13813            // already holds and the placeholder flag is only raised on
13814            // acceptance, so re-seeding PRIMARY here neither duplicates the
13815            // entry nor re-marks an application's own declaration as ours.
13816            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(index));
13817            // Issue 2023 — and `/parameter_events`, as rclcpp's and rclrs's
13818            // node does from its constructor. Seeded AFTER `use_sim_time`, so
13819            // the node's start-up event names it, as upstream's does.
13820            self.start_parameter_events_for_served_node(super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(
13821                index,
13822            ));
13823        }
13824        // Issue 1271 -- every node is served now, so a later failure (a node
13825        // registered after this one) is news again and earns its own line.
13826        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() {
13827            params.reconcile_failure_reported = false;
13828            // Issue 1268 -- and drop the record with it, so a later failure is
13829            // reported against the node it actually happened on.
13830            params.reconcile_failure = None;
13831        }
13832        Ok(())
13833    }
13834
13835    /// phase-426 W3 — create the six service servers for ONE node.
13836    ///
13837    /// Split out of [`register_parameter_services`](Self::register_parameter_services)
13838    /// because there are now N of these per image rather than one, and because
13839    /// the six `create_param_srv` call sites are what
13840    /// `check-infra-queryable-counts` reads to hold `PARAM_SERVICE_QUERYABLES`
13841    /// to the number of queryables a set actually claims.
13842    #[inline(never)]
13843    fn build_parameter_service_set(
13844        &mut self,
13845        node: nros_params::NodeKey,
13846        node_name: &str,
13847        namespace: &str,
13848    ) -> Result<crate::parameter_services::ParameterServiceServers, (NodeError, &'static str)> {
13849        use crate::parameter_services::{
13850            DescribeParameters, GetParameterTypes, GetParameters, ListParameters,
13851            ParamServiceHandle as PSrv, ParameterServiceServers, SetParameters,
13852            SetParametersAtomically,
13853        };
13854        use nros_core::RosService;
13855
13856        // The node FQN, from the one implementation. This was the third
13857        // hand-rolled copy of the same join (`crate::names::fully_qualified_name`
13858        // is the first, `Node::fully_qualified_name` was the second) — and the
13859        // three did not agree: this one absolutised a bare namespace, that one
13860        // did not. A join with three spellings has no answer to "what does the
13861        // tree do with `my_ns`".
13862        let node_fqn = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(node_name, namespace)
13863            .map_err(|()| (NodeError::NameTooLong, "get_parameters"))?;
13864        // The service names below still take the two halves separately.
13865        let ns: &str = namespace;
13866        let nn: &str = node_name;
13867
13868        /// Build a service name like `{node_fqn}/{suffix}` and create the server handle.
13869        ///
13870        /// Issue 1268 — the error carries the SUFFIX, so a failure can name the
13871        /// service a tool would have called instead of "one of six".
13872        fn create_param_srv<Svc>(
13873            session: &mut session::ConcreteSession,
13874            domain_id: u32,
13875            node_fqn: &str,
13876            namespace: &str,
13877            node_name: &str,
13878            suffix: &'static str,
13879        ) -> Result<session::RmwServiceServer, (NodeError, &'static str)>
13880        where
13881            Svc: RosService,
13882            Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
13883            Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
13884        {
13885            // Issue 1268 — REGISTER THE TYPES FIRST, exactly as a typed user
13886            // service does (`register_service_sized`). A backend that keys
13887            // topics on a registered type descriptor — Cyclone does — fails
13888            // `create_service` with `Unsupported` for a type it has never been
13889            // told about, and nothing else in the image registers the
13890            // `rcl_interfaces` service types: the generated typesupport of a
13891            // downstream covers ITS OWN message packages, and the backend bakes
13892            // in only `ParticipantEntitiesInfo` for the graph. So the six
13893            // parameter services failed on every spin while the image's own
13894            // services worked, which is what made the cause look like "no
13895            // service support" for two phases (the issue-0745 comment).
13896            //
13897            // A no-op on backends that need no descriptors (zenoh, xrce), which
13898            // is why zenoh served this same image all along.
13899            let register = |e: NodeError| (e, suffix);
13900            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Request>().map_err(register)?;
13901            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Reply>().map_err(register)?;
13902            let mut name = heapless::String::<256>::new();
13903            name.push_str(node_fqn)
13904                .map_err(|_| (NodeError::NameTooLong, suffix))?;
13905            name.push_str("/")
13906                .map_err(|_| (NodeError::NameTooLong, suffix))?;
13907            name.push_str(suffix)
13908                .map_err(|_| (NodeError::NameTooLong, suffix))?;
13909            let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(&name, Svc::SERVICE_NAME, Svc::SERVICE_HASH)
13910                // issue 0824 follow-up — `domain_id` is a PARAMETER, not `self.domain_id`:
13911                // this is a nested `fn`, not a method, so `self` is not in scope and
13912                // the original spelling was E0434. It only fails under feature sets
13913                // that compile this arm, which is why `--all-features` caught it and
13914                // the narrower lanes did not.
13915                .with_domain(domain_id)
13916                .with_namespace(namespace);
13917            if !node_name.is_empty() {
13918                info = info.with_node_name(node_name);
13919            }
13920            // issue 0793 — the parameter services get the PARAMETER profile
13921            // (`rmw_qos_profile_parameters`: KEEP_LAST(1000), reliable,
13922            // volatile), not the generic services one. `QOS_PROFILE_PARAMETERS`
13923            // existed with the right depth and had no caller, so every parameter
13924            // server ran on a depth-10 queue while ROS 2 gives them 1000 — which
13925            // matters exactly when a tool sets many parameters at once, the case
13926            // the deep queue is for.
13927            session
13928                .create_service(&info, QoSProfile::parameter_services_default())
13929                .map_err(|e| (NodeError::Transport(e), suffix))
13930        }
13931
13932        let get_handle = create_param_srv::<GetParameters>(
13933            &mut self.session,
13934            self.domain_id,
13935            &node_fqn,
13936            ns,
13937            nn,
13938            "get_parameters",
13939        )?;
13940        let set_handle = create_param_srv::<SetParameters>(
13941            &mut self.session,
13942            self.domain_id,
13943            &node_fqn,
13944            ns,
13945            nn,
13946            "set_parameters",
13947        )?;
13948        let set_atomic_handle = create_param_srv::<SetParametersAtomically>(
13949            &mut self.session,
13950            self.domain_id,
13951            &node_fqn,
13952            ns,
13953            nn,
13954            "set_parameters_atomically",
13955        )?;
13956        let list_handle = create_param_srv::<ListParameters>(
13957            &mut self.session,
13958            self.domain_id,
13959            &node_fqn,
13960            ns,
13961            nn,
13962            "list_parameters",
13963        )?;
13964        let desc_handle = create_param_srv::<DescribeParameters>(
13965            &mut self.session,
13966            self.domain_id,
13967            &node_fqn,
13968            ns,
13969            nn,
13970            "describe_parameters",
13971        )?;
13972        let types_handle = create_param_srv::<GetParameterTypes>(
13973            &mut self.session,
13974            self.domain_id,
13975            &node_fqn,
13976            ns,
13977            nn,
13978            "get_parameter_types",
13979        )?;
13980
13981        Ok(ParameterServiceServers::new(
13982            // phase-426 W3 — the set carries the node whose parameters it
13983            // serves, so a handler can never read the store without saying
13984            // whose parameters it means.
13985            node,
13986            // Issue 1271 -- carried so a dropped request is reported against
13987            // the service a tool actually called.
13988            node_fqn,
13989            // Issue 1270 -- handles only. The buffers are the executor's one
13990            // shared pair (`ParamState::buffers`), not six per node.
13991            PSrv::<GetParameters>::new(get_handle),
13992            PSrv::<SetParameters>::new(set_handle),
13993            PSrv::<SetParametersAtomically>::new(set_atomic_handle),
13994            PSrv::<ListParameters>::new(list_handle),
13995            PSrv::<DescribeParameters>::new(desc_handle),
13996            PSrv::<GetParameterTypes>::new(types_handle),
13997        ))
13998    }
13999
14000    /// phase-426 W3 — the node FQNs this executor publishes parameter services
14001    /// under, in registration order.
14002    ///
14003    /// The acceptance question for W3 ("does a two-node image expose both
14004    /// FQNs?") answered without a wire: the six services are created from
14005    /// exactly this list, so asserting it asserts what `ros2 param list` will
14006    /// enumerate. The wire assertion is W6.
14007    pub fn parameter_service_node_names(
14008        &self,
14009    ) -> heapless::Vec<crate::names::ResolvedName, { crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS }> {
14010        let mut out = heapless::Vec::new();
14011        let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref() else {
14012            return out;
14013        };
14014        for set in params.services.iter() {
14015            let index = set.param_node().raw() as usize;
14016            let (name, namespace) = match self.nodes.get(index) {
14017                Some(record) => (record.name.as_str(), record.namespace.as_str()),
14018                None => (self.node_name.as_str(), self.namespace.as_str()),
14019            };
14020            if let Ok(fqn) = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(name, namespace) {
14021                let _ = out.push(fqn);
14022            }
14023        }
14024        out
14025    }
14026
14027    // phase-359 W10 / issue 0080 — `enable_parameter_persistence{,_with}` are
14028    // GONE with the seam they attached. Issue 0080 ruled on-device parameter
14029    // persistence a non-goal in July and listed both by name; nothing in the
14030    // tree ever called them, and the only backend that could be passed
14031    // (`FileParamStore`) is deleted. Runtime get/set/describe stay — it is the
14032    // PERSISTENCE half that was dropped.
14033}
14034
14035// ============================================================================
14036// Lifecycle services (cfg lifecycle-services)
14037// ============================================================================
14038
14039#[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
14040impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
14041    /// Register the five REP-2002 lifecycle services on this executor.
14042    ///
14043    /// After this call, `ros2 lifecycle set|get|list|nodes` can drive the
14044    /// stored [`LifecyclePollingNodeCtx`](crate::lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx)
14045    /// through the node's lifecycle. The state machine is created fresh
14046    /// (starting in `Unconfigured`); callers register their transition
14047    /// callbacks via [`Executor::lifecycle_state_machine_mut`].
14048    ///
14049    /// # Safety
14050    /// Registered callbacks on the state machine are C FFI function pointers.
14051    /// The caller must keep the callback code and any context it captures
14052    /// valid for as long as the executor processes services.
14053    pub fn register_lifecycle_services(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
14054        let ns = self.namespace.clone();
14055        let nn = self.node_name.clone();
14056        self.register_lifecycle_services_named(&ns, &nn)
14057    }
14058
14059    /// [`register_lifecycle_services`](Self::register_lifecycle_services),
14060    /// named after `node` rather than the executor's own identity.
14061    ///
14062    /// phase-488 node 2 (Nav2): a hosted C++ `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode`
14063    /// is a node CREATED on the process executor, whose own identity is the
14064    /// default `node`. Registering through the executor served
14065    /// `/node/change_state` beside a phantom `/node`, and `ros2 lifecycle get
14066    /// /velocity_smoother` answered "Node not found". Parameter services were
14067    /// already per node (the reconcile); this is the same for lifecycle.
14068    pub fn register_lifecycle_services_on(
14069        &mut self,
14070        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14071    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
14072        let (ns, nn) = {
14073            let r = self.node(node).ok_or(NodeError::NotInitialized)?;
14074            (r.namespace.clone(), r.name.clone())
14075        };
14076        self.register_lifecycle_services_named(&ns, &nn)
14077    }
14078
14079    fn register_lifecycle_services_named(&mut self, ns: &str, nn: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
14080        use crate::{
14081            lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx,
14082            lifecycle_services::{
14083                ChangeState, GetAvailableStates, GetAvailableTransitions, GetState,
14084                LifecycleRuntimeState, LifecycleServiceServers,
14085            },
14086        };
14087        use nros_core::RosService;
14088
14089        // Build the node FQN from namespace + node_name (same convention as
14090        // register_parameter_services).
14091        let mut node_fqn = heapless::String::<256>::new();
14092        if ns.is_empty() || ns == "/" {
14093            node_fqn.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14094            node_fqn.push_str(nn).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14095        } else {
14096            node_fqn.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14097            node_fqn
14098                .push_str(ns.trim_matches('/'))
14099                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14100            node_fqn.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14101            node_fqn.push_str(nn).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14102        }
14103
14104        fn create_lc_srv<Svc>(
14105            session: &mut session::ConcreteSession,
14106            domain_id: u32,
14107            node_fqn: &str,
14108            namespace: &str,
14109            node_name: &str,
14110            suffix: &str,
14111        ) -> Result<session::RmwServiceServer, NodeError>
14112        where
14113            Svc: RosService,
14114            Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
14115            Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
14116        {
14117            // Issue 1293 — register both halves first, as `create_param_srv`
14118            // does since issue 1268: Cyclone creates a topic only for a type it
14119            // holds a descriptor for. Three of the five request types are
14120            // EMPTY, and an empty schema had no descriptor until codegen gave
14121            // it rosidl's `structure_needs_at_least_one_member` byte. A no-op
14122            // on backends that need no descriptors (zenoh, xrce).
14123            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Request>()?;
14124            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Reply>()?;
14125            let mut name = heapless::String::<256>::new();
14126            name.push_str(node_fqn)
14127                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14128            name.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14129            name.push_str(suffix).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14130            let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(&name, Svc::SERVICE_NAME, Svc::SERVICE_HASH)
14131                .with_domain(domain_id)
14132                .with_namespace(namespace);
14133            if !node_name.is_empty() {
14134                info = info.with_node_name(node_name);
14135            }
14136            session
14137                .create_service(&info, QoSProfile::services_default())
14138                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)
14139        }
14140
14141        /// Issue 1587 — the ONE publisher the REP-2002 family claims,
14142        /// `~/transition_event`. Shaped like `create_lc_srv` beside it both
14143        /// because the naming rule is the same (node FQN + suffix) and
14144        /// because `check-infra-queryable-counts` counts the creation sites
14145        /// to hold `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_PUBLISHERS` to them, exactly as it
14146        /// already holds `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_QUERYABLES` to the five above.
14147        fn create_lc_pub<Msg: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw>(
14148            session: &mut session::ConcreteSession,
14149            domain_id: u32,
14150            node_fqn: &str,
14151            namespace: &str,
14152            node_name: &str,
14153            suffix: &str,
14154            qos: QoSProfile,
14155        ) -> Result<session::RmwPublisher, NodeError> {
14156            // Issue 1293 — same rule as `create_lc_srv`: Cyclone needs the
14157            // `TransitionEvent` descriptor before it can create the topic.
14158            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Msg>()?;
14159            let mut name = heapless::String::<256>::new();
14160            name.push_str(node_fqn)
14161                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14162            name.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14163            name.push_str(suffix).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
14164            let mut info = TopicInfo::new(
14165                &name,
14166                <Msg as nros_core::RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
14167                Msg::TYPE_HASH,
14168            )
14169            .with_domain(domain_id)
14170            .with_namespace(namespace);
14171            if !node_name.is_empty() {
14172                info = info.with_node_name(node_name);
14173            }
14174            session
14175                .create_publisher(&info, qos)
14176                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)
14177        }
14178
14179        let cs_handle = create_lc_srv::<ChangeState>(
14180            &mut self.session,
14181            self.domain_id,
14182            &node_fqn,
14183            ns,
14184            nn,
14185            "change_state",
14186        )?;
14187        let gs_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetState>(
14188            &mut self.session,
14189            self.domain_id,
14190            &node_fqn,
14191            ns,
14192            nn,
14193            "get_state",
14194        )?;
14195        let gas_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetAvailableStates>(
14196            &mut self.session,
14197            self.domain_id,
14198            &node_fqn,
14199            ns,
14200            nn,
14201            "get_available_states",
14202        )?;
14203        let gat_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetAvailableTransitions>(
14204            &mut self.session,
14205            self.domain_id,
14206            &node_fqn,
14207            ns,
14208            nn,
14209            "get_available_transitions",
14210        )?;
14211        let gtg_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetAvailableTransitions>(
14212            &mut self.session,
14213            self.domain_id,
14214            &node_fqn,
14215            ns,
14216            nn,
14217            "get_transition_graph",
14218        )?;
14219
14220        // Issue 1587 — REP-2002's communication interface is the five
14221        // services PLUS this. VOLATILE, so it costs a publisher slot and a
14222        // liveliness token and NO queryable; see
14223        // `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_PUBLISHERS` for the measurement that settled it.
14224        let te_handle = create_lc_pub::<nros_lifecycle_msgs::msg::TransitionEvent>(
14225            &mut self.session,
14226            self.domain_id,
14227            &node_fqn,
14228            ns,
14229            nn,
14230            crate::lifecycle_services::TRANSITION_EVENT_SUFFIX,
14231            crate::lifecycle_services::transition_event_qos(),
14232        )?;
14233
14234        // Issue 2070 -- built in their allocation, never on this frame.
14235        let servers = LifecycleServiceServers::try_new_boxed([
14236            cs_handle, gs_handle, gas_handle, gat_handle, gtg_handle,
14237        ])
14238        .ok_or(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc))?;
14239
14240        self.lifecycle = Some(alloc::boxed::Box::new(LifecycleRuntimeState {
14241            state_machine: LifecyclePollingNodeCtx::new(),
14242            services: servers,
14243            transition_event: te_handle,
14244        }));
14245
14246        Ok(())
14247    }
14248
14249    /// The `~/transition_event` publisher, for the tests that assert what
14250    /// reached the wire. Not a public capability: the executor announces, and
14251    /// a second publisher on the same topic would be a second source of truth.
14252    /// Its only callers are the mock-session tests, which a `rmw-cffi` build
14253    /// does not compile.
14254    #[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
14255    pub(crate) fn lifecycle_transition_event_publisher(&self) -> Option<&session::RmwPublisher> {
14256        self.lifecycle.as_ref().map(|lc| &lc.transition_event)
14257    }
14258
14259    /// Mutable access to the lifecycle state machine, if registered.
14260    ///
14261    /// Used to register transition callbacks before spinning and to read the
14262    /// current state from application code.
14263    pub fn lifecycle_state_machine_mut(
14264        &mut self,
14265    ) -> Option<&mut crate::lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx> {
14266        self.lifecycle.as_mut().map(|lc| &mut lc.state_machine)
14267    }
14268
14269    /// Immutable access to the lifecycle state machine, if registered.
14270    pub fn lifecycle_state_machine(&self) -> Option<&crate::lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx> {
14271        self.lifecycle.as_ref().map(|lc| &lc.state_machine)
14272    }
14273
14274    /// Register a safe lifecycle node (issue 0335 / phase-317).
14275    ///
14276    /// Binds the five REP-2002 lifecycle services and wires each transition to
14277    /// the [`LifecycleCallbacks`](crate::lifecycle::LifecycleCallbacks) trait
14278    /// impl — the safe Rust counterpart to the C++ `nros::LifecycleNode`. No
14279    /// `unsafe` in user code; alloc-free (monomorphized trampolines).
14280    ///
14281    /// `node` must outlive this executor's lifecycle registration: the context
14282    /// pointer stored here is dereferenced on every transition until the
14283    /// executor is finalized. The executor spins single-threaded, so the
14284    /// `&mut node` reconstituted inside a callback is never aliased.
14285    pub fn register_lifecycle_node<T: crate::lifecycle::LifecycleCallbacks>(
14286        &mut self,
14287        node: &mut T,
14288    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
14289        use crate::lifecycle::{LifecycleCallbackSlot as Slot, trampolines};
14290
14291        self.register_lifecycle_services()?;
14292        let sm = self
14293            .lifecycle_state_machine_mut()
14294            .ok_or(NodeError::NotInitialized)?;
14295        sm.set_context(node as *mut T as *mut core::ffi::c_void);
14296        sm.register(Slot::Configure, Some(trampolines::on_configure::<T>));
14297        sm.register(Slot::Activate, Some(trampolines::on_activate::<T>));
14298        sm.register(Slot::Deactivate, Some(trampolines::on_deactivate::<T>));
14299        sm.register(Slot::Cleanup, Some(trampolines::on_cleanup::<T>));
14300        sm.register(Slot::Shutdown, Some(trampolines::on_shutdown::<T>));
14301        sm.register(Slot::Error, Some(trampolines::on_error::<T>));
14302        Ok(())
14303    }
14304}
14305
14306// ============================================================================
14307// phase-446 W6 -- the contract's declared parameters (cfg param-services)
14308// ============================================================================
14309
14310#[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
14311impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
14312    /// Hand the executor the parameters each node's contract declares.
14313    ///
14314    /// The entry calls this before any node registers. It only RECORDS the
14315    /// table: the check runs where an application declares a parameter (the
14316    /// `nros` node runtime), not in [`Self::declare_parameter_on`], because
14317    /// that funnel also carries the launch seed, whose value type is still
14318    /// inferred from text and was already held to the contract by the
14319    /// resolver.
14320    pub fn set_declared_params(&mut self, declared: nros_params::DeclaredParams) {
14321        self.declared_params = declared;
14322    }
14323
14324    /// The table [`Self::set_declared_params`] recorded (empty by default).
14325    pub fn declared_params(&self) -> nros_params::DeclaredParams {
14326        self.declared_params
14327    }
14328}
14329
14330// ============================================================================
14331// Parameter declaration API (cfg param-services)
14332// ============================================================================
14333
14334#[cfg(feature = "param-store")]
14335impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
14336    /// phase-461 W6 — build the parameter STORE and register no service.
14337    ///
14338    /// What an image declaring the `params` axis (and not `param_services`)
14339    /// calls ahead of its nodes: launch seeds and `declare_parameter` land in
14340    /// the store, and `ros2 param` reaches none of it, because no queryable
14341    /// was created. The primary node's `use_sim_time` placeholder is seeded
14342    /// as it is for a served store; nothing can SET it here, which is the
14343    /// axis' stated limit.
14344    ///
14345    /// Idempotent, and a later [`Self::register_parameter_services`] keeps
14346    /// this store and adds the six services on top of it.
14347    pub fn register_parameter_store(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
14348        if self.ensure_parameter_store() {
14349            Ok(())
14350        } else {
14351            Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc))
14352        }
14353    }
14354
14355    /// Issue 0745 — lazily create the parameter STORE (no services yet).
14356    /// Launch-param seeding runs before any node is constructed; the six
14357    /// service servers attach later in `register_parameter_services`,
14358    /// which preserves this store.
14359    /// `true` when the store exists afterwards. `false` only when the platform
14360    /// heap refused its allocation (issue 1706), which is reported once, here,
14361    /// with the size it asked for.
14362    fn ensure_parameter_store(&mut self) -> bool {
14363        if self.params.is_none() {
14364            if self.param_store_refused {
14365                return false;
14366            }
14367            let Some(state) = Self::new_param_state(
14368                core::mem::take(&mut self.param_slots),
14369                core::mem::take(&mut self.param_home),
14370            ) else {
14371                self.param_store_refused = true;
14372                report_parameter_store_refused();
14373                return false;
14374            };
14375            self.params = Some(state);
14376            // phase-430 W2 — the executor's implicit PRIMARY node exists the
14377            // moment the store does, whether or not a node record has been
14378            // built yet, so it is seeded here. The other node keys are seeded
14379            // in `reconcile_parameter_services`, as each one's set of six goes
14380            // up.
14381            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY);
14382        }
14383        true
14384    }
14385
14386    /// phase-430 W2 — declare `use_sim_time = false`, as rclcpp does on EVERY
14387    /// node.
14388    ///
14389    /// Upstream auto-declares the parameter in `rclcpp::Node`'s constructor, so
14390    /// `ros2 param list` shows it and `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true`
14391    /// reaches a node whose author never wrote a line about simulated time.
14392    /// Ours honoured the parameter only if the APP had declared it: the store
14393    /// refuses an undeclared set (`allow_undeclared` is false), so the runtime
14394    /// switch worked on exactly the nodes that least needed it.
14395    ///
14396    /// The seed is a PLACEHOLDER, tracked by `ParamState::sim_time_seeded`,
14397    /// because the store refuses a duplicate name: without that flag, seeding
14398    /// here would turn an application's own `declare_parameter("use_sim_time",
14399    /// Bool(true))` into a refusal and the auto-declared default would silently
14400    /// beat the app. `yield_seeded_use_sim_time` steps the placeholder aside
14401    /// for the first real declaration, whatever value or descriptor it carries.
14402    ///
14403    /// PER NODE, both here and in the flag. phase-426 keyed the store and the
14404    /// six services by node, so "every node" is now literally expressible and
14405    /// this is where it is said: `ensure_parameter_store` seeds the executor's
14406    /// implicit PRIMARY, and `reconcile_parameter_services` seeds each further
14407    /// node key as its set of six goes up — which is exactly the set of nodes a
14408    /// `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true` can reach.
14409    ///
14410    /// It deliberately does NOT go through `note_reserved_parameter`, so
14411    /// `sim_time_stated` stays false: an auto-declared default is not a
