14412    /// STATEMENT by anyone. Recording it as one would make every executor with
14413    /// parameter services write `set_active(false)` onto a PROCESS-GLOBAL gate
14414    /// on its first spin — switching off a simulated clock another executor in
14415    /// the same image installed, which is exactly the collision
14416    /// `sim_time_stated` was added for (issue 1104). That property is per node
14417    /// too: seeding N nodes must still be N statements by nobody.
14418    ///
14419    /// Gated on `sim-time` as well as `param-services`: an image that cannot
14420    /// act on the parameter should not advertise it, because a settable knob
14421    /// that does nothing is worse than an absent one.
14422    fn seed_use_sim_time_default(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId) {
14423        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
14424        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut()
14425            && let Some(seeded) = params.sim_time_seeded.get_mut(node.index())
14426            && params.server.declare(
14427                node.into(),
14428                crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM,
14429                nros_params::ParameterValue::Bool(false),
14430            )
14431        {
14432            *seeded = true;
14433        }
14434        let _ = node;
14435    }
14436
14437    /// phase-430 W2 — step the seeded `use_sim_time` aside for an application
14438    /// that declares it itself on `node`. Returns whether it did.
14439    ///
14440    /// The app's declaration must WIN — its own default, its own descriptor —
14441    /// and a declaration is refused when the name is already taken, so the
14442    /// placeholder has to leave before the real one arrives. Only ever the
14443    /// placeholder: once a real declaration has landed the flag is false and a
14444    /// second declaration is refused exactly as it was before W2.
14445    ///
14446    /// Only ever THIS node's placeholder, too: an app that names
14447    /// `use_sim_time` on one node of an image has said nothing about the
14448    /// others, and their seeds stay placeholders for whoever declares next.
14449    fn yield_seeded_use_sim_time(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId, name: &str) -> bool {
14450        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
14451        if name == crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM
14452            && let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut()
14453            && let Some(seeded) = params.sim_time_seeded.get_mut(node.index())
14454            && core::mem::replace(seeded, false)
14455        {
14456            return params.server.remove(node.into(), name);
14457        }
14458        let _ = (node, name);
14459        false
14460    }
14461
14462    /// The HEAP home for the parameter slot table, used only when the
14463    /// executor's backing carved none.
14464    ///
14465    /// phase-382 W2' — `ParameterServer` no longer OWNS its slots; it borrows
14466    /// a caller-placed [`nros_params::ParameterTable`]. phase-382 W3' carves
14467    /// that table out of the caller's executor backing whenever the build
14468    /// KNOWS the image builds a store ([`ExecutorSizing::params`](super::storage::ExecutorSizing::params), from
14469    /// `nros_params::IMPLIED_STORE_SLOTS`); this function is what remains for a
14470    /// store the build could not see — one reached only from application
14471    /// code — and for an executor opened with a sizing that carves none. It
14472    /// makes a single heap allocation, leaked, one per such executor that
14473    /// touches parameters. The leak is what buys the `'static`
14474    /// the borrow needs without making `ParamState` self-referential (a
14475    /// `ParamState` that owned the storage AND a server borrowing it is not
14476    /// expressible), and it is bounded — `ensure_parameter_store` runs this
14477    /// at most once per executor.
14478    ///
14479    /// Issue 0756 — the placement dance is still here because the SIZE is
14480    /// still here; it only moved off `ParameterServer` and onto
14481    /// `ParameterStorage`. That storage is 285,184 bytes at the default
14482    /// `MAX_PARAMETERS=32` and 2,281,472 at 256 (`ParameterValue` is sized by
14483    /// its `StringArray` variant, so every slot costs ~8.5 KiB regardless of
14484    /// what it holds). `Box::new(ParameterStorage::new())` materialises all of
14485    /// that on the caller's stack before copying it into the allocation,
14486    /// because Rust has no placement-new. On the Zephyr lane that silently
14487    /// overran the thread stack: an image built with 256 slots boots to
14488    /// `dds_create_participant` and hangs with no fault and no output, while
14489    /// 32 — which fits the 512 KiB main stack the cyclonedds snippet asks for
14490    /// — runs clean. Initialising through the allocation bounds the largest
14491    /// stack temporary at one slot, so the knob no longer decides whether boot
14492    /// survives.
14493    ///
14494    /// Issue 1706 -- FALLIBLE. This is the one allocation every parameter
14495    /// declaration reaches, in every language and on every RTOS, and it is the
14496    /// largest single request most images make. `Box::new_uninit` sent a
14497    /// failure to the OOM handler: Zephyr printed `HEAP EXHAUSTED` and died in
14498    /// issue 0589's recursion, FreeRTOS heap_4 hung in `MALLOC FAILED`. Every
14499    /// caller already has a refusal to return (`declare_parameter` is a
14500    /// `bool`), so the failure is now one, named by
14501    /// [`report_parameter_store_refused`] with the size it asked for.
14502    ///
14503    /// Issue 1812 -- `alloc` only. Without a heap there is no fallback, and
14504    /// the store is the carved one or none (see `new_param_state`).
14505    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
14506    fn leak_parameter_storage() -> Option<nros_params::ParameterTable<'static>> {
14507        #[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc"))]
14508        if RefuseParameterStore::armed() {
14509            return None;
14510        }
14511        let mut uninit = nros_rmw::fallible::try_box_uninit::<nros_params::ParameterStorage>()?;
14512        // Safety: `try_box_uninit` gives a correctly-sized, correctly-aligned
14513        // allocation for exactly this type, and `init_in_place` writes every
14514        // slot exactly once before `assume_init` observes it.
14515        unsafe {
14516            nros_params::ParameterStorage::init_in_place(uninit.as_mut_ptr());
14517            Some(alloc::boxed::Box::leak(uninit.assume_init()).as_table())
14518        }
14519    }
14520
14521    /// Build the executor's `ParamState`.
14522    ///
14523    /// phase-382 W3' — `carved` are the backing's store slots: non-empty, they
14524    /// ARE the store and the heap is not asked; empty, the store falls back to
14525    /// [`leak_parameter_storage`](Self::leak_parameter_storage).
14526    ///
14527    /// Issue 1812 — and `home` is the services' carved region, which the
14528    /// backing places on the same condition: non-empty, the state, its service
14529    /// sets, the buffer pair and the staging slot are built IN it and nothing
14530    /// here allocates. Otherwise the state is one heap allocation, initialised
14531    /// in place (`ParamState::try_boxed` — it is several KiB now, so never a
14532    /// by-value `Box::new`). Without `alloc` that fallback does not exist and
14533    /// an executor whose backing carved nothing gets `None`, which every caller
14534    /// reports as the named refusal (`report_parameter_store_refused`).
14535    fn new_param_state(
14536        carved: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<nros_params::ParameterSlot>],
14537        home: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<super::storage::ParamHome>],
14538    ) -> Option<crate::param_store::Placed<'s, crate::param_store::ParamState<'s>>> {
14539        let table = if carved.is_empty() {
14540            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
14541            {
14542                Self::leak_parameter_storage()?
14543            }
14544            #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
14545            {
14546                return None;
14547            }
14548        } else {
14549            // Said once per store, so a boot log answers "where did the store
14550            // come from" without a debugger: issue 1706's measurements were
14551            // all heap-peak arithmetic, and this line is the direct answer.
14552            nros_log::log_info!(
14553                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
14554                "parameter store: {} slots ({} B) + {} ({} B) carved from the executor backing",
14555                carved.len(),
14556                core::mem::size_of_val(carved),
14557                // Issue 1897 -- the home is the store's state, plus the
14558                // services' sets and buffers only where they are compiled.
14559                if cfg!(feature = "param-services") {
14560                    "state and services"
14561                } else {
14562                    "state"
14563                },
14564                core::mem::size_of_val(home)
14565            );
14566            nros_params::ParameterTable::init_in(carved)
14567        };
14568        let server = nros_params::ParameterServer::new_in(table);
14569        match home.first_mut() {
14570            Some(home) => Some(crate::param_store::ParamHome::init_in(home, server)),
14571            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
14572            None => crate::param_store::ParamState::try_boxed(server),
14573            #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
14574            None => None,
14575        }
14576    }
14577
14578    /// Install `-p` / `--params-file` parameter overrides — phase-482 W5.
14579    ///
14580    /// They are applied when a parameter is DECLARED: the declaration's value
14581    /// is replaced by the override's, typed by it (`apply_argv_param_override`).
14582    /// So an override reaches a parameter on every road that declares through
14583    /// this executor — C, C++ and Rust — including the launch file's baked
14584    /// values, which the generated entry declares through the same seam.
14585    ///
14586    /// That makes argv WIN over a launch-baked parameter, the opposite of the
14587    /// remap tiers, deliberately: overriding a baked value at run time without
14588    /// a rebuild is what RFC-0015 §9 asks for ("a runtime override has
14589    /// identical effect to a `set_parameter` request after boot"), and upstream
14590    /// agrees — a launch file's parameters reach the node as command-line
14591    /// arguments themselves, where the later one wins.
14592    ///
14593    /// Overrides accumulate in argv order and the LAST one that matches a
14594    /// declaration wins, as rcl's do. A `node:` override matches the node of
14595    /// that NAME; one without matches every node.
14596    ///
14597    /// Fails only when the parameter store could not be allocated (issue 1706),
14598    /// in which case nothing is installed.
14599    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
14600    pub fn install_argv_params<'p, I>(&mut self, params: I) -> Result<usize, NodeError>
14601    where
14602        I: IntoIterator<Item = crate::ros_args::ParamArg<'p>>,
14603    {
14604        if !self.ensure_parameter_store() {
14605            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
14606        }
14607        let Some(state) = self.params.as_deref_mut() else {
14608            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
14609        };
14610        let mut n = 0;
14611        for p in params {
14612            state
14613                .argv_overrides
14614                .push(crate::param_store::ArgvParamOverride {
14615                    node: p.node.map(alloc::string::String::from),
14616                    name: alloc::string::String::from(p.name),
14617                    value: alloc::string::String::from(p.value),
14618                });
14619            n += 1;
14620        }
14621        Ok(n)
14622    }
14623
14624    /// The `-p` / `--params-file` overrides that apply to `node`, one per
14625    /// name — issue 2057, for rclcpp's
14626    /// `NodeParametersInterface::get_parameter_overrides()`.
14627    ///
14628    /// The selection is the one a declaration makes
14629    /// (`apply_argv_param_override`): the LAST override of a name that applies
14630    /// wins, and a `node:` override applies only to the node of that name.
14631    /// Each text is typed as a declaration with no default types it (bool,
14632    /// integer, double, then string), because a listing has no declared type
14633    /// to follow. An override no type accepts (a string past the store's
14634    /// bound) is left out. Yields in argv order of the winning override.
14635    #[cfg(all(feature = "param-store", feature = "alloc"))]
14636    pub fn argv_param_overrides_on(
14637        &self,
14638        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14639    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, nros_params::ParameterValue)> + '_ {
14640        let node_name = self.node(node).map(|r| r.name.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
14641        let list: &[crate::param_store::ArgvParamOverride] = self
14642            .params
14643            .as_deref()
14644            .map(|s| s.argv_overrides.as_slice())
14645            .unwrap_or(&[]);
14646        let applies = move |o: &crate::param_store::ArgvParamOverride| {
14647            o.node.as_deref().is_none_or(|n| n == node_name)
14648        };
14649        list.iter()
14650            .enumerate()
14651            .filter(move |(i, o)| {
14652                applies(o) && !list[i + 1..].iter().any(|l| l.name == o.name && applies(l))
14653            })
14654            .filter_map(|(_, o)| {
14655                typed_param_override(&o.value, &nros_params::ParameterValue::NotSet)
14656                    .map(|v| (o.name.as_str(), v))
14657            })
14658    }
14659
14660    /// Issue 2070 — does an argv override name this parameter? The cheap
14661    /// question [`declare_parameter_on_ref`](Self::declare_parameter_on_ref)
14662    /// asks before it enters the frame that types one.
14663    #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
14664    fn has_argv_param_override(&self, _node: super::node_record::NodeId, _name: &str) -> bool {
14665        false
14666    }
14667
14668    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
14669    fn has_argv_param_override(&self, node: super::node_record::NodeId, name: &str) -> bool {
14670        let Some(state) = self.params.as_deref() else {
14671            return false;
14672        };
14673        if state.argv_overrides.is_empty() {
14674            return false;
14675        }
14676        let node_name = self.node(node).map(|r| r.name.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
14677        state
14678            .argv_overrides
14679            .iter()
14680            .any(|o| o.name == name && o.node.as_deref().is_none_or(|n| n == node_name))
14681    }
14682
14683    /// The value a declaration of `name` on `node` should take — the last
14684    /// matching argv override, typed by `declared`, or `declared` itself — and
14685    /// whether an override was applied.
14686    ///
14687    /// An override whose text does not parse as the declared type is NOT
14688    /// applied: it is logged at error severity, naming the parameter, the text
14689    /// and the type, and the declared default stands (RFC-0015 §9.6 — "log +
14690    /// ignore, never panic"). An array-typed declaration takes no override yet.
14691    #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
14692    fn apply_argv_param_override(
14693        &self,
14694        _node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14695        _name: &str,
14696        declared: nros_params::ParameterValue,
14697    ) -> (nros_params::ParameterValue, bool) {
14698        // Issue 1812 -- argv overrides are a hosted-edge input installed
14699        // through `install_argv_params`, which is `alloc`-only.
14700        (declared, false)
14701    }
14702
14703    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
14704    fn apply_argv_param_override(
14705        &self,
14706        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14707        name: &str,
14708        declared: nros_params::ParameterValue,
14709    ) -> (nros_params::ParameterValue, bool) {
14710        let Some(state) = self.params.as_deref() else {
14711            return (declared, false);
14712        };
14713        if state.argv_overrides.is_empty() {
14714            return (declared, false);
14715        }
14716        let node_name = self.node(node).map(|r| r.name.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
14717        let Some(o) = state
14718            .argv_overrides
14719            .iter()
14720            .rev()
14721            .find(|o| o.name == name && o.node.as_deref().is_none_or(|n| n == node_name))
14722        else {
14723            return (declared, false);
14724        };
14725        match typed_param_override(&o.value, &declared) {
14726            Some(v) => (v, true),
14727            None => {
14728                nros_log::log_error!(
14729                    nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
14730                    "parameter override `{}:={}` is not a {:?}; the declared default stands",
14731                    name,
14732                    o.value,
14733                    declared.param_type()
14734                );
14735                (declared, false)
14736            }
14737        }
14738    }
14739
14740    /// Declare a parameter with a value on the executor's PRIMARY node.
14741    ///
14742    /// phase-426 W1 — the store is keyed by node, and this is the spelling for
14743    /// the executor's implicit primary node (`NodeId::PRIMARY`), which is the
14744    /// identity `register_parameter_services` publishes and the one every
14745    /// single-node entry means. Name a different node with
14746    /// [`declare_parameter_on`](Self::declare_parameter_on).
14747    ///
14748    /// phase-428 W6 — `#[must_use]`, for the reason `[[nodiscard]]` went on
14749    /// C++'s `Result`: the `else { false }` arm is silently discarded at a
14750    /// call site that drops the value, and `Node::logger` two files over
14751    /// already carries the attribute — so this was inconsistency, not house
14752    /// style. A declare that failed and was ignored is a parameter the program
14753    /// believes it has.
14754    #[must_use]
14755    pub fn declare_parameter(&mut self, name: &str, value: nros_params::ParameterValue) -> bool {
14756        self.declare_parameter_on(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY, name, value)
14757    }
14758
14759    /// Declare a parameter with a value on a named node.
14760    ///
14761    /// `#[must_use]` for the reason [`declare_parameter`](Self::declare_parameter)
14762    /// carries it: issue 1257's two dropped results moved to THIS method when
14763    /// they were fixed, so the attribute on the wrapper alone guarded nothing
14764    /// a launch-seed site could still drop.
14765    #[must_use]
14766    pub fn declare_parameter_on(
14767        &mut self,
14768        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14769        name: &str,
14770        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
14771    ) -> bool {
14772        self.declare_parameter_on_ref(node, name, &value)
14773    }
14774
14775    /// [`declare_parameter_on`](Self::declare_parameter_on), borrowing the
14776    /// value — issue 2070, and THE declare path the by-value spelling forwards
14777    /// to. A `ParameterValue` is ~8 KiB at the default capacities, and moving
14778    /// it through each frame of the declare path cost ~57 KiB of stack for one
14779    /// `declare_parameter<double>` (aarch64; ~67 KiB on Cortex-M3). Borrowed,
14780    /// it is copied once, into its slot.
14781    #[must_use]
14782    pub fn declare_parameter_on_ref(
14783        &mut self,
14784        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14785        name: &str,
14786        value: &nros_params::ParameterValue,
14787    ) -> bool {
14788        self.ensure_parameter_store();
14789        // The argv override is a hosted-edge input and rare; its frame (which
14790        // holds the typed override) is entered only when one applies, so the
14791        // common path carries no second value.
14792        if self.has_argv_param_override(node, name) {
14793            return self.declare_parameter_overridden(node, name, value);
14794        }
14795        self.declare_parameter_resolved(node, name, value)
14796    }
14797
14798    /// Issue 2070 — the override branch of
14799    /// [`declare_parameter_on_ref`](Self::declare_parameter_on_ref), in its
14800    /// own frame.
14801    #[inline(never)]
14802    fn declare_parameter_overridden(
14803        &mut self,
14804        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14805        name: &str,
14806        declared: &nros_params::ParameterValue,
14807    ) -> bool {
14808        let (value, _) = self.apply_argv_param_override(node, name, declared.clone());
14809        self.declare_parameter_resolved(node, name, &value)
14810    }
14811
14812    /// The store write and the reserved-name hook, for a value whose argv
14813    /// override has already been applied.
14814    fn declare_parameter_resolved(
14815        &mut self,
14816        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
14817        name: &str,
14818        value: &nros_params::ParameterValue,
14819    ) -> bool {
14820        // phase-430 W2 — an application declaring `use_sim_time` itself wins
14821        // over the auto-declared default, so the placeholder leaves first.
14822        let yielded = self.yield_seeded_use_sim_time(node, name);
14823        let accepted = match &mut self.params {
14824            Some(params) => params.server.declare_ref(node.into(), name, value),
14825            None => false,
14826        };
14827        if yielded && !accepted {
14828            // The app's own declaration was refused on its own terms (a full
14829            // store, an ill-formed range). Put the rclcpp default back rather
14830            // than leaving the name undeclared — that is a state neither the
14831            // app nor upstream asked for, and it would silently un-do W2 for
14832            // this node.
14833            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(node);
14834        }
14835        // phase-425 W3b — `use_sim_time` is RESERVED, exactly as in ROS 2: its
14836        // value is not a value the app reads, it is the switch that attaches the
14837        // time source. This is the one seam every language funnels through
14838        // (`nros::main!`'s launch bakes via `apply_param_services`, nros-c's
14839        // the rclc parameter server's `declare`, nros-cpp's `params_shim`), so hooking it
14840        // here covers all of them instead of once per entry path.
14841        //
14842        // phase-430 W3 / issue 1202 — the hook runs AFTER the store's verdict
14843        // and only on acceptance. It used to run first and unconditionally, so
14844        // a re-declaration the store REFUSES (the name is already there) still
14845        // flipped the switch: the store kept `use_sim_time = true` while the
14846        // `/clock` source detached, leaving an executor with sim time recorded
14847        // as on and no source attached, which is neither of the two states the
14848        // parameter can name.
14849        if accepted {
14850            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
14851        }
14852        accepted
14853    }
14854
14855    /// phase-425 W3b — record a reserved parameter's effect. Today that is
14856    /// `use_sim_time` and nothing else: it is the tree's only reserved name,
14857    /// and [`time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM`](crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM)
14858    /// is the only such constant.
14859    ///
14860    /// Called only after the store ACCEPTED a declaration, and it reads the
14861    /// value back OUT of the store instead of taking the caller's: what the
14862    /// switch must follow is what the store holds, and the two are the same
14863    /// thing only while every write succeeds (issue 1202). The read is
14864    /// [`refresh_use_sim_time_from_store`](Self::refresh_use_sim_time_from_store),
14865    /// the same one the runtime `ros2 param set` path uses, so the declare path
14866    /// and the wire path cannot disagree about the value.
14867    ///
14868    /// A non-bool `use_sim_time` is IGNORED rather than rejected: parameter
14869    /// declaration has no channel to report a complaint on (it returns "did the
14870    /// store take it"), and refusing the declaration outright would fail a node
14871    /// for a parameter ROS 2 lets it declare. The time source simply does not
14872    /// attach, which is the same outcome as `false`.
14873    ///
14874    /// Not covered: [`Executor::parameter`](Self::parameter)'s
14875    /// [`ParameterBuilder`](nros_params::ParameterBuilder) borrows the server
14876    /// and declares through it, so the executor never sees the write and
14877    /// `use_sim_time` named that way attaches nothing — issue 1203.
14878    /// Issue 1203 — finish a `use_sim_time` that went through
14879    /// [`parameter`](Self::parameter)'s builder.
14880    ///
14881    /// The builder held the store while it declared, so nothing told the
14882    /// executor; this is the spin after, reading the store back. A builder that
14883    /// declared the name gets the reserved-parameter hook a `declare_parameter`
14884    /// would have run. One that was dropped without declaring leaves the node
14885    /// with no `use_sim_time`, because `parameter_on` stepped the placeholder
14886    /// aside for it, so the placeholder goes back.
14887    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
14888    fn settle_builder_reserved_parameters(&mut self) {
14889        let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() else {
14890            return;
14891        };
14892        if !params.sim_time_via_builder.contains(&true) {
14893            return;
14894        }
14895        let pending = core::mem::replace(
14896            &mut params.sim_time_via_builder,
14897            [false; crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS],
14898        );
14899        let mut declared = false;
14900        for (index, _) in pending.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, p)| **p) {
14901            let node = super::node_record::NodeId(index as u8);
14902            let present = self.params.as_deref().is_some_and(|p| {
14903                p.server
14904                    .get(node.into(), crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM)
14905                    .is_some()
14906            });
14907            if present {
14908                declared = true;
14909            } else {
14910                self.seed_use_sim_time_default(node);
14911            }
14912        }
14913        if declared {
14914            self.note_reserved_parameter(crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM);
14915        }
14916    }
14917
14918    fn note_reserved_parameter(&mut self, name: &str) {
14919        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
14920        if name == crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM {
14921            self.refresh_use_sim_time_from_store();
14922        }
14923        let _ = name;
14924    }
14925
14926    /// phase-425 W3b — a parameter service handled `n` requests this spin.
14927    ///
14928    /// The hook exists so `use_sim_time` can be re-read after a runtime
14929    /// `ros2 param set`, WITHOUT a per-spin scan of the store. It takes the
14930    /// count unconditionally and ignores it when `sim-time` is off, rather than
14931    /// the call sites carrying the feature test: `handled` was then assigned and
14932    /// never read in the `param-services`-without-`sim-time` combo, which is a
14933    /// `-D warnings` error `check-build` catches and the narrower per-crate
14934    /// clippy runs do not.
14935    #[inline]
14936    fn note_param_services_ran(&mut self, handled: usize) {
14937        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
14938        if handled > 0 {
14939            self.refresh_use_sim_time_from_store();
14940        }
14941        let _ = handled;
14942        self.report_truncated_descriptions();
14943        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
14944        self.flush_parameter_events();
14945    }
14946
14947    /// phase-446 F2 -- log each parameter whose description did not fit
14948    /// `NROS_MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN`, once, naming the knob.
14949    ///
14950    /// `nros-params` has no logger, so it truncates, records the truncation on
14951    /// the stored descriptor, and hands it over here. Asked on every spin
14952    /// because a declaration can arrive through builders this executor never
14953    /// sees the end of (`parameter::<T>()` returns the store's own builder);
14954    /// while nothing is pending the store answers from one flag, without
14955    /// walking its table.
14956    #[cold]
14957    fn report_truncated_descriptions(&mut self) {
14958        let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() else {
14959            return;
14960        };
14961        let nodes = &self.nodes;
14962        params.server.take_truncated_descriptions(|key, name| {
14963            let (ns, node) = nodes
14964                .get(key.index())
14965                .map_or(("", "?"), |r| (r.namespace.as_str(), r.name.as_str()));
14966            nros_log::log_warn!(
14967                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
14968                "parameter `{}` on node {}/{}: its description is longer than \
14969                 NROS_MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN ({} bytes), so `ros2 param describe` \
14970                 answers it truncated at a character boundary. Raise \
14971                 NROS_MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN to keep it whole; 0 stores no \
14972                 descriptions. Logged once for this parameter (phase-446 F2).",
14973                name,
14974                ns.trim_end_matches('/'),
14975                node,
14976                nros_params::MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN
14977            );
14978        });
14979    }
14980
14981    /// Declare a parameter with a value and descriptor on the PRIMARY node.
14982    /// Returns `true` if successful.
14983    ///
14984    /// phase-428 W6 remainder — the sibling of [`Self::declare_parameter`],
14985    /// with the identical `else { false }` arm and no attribute. W6 marked the
14986    /// one method its audit named; this is the site three lines below it, which
14987    /// is the shape CLAUDE.md's "fix the CLASS, not the reported site" rule
14988    /// exists for.
14989    #[must_use]
14990    pub fn declare_parameter_with_descriptor(
14991        &mut self,
14992        name: &str,
14993        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
14994        descriptor: nros_params::ParameterDescriptor,
14995    ) -> bool {
14996        self.declare_parameter_with_descriptor_on(
14997            super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY,
14998            name,
14999            value,
15000            descriptor,
15001        )
15002    }
15003
15004    /// Declare a parameter with a value and descriptor on a named node.
15005    pub fn declare_parameter_with_descriptor_on(
15006        &mut self,
15007        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15008        name: &str,
15009        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
15010        descriptor: nros_params::ParameterDescriptor,
15011    ) -> bool {
15012        self.ensure_parameter_store();
15013        // phase-430 W2 — same rule as the sibling above: the app's own
15014        // declaration, descriptor and all, replaces the auto-declared default.
15015        let yielded = self.yield_seeded_use_sim_time(node, name);
15016        // Issue 2070 — borrowed, as on the sibling path; the override branch
15017        // has its own frame.
15018        let accepted = if self.has_argv_param_override(node, name) {
15019            self.declare_described_overridden(node, name, &value, descriptor)
15020        } else {
15021            match &mut self.params {
15022                Some(params) => params
15023                    .server
15024                    .try_declare_ref(node.into(), name, &value, Some(descriptor))
15025                    .is_ok(),
15026                None => false,
15027            }
15028        };
15029        if yielded && !accepted {
15030            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(node);
15031        }
15032        // phase-430 W3 / issue 1202 — the sibling declare path, which had NO
15033        // reserved hook at all: `declare_parameter_with_descriptor` stored
15034        // `use_sim_time` and attached nothing, so the same declaration meant
15035        // two different things depending on whether the app passed a
15036        // descriptor. Same seam, same verdict ordering, one shared hook.
15037        if accepted {
15038            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
15039        }
15040        accepted
15041    }
15042
15043    /// Issue 2070 — the override branch of
15044    /// [`declare_parameter_with_descriptor_on`](Self::declare_parameter_with_descriptor_on),
15045    /// in its own frame.
15046    ///
15047    /// phase-482 W5 — an argv override that the DESCRIPTOR refuses (out of
15048    /// range, or read-only with a different value) must not cost the
15049    /// parameter its existence: log it, then declare the code's default.
15050    #[inline(never)]
15051    fn declare_described_overridden(
15052        &mut self,
15053        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15054        name: &str,
15055        declared: &nros_params::ParameterValue,
15056        descriptor: nros_params::ParameterDescriptor,
15057    ) -> bool {
15058        let (overridden, differs) = self.apply_argv_param_override(node, name, declared.clone());
15059        let Some(params) = &mut self.params else {
15060            return false;
15061        };
15062        if params
15063            .server
15064            .try_declare_ref(node.into(), name, &overridden, Some(descriptor.clone()))
15065            .is_ok()
15066        {
15067            return true;
15068        }
15069        if !differs {
15070            return false;
15071        }
15072        nros_log::log_error!(
15073            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
15074            "parameter override for `{}` was refused by its descriptor; the declared \
15075             default stands",
15076            name
15077        );
15078        params
15079            .server
15080            .try_declare_ref(node.into(), name, declared, Some(descriptor))
15081            .is_ok()
15082    }
15083
15084    /// THE writer — phase-426 W2.
15085    ///
15086    /// Set an ALREADY-DECLARED parameter on the executor's primary node, with
15087    /// the same rules a remote `ros2 param set` gets: read-only, type, range
15088    /// (min/max/step), and issue 1151's refusal of a name the node never
15089    /// declared unless that node opted in through
15090    /// [`allow_undeclared_parameters_on`](Self::allow_undeclared_parameters_on).
15091    ///
15092    /// It routes through [`ParameterServer::apply`](nros_params::ParameterServer::apply),
15093    /// which is what makes the C and C++ facades, the by-value oracle, the
15094    /// streaming service path and the atomic pre-check agree — a facade that
15095    /// wrote the slot directly would be a second answer to "may this set
15096    /// happen", which is the class RFC-0019/0020 forbids. An in-image caller
15097    /// that genuinely wants declare-on-write names
15098    /// `params_mut()`/`set_or_declare` and has opted in by naming it.
15099    ///
15100    /// Returns [`SetParameterResult::NotFound`] when the store does not exist
15101    /// yet (no parameter has been declared and no services registered).
15102    pub fn set_parameter(
15103        &mut self,
15104        name: &str,
15105        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
15106    ) -> nros_params::SetParameterResult {
15107        self.set_parameter_on(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY, name, value)
15108    }
15109
15110    /// [`set_parameter`](Self::set_parameter) on a named node.
15111    pub fn set_parameter_on(
15112        &mut self,
15113        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15114        name: &str,
15115        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
15116    ) -> nros_params::SetParameterResult {
15117        // Reserved parameters (`use_sim_time`) take effect on a set exactly as
15118        // they do on a declare — this is the seam every language funnels
15119        // through, so hooking it once here covers all of them.
15120        //
15121        // AFTER the store's verdict and only on `Success`, for the reason issue
15122        // 1202 gives one function up: the hook used to run first and off the
15123        // caller's value, so a write the store REFUSED still moved the switch
15124        // and left sim time recorded as on with no source attached. `apply` has
15125        // more ways to refuse than `declare` does — read-only, type, range,
15126        // undeclared-without-the-node-option — so a writer that hooked first
15127        // would reach that state from four directions instead of one.
15128        let result = match &mut self.params {
15129            Some(params) => params.server.apply(node.into(), name, value),
15130            None => nros_params::SetParameterResult::NotFound,
15131        };
15132        if result == nros_params::SetParameterResult::Success {
15133            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
15134        }
15135        result
15136    }
15137
15138    /// phase-491 W2 (RFC-0105 D7) — rclc's LOCAL typed set on `node`:
15139    /// type, the on-set hooks with `(old, new)`, the write. Read-only and
15140    /// range are NOT checked, because rclc's owner of a parameter is not bound
15141    /// by them; remote writes keep [`set_parameter_on`](Self::set_parameter_on)'s
15142    /// rules. The reserved-parameter hook runs on success, as on every writer.
15143    pub fn set_parameter_local_on(
15144        &mut self,
15145        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15146        name: &str,
15147        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
15148    ) -> nros_params::SetParameterResult {
15149        let result = match &mut self.params {
15150            Some(params) => params.server.set_local(node.into(), name, value),
15151            None => nros_params::SetParameterResult::NotFound,
15152        };
15153        if result == nros_params::SetParameterResult::Success {
15154            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
15155        }
15156        result
15157    }
15158
15159    #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
15160    /// Issue 2023 — the serving half of `/parameter_events`: a node whose six
15161    /// services just came up publishes its events unless it opted out. A
15162    /// failure is LOGGED and the services stay up: `ros2 param` still works,
15163    /// and a publisher slot the image did not size for is a fact to report,
15164    /// not a reason to take the services down with it.
15165    #[inline(never)]
15166    fn start_parameter_events_for_served_node(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId) {
15167        if self
15168            .params
15169            .as_deref()
15170            .is_some_and(|p| p.events_opt_out.get(node.into()))
15171        {
15172            return;
15173        }
15174        if let Err(e) = self.enable_parameter_events_on(node) {
15175            report_parameter_events_refused(e);
15176        }
15177    }
15178
15179    #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
15180    /// Issue 2023 — `node` publishes no `/parameter_events` (rclc's
15181    /// `notify_changed_over_dds = false`; rclcpp's
15182    /// `start_parameter_event_publisher(false)`). Stops logging its changes,
15183    /// and keeps [`register_parameter_services`](Self::register_parameter_services)
15184    /// from switching them on. The executor's one publisher stays up if
15185    /// another node uses it.
15186    pub fn disable_parameter_events_on(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId) {
15187        if !self.ensure_parameter_store() {
15188            return;
15189        }
15190        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() {
15191            params.events_opt_out.set(node.into(), true);
15192            params.server.set_parameter_events(node.into(), false);
15193        }
15194    }
15195
15196    #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
15197    /// phase-491 W3 (RFC-0105 D8) — publish `node`'s parameter changes on
15198    /// `/parameter_events` (rclc's `notify_changed_over_dds`).
15199    ///
15200    /// Creates the executor's one `/parameter_events` publisher on the first
15201    /// call (see `ParamState::event_publisher`), typed
15202    /// `rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterEvent`, RELIABLE + VOLATILE as upstream's
15203    /// `parameter_events` profile. Its depth is upstream's 1000 on a hosted
15204    /// build and `NROS_PARAM_EVENTS_DEPTH` (default 1) otherwise, because a
15205    /// reliable DDS writer's history is memory the RMW reserves; depth is not
15206    /// a matching criterion, so an upstream subscriber still matches.
15207    /// Idempotent.
15208    pub fn enable_parameter_events_on(
15209        &mut self,
15210        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15211    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
15212        type Event = nros_rcl_interfaces::msg::ParameterEvent;
15213        if !self.ensure_parameter_store() {
15214            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
15215        }
15216        let idx = node.index();
15217        if idx >= crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS {
15218            return Err(NodeError::NodeTableFull);
15219        }
15220        // Issue 2023 — an explicit request overrides an earlier opt-out.
15221        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref_mut() {
15222            params.events_opt_out.set(node.into(), false);
15223        }
15224        if self
15225            .params
15226            .as_ref()
15227            .is_some_and(|p| p.event_publisher.is_some())
15228        {
15229            if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() {
15230                params.server.set_parameter_events(node.into(), true);
15231            }
15232            return Ok(());
15233        }
15234        // The event is encoded into the services' reply buffer; on the heap
15235        // road that pair is allocated with the first service set, which may
15236        // not exist yet.
15237        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
15238        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut()
15239            && params.buffers.is_none()
15240        {
15241            params.buffers = Some(
15242                crate::parameter_services::ParamServiceBuffers::try_with_capacity(
15243                    crate::parameter_services::param_service_buffer_bytes(),
15244                )
15245                .ok_or(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc))?,
15246            );
15247        }
15248        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Event>()?;
15249        let qos = QoSProfile::parameter_events_default().depth(nros_params::PARAM_EVENTS_DEPTH);
15250        let handle = create_param_event_pub(self, node, qos)?;
15251        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() {
15252            params.event_publisher = Some(handle);
15253            params.server.set_parameter_events(node.into(), true);
15254        }
15255        Ok(())
15256    }
15257
15258    #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
15259    /// phase-491 W3 — publish every pending parameter change, one
15260    /// `ParameterEvent` each, oldest first. Runs after each spin's parameter
15261    /// services and after every C or C++ parameter call; nothing allocates.
15262    pub fn flush_parameter_events(&mut self) {
15263        let stamp_ns = self
15264            .epoch_us_fn
15265            .or(self.clock_us_fn)
15266            .map_or(0, |clock| clock().saturating_mul(1000));
15267        let mut lost: u32 = 0;
15268        loop {
15269            let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() else {
15270                return;
15271            };
15272            // Issue 2023 — a node's start-up event first, then the log.
15273            let Some(event) = params
15274                .server
15275                .pop_initial_parameter_event()
15276                .or_else(|| params.server.pop_parameter_event())
15277            else {
15278                break;
15279            };
15280            let idx = event.node.index();
15281            let mut fqn = heapless::String::<256>::new();
15282            match self.nodes.get(idx) {
15283                Some(r) => {
15284                    if let Ok(f) = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(&r.name, &r.namespace) {
15285                        let _ = fqn.push_str(f.as_str());
15286                    }
15287                }
15288                None => {
15289                    if let Ok(f) =
15290                        crate::names::fully_qualified_name(&self.node_name, &self.namespace)
15291                    {
15292                        let _ = fqn.push_str(f.as_str());
15293                    }
15294                }
15295            }
15296            let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() else {
15297                return;
15298            };
15299            let crate::param_store::ParamState {
15300                server,
15301                buffers,
15302                event_publisher,
15303                ..
15304            } = &mut **params;
15305            let (Some(publisher), Some(buffers)) = (event_publisher.as_ref(), buffers.as_mut())
15306            else {
15307                continue;
15308            };
15309            let value = match event.kind {
15310                nros_params::ParameterEventKind::Deleted => None,
15311                _ => server.get(event.node, event.name.as_str()),
15312            };
15313            let encoded = crate::parameter_services::encode_parameter_event(
15314                buffers.reply_mut(),
15315                stamp_ns,
15316                fqn.as_str(),
15317                event.kind,
15318                event.name.as_str(),
15319                value,
15320            );
15321            match encoded {
15322                Some(n) => {
15323                    use nros_rmw::Publisher as _;
15324                    if publisher.publish_raw(&buffers.reply_mut()[..n]).is_err() {
15325                        lost = lost.saturating_add(1);
15326                    }
15327                }
15328                None => {
15329                    lost = lost.saturating_add(1);
15330                }
15331            }
15332        }
15333        let dropped = self
15334            .params
15335            .as_mut()
15336            .map_or(0, |p| p.server.take_parameter_events_dropped());
15337        let lost = lost.saturating_add(dropped);
15338        if lost > 0 {
15339            Self::report_parameter_events_lost(lost);
15340        }
15341    }
15342
15343    #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
15344    #[cold]
15345    fn report_parameter_events_lost(lost: u32) {
15346        // Issue 2023 — an event that does not fit is REFUSED whole, never
15347        // truncated into a malformed sample; this line is how anyone hears.
15348        nros_log::log_error!(
15349            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
15350            "{} /parameter_events message(s) were not published: the change log \
15351             (PARAMETER_EVENT_LOG_LEN) filled between two flushes, an event did not fit the \
15352             parameter-service reply buffer (NROS_PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE) and was refused \
15353             rather than truncated, or the publish failed. The parameters themselves changed \
15354             (phase-491 W3, issue 2023).",
15355            lost
15356        );
15357    }
15358
15359    /// phase-491 W2 — a remote `NOT_SET` on `node` deletes the parameter
15360    /// (rclc) instead of being refused (rclcpp). See
15361    /// [`ParameterServer::set_delete_on_not_set`](nros_params::ParameterServer::set_delete_on_not_set).
15362    pub fn delete_parameters_on_not_set_on(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId, on: bool) {
15363        self.ensure_parameter_store();
15364        if let Some(params) = &mut self.params {
15365            params.server.set_delete_on_not_set(node.into(), on);
15366        }

15422    /// Create a typed parameter builder (rclrs-compatible API).
15423    ///
15424    /// Returns a [`ParameterBuilder`] for fluent parameter declaration with
15425    /// `.default()`, `.description()`, `.range()`, and terminal methods
15426    /// `.mandatory()`, `.optional()`, or `.read_only()`.
15427    ///
15428    /// Returns [`NodeError::NotInitialized`] if parameter services have
15429    /// not been registered yet — call [`register_parameter_services`]
15430    /// first.
15431    ///
15432    /// # Example
15433    ///
15434    /// ```ignore
15435    /// let max_speed = executor.parameter::<f64>("max_speed")?
15436    ///     .default(25.0)
15437    ///     .description("Maximum velocity (m/s)")
15438    ///     .read_only()?;
15439    /// ```
15440    ///
15441    /// [`ParameterBuilder`]: nros_params::ParameterBuilder
15442    /// [`register_parameter_services`]: Self::register_parameter_services
15443    pub fn parameter<'a, T: nros_params::ParameterVariant>(
15444        &'a mut self,
15445        name: &'a str,
15446    ) -> Result<nros_params::ParameterBuilder<'a, 's, T>, NodeError> {
15447        self.parameter_on(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY, name)
15448    }
15449
15450    /// [`parameter`](Self::parameter) on a named node.
15451    pub fn parameter_on<'a, T: nros_params::ParameterVariant>(
15452        &'a mut self,
15453        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15454        name: &'a str,
15455    ) -> Result<nros_params::ParameterBuilder<'a, 's, T>, NodeError> {
15456        // Issue 1203 — a reserved name the executor acts on. The builder
15457        // declares through its own borrow of the store, so the seeded
15458        // placeholder has to leave first (or the declaration is refused, the
15459        // way a second `declare_parameter` is), and the next spin reads back
15460        // what was declared.
15461        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
15462        if name == crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM {
15463            self.yield_seeded_use_sim_time(node, name);
15464            if let Some(pending) = self
15465                .params
15466                .as_deref_mut()
15467                .and_then(|p| p.sim_time_via_builder.get_mut(node.index()))
15468            {
15469                *pending = true;
15470            }
15471        }
15472        let server = self
15473            .params
15474            .as_mut()
15475            .map(|p| &mut p.server)
15476            .ok_or(NodeError::NotInitialized)?;
15477        Ok(nros_params::ParameterBuilder::new(
15478            server,
15479            node.into(),
15480            name,
15481        ))
15482    }

15484    // ========================================================================
15485    // phase-417 W4.a — the surface C and C++ forward to
15486    //
15487    // Every one of these is a forwarder onto `nros_params::ParameterServer`,
15488    // the ONE store. They exist on the executor because that is the object the
15489    // FFI holds: a C caller has an `rclc_executor_t*` and an `rcl_node_t*`,
15490    // and a C++ node has its `node_id`. Nothing here keeps state — a wrapper
15491    // that did would be the second store phase-426 removed.
15492    // ========================================================================
15493
15494    /// Attach a description and free-text constraints to a declared parameter
15495    /// on `node` — rclc's `rclc_add_parameter_description`.

15498        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
15499        name: &str,
15500        description: &str,
15501        additional_constraints: &str,
15502    ) -> bool {
15503        match &mut self.params {
15504            Some(params) => params.server.set_parameter_description(
15505                node.into(),
15506                name,
15507                description,
15508                additional_constraints,
15509            ),
15510            None => false,
15511        }
15512    }

15791// ============================================================================
15792// Executor lifecycle — cancel / is_spinning (phase-417 W4.c)
15793// ============================================================================
15794
15795// Issue 1177 -- UN-GATED. This block was `#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]` because
15796// `halt_flag` and `spinning` were `alloc` fields, and neither needed to be: the
15797// allocator is required to SHARE the halt flag (`halt_flag()` hands out a
15798// refcounted handle), never to hold it.
15799//
15800// Gating it meant a no_std executor could not be stopped, and worse, that
15801// `nros-c`'s spin loop -- which calls `cancel`, `is_halted`, `is_spinning`,
15802// `enter_spin_loop` and `exit_spin_loop` with no cfg of its own -- did not
15803// COMPILE for an embedded image. The safety island found that; no
15804// merge-gating lane builds this crate without `alloc`.
15805impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
15806    /// Request the executor to stop spinning — `rclcpp::Executor::cancel`.
15807    ///
15808    /// # ADOPT-BOUNDED (RFC-0089)
15809    ///
15810    /// `cancel` sets a flag the spin loop observes at the NEXT POLL BOUNDARY,
15811    /// so it returns BEFORE spinning has actually stopped;
15812    /// [`is_spinning()`](Self::is_spinning) is the observable that tells you
15813    /// when it has. rclcpp makes the same promise in the same shape, but the
15814    /// boundary here is one `spin_once` timeout wide (a backend's `drive_io`
15815    /// blocks up to the poll interval), so "next boundary" is a duration a
15816    /// caller can measure rather than an implementation detail. The wake flag
15817    /// below shortens it; it does not remove it.
15818    ///
15819    /// Nothing here tears down the session: an executor that has been cancelled
15820    /// is still initialised, still owns its entities, and can be spun again.
15821    /// Teardown is a different verb (`fini` / `shutdown`), and collapsing the
15822    /// two costs a full discovery round on every mode change.
15823    ///
15824    /// Safe to call from another thread or a signal handler.
15825    ///
15826    /// Also raises the Phase 104.C.6 wake flag so a `spin_once` already blocked
15827    /// inside a backend's `drive_io` falls through to the cancel check on its
15828    /// next loop iteration instead of waiting out its full `timeout_ms` first.
15829    pub fn cancel(&self) {
15830        self.halt_flag
15831            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
15832        // The wake flag is the `Arc` half and still needs an allocator. A
15833        // core-only image simply waits out the poll interval, which is the
15834        // bounded behaviour the envelope above already promises.
15835        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
15836        self.wake_flag
15837            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
15838    }
15839
15840    /// Has a [`cancel()`](Self::cancel) been REQUESTED?
15841    ///
15842    /// Not the same question as [`is_spinning()`](Self::is_spinning), and both
15843    /// are kept because both have callers:
15844    ///
15845    /// * `is_halted()` — "someone asked this executor to stop." True the instant
15846    ///   `cancel()` returns, and it stays true until the next spin loop clears
15847    ///   it on entry. This is the flag a hand-rolled `while !exec.is_halted()`
15848    ///   loop polls, which is what a BSP that drives `spin_once` itself writes.
15849    /// * `is_spinning()` — "a spin loop is running right now." Answers the other
15850    ///   half of the envelope: whether the cancel has been ACTED on yet.
15851    ///
15852    /// The two are true together for as long as one poll takes, which is exactly
15853    /// the window the ADOPT-BOUNDED envelope on `cancel()` describes. Neither is
15854    /// derivable from the other: an executor that was never spun is neither
15855    /// halted nor spinning, and one cancelled mid-poll is both.
15856    ///
15857    /// The name is the pre-rename spelling and is deliberately NOT deprecated —
15858    /// `cancel`'s rclcpp pair is a `spinning` observable, not an
15859    /// `is_cancel_requested` one, so there is no ROS 2 name to adopt here and a
15860    /// third spelling would buy nothing.
15861    pub fn is_halted(&self) -> bool {
15862        self.halt_flag.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
15863    }
15864
15865    /// Is a spin loop running on this executor right now?
15866    ///
15867    /// rclcpp spells this `Executor::is_spinning()`. True between the entry and
15868    /// the exit of [`spin`](Self::spin),
15869    /// [`spin_period`](Self::spin_period), the `open_threaded` worker loop, and
15870    /// the C / C++ API loops — every construct that owns its own iteration.
15871    ///
15872    /// A bare `spin_once` does NOT set it: one poll is not a spin, and a caller
15873    /// running its own `while` around `spin_once` is the one who knows it is
15874    /// looping. Such a caller can say so with
15875    /// [`enter_spin_loop`](crate::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi::enter_spin_loop).
15876    ///
15877    /// See [`is_halted()`](Self::is_halted) for why this is a different question
15878    /// from "was cancel requested".
15879    pub fn is_spinning(&self) -> bool {
15880        self.spinning.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
15881    }
15882
15883    /// Declare that the caller is entering a spin loop it drives itself.
15884    ///
15885    /// The seam the C and C++ APIs use so their loops answer
15886    /// [`is_spinning()`](Self::is_spinning) without keeping a flag of their own
15887    /// (RFC-0019: ergonomics may live in the wrapper, state may not). Also
15888    /// CLEARS any pending cancel, matching what `spin` does on entry:
15889    /// a cancel requested before a spin started is not a cancel of THIS spin.
15890    ///
15891    /// Pair it with [`exit_spin_loop`](Self::exit_spin_loop) on EVERY exit path,
15892    /// `break` and early `return` alike — a loop that leaves without it reports
15893    /// `is_spinning() == true` forever. It is a method pair rather than an RAII
15894    /// guard on purpose: a guard would have to borrow the executor for the whole
15895    /// loop, and every caller needs `&mut` inside the body to poll.
15896    ///
15897    /// Takes `&self` (the flags are atomics), so the borrow ends at the call.
15898    pub(crate) fn enter_spin_loop(&self) {
15899        self.halt_flag
15900            .store(false, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
15901        self.spinning
15902            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
15903    }
15904
15905    /// End the scope opened by [`enter_spin_loop`](Self::enter_spin_loop).
15906    ///
15907    /// Idempotent. Leaves the cancel flag alone: "someone asked me to stop" is
15908    /// the caller's answer to keep or clear, and clearing it here would lose the
15909    /// reason the loop exited.
15910    pub(crate) fn exit_spin_loop(&self) {
15911        self.spinning
15912            .store(false, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
15913    }
15914}
15915
15916// ============================================================================
15917// std-gated spin and halt methods
15918// ============================================================================
15919
15920// phase-359 W10 — this impl used to be ONE `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` block.
15921// Only the wall-clock spin loops in it need `std` (`Instant`, `thread::sleep`,
15922// `thread::spawn`); `halt` / `is_halted` / `wake` are plain atomic stores on
15923// flags the struct already owns, and `halt_flag` / `wake_handle` only need
15924// `Arc`. Gating the BLOCK rather than the items made a no_std image unable to
15925// stop its own executor — `ExecutorNodeRuntime::spin` carried a matching `std`
15926// gate for no reason but this one.
15927// phase-359 W10 — `alloc`, not `std`. The wall-clock spin loops were the
15928// reason this block was std-gated: `Instant` for the deadline and
15929// `thread::sleep` for the pacing. Both now go through the platform — the
15930// executor's own `now_us()` and `nros_platform_sleep_us` — so a no_std
15931// image can run the same blocking loops a hosted one does instead of
15932// hand-rolling them in its BSP.
15933#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
15934impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
15935    /// Blocking spin loop with configurable exit conditions — rclrs's
15936    /// `Executor::spin(SpinOptions)`.
15937    ///
15938    /// ADOPT-BOUNDED (RFC-0089). Same name, same argument, same meaning: run
15939    /// until an exit condition in `opts` says stop. Two bounds, both visible in
15940    /// the signature:
15941    ///
15942    /// * **The error channel is one error, not all of them.** rclrs returns
15943    ///   `Vec<RclrsError>` and the caller writes `.first_error()?`; there is no
15944    ///   allocator here, so ours returns `Result<(), NodeError>` carrying the
15945    ///   FIRST failing callback's error and drops the rest (they are still
15946    ///   counted in each pass's [`SpinOnceResult`]). Ported line for line, the
15947    ///   edit is `.first_error()?` -> `?`, which the compiler points at.
15948    /// * **The loop is a poll loop**, so `opts.poll_interval` is the quantum at
15949    ///   which every exit condition is observed — a `cancel()` from another
15950    ///   task, the `timeout` expiring, `max_callbacks` being reached. Requesting
15951    ///   a `timeout` on a build with no clock is an ERROR, not a silent
15952    ///   never-ending loop (issue 0709).
15953    ///
15954    /// phase-427 — this method was `spin_blocking`. `spin` was taken by the
15955    /// `-> !` task body, which is now [`spin_forever`](Self::spin_forever).
15956    ///
15957    /// Runs until one of:
15958    /// - [`cancel()`](Self::cancel) is called (from
15959    ///   another thread or signal handler)
15960    /// - `opts.timeout` expires (if set)
15961    /// - `opts.max_callbacks` is reached (if set)
15962    /// - `opts.only_next` is true (single iteration)
15963    /// - a callback failed and `opts.stop_on_first_error` is set
15964    ///
15965    /// # Example
15966    ///
15967    /// ```ignore
15968    /// // Spin until cancelled
15969    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::default())?;
15970    ///
15971    /// // Spin with 5-second timeout
15972    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::new().timeout(core::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))?;
15973    ///
15974    /// // Single iteration
15975    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::spin_once())?;
15976    /// ```
15977    pub fn spin(&mut self, opts: SpinOptions) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
15978        // phase-427 — was a private `POLL_INTERVAL` const; it is
15979        // `SpinOptions::poll_interval` now, defaulting to the same 10 ms, so
15980        // `spin` and `spin_forever` read one value instead of two literals.
15981        let poll_interval = opts.poll_interval;
15982
15983        // phase-359 W10 — the executor's own clock. `now_us()` reads the
15984        // PLATFORM's monotonic counter, and nothing else: the platform API is
15985        // the clock, so a build with a port has one and a build without has
15986        // none. There is no `std::time::Instant` third answer any more, which
15987        // is what used to make "what time is it" depend on whether some crate
15988        // in the graph happened to name `std`.
15989        //
15990        // `None` means this build has NO clock at all — and issue 0709 is what
15991        // the previous answer here cost. It read: "a timeout cannot be honoured
15992        // then, and pretending otherwise would exit immediately or never; the
15993        // honest reading is no deadline". It then picked NEVER. A caller that
15994        // asked for 50 ms got an infinite loop, silently, in the one API whose
15995        // whole contract is "returns after N ms" — ten hours of a CI lane
15996        // before anyone read it as stuck rather than slow.
15997        //
15998        // Neither of the two silent readings is honest. An unmet precondition
15999        // is an ERROR (repo rule, fail-loud): the caller supplied a time
16000        // quantity this build cannot measure, and only they can decide what to
16001        // do about it. An UNTIMED `spin` still runs until halt, which
16002        // is a promise this build can keep.
16003        let start_us = self.now_us();
16004        if opts.timeout.is_some() && start_us.is_none() {
16005            nros_log::log_error!(
16006                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
16007                "spin: a timeout was requested but this build has no clock \
16008                 — install one with `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` (issue 0709)"
16009            );
16010            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
16011        }
16012        // `as_micros()` rather than a hand-rolled `ms * 1_000`: the multiply
16013        // was unchecked, and the unit conversion is `Duration`'s job.
16014        let timeout_us = opts.timeout.map(|d| d.as_micros() as u64);
16015        let mut total_callbacks = 0usize;
16016
16017        // phase-417 W4.c — clears the cancel flag AND raises `is_spinning`. The
16018        // clear is the pre-existing behaviour (a cancel requested before this
16019        // spin is not a cancel of this spin); the raise is what lets a peer
16020        // thread see that its `cancel()` has not been acted on yet. Every exit
16021        // below is a `break` to the single tail, which is where the scope ends.
16022        self.enter_spin_loop();
16023
16024        loop {
16025            if self.halt_flag.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
16026                break;
16027            }
16028
16029            if let (Some(start), Some(limit)) = (start_us, timeout_us)
16030                && self
16031                    .now_us()
16032                    .is_some_and(|now| now.saturating_sub(start) >= limit)
16033            {
16034                break;
16035            }
16036
16037            let mut callback_error = None;
16038            let result = self.spin_once_capturing(poll_interval, &mut callback_error);
16039            total_callbacks += result.total();
16040
16041            // phase-427 — the first error, and only the first: rclrs's
16042            // `Vec<RclrsError>` needs an allocator we do not have. The scope is
16043            // closed before returning so a caller that reads `is_spinning()`
16044            // after an error sees `false`, exactly as after a clean exit.
16045            if opts.stop_on_first_error
16046                && let Some(e) = callback_error
16047            {
16048                self.exit_spin_loop();
16049                return Err(NodeError::Transport(e));
16050            }
16051
16052            if opts.max_callbacks.is_some_and(|max| total_callbacks >= max) {
16053                break;
16054            }
16055
16056            if opts.only_next {
16057                break;
16058            }
16059        }
16060
16061        self.exit_spin_loop();
16062        Ok(())
16063    }
16064
16065    /// Execute one period with wall-clock overrun detection.
16066    ///
16067    /// Calls [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once), measures wall-clock time, sleeps
16068    /// for the remainder if under budget.
16069    ///
16070    /// # Example
16071    ///
16072    /// ```ignore
16073    /// let period = core::time::Duration::from_millis(10);
16074    /// let result = executor.spin_one_period_timed(period);
16075    /// if result.overrun {
16076    ///     log::warn!("Period overrun: {:?}", result.elapsed);
16077    /// }
16078    /// ```
16079    pub fn spin_one_period_timed(
16080        &mut self,
16081        period: core::time::Duration,
16082    ) -> super::types::SpinPeriodResult {
16083        let start_us = self.now_us();
16084        let result = self.spin_once(period);
16085        // With no clock there is nothing to measure and nothing to sleep off;
16086        // report zero elapsed and no overrun, which is what an unmeasured
16087        // period is.
16088        let elapsed = start_us
16089            .zip(self.now_us())
16090            .map(|(s, e)| core::time::Duration::from_micros(e.saturating_sub(s)))
16091            .unwrap_or_default();
16092        let overrun = elapsed > period;
16093        if !overrun && start_us.is_some() {
16094            platform_sleep(period - elapsed);
16095        }
16096        super::types::SpinPeriodResult {
16097            work: result,
16098            overrun,
16099            elapsed,
16100        }
16101    }
16102
16103    /// Spin at a fixed rate with drift compensation. Blocks until halted.
16104    ///
16105    /// Uses wall-clock time to maintain the target rate. The next invocation
16106    /// time is accumulated (not reset to `now + period`) to prevent cumulative
16107    /// drift.
16108    ///
16109    /// # Example
16110    ///
16111    /// ```ignore
16112    /// // 100Hz control loop — blocks until halt() is called
16113    /// executor.spin_period(core::time::Duration::from_millis(10))?;
16114    /// ```
16115    pub fn spin_period(&mut self, period: core::time::Duration) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
16116        let period_us = period.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
16117        // Absolute next-deadline in the executor's own clock. issue 0709 — the
16118        // sibling of `spin`'s guard above: with no clock there is no
16119        // pacing, and the loop would run as fast as `spin_once` returns while
16120        // the caller believes it is running at `period`. A requested period
16121        // this build cannot honour is a configuration error, not a silent
16122        // busy-loop.
16123        let Some(start_us) = self.now_us() else {
16124            nros_log::log_error!(
16125                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
16126                "spin_period: a period was requested but this build has no clock \
16127                 — install one with `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` (issue 0709)"
16128            );
16129            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
16130        };
16131        // phase-417 W4.c — after the clock guard, not before it: a call that
16132        // returns an error never spun, and must not report that it did. (This
16133        // also moved the cancel-flag clear past the guard, which is the same
16134        // correction.)
16135        self.enter_spin_loop();
16136        let mut next_us = Some(start_us + period_us);
16137
16138        loop {
16139            if self.halt_flag.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
16140                break;
16141            }
16142
16143            self.spin_once(period);
16144
16145            if let Some(next) = next_us {
16146                // Jitter is recorded in `spin_once` above, which this loop
16147                // calls every iteration -- counting it here as well would
16148                // double every wake on this one driver.
16149                if let Some(now) = self.now_us()
16150                    && now < next
16151                {
16152                    platform_sleep(core::time::Duration::from_micros(next - now));
16153                }
16154                // Accumulate to prevent drift (not = now + period)
16155                next_us = Some(next + period_us);
16156            }
16157        }
16158        self.exit_spin_loop();
16159        Ok(())
16160    }
16161}

16163#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16164impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
16165    /// Phase 110.D.b — move this Executor onto a fresh OS thread,
16166    /// apply a per-thread scheduling policy via the caller-supplied
16167    /// `apply_policy` function, and run the spin loop until
16168    /// `ThreadHandle::halt` fires.
16169    ///
16170    /// The function-pointer indirection on `apply_policy` lets the
16171    /// caller pass any platform's `PlatformScheduler::set_current_thread_policy`
16172    /// without forcing `Executor` to be generic over the platform —
16173    /// keeps the existing `Executor` type stable.
16174    ///
16175    /// Multi-executor preemption (the actual hard-RT win) comes from
16176    /// the OS scheduler — call `open_threaded` once per criticality
16177    /// tier, each with its own policy / priority. The kernel handles
16178    /// preemption across executors; within a single executor,
16179    /// dispatch remains non-preemptive (110.A–C bucketed sets).
16180    ///
16181    /// # Safety
16182    ///
16183    /// Moves `self` across thread boundaries. `Executor` contains a
16184    /// raw `*mut session::ConcreteSession` when constructed via
16185    /// `from_session_ptr`; the caller must ensure that pointer's
16186    /// referent stays valid across the lifetime of the spawned thread
16187    /// and that no other thread mutates the session concurrently.
16188    /// `from_session` (Owned) is safer — `ConcreteSession` ownership
16189    /// transfers cleanly into the thread.
16190    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16191    pub unsafe fn open_threaded(
16192        self,
16193        policy: nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
16194        apply_policy: fn(
16195            nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
16196        ) -> Result<(), nros_platform_api::SchedError>,
16197        spin_period: core::time::Duration,
16198    ) -> ThreadHandle
16199    where
16200        // phase-271 — the spawned thread owns `self` for an unbounded lifetime,
16201        // so its borrowed storage must be `'static` (a leaked/`static` backing —
16202        // the `alloc` convenience constructors or a program-lifetime region).
16203        's: 'static,
16204    {
16205        let halt = self.halt_flag.clone();
16206        // phase-359 W10 — a platform task, not `std::thread`. The two other
16207        // executor-owned workers moved earlier; this is the third and last, and
16208        // it is the one the ABI fits best: `open_threaded` exists to give a
16209        // spin loop an OS SCHEDULING POLICY, which is not something a build
16210        // without an OS was ever going to get from `std`.
16211        //
16212        // The closure becomes a heap context because the entry point crosses C
16213        // as `*mut c_void`. It is reclaimed by the trampoline on exit rather
16214        // than leaked: unlike a tier task, this loop RETURNS — that is what
16215        // `halt` is for.
16216        let ctx = alloc::boxed::Box::into_raw(alloc::boxed::Box::new(ThreadedCtx {
16217            executor: self,
16218            policy,
16219            apply_policy,
16220            spin_period,
16221        }));
16222        // SAFETY: `ctx` stays live until the trampoline reclaims it, which
16223        // happens on the spawned task and only after the loop exits.
16224        let task = unsafe {
16225            nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask::spawn(
16226                threaded_spin_trampoline,
16227                ctx as *mut core::ffi::c_void,
16228                OPEN_THREADED_STACK_BYTES,
16229                c"nros-exec".as_ptr(),
16230            )
16231        };
16232        let Some(task) = task else {
16233            // The platform refused (or cannot size) a task. Reclaim the
16234            // context and hand back a handle that owns nothing — `halt` and
16235            // `join` stay callable, which keeps the caller's shape identical to
16236            // the success path.
16237            //
16238            // SAFETY: nothing was spawned, so this pointer has no other owner.
16239            drop(unsafe { alloc::boxed::Box::from_raw(ctx) });
16240            return ThreadHandle { task: None, halt };
16241        };
16242        ThreadHandle {
16243            task: Some(task),
16244            halt,
16245        }
16246    }
16247
16248    /// Phase 104.C.6 — wake the executor from another thread / ISR /
16249    /// signal handler.
16250    ///
16251    /// Sets the shared `wake_flag`. The next `spin_once` swap-clears the
16252    /// flag, skips the blocking wait on the primary session, and polls
16253    /// every session non-blockingly so whatever queued the wake is
16254    /// observed in a single iteration. Idempotent — multiple `wake()`
16255    /// calls collapse into one observed wake per `spin_once`.
16256    pub fn wake(&self) {
16257        self.wake_flag
16258            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
16259    }
16260}
16261
16262#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16263impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
16264    /// Get a clone of the halt flag for use in signal handlers or other threads.
16265    ///
16266    /// # Example
16267    ///
16268    /// ```ignore
16269    /// let halt = executor.halt_flag();
16270    /// std::thread::spawn(move || {
16271    ///     std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(5));
16272    ///     halt.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
16273    /// });
16274    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::default())?;
16275    /// ```
16276    pub fn halt_flag(&self) -> portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool> {
16277        self.halt_flag.clone()
16278    }
16279
16280    /// Phase 104.C.6 — clone of the shared wake flag for cross-thread
16281    /// use (signal handlers, foreign threads, future per-backend vtable
16282    /// wake hooks).
16283    ///
16284    /// # Example
16285    ///
16286    /// ```ignore
16287    /// let wake = executor.wake_handle();
16288    /// std::thread::spawn(move || {
16289    ///     // ... compute something ...
16290    ///     // hand off to executor by setting the flag.
16291    ///     wake.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
16292    /// });
16293    /// loop { executor.spin_once(Duration::from_millis(100)); }
16294    /// ```
16295    pub fn wake_handle(&self) -> portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool> {
16296        self.wake_flag.clone()
16297    }
16298}
