16300/// Phase 110.E.b — opaque per-platform timer handle. Stores the
16301/// raw platform handle (POSIX `timer_t` boxed via `PosixTimerHandle`,
16302/// FreeRTOS `TimerHandle_t`, etc.) plus a destroy thunk so the
16303/// Executor can clean up without being generic over the platform.
16304///
16305/// Caller of `register_sporadic_timer` builds this via
16306/// `OpaqueTimerHandle::new(handle, destroy_fn)` after their
16307/// `PlatformTimer::create_periodic` call returns.
16308#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16309pub struct OpaqueTimerHandle {
16310    handle: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
16311    destroy_fn: extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
16312}
16313
16314#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16315unsafe impl Send for OpaqueTimerHandle {}
16316#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16317unsafe impl Sync for OpaqueTimerHandle {}
16318
16319#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16320impl OpaqueTimerHandle {
16321    /// # Safety
16322    /// `handle` must be a live platform-specific timer handle that
16323    /// `destroy_fn` knows how to drop. Caller surrenders ownership
16324    /// of the underlying handle to the Executor.
16325    pub unsafe fn new(
16326        handle: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
16327        destroy_fn: extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
16328    ) -> Self {
16329        Self { handle, destroy_fn }
16330    }
16331}
16332
16333#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16334impl Drop for OpaqueTimerHandle {
16335    fn drop(&mut self) {
16336        if !self.handle.is_null() {
16337            (self.destroy_fn)(self.handle);
16338            self.handle = core::ptr::null_mut();
16339        }
16340    }
16341}
16342
16343/// Handle returned from [`Executor::open_threaded`]. Holds the
16344/// spawned thread's join handle and a clone of the executor's halt
16345/// flag. Drop runs `halt() + join()` so the thread can't outlive the
16346/// handle.
16347#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16348pub struct ThreadHandle {
16349    task: Option<nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask>,
16350    halt: portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>,
16351}
16352
16353/// Default stack for an `open_threaded` spin loop. `std::thread`'s default was
16354/// 2 MiB; the executor's own storage is caller-carved and lives elsewhere, so
16355/// this carries call frames only — the same reasoning (and size) as the NuttX
16356/// tier spawn, which measured this against a real RTOS default.
16357#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16358const OPEN_THREADED_STACK_BYTES: usize = 65536;
16359
16360/// What [`Executor::open_threaded`] hands its task, in place of a closure's
16361/// captures. Owned by the trampoline, which reclaims it when the loop exits.
16362#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16363struct ThreadedCtx {
16364    executor: Executor<'static>,
16365    policy: nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
16366    apply_policy: fn(nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy) -> Result<(), nros_platform_api::SchedError>,
16367    spin_period: core::time::Duration,
16368}
16369
16370/// The spawned spin loop.
16371///
16372/// # Safety
16373/// `arg` must be the `Box<ThreadedCtx>` raw pointer `open_threaded` created,
16374/// passed exactly once.
16375#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16376unsafe extern "C" fn threaded_spin_trampoline(
16377    arg: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
16378) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
16379    // SAFETY: the caller's contract — this is the pointer `open_threaded`
16380    // leaked, and the task is the only consumer of it.
16381    let mut ctx = unsafe { alloc::boxed::Box::from_raw(arg as *mut ThreadedCtx) };
16382    // Apply the requested OS scheduling policy to this fresh task. Failure is
16383    // reported but not propagated — a runtime that fails to lift to SCHED_FIFO
16384    // still spins correctly at SCHED_OTHER (just without RT guarantees).
16385    let _ = (ctx.apply_policy)(ctx.policy);
16386    // phase-417 W4.c — this loop owns its own iteration, so it is a spin and
16387    // must say so. NOT `enter_spin_loop()`: that clears the cancel flag, and
16388    // `open_threaded` hands the caller a `ThreadHandle` whose `halt()` may
16389    // already have fired before this task was scheduled. Raising `is_spinning`
16390    // without touching the cancel bit is the honest report here.
16391    ctx.executor
16392        .spinning
16393        .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
16394    while !ctx.executor.is_halted() {
16395        ctx.executor.spin_once(ctx.spin_period);
16396    }
16397    ctx.executor.exit_spin_loop();
16398    core::ptr::null_mut()
16399}
16400
16401#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16402impl ThreadHandle {
16403    /// Signal the spawned executor thread to stop. The thread exits
16404    /// on its next `spin_once` iteration.
16405    pub fn halt(&self) {
16406        self.halt.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
16407    }
16408
16409    /// Wait for the spawned task to exit. After `join`, calling it again is a
16410    /// no-op.
16411    ///
16412    /// phase-359 W10 — was `std::thread::Result<()>`, which carried a panic
16413    /// payload this can no longer produce: a platform task has no unwinding
16414    /// join. Same two outcomes, an error type that does not require `std` —
16415    /// the trade `signal_fd` already made in this campaign. `NotInitialized`
16416    /// means the platform refused to host the task at spawn time — nothing was
16417    /// started, so there is nothing to wait for. (An existing variant rather
16418    /// than a new one: `NodeError` is mapped across the C and C++ FFI, so a new
16419    /// variant is a gate-checked ABI change and this needs no new meaning.)
16420    pub fn join(mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
16421        self.halt();
16422        match self.task.take() {
16423            Some(t) => {
16424                t.join();
16425                Ok(())
16426            }
16427            None => Err(NodeError::NotInitialized),
16428        }
16429    }
16430}
16431
16432#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16433impl Drop for ThreadHandle {
16434    fn drop(&mut self) {
16435        self.halt.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
16436        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
16437            t.join();
16438        }
16439    }
16440}

16442// SAFETY: Phase 110.D.b — `Executor` contains a raw `*mut
16443// session::ConcreteSession` only on the `from_session_ptr` (Borrowed)
16444// path; the `from_session` (Owned) path is plain Send-able. The
16445// `unsafe fn open_threaded` entry point documents the safety
16446// contract for Borrowed sessions; for Owned sessions the Send claim
16447// is unconditional.
16448// phase-359 W10 — `alloc`, not `std`: this assertion exists for
16449// `open_threaded`, which now hands the executor to a PLATFORM task. The
16450// crossing is the same one; only the thing doing the crossing changed.
16451#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
16452unsafe impl<'s> Send for Executor<'s> {}
16453
16454/// phase-509 P9b item 2 -- take the bits of `mask` out of a ready word and
16455/// leave the rest for the workers of the other bands. One swap for the
16456/// one-level worker's every-slot mask, as before.
16457#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
16458#[allow(dead_code)] // no ready word without `alloc` + `rmw-cffi`
16459#[inline]
16460fn take_band_bits(word: &portable_atomic::AtomicUsize, mask: u64) -> u64 {
16461    if mask == u64::MAX {
16462        word.swap(0, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) as u64
16463    } else {
16464        (word.fetch_and(!(mask as usize), portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) as u64) & mask
16465    }
16466}
16467
16468/// phase-509 P9b item 2 (RFC-0108 "As built in P9b") -- how a pass runs.
16469#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
16470pub(crate) enum PassMode<'w> {
16471    /// `spin_once(&mut self)`: the executor's own worker; the lock, if one
16472    /// is installed, is held for the whole pass.
16473    Owned,
16474    /// The executor's own worker through a raw pointer
16475    /// ([`Executor::spin_once_shared`]): the lock is released around each
16476    /// user callback when it carries a thread identity.
16477    Shared,
16478    /// A band worker's pass ([`Executor::spin_band_once`]).
16479    Band(&'w mut super::scheduler::BandWorker),
16480}
16481
16482impl<'s> Drop for Executor<'s> {
16483    fn drop(&mut self) {
16484        // Issue 0790 — a teardown that never went through `close()` still gets
16485        // its ordered shutdown hooks, and gets them in the SAME order. The C
16486        // API's `nros_executor_fini` is exactly that path: it drops the
16487        // executor in place and leaves the session to `nros_support_fini`, so
16488        // without this the whole facility would be silently inert for every C
16489        // entry. Entities are still live at the top of `drop` — the component
16490        // cells and the arena entries below are what tears them down — so this
16491        // is the last moment a pre-shutdown hook can do what it exists to do.
16492        //
16493        // After a normal `close()` both tables are already empty and these two
16494        // calls are a pair of `None` scans.
16495        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre);
16496        // Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — release executor-owned component cells
16497        // first (before the arena entries), so a component's `drop`
16498        // trampoline can still touch its own (cell-owned) state. Each slot
16499        // owns a leaked `Arc<ComponentCell>`; its `drop` reconstitutes +
16500        // drops that Arc exactly once.
16501        for slot in self.component_slots.iter() {
16502            // SAFETY: `slot.state` is the leaked cell enrolled via
16503            // `enroll_component`; `slot.drop` is its matching trampoline, run
16504            // exactly once here (slots are not removed before Drop).
16505            unsafe {
16506                (slot.drop)(slot.state);
16507            }
16508        }
16509        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
16510        for meta in self.entries.iter().flatten() {
16511            // SAFETY: each entry was written by `ptr::write` in `add_*` and
16512            // has not been dropped yet. `drop_fn` matches the concrete type.
16513            unsafe {
16514                let data_ptr = arena_ptr.add(meta.offset);
16515                (meta.drop_fn)(data_ptr);
16516            }
16517        }
16518        // Issue 0790 — the post-teardown half, after the entities are gone.
16519        // Same "already empty after `close()`" note as the pre pass above.
16520        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post);
16521        // Issue 1385 — LAST in the body, and that is the whole point: the
16522        // context the backend holds is `wake_ctx`, a field, so it is still
16523        // alive for every line above and is freed only after `drop` returns.
16524        // Clearing here is therefore the SHORTEST window in which a callback
16525        // can fire into live state, not the longest — entity teardown above
16526        // may still be talking to the backend.
16527        //
16528        // A no-op after `close()` (the latch), and a no-op for an executor
16529        // that never installed. For the C path this is the only clear there
16530        // is: `rclc_executor_fini` runs this `drop_in_place` and THEN
16531        // zero-fills the storage the callback pointed into.
16532        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
16533        self.clear_wake_signal();
16534        // phase-467 Row 8 — and the graph-change target, before the box it
16535        // names is freed with this executor.
16536        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
16537        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
16538    }
16539}

16541#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
16542mod dispatch_registry_tests {
16543    //! Phase 216 follow-up — `Executor::register_dispatch_slot` +
16544    //! `Executor::dispatch_callback` round-trip.
16545    //!
16546    //! Uses `MockSession` (same pattern as
16547    //! `lifecycle_services::tests::mock_integration`) so the test
16548    //! doesn't need a live RMW backend. Gated `not(feature =
16549    //! "rmw-cffi")` because under `rmw-cffi` the `ConcreteSession`
16550    //! type alias resolves to the cffi session, which `MockSession`
16551    //! can't impersonate.
16552
16553    extern crate alloc;
16554
16555    use super::Executor;
16556    use crate::mock::MockSession;
16557    use std::sync::Mutex;
16558
16559    static CAPTURED: Mutex<alloc::vec::Vec<(usize, alloc::vec::Vec<u8>, usize)>> =
16560        Mutex::new(alloc::vec::Vec::new());
16561
16562    /// Test trampoline matching the per-Node
16563    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` ABI shape (Phase 216.A.5).
16564    unsafe extern "C" fn recording_on_callback(
16565        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
16566        cb_id_ptr: *const u8,
16567        cb_id_len: usize,
16568        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
16569    ) {
16570        // SAFETY: caller (test body below) holds storage live;
16571        // `cb_id_ptr..len` points into a `&str` literal.
16572        let cb_id_bytes = unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len).to_vec() };
16573        let mut guard = CAPTURED.lock().expect("CAPTURED poisoned");
16574        guard.push((state as usize, cb_id_bytes, ctx as usize));
16575    }
16576
16577    #[test]
16578    fn register_dispatch_slot_round_trip() {
16579        let session = MockSession::new();
16580        let mut executor: Executor = Executor::from_session(session);
16581
16582        // Pre-condition: empty registry.
16583        assert_eq!(executor.dispatch_slot_count(), 0);
16584
16585        // Two distinct "states" so we prove every slot gets called
16586        // with its OWN state.
16587        let mut state_blob_a: u32 = 0xABCD_0001;
16588        let mut state_blob_b: u32 = 0xABCD_0002;
16589        let state_a_ptr = &mut state_blob_a as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
16590        let state_b_ptr = &mut state_blob_b as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
16591
16592        executor
16593            .register_dispatch_slot(state_a_ptr, recording_on_callback)
16594            .expect("register slot A");
16595        executor
16596            .register_dispatch_slot(state_b_ptr, recording_on_callback)
16597            .expect("register slot B");
16598        assert_eq!(executor.dispatch_slot_count(), 2);
16599
16600        let mut ctx_blob: u32 = 0xFEED_BEEF;
16601        let ctx_ptr = &mut ctx_blob as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
16602        let cb_id = "/talker/timer/publish";
16603
16604        CAPTURED.lock().expect("CAPTURED poisoned").clear();
16605        executor.dispatch_callback(cb_id, ctx_ptr);
16606
16607        let captured = CAPTURED.lock().expect("CAPTURED poisoned").clone();
16608        assert_eq!(
16609            captured.len(),
16610            2,
16611            "every registered slot must be invoked — linear scan, \
16612             no self-filter at the registry layer"
16613        );
16614        // The carved dispatch table iterates in insertion order.
16615        assert_eq!(captured[0].0, state_a_ptr as usize, "slot A's state");
16616        assert_eq!(captured[1].0, state_b_ptr as usize, "slot B's state");
16617        for (idx, capture) in captured.iter().enumerate() {
16618            assert_eq!(
16619                capture.1.as_slice(),
16620                cb_id.as_bytes(),
16621                "slot {idx} cb_id bytes round-trip"
16622            );
16623            assert_eq!(
16624                capture.2, ctx_ptr as usize,
16625                "slot {idx} ctx pointer round-trip"
16626            );
16627        }
16628    }
16629
16630    #[test]
16631    fn register_dispatch_slot_capacity_full() {
16632        let session = MockSession::new();
16633        let mut executor: Executor = Executor::from_session(session);
16634
16635        let mut state_blob: u32 = 0;
16636        let state_ptr = &mut state_blob as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
16637
16638        // `MAX_NODES` slots fit; the next one must error.
16639        for _ in 0..crate::config::MAX_NODES {
16640            executor
16641                .register_dispatch_slot(state_ptr, recording_on_callback)
16642                .expect("under-capacity push must succeed");
16643        }
16644        assert_eq!(executor.dispatch_slot_count(), crate::config::MAX_NODES);
16645        let overflow = executor.register_dispatch_slot(state_ptr, recording_on_callback);
16646        assert!(
16647            overflow.is_err(),
16648            "over-capacity push must return Err(()) — raise \
16649             NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES at build time to grow the registry"
16650        );
16651    }
16652}

16654/// Phase 274.W1 — borrowed-executor session sharing + active-groups gating.
16655///
16656/// Validates three primitives introduced for RFC-0015 Model 1:
16657/// - `session_handle` / `open_with_session_handle` (Borrowed session store —
16658///   the borrowed executor does not own or close the session on drop).
16659/// - `set_active_groups` + `group_active` (callback-group filter gating).
16660///
16661/// Uses `MockSession` (same pattern as `dispatch_registry_tests`); gated
16662/// `not(feature = "rmw-cffi")` for the same reason.
16663#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
16664mod p274_w1_tier_executor_tests {
16665    use super::Executor;
16666    use crate::mock::MockSession;
16667
16668    #[test]
16669    fn session_handle_borrowed_executor_shares_session_ptr() {
16670        // Open the primary executor (session owner).
16671        let session = MockSession::new();
16672        let mut primary = Executor::from_session(session);
16673
16674        // Record the primary's session pointer for later comparison.
16675        let primary_session_ptr = primary.session_ptr();
16676
16677        // Get the opaque session handle (into_raw for C FFI; here we keep it raw).
16678        let handle = primary.session_handle();
16679
16680        // Open a second executor over the SAME session (Borrowed — does not own it).
16681        // SAFETY: `primary` (the session owner) outlives `borrowed` in this scope.
16682        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle) };
16683
16684        // Both executors must expose the same session pointer.
16685        assert_eq!(
16686            primary.session_ptr(),
16687            borrowed.session_ptr(),
16688            "borrowed executor must share the primary's session pointer"
16689        );
16690        assert_eq!(
16691            borrowed.session_ptr(),
16692            primary_session_ptr,
16693            "session pointer must be stable across session_handle / open_with_session_handle"
16694        );
16695
16696        // Drop the borrowed executor — the primary's session must remain valid.
16697        drop(borrowed);
16698
16699        // Primary still exposes the same session pointer (session was NOT closed by drop).
16700        assert_eq!(
16701            primary.session_ptr(),
16702            primary_session_ptr,
16703            "primary session pointer must be unchanged after dropping the borrowed executor"
16704        );
16705    }
16706
16707    /// An oversized group name is REFUSED and fails CLOSED.
16708    ///
16709    /// issue 1172 — this used to be `if s.push_str(g).is_ok()`, which dropped
16710    /// the name and left the tier filtering on a set that silently lacked it.
16711    /// Two things are asserted because either alone would let the bug back:
16712    /// the call must REPORT the failure, and the resulting filter must accept
16713    /// NOTHING rather than fall back to the wildcard, which would be
16714    /// fail-open.
16715    #[test]
16716    fn an_oversized_group_name_is_refused_and_fails_closed() {
16717        let session = MockSession::new();
16718        let mut primary = Executor::from_session(session);
16719        let handle = primary.session_handle();
16720        // SAFETY: primary outlives borrowed.
16721        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle) };
16722
16723        // `GroupName` is `heapless::String<32>`.
16724        let too_long = "g".repeat(33);
16725        assert!(
16726            borrowed
16727                .set_active_groups(&[("n", "/", too_long.as_str())])
16728                .is_err(),
16729            "an oversized group name must be reported, not dropped"
16730        );
16731        assert!(
16732            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", &too_long),
16733            "the name that did not fit must not be active"
16734        );
16735        assert!(
16736            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "anything-else"),
16737            "a refused filter must accept NOTHING — falling back to the \
16738             wildcard would run every callback on this tier"
16739        );
16740    }
16741
16742    #[test]
16743    fn set_active_groups_gates_group_active() {
16744        let session = MockSession::new();
16745        let mut primary = Executor::from_session(session);
16746        let handle = primary.session_handle();
16747
16748        // SAFETY: primary outlives borrowed.
16749        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle) };
16750
16751        // Before gating: wildcard — every group is accepted.
16752        assert!(
16753            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "ctrl"),
16754            "default (wildcard) must accept every group"
16755        );
16756        assert!(
16757            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
16758            "default (wildcard) must accept every group"
16759        );
16760
16761        // Gate borrowed to only the "ctrl" group (one-tier filter).
16762        borrowed
16763            .set_active_groups(&[("n", "/", "ctrl")])
16764            .expect("fits");
16765
16766        assert!(
16767            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "ctrl"),
16768            "\"ctrl\" must be active after set_active_groups([\"ctrl\"])"
16769        );
16770        assert!(
16771            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
16772            "\"telem\" must NOT be active when only \"ctrl\" is gated"
16773        );
16774        assert!(
16775            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "planning"),
16776            "\"planning\" must NOT be active when only \"ctrl\" is gated"
16777        );
16778
16779        // Primary is unaffected (it still uses the wildcard).
16780        assert!(
16781            primary.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
16782            "primary executor must remain unaffected (still wildcard)"
16783        );
16784
16785        // Clear the filter on borrowed — back to wildcard.
16786        borrowed
16787            .set_active_groups(&[])
16788            .expect("the wildcard always fits");
16789        assert!(
16790            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
16791            "after clearing, borrowed must accept all groups again"
16792        );
16793    }
16794
16795    #[test]
16796    fn session_handle_into_raw_from_raw_round_trip() {
16797        let session = MockSession::new();
16798        let mut primary = Executor::from_session(session);
16799        let session_ptr = primary.session_ptr();
16800
16801        let handle = primary.session_handle();
16802        let raw = handle.into_raw();
16803
16804        // into_raw must return a non-null pointer matching the session address.
16805        assert!(!raw.is_null());
16806        assert_eq!(raw as *mut _, session_ptr);
16807
16808        // from_raw must reconstruct a handle that opens the same borrowed executor.
16809        // SAFETY: primary still owns the session, raw is its address.
16810        let handle2 = unsafe { crate::executor::SessionHandle::from_raw(raw) };
16811        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle2) };
16812        assert_eq!(
16813            borrowed.session_ptr(),
16814            session_ptr,
16815            "from_raw reconstructed handle must open executor on the same session"
16816        );
16817    }

16820/// W3b.5 — snapshot the monitored publishers' counters before a dispatch
16821/// (only when a latency contract exists; otherwise a zeroed array that
16822/// `attribute_latency` never reads).
16823fn snapshot_pub_counts(
16824    table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
16825    active: bool,
16826) -> [u32; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS] {
16827    let mut counts = [0u32; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS];
16828    if active {
16829        for (k, spec) in table.iter().take(super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS).enumerate() {
16830            counts[k] = spec.cell.count.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16831        }
16832    }
16833    counts
16834}
16835
16836/// W3b.5 — attribute one dispatch's elapsed time to every monitored
16837/// publisher whose counter advanced during it (an upper bound on the
16838/// node-path take → publish latency: the callback deserialized, ran, and
16839/// published within `elapsed_us`).
16840fn attribute_latency(
16841    table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
16842    active: bool,
16843    counts_before: &[u32; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS],
16844    elapsed_us: u32,
16845) {
16846    if !active {
16847        return;
16848    }
16849    for (k, spec) in table.iter().take(super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS).enumerate() {
16850        if spec.max_latency_ms == 0 {
16851            continue;
16852        }
16853        let now = spec.cell.count.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16854        if now != counts_before[k] {
16855            spec.cell
16856                .max_latency_us
16857                .fetch_max(elapsed_us, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16858        }
16859    }
16860}

16862/// W3b.5 — enforce the bound SC's deadline after a dispatch. A miss maps
16863/// through [`DeadlineAction`](super::sched_context::DeadlineAction):
16864/// `Warn`/`Skip`/`Fault` all report; `Skip` additionally masks the SC's
16865/// remaining callbacks for this cycle; `Fault` invokes the fault hook
16866/// (panic when none is registered).
16867/// phase-503 -- hand a route deadline verdict of `table[row]` to the reaction
16868/// hook, if one is installed (and the monitors are armed: the caller passes
16869/// `None` otherwise). Shared by the overdue check after the park and the
16870/// completion verdict of a late supervised route (`route_judge`).
16871fn call_route_reaction(
16872    hook: Option<(super::monitor::ReactionHookFn, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
16873    table: &[super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
16874    row: usize,
16875    v: &super::monitor::Violation,
16876) {
16877    let Some((f, ctx)) = hook else { return };
16878    let spec = &table[row];
16879    let ev = super::monitor::ReactionEvent {
16880        reaction_id: spec.reaction_id as u32,
16881        row: row as u32,
16882        rule_code: super::monitor::rule_code(v.rule),
16883        measured_ms: v.measured,
16884        declared_ms: v.declared,
16885        mechanism: spec.mechanism,
16886    };
16887    // SAFETY: `f` and `ctx` were registered together through
16888    // `set_reaction_hook`, whose caller keeps `ctx` valid for the executor's
16889    // life; the event lives across the call.
16890    unsafe { f(&ev, ctx) };
16891}
16892
16893/// phase-462 W3c -- [`call_route_reaction`] for a detected hazard: the event
16894/// names the hazard's reaction id and its index in the hazard table.
16895fn call_hazard_reaction(
16896    hook: Option<(super::monitor::ReactionHookFn, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
16897    spec: &super::monitor::HazardSpec,
16898    row: usize,
16899    v: &super::monitor::Violation,
16900) {
16901    let Some((f, ctx)) = hook else { return };
16902    let ev = super::monitor::ReactionEvent {
16903        reaction_id: spec.reaction_id as u32,
16904        row: row as u32,
16905        rule_code: super::monitor::rule_code(v.rule),
16906        measured_ms: v.measured,
16907        declared_ms: v.declared,
16908        mechanism: super::monitor::MECHANISM_EXECUTOR,
16909    };
16910    // SAFETY: as `call_route_reaction` -- `f` and `ctx` were registered
16911    // together through `set_reaction_hook`.
16912    unsafe { f(&ev, ctx) };
16913}
16914
16915fn check_deadline_miss(
16916    sc: Option<&super::sched_context::SchedContext>,
16917    sc_idx: usize,
16918    elapsed_us: u32,
16919    misses: &mut heapless::Vec<super::monitor::Violation, { super::monitor::MAX_VIOLATIONS }>,
16920    skipped_scs: &mut u64,
16921    fault_fn: Option<fn(&super::monitor::Violation)>,
16922    reaction_hook: Option<(super::monitor::ReactionHookFn, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
16923) {
16924    use super::sched_context::DeadlineAction;
16925    let Some(sc) = sc else { return };
16926    let Some(deadline_us) = sc.deadline_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()) else {
16927        return;
16928    };
16929    if matches!(sc.deadline_action, DeadlineAction::Ignore) || elapsed_us <= deadline_us {
16930        return;
16931    }
16932    let v = super::monitor::Violation {
16933        rule: "deadline-miss-runtime",
16934        // Entries carry no name at this altitude; the SC slot stands in.
16935        fqn: "sched-context",
16936        measured: elapsed_us,
16937        declared: deadline_us,
16938    };
16939    match sc.deadline_action {
16940        DeadlineAction::Ignore => {}
16941        DeadlineAction::Warn => {
16942            let _ = misses.push(v);
16943        }
16944        DeadlineAction::Skip => {
16945            if sc_idx < 64 {
16946                *skipped_scs |= 1u64 << sc_idx;
16947            }
16948            let _ = misses.push(v);
16949        }
16950        DeadlineAction::Fault => {
16951            if let Some(f) = fault_fn {
16952                f(&v);
16953                let _ = misses.push(v);
16954            } else if let Some((f, ctx)) = reaction_hook {
16955                // phase-503 — the reaction hook is the fault path a C or C++
16956                // image can install; reaction id 0, the SC slot as the row.
16957                let ev = super::monitor::ReactionEvent {
16958                    reaction_id: super::monitor::REACTION_NONE as u32,
16959                    row: sc_idx as u32,
16960                    rule_code: super::monitor::rule_code(v.rule),
16961                    measured_ms: elapsed_us / 1_000,
16962                    declared_ms: deadline_us / 1_000,
16963                    mechanism: super::monitor::MECHANISM_EXECUTOR,
16964                };
16965                // SAFETY: as in `check_route_deadlines`.
16966                unsafe { f(&ev, ctx) };
16967                let _ = misses.push(v);
16968            } else {
16969                panic!(
16970                    "nros: deadline fault — dispatch ran {elapsed_us} us past a {deadline_us} us deadline"
16971                );
16972            }
16973        }
16974    }
16975}
16976
16977// Timer-accounting clock default (issue: no_std tiers with no `clock_us`
16978// credited each spin the REQUESTED timeout — spin.rs `delta_us` fallback —
16979// so shared-session wakes made low-rate timers fire early (a 100 ms timer
16980// at ~67 ms on Zephyr native_sim) and tick rounding made fast tiers fire
16981// late. Measured on that native_sim image; mechanism documented at the
16982// fallback site.)
16983//
16984// Every platform port exports `nros_platform_clock_ns` through the same
16985// linkage contract the wake primitives rely on (`nros_platform_export_clock!`
16986// in nros-platform-cffi), so an rmw-cffi no_std build can safely default the
16987// executor clock to it; `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` stays as an override.
16988#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
16989unsafe extern "C" {
16990    fn nros_platform_clock_ns() -> u64;
16991}
16992
16993#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
16994fn default_platform_clock_us() -> u64 {
16995    // SAFETY: bare query of the platform's monotonic ns counter; the symbol
16996    // is guaranteed by whichever platform port linked the binary (the same
16997    // contract `nros_platform_wake_*` already depends on).
16998    //
16999    // RFC-0073 made the ABI nanoseconds; the executor's own accounting is
17000    // still microseconds (`clock_us_fn`, `delta_us`), so the division lives
17001    // here rather than being pushed into every port.
17002    unsafe { nros_platform_clock_ns() / 1_000 }
17003}
17004
17005/// Sleep, through the platform ABI.
17006///
17007/// phase-359 W10 — the spin loops used `std::thread::sleep`. Every port already
17008/// exports `nros_platform_sleep_us` (the ABI's own pacing primitive, the one an
17009/// RTOS build has always used), so a hosted loop and an embedded one now pace
17010/// the same way. The µs entry point is used rather than `_ms` because
17011/// `spin_one_period_timed` sleeps off a remainder, which rounds badly at
17012/// millisecond granularity on short periods.
17013#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
17014pub(crate) fn platform_sleep(d: core::time::Duration) {
17015    unsafe extern "C" {
17016        fn nros_platform_sleep_us(us: usize);
17017    }
17018    let us = d.as_micros().min(usize::MAX as u128) as usize;
17019    if us == 0 {
17020        return;
17021    }
17022    // SAFETY: a bare pacing call with no pointer arguments, guaranteed by
17023    // whichever port linked the binary — the same contract the clock and wake
17024    // symbols in this file already rely on.
17025    unsafe { nros_platform_sleep_us(us) }
17026}
17027
17028/// A monotonic µs reader, or `None` when this build has no clock at all.
17029///
17030/// phase-359 W10 — one provider, chosen by what is LINKED rather than by which
17031/// flavour the crate was built in. W4 unified the executor's clock ACCESSOR and
17032/// said the provider was the last piece; this is it.
17033///
17034/// `rmw-cffi` means a platform port is linked, and every port exports
17035/// `nros_platform_clock_ns` under the same contract the wake primitives use —
17036/// so a hosted build reads the same counter an embedded one does, instead of
17037/// `Instant` on one and the platform on the other. `Instant` survives only
17038/// where there is no port to ask: `std` without `rmw-cffi`.
17039///
17040/// phase-359 W10 follow-up — this comment claimed the metadata PROBE was that
17041/// configuration, and **it is not**. The probe's generated manifest deps
17042/// `nros-platform-cffi` with `posix-c-port` (issue 0288 layer 5, so it links),
17043/// and its `nros` resolves with `rmw-cffi` ON — feature-unified from the
17044/// component's board crate. Measured on a real probe tree: `alloc default
17045/// macros rmw-cffi ros-humble std`. It takes the PORT arm.
17046///
17047/// What is real: `nros-rmw-metadata` and `nros-tests` do resolve `nros` with
17048/// `std` and no `rmw-cffi`, and have no port crate in their graphs. But nothing
17049/// in either uses this arm — deleting it and building the workspace
17050/// `--all-targets` is clean, and there is no in-tree caller of
17051/// `nros::time::now` at all. So the arm serves an OUT-OF-TREE contract only: a
17052/// consumer with `std`, no `rmw-cffi`, and its own `Session`.
17053pub(crate) fn default_clock_us_fn() -> Option<fn() -> u64> {
17054    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
17055    {
17056        Some(default_platform_clock_us)
17057    }
17058    #[cfg(not(feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
17059    {
17060        None
17061    }
17062}
17063
17064// =============================================================================
17065// phase-425 W3b — the `/clock` time source's executor half.
17066//
17067// Its OWN impl block, gated on `sim-time`, because the methods were first
17068// written next to `declare_parameter` — which lives in a
17069// `#[cfg(feature = "param-store")]` block, so `reconcile_ros_time_source`
17070// silently disappeared in every combo without parameter services, including the
17071// one `spin_once` calls it from.
17072// =============================================================================
17073#[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17074impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
17075    /// phase-425 W3b — bring the `/clock` subscription in line with the last
17076    /// requested `use_sim_time`.
17077    ///
17078    /// Called at the head of every spin, and cheap when there is nothing to do:
17079    /// the common case is one bool comparison. It is a RECONCILE rather than an
17080    /// action at the request site because the request routinely arrives before
17081    /// there is a node to hang the subscription on — `nros::main!` emits
17082    /// `apply_param_services` before its per-node `register` calls, by design,
17083    /// so the store exists when each cell is created.
17084    ///
17085    /// Turning it off stops SAMPLES from being installed; the subscription
17086    /// itself stays, because the executor has no entity removal and inventing
17087    /// one for this would be a much larger change than the switch is worth. The
17088    /// gate is `time_source::set_active`, which the subscription callback reads.
17089    ///
17090    /// Turning it off also does NOT clear the override: a node that stops
17091    /// listening keeps the last simulated time rather than jumping back to the
17092    /// wall clock, which every ROS-time timer would otherwise absorb as a
17093    /// backwards jump.
17094    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17095    pub(crate) fn reconcile_ros_time_source(&mut self) {
17096        // An executor nobody told about `use_sim_time` has NO opinion, and the
17097        // gate is process-global, so writing its default here is not a no-op --
17098        // it is one executor overruling another. Say nothing until asked.
17099        if !self.sim_time_stated {
17100            return;
17101        }
17102        if self.sim_time_requested == crate::time_source::is_active()
17103            && (!self.sim_time_requested || self.sim_time_source.is_some())
17104        {
17105            return;
17106        }
17107        crate::time_source::set_active(self.sim_time_requested);
17108        if !self.sim_time_requested {
17109            // phase-430 W1 — the source is no longer wanted, so its silence is
17110            // no longer a symptom. Disarming here (rather than only re-arming
17111            // on attach) is what makes a later re-attach start a FRESH
17112            // interval: the watch that was counting is put down, not paused.
17113            self.sim_time_silence.disarm();
17114            return;
17115        }
17116        if self.sim_time_source.is_none() {
17117            // No node yet — stay pending and try again next spin. Not an error:
17118            // it is the ordinary order of a generated entry, which declares
17119            // parameters before it registers components.
17120            if self.nodes.is_empty() {
17121                return;
17122            }
17123            if let Ok(handle) = self.install_ros_time_source(
17124                super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY,
17125                crate::time_source::CLOCK_TOPIC,
17126            ) {
17127                self.sim_time_source = Some(handle);
17128                // phase-430 W1 — the interval starts HERE, at attach, and not
17129                // at construction: before the subscription exists there is
17130                // nothing to be silent about, so counting from boot would
17131                // accuse an image that spent the interval bringing a transport
17132                // up.
17133                self.sim_time_silence.arm();
17134            }
17135        } else {
17136            // Re-attached: `use_sim_time` went false and back to true while the
17137            // subscription (which the executor cannot remove) stayed. W1 asks
17138            // for the one-shot to reset in exactly this case.
17139            self.sim_time_silence.arm();
17140        }
17141    }
17142
17143    /// phase-430 W1 — credit one spin's elapsed time to the silence watch and
17144    /// emit the diagnostic if this is the spin that crosses the threshold.
17145    ///
17146    /// `delta_us` is the executor's OWN per-spin elapsed measure — the same one
17147    /// every wall timer on this executor accumulates, including its "no clock,
17148    /// credit the requested timeout" fallback. See
17149    /// [`SILENCE_WARN_US`](crate::time_source::SILENCE_WARN_US) for why that is
17150    /// the unit and not a spin count or an independent wall clock.
17151    ///
17152    /// Scope: the source the EXECUTOR installed for `use_sim_time`. An
17153    /// application that calls
17154    /// [`Node::install_ros_time_source`](super::node::Node::install_ros_time_source)
17155    /// directly is not watched, because the line this would print names
17156    /// `use_sim_time`, and that application never set it — the honest
17157    /// diagnostic for the explicit path would be a different sentence, and
17158    /// inventing one nobody asked for is how a warning becomes noise.
17159    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17160    fn note_sim_time_silence(&mut self, delta_us: u64) {
17161        if self.sim_time_silence.tick(
17162            delta_us,
17163            nros_core::clock::Clock::is_ros_time_override_active(),
17164        ) {
17165            crate::time_source::report_silence(crate::time_source::CLOCK_TOPIC);
17166        }
17167    }
17168
17169    /// phase-430 W1 — how many times this executor has reported that
17170    /// `use_sim_time` is on with no `/clock` sample.
17171    ///
17172    /// The count rather than a bool, and an accessor rather than a log grep: a
17173    /// diagnostic whose contract is "exactly once" needs an assertion that can
17174    /// tell one from two, and a log sink is not present on every target that
17175    /// runs the test. It is also the question an application supervising its
17176    /// own configuration would ask.
17177    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17178    pub fn sim_time_silence_warnings(&self) -> u32 {
17179        self.sim_time_silence.reports()
17180    }
17181
17182    /// phase-425 W3b — re-read `use_sim_time` from the parameter store.
17183    ///
17184    /// Called after a parameter service actually handled something, which is
17185    /// what makes a runtime `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true` work
17186    /// without a per-spin scan of the store.
17187    ///
17188    /// phase-430 W3 / issue 1202 — the declaration path calls it too, through
17189    /// `note_reserved_parameter`, once the store has accepted the write. It
17190    /// used to record the value directly from the caller's argument, which is
17191    /// the same thing only while the store never refuses. One read for both
17192    /// paths; a second spelling is the drift this function exists to prevent.
17193    /// `pub(crate)` for the same reason: a test that changes the store directly
17194    /// needs the entry point a parameter service uses, not a copy of it.
17195    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", feature = "param-store", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17196    pub(crate) fn refresh_use_sim_time_from_store(&mut self) {
17197        // phase-426 W1 — the store is keyed by NODE, and the simulated clock is
17198        // not. This function is where those two facts meet, so the rule is
17199        // stated here rather than left to whichever call site got there first.
17200        //
17201        // `use_sim_time` is a per-node parameter in ROS 2, and rclcpp means it:
17202        // every `Node` builds its own `TimeSource` over its own `Clock`, so two
17203        // nodes composed into one process CAN be configured differently and
17204        // stamp messages from different clocks at the same instant. This tree
17205        // deliberately does not follow that (phase-425): "the override is
17206        // process-global — one simulated clock per image, the model
17207        // `nros_core::Clock` already documents — so there is nothing to attach
17208        // to and nothing to fan out." That is the right trade for an image with
17209        // a fixed RAM budget, and it makes "whose `use_sim_time`?" a question
17210        // rclcpp never has to answer and this executor now does.
17211        //
17212        // ANY node asking arms the one source. Two reasons, and the second is
17213        // the binding one:
17214        //
17215        //   * it is the only rule the CALLERS can implement. `note_param_
17216        //     services_ran` fires after a runtime `ros2 param set` and knows
17217        //     only that N requests were handled — not which node was written.
17218        //     A last-writer-wins rule would need a writer identity that does
17219        //     not reach here, so it would silently degrade to "whatever node 0
17220        //     says", which is the default-to-primary bug phase-426 W1 exists to
17221        //     remove.
17222        //   * one node still wanting simulated time is a reason to keep the
17223        //     source attached, and detaching is the destructive direction:
17224        //     phase-425 already records that turning it off "stops SAMPLES, not
17225        //     the subscription", precisely so a mid-run change does not read as
17226        //     a clock jump.
17227        //
17228        // The scan is over the executor's own node table, which is the same
17229        // `u8` index space `NodeKey` wraps, so there is one node identity here
17230        // and not two.
17231        let Some(params) = self.params.as_deref() else {
17232            return;
17233        };
17234        let mut stated = false;
17235        let mut enable = false;
17236        // A `NodeId` IS the index into this table (`NodeId::index`), so the
17237        // enumeration is the key space — no second derivation of the number.
17238        //
17239        // `.max(1)` because `NodeId::PRIMARY` is IMPLICIT: the executor's node
17240        // table starts empty and a parameter can be declared on the primary
17241        // node before any `create_node` puts a record in it. Scanning only the
17242        // table would then find nothing and leave `sim_time_stated` false, so a
17243        // `use_sim_time` declared before the first node would never arm the
17244        // source — which `use_sim_time_attaches_and_detaches_the_clock_source`
17245        // catches, since its whole first half runs while "there is still no
17246        // node". Slot 0 is always a legitimate key; at worst the lookup misses.
17247        for idx in 0..self.nodes.len().max(1) {
17248            let key = nros_params::NodeKey::new(idx as u8);
17249            if let Some(v) = params
17250                .server
17251                .get_bool(key, crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM)
17252            {
17253                stated = true;
17254                enable |= v;
17255            }
17256        }
17257        if stated {
17258            self.sim_time_requested = enable;
17259            self.sim_time_stated = true;
17260        }
17261    }
17262
17263    /// phase-425 W3b — the installed `/clock` subscription, if any.
17264    ///
17265    /// The HANDLE rather than a bool, because "did we subscribe twice" is the
17266    /// question a reconciliation loop has to be able to answer: a second
17267    /// registration takes a new slot, so a stable handle across spins is the
17268    /// evidence that the loop is idempotent.
17269    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17270    pub fn ros_time_source_handle(&self) -> Option<HandleId> {
17271        self.sim_time_source
17272    }
17273
17274    /// phase-425 W3b — whether a `/clock` subscription is currently installed.
17275    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17276    pub fn ros_time_source_installed(&self) -> bool {
17277        self.sim_time_source.is_some()
17278    }
17279
17280    /// phase-425 W3 — subscribe `topic` and install every sample as this
17281    /// image's ROS time. The registration behind
17282    /// [`Node::install_ros_time_source`](super::node::Node::install_ros_time_source)
17283    /// and behind the `use_sim_time` reconciliation, so both spell the QoS and
17284    /// the conversion exactly once.
17285    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
17286    pub(crate) fn install_ros_time_source(
17287        &mut self,
17288        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
17289        topic: &str,
17290    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
17291        self.register_subscription_buffered_on::<
17292            nros_rosgraph_msgs::msg::Clock,
17293            _,
17294            { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
17295        >(
17296            node_id,
17297            topic,
17298            QoSProfile::clock_default(),
17299            |msg: &nros_rosgraph_msgs::msg::Clock| {
17300                // The `use_sim_time` gate is read HERE rather than by removing
17301                // the subscription, because there is no entity removal. An
17302                // image that never touches `use_sim_time` and installs the
17303                // source explicitly is active by default.
17304                if !crate::time_source::is_active() {
17305                    return;
17306                }
17307                if let Some(nanos) =
17308                    crate::time_source::override_nanos(msg.clock.sec, msg.clock.nanosec)
17309                {
17310                    nros_core::clock::Clock::set_ros_time_override(nanos);
17311                }
17312            },
17313            None, // no group — node default
17314            None, // the configured default RX buffer, unchanged
17315        )
17316    }
17317}

17319// ============================================================================
17320// phase-417 W4.c — cancel / is_spinning
17321// ============================================================================
17322//
17323// Same gate as `executor::tests`, exactly: `ConcreteSession` is `MockSession`
17324// only while no rmw-* feature is unified in (see `executor/mod.rs`), and
17325// `from_session_with` / `halt_flag` are `alloc`. No `std` gate — `cfg(test)`
17326// already means a hosted harness, which is why `lib.rs` brings `std` in under
17327// `test` as well. (It said "exactly" while missing `alloc`, and `std` was not in
17328// scope: 20 errors, hidden by feature unification under `--workspace`.)
17329#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
17330mod cancel_tests {
17331    use super::Executor;
17332    use crate::{executor::types::ExecutorConfig, mock::MockSession};
17333
17334    /// The core has no default clock and says so (issue 0709), so a test that
17335    /// measures elapsed time brings its own — the same seam a board uses.
17336    fn test_clock_us() -> u64 {
17337        use std::{sync::OnceLock, time::Instant};
17338        static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant> = OnceLock::new();
17339        EPOCH.get_or_init(Instant::now).elapsed().as_micros() as u64
17340    }
17341
17342    fn executor() -> Executor<'static> {
17343        let cfg = ExecutorConfig::default().clock_us(test_clock_us);
17344        Executor::from_session_with(MockSession::new(), &cfg)
17345    }
17346
17347    /// A fresh executor is neither cancelled nor spinning — the two questions
17348    /// are independent, and this is the state where both answers are `false`.
17349    #[test]
17350    fn a_fresh_executor_is_neither_cancelled_nor_spinning() {
17351        let exec = executor();
17352        assert!(!exec.is_halted(), "nothing has asked it to stop");
17353        assert!(!exec.is_spinning(), "no spin loop is running");
17354    }
17355
17356    /// `cancel()` raises the request bit without starting or stopping anything.
17357    #[test]
17358    fn cancel_requests_without_spinning() {
17359        let exec = executor();
17360        exec.cancel();
17361        assert!(exec.is_halted(), "cancel() must be observable immediately");
17362        assert!(
17363            !exec.is_spinning(),
17364            "cancel() must not make a non-spinning executor claim to spin"
17365        );
17366    }
17367
17368    /// The load-bearing one: `cancel()` from a peer thread TERMINATES a running
17369    /// `spin`, `is_spinning()` is true while the loop runs, and false
17370    /// once it has returned.
17371    ///
17372    /// The peer asserts `is_spinning()` from OUTSIDE the spinning thread, which
17373    /// is the whole point of the observable — it is what a signal handler or a
17374    /// supervisor sees.
17375    #[test]
17376    fn cancel_terminates_a_spin_and_is_spinning_tracks_it() {
17377        use std::{
17378            sync::{
17379                Arc,
17380                atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
17381            },
17382            thread,
17383            time::{Duration, Instant},
17384        };
17385
17386        let mut exec = executor();
17387        assert!(!exec.is_spinning());
17388
17389        // `Executor` is not `Sync`, so the peer thread cannot hold a reference
17390        // to it. It observes and drives through the two flag handles instead —
17391        // which is the supported cross-thread surface (`halt_flag()`), and
17392        // keeps this test on the same seam a signal handler uses.
17393        let cancel_bit = exec.halt_flag();
17394        let saw_spinning = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
17395        let saw_spinning_peer = Arc::clone(&saw_spinning);
17396
17397        let peer = thread::spawn(move || {
17398            // Give the loop time to enter. Bounded, and the assertion below is
17399            // on what was OBSERVED, so a slow host cannot turn this green by
17400            // accident — it fails instead.
17401            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
17402            saw_spinning_peer.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
17403            cancel_bit.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
17404        });
17405
17406        let started = Instant::now();
17407        exec.spin(crate::executor::types::SpinOptions::default())
17408            .expect("an untimed spin runs until cancelled");
17409        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
17410
17411        peer.join().expect("peer thread must not panic");
17412
17413        assert!(
17414            saw_spinning.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
17415            "the peer must have run before spin returned"
17416        );
17417        assert!(
17418            !exec.is_spinning(),
17419            "is_spinning() must be false once the loop has returned"
17420        );
17421        assert!(
17422            exec.is_halted(),
17423            "the cancel request survives the loop it ended"
17424        );
17425        // LOWER bound too: a spin that never waited would prove nothing about
17426        // termination. The peer sleeps 50 ms before cancelling.
17427        assert!(
17428            elapsed >= Duration::from_millis(40),
17429            "spin returned in {elapsed:?} — it cannot have spun"
17430        );
17431        // ...and an UPPER bound, because "terminated" is the claim: without the
17432        // cancel check this loop never returns and the test would hang rather
17433        // than fail. 10 s is far past any scheduling noise.
17434        assert!(
17435            elapsed < Duration::from_secs(10),
17436            "spin took {elapsed:?} to observe the cancel"
17437        );
17438    }
17439
17440    /// `is_spinning()` is true from INSIDE the loop. Read from a timer callback,
17441    /// which is the only place the executor is genuinely mid-spin, and asserted
17442    /// after the loop so a callback that never fired cannot pass silently.
17443    #[test]
17444    fn is_spinning_is_true_inside_the_loop() {
17445        use std::time::Duration;
17446
17447        let mut exec = executor();
17448        // `only_next` runs exactly one iteration, so this is a single poll
17449        // inside a spin scope — bounded, no thread, no clock dependency beyond
17450        // the one the fixture installs.
17451        assert!(!exec.is_spinning());
17452        exec.spin(crate::executor::types::SpinOptions::spin_once())
17453            .expect("a single-iteration spin must succeed");
17454        assert!(
17455            !exec.is_spinning(),
17456            "the scope must close when the loop returns"
17457        );
17458
17459        // The inside-the-loop reading needs a second thread to do it, because
17460        // the spinning thread is blocked in the loop and `Executor` is `!Sync`
17461        // so no `&Executor` may cross. What crosses is a pointer to the one
17462        // atomic, which is the same thing the C and C++ APIs hold: they observe
17463        // `is_spinning` through a raw executor handle, and that is the case this
17464        // flag exists to serve.
17465        struct FlagPtr(*const portable_atomic::AtomicBool);
17466        // SAFETY: the pointee is an `AtomicBool`, which is `Sync`; the only
17467        // operation performed through it is a relaxed-or-stronger load. The
17468        // executor outlives the thread — `peer.join()` below happens before
17469        // `exec` is dropped at the end of the test.
17470        unsafe impl Send for FlagPtr {}
17471
17472        let cancel_bit = exec.halt_flag();
17473        let observed = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
17474        let spinning_bit_seen = std::sync::Arc::clone(&observed);
17475        let flag = FlagPtr(&exec.spinning as *const portable_atomic::AtomicBool);
17476        let peer = std::thread::spawn(move || {
17477            let flag = flag;
17478            for _ in 0..500 {
17479                // SAFETY: see the `unsafe impl Send` above.
17480                if unsafe { &*flag.0 }.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
17481                    spinning_bit_seen.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
17482                    break;
17483                }
17484                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
17485            }
17486            cancel_bit.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
17487        });
17488
17489        exec.spin(crate::executor::types::SpinOptions::default())
17490            .expect("an untimed spin runs until cancelled");
17491        peer.join().expect("peer thread must not panic");
17492
17493        assert!(
17494            observed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),
17495            "is_spinning() must read true while spin is running"
17496        );
17497    }
17498
17499    /// `spin_period` maintains the same scope, and a period this build cannot
17500    /// pace is an error that must NOT leave the executor claiming to spin.
17501    #[test]
17502    fn spin_period_with_no_clock_leaves_is_spinning_false() {
17503        let mut exec = executor();
17504        exec.clock_us_fn = None;
17505        let err = exec
17506            .spin_period(core::time::Duration::from_millis(10))
17507            .expect_err("a period with no clock must fail (issue 0709)");
17508        assert_eq!(err, crate::NodeError::NotInitialized);
17509        assert!(
17510            !exec.is_spinning(),
17511            "a spin that never started must not report that it did"
17512        );
17513    }
17514
17515    /// Entering a spin CLEARS a stale cancel: a cancel requested before this
17516    /// spin is not a cancel of this spin. Documents the ADOPT-BOUNDED envelope's
17517    /// one sharp edge.
17518    #[test]
17519    fn entering_a_spin_clears_a_stale_cancel() {
17520        let exec = executor();
17521        exec.cancel();
17522        assert!(exec.is_halted());
17523        exec.enter_spin_loop();
17524        assert!(
17525            !exec.is_halted(),
17526            "a cancel raised before the loop started must not end it instantly"
17527        );
17528        assert!(exec.is_spinning());
17529        exec.exit_spin_loop();
17530        assert!(!exec.is_spinning());
17531    }
17532}

17534/// phase-509 P9b item 3 (RFC-0108 D7) -- the arrival path wakes only the
17535/// worker whose band holds the slot.
17536#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
17537mod band_wake_routing_tests {
17538    use super::{super::scheduler::BandWaiter, WakeCtx};
17539    use core::ffi::c_void;
17540    use portable_atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
17541
17542    static WOKEN: [AtomicUsize; 2] = [AtomicUsize::new(0), AtomicUsize::new(0)];
17543
17544    unsafe extern "C" fn wake(ctx: *mut c_void) {
17545        WOKEN[ctx as usize].fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
17546    }
17547
17548    unsafe extern "C" fn wait(_ctx: *mut c_void, _us: u64) -> i32 {
17549        0
17550    }
17551
17552    #[test]
17553    fn an_attributed_arrival_wakes_its_band_and_an_unattributed_one_wakes_all() {
17554        // SAFETY: the contexts are plain indices `wake` decodes.
17555        static A: BandWaiter = unsafe { BandWaiter::new(wake, wait, core::ptr::null_mut()) };
17556        static B: BandWaiter =
17557            unsafe { BandWaiter::new(wake, wait, core::ptr::without_provenance_mut(1)) };
17558        A.slots.store(0b0011, Ordering::SeqCst);
17559        B.slots.store(0b0100, Ordering::SeqCst);
17560        let flag = portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
17561        let ctx = WakeCtx::new(flag.clone(), None);
17562        B.next.store(&A as *const _ as *mut _, Ordering::SeqCst);
17563        ctx.band_waiters
17564            .store(&B as *const _ as *mut _, Ordering::SeqCst);
17565
17566        ctx.mark_ready(2);
17567        assert_eq!(WOKEN[1].load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1, "slot 2 is B's");
17568        assert_eq!(WOKEN[0].load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
17569        assert!(
17570            !flag.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
17571            "the executor's own worker sleeps on"
17572        );
17573
17574        ctx.mark_ready(1);
17575        assert_eq!(WOKEN[0].load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1, "slot 1 is A's");
17576
17577        ctx.mark_ready(5);
17578        assert!(
17579            flag.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
17580            "no band holds slot 5: own worker"
17581        );
17582        assert_eq!(
17583            WOKEN[0].load(Ordering::SeqCst) + WOKEN[1].load(Ordering::SeqCst),
17584            2
17585        );
17586
17587        ctx.signal();
17588        assert_eq!(
17589            WOKEN[0].load(Ordering::SeqCst),
17590            2,
17591            "unattributed: every band"
17592        );
17593        assert_eq!(WOKEN[1].load(Ordering::SeqCst), 2);
17594        assert_eq!(ctx.ready.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0b100110);
17595    }
17596}
